5216.q: Why is a force a vector quantity in physics and not a scalar?
a: Because a force has both a magnitude and a direction
Because forces can never be measured
Because a force is always zero
Because a force has no unit
5216.e: A value such as 10 newtons is not enough for a force; you also need to know in which direction it acts. Quantities such as temperature or mass, on the other hand, are scalars that only need a number.

5217.q: Why is the giant panda endangered in the wild?
a: Because its habitat is disappearing through deforestation
Because it has too many enemies in the water
Because it is too small to survive
5217.e: When forests are cut down, the panda loses its habitat and its bamboo. That is why protecting the forests is so important.

5218.q: What do bees make from nectar?
5218.e: The bees carry the nectar into the hive and turn it into honey there. Honey is their most important winter store.

5219.q: Which animal group does the hedgehog belong to?
5219.e: The hedgehog is a mammal, which means its young drink their mother's milk at first. It also has a coat with special spines.

5220.q: What is the difference between the EU and NATO?
a: The EU is an economic and political union, NATO a military defence alliance
The EU has a shared army, NATO does not
5220.e: The EU mainly promotes economic and political cooperation between its member states. NATO, on the other hand, is a military alliance whose members promise to help each other in case of attack. Switzerland belongs to neither.
5220.m: The EU is economic and political, NATO is military.

5221.q: What is the shape of the garden spider's web called?
5221.e: The garden spider's web looks like a wheel with lots of spokes. That is why such spiders are also called orb-weaver spiders.
5221.m: Its web looks like a wheel.

5222.q: At what altitude is the Alpine salamander mainly found?
a: About 700 to 2800 metres above sea level
5222.e: The Alpine salamander prefers to live at medium to high altitudes in the Alps. It is even found much higher up than the fire salamander.
5222.m: It lives high in the mountains.

5224.q: How do falcons usually kill their prey, unlike eagles and buzzards?
a: With a bite of the beak
5224.e: Eagles and buzzards kill their prey mainly with their talons. Falcons have a small tooth on their beak and usually kill with a bite to the neck.
5224.m: The beak is the falcon's weapon.

5225.q: Where do millipedes typically shelter in winter?
5225.e: In winter they retreat deeper into the soil. There it is free of frost and damp.
5225.m: In winter they move down into the soil.

5226.q: Why do African buffalo usually stay near watering holes?
a: They lay their eggs in the water
5226.e: Buffalo need water every day. That is why they often stay near rivers and water holes.

5227.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult male lion get?
5227.e: A large male lion can weigh up to about 250 kilograms. Lionesses are usually much lighter than the males.
5227.m: Male lions weigh up to 250 kilograms.

5228.q: What do ants use their antennae for when they meet?
5228.e: When two ants meet, they often touch each other with their antennae. This is how they exchange information.
5228.m: Antennae are used to exchange information.

5229.q: How does a bumblebee develop before it is an adult?
a: Egg, then straight to adult bumblebee
It is born as a small bumblebee
5229.e: Like many insects, the bumblebee goes through several stages. The egg becomes a larva, the larva becomes a pupa, and finally the adult bumblebee appears.

5230.q: How many toes does a common frog usually have on each back foot?
5230.e: The common frog has five toes on each back foot, joined by webbing. This helps it swim in the water.
5230.m: The common frog has five toes on each back foot.

5231.q: How does an octopus often hide from enemies?
a: It puffs itself up like a pufferfish
It makes itself hard like a stone
It swims to the water surface
5231.e: The octopus can change the colour of its skin in a flash. This is how it hides from predators.
5231.m: The octopus hides by changing colour.

5232.q: What can you see in some centipedes after an attack?
a: They change colour like a chameleon
They hide in the sand like crabs
5232.e: Some species shed legs when in danger so that they can escape. This is a defence strategy that lizards also use with their tails.

a: Only one party is allowed to govern.
Anyone may start their own party.
5233.e: In a one-party system only a single party is allowed. Other opinions and groups may not take part.
5233.m: Only one party has a say.

5234.q: What does it mean that the puma is a predator?
a: It catches and eats other animals
It only lives on dead animals in the water
5234.e: The puma usually kills its own prey. For this it has sharp teeth and strong jaws.

5235.q: Can you also see rhinos in Swiss zoos?
a: Yes, for example at Zurich Zoo
5235.e: In some Swiss zoos, such as Zurich Zoo, you can watch rhinos up close. They are well looked after there.
5235.m: Rhinos also live in Swiss zoos.

5236.q: Which predator is even bigger than the lion?
5236.e: The tiger is the largest big cat in the world, just ahead of the lion. Both belong to the same animal family.
5236.m: The tiger is a little bigger than the lion.

5237.q: How many legs does a honeybee have?
5237.e: Like all insects, the honeybee has six legs. It even carries pollen home on its back legs.
5237.m: Bees have six legs, like all insects.

5238.q: How do elephants communicate with each other over long distances?
a: With very low sounds that people can hardly hear
5238.e: Elephants make low sounds called infrasound. They can hear these over several kilometres, even though people cannot notice them.

5239.q: What does the Roman snail need lime for?
5239.e: Lime is important so that the snail's shell can grow and stay strong. Without lime it could not build a solid house.

5240.q: In which Swiss canton is the ibex especially well known as the animal on the coat of arms?
5240.e: The ibex has decorated the coat of arms of the canton of the Grisons for centuries. There it is seen as a symbol of the mountains.
5240.m: The Grisons shows the ibex on its coat of arms.

5241.q: Why do people sometimes fit special grilles or guards to cars?
a: To stop martens damaging cables in the engine compartment
To keep fish away from the radiator
To make it harder for insects to get inside
5241.e: Because martens sometimes damage cables in the engine compartment, some car owners fit special guards or deterrents. These are meant to stop martens getting into the engine compartment at all.

5242.q: How does a fire salamander usually react when you find one in the wild?
a: It usually moves only slowly and does not run away fast
5242.e: Because the fire salamander relies on its poison glands, it does not flee as hastily as other animals. It tends to move off at a leisurely pace.
5242.m: It moves off at a leisurely pace.

5243.q: What does a housefly use to taste whether something is delicious?
5243.e: As soon as a housefly lands on something, it can taste it with its feet. So it knows straight away whether the food is good.

5244.q: What do goldfish need in an aquarium so they can hide?
5244.e: Plants and hiding places make goldfish feel safe and make their home more varied. Without hiding places they sometimes feel stressed.
5244.m: Plants give goldfish places to hide.

5246.q: What are a pike's scales like?
a: Small and firmly attached to the body
There are no scales at all
5246.e: The pike's body is covered with lots of small, firm scales. These protect it in the water.
5246.m: Small scales protect the pike's body.

5247.q: What happens to an ibex's horns during its life?
a: They keep growing and are never shed
They fall off every year like a deer's
They change colour completely every year
5247.e: Unlike deer, which shed their antlers every year, ibex keep their horns for life. They keep on growing.
5247.m: Ibex horns grow all their life.

5248.q: What colour are young sparrows usually?
5248.e: Young sparrows at first look more like adult females, plain and brownish grey. Only later do the males get their black patch on the throat.
5248.m: Young sparrows look like the females.

5249.q: How many gold stars are on the flag of the European Union?
5249.e: The EU flag always shows 12 gold stars in a circle, no matter how many countries are members. The number 12 stands for unity and completeness.
5249.m: The EU flag always has twelve stars.

5250.q: What do you call a habitat such as the rainforest together with all the living things in it that depend on each other?
5250.e: An ecosystem is made up of a habitat and all the plants and animals in it that depend on each other. Gibbons are part of the rainforest ecosystem.
5250.m: Gibbons are part of the rainforest ecosystem.

5251.q: How do jackals walk on the ground?
a: On the whole sole of the foot
5251.e: Jackals are toe walkers. This makes them fast and gives them stamina.

5252.q: How can you often tell young common buzzards apart from adults?
a: By their more heavily streaked underside
By their tiny size, like a hummingbird
5252.e: Young common buzzards often have a more heavily streaked underside than adult birds. Over time their plumage changes and gets its typical markings.
5252.m: Young birds are more heavily streaked.

5253.q: Does the Roman snail have bones?
a: Yes, but only in its head
Yes, but only in its foot
5253.e: The Roman snail has no bones at all in its body. Instead, its shell made of lime protects it.

5254.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker especially like to eat in winter?
5254.e: In winter there are fewer insects, so it eats seeds from cones and nuts instead. These are rich in energy.
5254.m: In winter it eats seeds and nuts.

5256.q: What is it called when cantons, parties and associations may give their views on a planned law before it goes to parliament?
5256.e: In the consultation procedure, different groups can comment on a draft law before it is debated in parliament.
5256.m: The consultation procedure collects opinions in advance.

5257.q: What can you often see on a comb jelly when light falls on it?
5257.e: Comb jellies have rows of tiny hairs that they use to swim. When light falls on them, they shimmer in all the colours of the rainbow.

5258.q: What does a magpie's nest typically look like?
a: Large, with a roof of twigs
Small and in a hole in the ground
Made of mud like a swallow's
5258.e: Magpie nests are large, ball-shaped structures made of twigs, closed at the top like a roof. This protects the eggs and chicks from enemies and bad weather.
5258.m: Magpie nests have a protective roof.

5259.q: What do tadpoles lose as they turn into frogs?
5259.e: When a tadpole turns into a little frog, its tail slowly shrinks away. At the same time it grows legs.
5259.m: The tadpole's tail disappears as it changes.

5261.q: How is a wasp's waist different from a bee's?
a: The wasp's waist is thinner and easier to see
Bees have no waist at all
5261.e: Wasps have a very narrow waist, almost like a thin string. In bees this join is much rounder and thicker.

5262.q: What do adult common frogs like to eat most?
5262.e: Adult common frogs are meat eaters and hunt small animals such as insects, snails and worms. They do not eat plants.

5263.q: Where does the barn swallow like to build its nest best?
a: On the ground in open meadows
5263.e: Barn swallows usually nest inside buildings such as cowsheds or barns. There they find shelter from the weather and enemies.
5263.m: The nest is usually on a beam in a cowshed.

5264.q: What does a guinea pig usually do when it is scared?
5264.e: Guinea pigs are prey animals that flee, not fighters. When in danger they would rather hide or stand completely still.
5264.m: Guinea pigs hide when in danger.

5265.q: What does the organisation KORA do in Switzerland?
a: It researches predators such as the lynx and wolf
It builds hiking trails in the Alps
It organises the hunting of roe deer
5265.e: KORA collects data on predators such as the lynx, wolf and golden jackal, for example with camera traps. It works closely with the authorities.

5266.q: What is used to measure weather data high up in the atmosphere?
5266.e: Weather balloons carry instruments high up and send data on temperature, pressure and humidity to ground stations.
5266.m: Weather balloons measure data high up in the air.

a: Yes, they see perfectly from the start
No, they never see in their whole life
5267.e: Tiger cubs are born blind and only open their eyes after a few days. During this time they depend especially on their mother.

5268.q: Roughly how long does a common earwig live?
5268.e: The earwig only lives a short time. It usually manages about a year.

5269.q: In which country do wild bonobos live?
a: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo
5269.e: Bonobos live in only one country, the Democratic Republic of the Congo. There they live in the rainforest south of the River Congo.
5269.m: Bonobos only live in the Congo.

5270.q: What colour is the milk a cow gives?
5270.e: The milk a cow gives is always white, whatever colour the cow's coat is. Some children think brown cows give chocolate milk, but that is not true.

5271.q: Why did researchers in Switzerland used to find it hard to observe the lynx?
a: Because it is very shy and hides well
Because it only lives in water
Because it never existed in Switzerland
5271.e: Lynxes are secretive, nocturnal animals that are rarely seen by people. Their well-camouflaged fur makes observing them even harder.
5271.m: The lynx likes to stay out of sight.

5272.q: How does the wood mouse behave towards others of its kind?
a: It mostly lives alone and defends its territory
It always lives in huge herds
It shares its burrow with foxes
5272.e: Wood mice mostly live alone and defend their own small territory against other mice.

a: An attempt by Czechoslovakia to make communism more humane, ended by Soviet troops
The start of communist rule in Czechoslovakia
A trade fair in Eastern Europe
5273.e: Under Alexander Dubček, Czechoslovakia tried to reform socialism. Warsaw Pact troops ended this attempt with an invasion.
5273.m: The Prague Spring was an attempt at reform that was crushed.

5274.q: What are dragonflies especially good at in flight?
a: Hovering on the spot and flying backwards
5274.e: Dragonflies control each of their four wings separately. This lets them hover, turn suddenly and sometimes fly backwards.

5275.q: What happens if a dolphin calf needs help while its mother is hunting?
a: Another female often looks after it
5275.e: In dolphin groups, the females often help each other. They also look after the young of other mothers.
5275.m: Dolphin mothers help each other babysit.

5276.q: What does a hippo's body look like?
a: Like a ball with no legs
5276.e: The hippo's body is round like a barrel and sits on short, strong legs. This helps it look heavy and be stable.
5276.m: Hippos have short legs and a big belly.

5277.q: What does a meerkat mainly eat?
5277.e: Meerkats feed mainly on insects, spiders and scorpions. Sometimes they also eat small vertebrates and eggs.

5278.q: Roughly what body length does an adult common raven reach?
5278.e: The common raven is a fairly large bird with a body length of around 54 to 67 centimetres. This makes it much bigger than a carrion crow.

5279.q: What does the ring-tailed lemur use the “tooth comb” in its lower jaw for?
a: Among other things, for grooming its fur
5279.e: The front teeth in the lower jaw stand close together like a comb. Ring-tailed lemurs use them to comb their own fur and that of their group members.
5279.m: The tooth comb is used for grooming.

5280.q: Which animal group do grasshoppers belong to?
5280.e: Grasshoppers are insects with six legs. Experts group them together with crickets and bush crickets.

a: Newspapers may write what really happens.
5281.e: With a free press, journalists may report the truth even if the government doesn’t like it. In dictatorships this is often forbidden.
5281.m: A free press reports the truth.

5282.q: Does the panda hibernate in winter like other bears?
5282.e: Pandas do not hibernate, because they need bamboo all year round. They stay active in winter too.

5283.q: How does the moon change its appearance in the sky over a month?
5283.e: The moon does not shine by itself; we only see the part lit by the sun. That is why the moon sometimes looks like a crescent and sometimes completely round.
5283.m: The moon changes shape every month.

5284.q: What happens when a sparrow in the group notices danger?
a: they all fly up together at once
5284.e: If a sparrow notices danger, it warns the others and the whole group flies up together at once. That way nobody is in danger for long.
5284.m: When there is danger, the whole group flies up.

5285.q: Roughly how big does an adult carrion crow get?
5285.e: An adult carrion crow measures about 45 to 47 centimetres from the tip of its beak to the tip of its tail. This makes it much smaller than the common raven.
5285.m: Carrion crows grow to around 46 centimetres.

5286.q: How does the polecat defend itself against enemies?
a: It releases a strong-smelling liquid from glands
5286.e: The polecat has scent glands with which it can release a strong-smelling liquid. This powerful smell is meant to scare enemies away.
5286.m: The polecat scares off enemies with a stink.

5287.q: What kind of social animals are llamas?
5287.e: Llamas live in groups. They do not feel comfortable alone.

5288.q: How does a gorilla usually move around?
a: On all fours, leaning on its knuckles
5288.e: Gorillas usually walk on all fours and lean on their knuckles as they go. This is called knuckle-walking.

5289.q: How many legs does a sand lizard have?
5289.e: Like almost all lizards, it has four strong legs for running and climbing. This makes it different from legless snakes, for example.

5290.q: What is the procedure for resolving differences?
a: The National Council and the Council of States bring their different decisions on a law into line
5290.e: If the National Council and the Council of States disagree on a law, the proposal is sent back and forth until they reach agreement. This is called resolving differences.
5290.m: Resolving differences settles disagreements between the chambers.

5291.q: Why is it a good idea to look at prices when shopping with your parents?
a: So you learn how much things cost and shop thoughtfully
Because the shop staff require it
Because otherwise you will be punished
5291.e: If you pay attention to prices, you learn what things are worth and can make more thoughtful decisions. This helps later when you run your own household.
5291.m: Looking at prices helps you learn.

5292.q: Which habitat does the great crested grebe prefer for breeding?
a: Lakes and ponds with reeds and water plants
5292.e: Great crested grebes need waters with enough reeds and water plants for building nests and for cover. Such habitats protect them from enemies.
5292.m: Lakes full of reeds are its breeding ground.

5293.q: What does the typical call of the kingfisher sound like?
a: a melodious twitter like a blackbird
5293.e: The kingfisher calls with a short, high, piercing whistle. You often hear it before you even see it.
5293.m: A high whistle gives the kingfisher away.

5294.q: In barn owls, who mainly sits on the eggs?
5294.e: Usually the female sits on the eggs and keeps them warm. The male helps by fetching food.
5294.m: The female sits on the eggs.

5295.q: What do mute swans do in winter when lakes freeze over?
5295.e: When water freezes, swans look for open patches where they can still swim and feed. Sometimes they gather there in groups.
5295.m: In winter swans look for open water.

5296.q: What are fox cubs like when they are born?
a: Able to run straight away like foals
Already with sharp teeth and fully independent
5296.e: Fox cubs are born blind and deaf and depend completely on their mother. They only open their eyes after about two weeks.
5296.m: Fox cubs are blind at first.

5297.q: According to conservationists, how is the hippo population assessed today?
a: It is not protected at all
5297.e: The hippo is considered a threatened species, because its habitat is getting smaller and smaller. Conservationists are trying to protect it.

5298.q: Do penguins have teeth in their mouths?
a: No, but they have spiky barbs on their tongue
Yes, sharp teeth like a shark
No, they have no mouth at all
5298.e: Penguins have no real teeth, but they do have spiky barbs in their throat and on their tongue. These help them hold on to slippery fish and swallow them.
5298.m: Penguins have barbs instead of teeth.

5299.q: What does an adult salmon mainly eat in the sea?
5299.e: In the sea, the salmon hunts fish such as herring and small crustaceans. This makes it big and strong.
5299.m: In the sea, salmon eat fish and crustaceans.

5300.q: What do meerkats have around their eyes that protects them from sunlight?
5300.e: The dark rings around the eyes work rather like sunglasses. They reduce the glare from the bright light.
5300.m: Dark eye rings work like sunglasses.

5301.q: Among other things, what does the Consumer Credit Act (KKG) in Switzerland provide?
a: A right of withdrawal to cancel a small loan within a short period
That small loans must always be interest-free
That minors may take out as many loans as they like
That everyone automatically gets a loan
5301.e: The Consumer Credit Act protects consumers, among other things with a right of withdrawal that allows a credit agreement to be cancelled within a short period. Lenders must also check whether the borrower can afford the loan.
5301.m: You can withdraw from a small loan within a short time.

5302.q: How do young blackbirds often leave the nest?
a: They can hop before they can fly properly
They fly away perfectly straight away
They stay in the nest all their life
5302.e: Young blackbirds often leave the nest before they can really fly well. They then hop around on the ground and are still fed by their parents.
5302.m: Young blackbirds often hop before they fly.

5303.q: Which Swiss city has a zoo where you can see snow leopards?
5303.e: Zurich Zoo keeps snow leopards in a mountain enclosure. They have also been kept at Basel Zoo.
5303.m: Snow leopards live at Zurich Zoo.

5304.q: What is social grooming in baboons?
a: They clean each other's fur and strengthen bonds
5304.e: When grooming, they remove dirt and parasites. At the same time it strengthens friendships and calms the animals.

5305.q: What does the spring dumbledor beetle mainly feed on?
5305.e: The spring dumbledor eats dung, for example from deer or cows, and also buries it for its larvae. This helps bring nutrients into the soil.
5305.m: Dung beetles make use of other animals' droppings.

5306.q: What is an adult female pig called?
5306.e: An adult female pig is called a sow. After giving birth she takes loving care of her piglets.
5306.m: An adult female pig is called a sow.

5307.q: How does an octopus move along the seabed?
5307.e: On the seabed, the octopus usually crawls along on its arms. To swim fast, however, it prefers to use jet propulsion.
5307.m: The octopus crawls with its arms.

5308.q: What is the badger especially good at?
5308.e: With its strong paws and claws, the badger digs long tunnels in the ground. That is where it lives.
5308.m: The badger is a good digger.

5309.q: Why is it sometimes hard to tell the edible frog apart from its two parent species with certainty?
a: Because it combines outward features of both parent species
Because it can never be seen
5309.e: Because the edible frog is a cross between the marsh frog and the pool frog, it often shows features of both species. That is why close examination is sometimes needed to tell the three species apart for sure.
5309.m: The edible frog mixes features of both parent species.

5310.q: What does a polar bear eat first when it catches a seal?
5310.e: The seal's fatty blubber is especially important for the polar bear. It gives it lots of energy for the cold.
5310.m: The polar bear eats the blubber first.

5311.q: What happens to goldfish in a pond when it gets cold in winter?
a: They become calmer and move less
5311.e: In winter, goldfish in a pond slow down their metabolism and hardly move. This way they survive the cold season, as long as the pond does not freeze solid.

5312.q: In which country do people often eat carp at Christmas?
5312.e: In the Czech Republic, fried carp is a traditional part of the Christmas meal. Many families buy a carp especially for it.
5312.m: In the Czech Republic people eat carp at Christmas.

5313.q: Where do most species of isopod live?
5313.e: Most isopod species live in water, especially in the sea. Woodlice that live on land are only part of the group.

5314.q: What does an especially dark mane on a male lion often show?
a: That he is strong and healthy
That he is still a baby
5314.e: In lions, a dark, thick mane is seen as a sign of strength and good health. Lionesses often prefer males with dark manes.
5314.m: A dark mane shows strength and health.

5316.q: What does it mean when a hippo opens its mouth wide?
a: It is threatening and showing its strength
It is tired and yawning before sleep
5316.e: Opening the mouth wide is usually a threat to other hippos. This is how they show who is stronger.
5316.m: A wide-open mouth is a threat.

5317.q: Why were foxes often linked with the disease rabies in the past?
a: Because back then they often spread rabies
Because rabies only occurs in foxes and nowhere else
Because foxes are immune to rabies and were therefore to blame
5317.e: In the past, foxes in Switzerland often spread the dangerous disease rabies. Thanks to targeted vaccination campaigns, rabies in foxes was successfully pushed back.
5317.m: Foxes used to spread rabies often.

a: A company or person can no longer pay their debts and the remaining assets are sold off by court order
A company makes a particularly high profit
5318.e: Bankruptcy means that someone cannot pay and their assets are shared out among the creditors through a court procedure. It can affect companies as well as private individuals.
5318.m: Bankruptcy means being unable to pay.

5319.q: Which particle in the atomic nucleus has no electric charge?
5319.e: Neutrons are in the atomic nucleus and are electrically neutral, unlike the positively charged protons. Electrons circle the nucleus and are negatively charged.

5320.q: How often a year does the stone marten change its coat?
5320.e: Stone martens have a summer coat and a thicker winter coat. The change adapts their coat to the different temperatures through the year.
5320.m: Stone martens change their coat twice a year.

5321.q: Where do many red kites from Switzerland go in winter?
a: to Africa south of the Sahara
5321.e: Many red kites leave Switzerland in autumn and spend the winter in warmer parts of western Europe such as Spain or southern France. There they find enough food even in winter.
5321.m: Many red kites spend the winter in Spain.

5322.q: What are price comparison websites useful for?
a: To compare prices or services of different providers before buying or signing up
To automatically choose the most expensive offer
5322.e: Comparison websites show different offers side by side clearly, for example for insurance or mobile phone contracts. This makes it easier to find a cheap offer that suits you.

5323.q: Roughly how long is a sow pregnant with her piglets before they are born?
5323.e: Pregnancy in pigs lasts about 115 days, so almost four months. Then the piglets are born.
5323.m: Piglets grow in the womb for about four months.

5324.q: What is the males' throat sac for?
a: It makes their loud calls stronger
It is used for carrying young
It keeps them warm at night
5324.e: The throat sac works like a sound chamber. This means the males' calls can be heard far away.
5324.m: The throat sac makes calls louder.

5326.q: In carrion crows, who builds the nest?
a: the whole crow family from the year before
5326.e: The male and female build their nest together, usually high up in a tree. This also strengthens the bond between the two birds.
5326.m: Carrion crow pairs build the nest together.

5327.q: What do tiger cubs drink in their first weeks?
5327.e: In their first weeks, tiger cubs drink only their mother's milk. Only later do they eat meat as well.

5328.q: Roughly how long does an Atlantic salmon live?
a: A few years, usually up to about 5 to 8
5328.e: Salmon usually live for several years, some up to about eight. The exact length depends on their environment and migration.

5329.q: How do common buzzard pairs often behave over several years?
a: They often stay together as a pair
They never live together as a pair
They only meet once in their lives
5329.e: Common buzzards are usually monogamous and often stay with the same partner for several years. They also often use the same nest again and again.
5329.m: Pairs often stay together for a long time.

5330.q: Which feature shows that the snow leopard is a mammal?
a: Its young drink their mother's milk
5330.e: Mammals feed their young with milk. The snow leopard also has fur and is warm-blooded.
5330.m: Mammals feed their young with milk.

5331.q: Where was the dromedary probably first domesticated?
5331.e: People there began keeping dromedaries a few thousand years ago. From there they spread to other desert regions.

5332.q: What colour is a cheetah's fur?
5332.e: The cheetah's fur is yellowish brown and covered with lots of small black spots. This lets it hide well in tall grass.
5332.m: Cheetah fur is yellow with spots.

5333.q: How many young does a female stone marten usually have in a litter?
5333.e: A litter usually has three to four young. They are born in spring, when there is more food again.
5333.m: Usually three to four young per litter.

5334.q: What is the legal status of the common raven in Switzerland today?
5334.e: Today the common raven is protected by law in Switzerland. This has helped its numbers recover.
5334.m: The common raven is protected today.

5335.q: What is a jellyfish's body made of almost entirely?
5335.e: A jellyfish's body is almost 95 percent water. That is why it is so see-through and soft.
5335.m: Jellyfish are made almost only of water.

5336.q: Why does a sow have so many teats on her belly?
a: So that all her many piglets can drink at the same time
So that she can walk better
So that she can grow faster
So that she can hear better
5336.e: Because a sow often has eight or more piglets at once, she needs lots of teats. That way all the piglets can drink milk together.
5336.m: Lots of piglets need lots of teats.

5337.q: What is special about many aphids in summer?
a: The females give birth to live young
They only lay eggs in water
They only live in the soil
5337.e: In summer, many female aphids give birth to live young. These soon have young of their own.
5337.m: Summer aphids give birth to live young.

5339.q: When is the stone marten's mating season?
5339.e: Mating takes place in summer, but the young are not born until much later. The reason is a special delay in their development.

5340.q: What do bees do in winter?
a: They form a winter cluster and keep each other warm
They sleep deep in the ground
5340.e: In winter, bees huddle close together and shiver their flight muscles. This produces heat and helps them survive the cold.
5340.m: In winter bees keep each other warm.

5341.q: Where do wild boar most like to sleep during the day?
a: In a bed made of leaves
In a nest of branches high in a tree
In a cave in the rock
In an open field with no shelter
5341.e: Wild boar make a soft bed out of leaves and twigs, which German hunters call a “Kessel”. There they hide and rest.
5341.m: Their resting bed is made of leaves.

5342.q: Roughly how old can a snow leopard get in the wild?
5342.e: In captivity they often live longer, up to about 20 years. Life in the wild is harder.
5342.m: In the wild they live to about 10 to 12.

5343.q: How is the sand lizard especially good at picking up smells around it?
a: With its tongue, which it uses for smelling
5343.e: It sticks out its tongue to pick up scent particles and senses them with a special organ in its mouth. This is how it finds prey and others of its kind.
5343.m: The tongue is also used for smelling.

5344.q: Roughly how old can a hedgehog get in the wild?
5344.e: In the wild, hedgehogs usually live between three and seven years. Sadly, many do not survive their first winters.
5344.m: Wild hedgehogs usually live a few years.

a: The distance light travels in one year
The time a planet takes to go round once
An especially bright year for astronomers
The time between two solar eclipses
5345.e: A light year is a unit of distance, not of time, and is about 9.5 trillion kilometres. It is used to make the huge distances in space easier to understand.
5345.m: A light year measures distance, not time.

5347.q: What happens to a harbour seal's heartbeat when it dives deep?
a: It goes faster and slower by turns
5347.e: When a harbour seal dives deep, its heartbeat slows down so that it uses less oxygen. This lets it stay underwater for longer.
5347.m: When diving, the heart beats more slowly.

5348.q: What damage can an earwig sometimes do in the garden?
a: It nibbles tender flowers and ripe fruit
It sucks roots dry like a leech
5348.e: Sometimes it nibbles flowers such as dahlias or soft fruit. Overall, though, it usually does more good than harm.
5348.m: Sometimes it nibbles flowers and fruit.

5349.q: What is the tiger's typical hunting technique, in which it creeps up close to its prey, called?
5349.e: Tigers hunt by stalking: they creep silently up close to their prey. Only at the last moment do they attack at lightning speed.

5350.q: Why do wall lizards often sunbathe on stone walls?
a: Because stones store the sun's heat well
Because they have to build nests there
5350.e: Stones warm up in the sun and give off the heat for a long time. This makes walls ideal places to sunbathe.
5350.m: Stones store a lot of heat.

5351.q: How is the cheetah's coat pattern different from the leopard's?
a: The cheetah has simple spots instead of rosettes
The cheetah has no spots at all
The cheetah is striped like a zebra
5351.e: The leopard has ring-shaped spots called rosettes. The cheetah, on the other hand, only has simple, round black spots.
5351.m: Cheetah spots are simple, not rosettes.

5352.q: You see a leopard and a cheetah. How can you recognise the cheetah?
a: By the black tear stripes on its face
5352.e: Cheetahs have black lines running from the eyes to the mouth and simple spots on their fur. Leopards have rosettes.
5352.m: The cheetah has tear stripes on its face, the leopard has rosettes in its fur.

5353.q: Which bird do some people confuse with the blackbird?
5353.e: From a distance, the starling looks just as black as a blackbird. If you look more closely, though, you can see clear differences.
5353.m: Blackbirds and starlings are sometimes confused.

5354.q: Roughly how long is a female ibex pregnant?
5354.e: After mating in winter, the female carries her young for around five to six months. The kid is usually born in early summer.

5355.q: What are tiny trout that have just hatched called?
5355.e: When a trout hatches from its egg, it is called fry. At that point it is still very small and weak.
5355.m: Newly hatched trout are called fry.

5356.q: Where does the rainbow trout originally come from?
5356.e: The rainbow trout originally comes from North America. Later it was brought to Switzerland and released here too.
5356.m: Rainbow trout come from North America.

5357.q: What do tiny, newly hatched pike eat first?
5357.e: Very young pike are still too small for big prey. At first they eat tiny creatures in the water.
5357.m: Young pike eat tiny animals first.

5358.q: How does the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) rate the wolf worldwide?
5358.e: Worldwide, the wolf is not considered threatened, because there are still large populations in many regions. In individual countries or areas, however, the situation can be very different.
5358.m: Worldwide, the wolf is not considered threatened.

5359.q: How many animals often live together in a group of meerkats?
5359.e: A group usually has about 10 to 30 animals. Sometimes there are a few more.

5360.q: What temperatures can Bactrian camels cope with?
a: From hard frost to great heat
5360.e: In the Gobi Desert it is very cold in winter and hot in summer. Bactrian camels are adapted to both.
5360.m: They can cope with frost and heat.

5361.q: Which body posture often shows that a brown bear feels threatened?
a: It lowers its head and lays its ears back
It wags its tail in a friendly way
It just lies down to sleep
5361.e: When a bear feels threatened, it often lowers its head, lays its ears back and stares at the danger. Such signals should be taken as a clear warning.
5361.m: A lowered head often shows it feels threatened.

5362.q: What is the part of a beaver's territory created by the dam called?
5362.e: The dam holds back the water and creates a calm beaver pond, which the beaver uses for protection and as a route for moving things. At the same time, this pond provides a home for many other animals.
5362.m: The dam creates a beaver pond.

5364.q: What does it mean when an animal species is “endangered”?
a: It could die out in the future
5364.e: Endangered means that the survival of the species is under threat. Several species of tapir are on the Red List.
5364.m: An endangered species is at risk of dying out.

5365.q: What are a tapir's eyes like compared with its body?
5365.e: Tapirs have small eyes and do not see very well. They make up for this with their sense of smell and hearing.

5366.q: What job do millipedes do in the forest?
a: They break down leaves and make nutrients usable again
They chase away all the mice
5366.e: By eating leaves and breaking them up, they help to make humus. This improves the soil for plants.
5366.m: They help keep forest soil healthy.

5367.q: What are an elephant's tusks for?
5367.e: Elephants use their tusks to strip bark from trees, dig for water or defend themselves. They are very important tools.

5368.q: What does the wall lizard use to pick up smells from the air?
5368.e: The wall lizard's tongue picks up scent particles and passes them on to a special sense organ. This is how it explores its surroundings.

5369.q: Roughly how small can the smallest known shark be?
a: About as long as a hand
About as long as a car
About as long as a football pitch
About as long as a house
5369.e: Some dwarf sharks only grow to about 20 centimetres long. That is tiny compared with big sharks.
5369.m: The smallest shark is only the size of a hand.

5370.q: Is the polar bear a big bear or a small bear?
a: One of the biggest bears in the world
The smallest bear in the world
About as big as a dog
About as big as a cat
5370.e: The polar bear is one of the largest bears there are. A male can weigh as much as several horses together.
5370.m: The polar bear is one of the biggest bears.

5371.q: According to Karl Marx, what was the long-term final goal of the communist movement?
a: A classless society without private ownership of the means of production
A society with even more social classes
5371.e: Marx saw the final goal as a society without class differences and without private ownership of factories and land. In this phase the state would, in theory, become unnecessary.
5371.m: Marx's goal was a classless society without private property.

5372.q: Which disease can mosquitoes spread in warm countries?
5372.e: In some warm countries, certain mosquitoes carry germs that can cause malaria. In Switzerland, however, this practically never happens.

5373.q: What danger do hyenas face from humans today?
a: Loss of their habitat and persecution
Too many predators in the sea
Too cold a climate in Africa
5373.e: Where people use the land, hyenas often come into conflict with herders. They are persecuted or lose their habitat.
5373.m: Hyenas are losing habitat because of people.

5374.q: Roughly how many eggs does a female wall lizard lay in each clutch?
5374.e: A wall lizard's clutch is fairly small. Depending on the female and the conditions, there can be several clutches a year.
5374.m: The wall lizard lays few eggs per clutch.

5375.q: Why is there a closed season for fish such as the lake trout?
a: So that they can breed undisturbed
5375.e: During the spawning season, fish must not be caught. That way enough fish are left to produce young.

a: No, not a single species can fly
5376.e: Many species of grasshopper use their wings to fly. Others prefer to jump.

5377.q: Do dolphins come onto land to rest?
a: No, they always stay in the water
5377.e: Dolphins spend their whole lives in the water. Even for resting and sleeping they stay in the sea.
5377.m: Dolphins always stay in the water.

5378.q: How is a dolphin's tail fin different from a fish's?
a: It is horizontal instead of vertical
It is much smaller than a fish's
5378.e: A dolphin's tail fin is horizontal, while a fish's is usually vertical. This suits the up-and-down movement of dolphins.
5378.m: Dolphin tails are horizontal, fish tails vertical.

5379.q: On which continent do most white rhinos live?
5379.e: White rhinos live in the African savannah, for example in South Africa. There is plenty of grass to eat there.

5380.q: When is the lynx mainly active?
5380.e: The lynx is active at dusk and at night. During the day it usually rests hidden in sheltered places.
5380.m: The lynx hunts mainly at night.

5381.q: When was the okapi discovered by science?
a: At the start of the 20th century
5381.e: Science only knew about the okapi from around 1901. This makes it one of the large mammals discovered late.
5381.m: The okapi only became known in 1901.

5382.q: Roughly how fast can a dolphin swim?
a: Up to about 30 kilometres per hour
5382.e: Dolphins are very fast swimmers and can reach up to around 30 kilometres per hour. This helps them hunt and escape.
5382.m: Dolphins swim at up to 30 km/h.

5383.q: Do grass snake parents look after their hatched young?
a: No, the young are independent straight away
Yes, they carry them on their backs
Yes, they guard them for a year
5383.e: After hatching, the young do not stay with their mother. They find food themselves.
5383.m: Young grass snakes are on their own from the start.

5384.q: What colour are young storks' legs at first?
5384.e: Young storks have grey legs and a darker beak at first. Only over time do these turn bright red.
5384.m: Young storks have grey legs at first.

5385.q: Why do some cats nibble grass?
a: To get rid of hair they have swallowed
Because grass is their favourite food
5385.e: Even though cats are meat eaters, they sometimes eat a little grass. This helps them get rid of hair they have swallowed.

5386.q: Which animal is an enemy that often tries to take the wild dogs' prey?
5386.e: Lions and spotted hyenas sometimes steal the wild dogs' prey. Lions can also kill wild dogs.
5386.m: Lions and hyenas are rivals of wild dogs.

5387.q: What do some ducks do in winter to reach warmer areas?
a: They fly south as migrating birds
They hide in holes in trees
They swim all the way to Africa
5387.e: When it gets too cold here, some species of duck fly to warmer countries as migrating birds. In spring they come back again.
5387.m: Some ducks fly away in winter.

5388.q: Can a housefly bite like a mosquito?
a: No, its mouthpart can only suck
Yes, it bites just the same
5388.e: The mosquito has a sharp, piercing mouthpart. The housefly's mouthpart, on the other hand, is soft and can only suck up liquids, so it does not bite.

5389.q: What is a typical difference between the noses of the stone marten and the pine marten?
a: The stone marten's is lighter, the pine marten's darker
Only the stone marten has a nose at all
The pine marten's nose is completely white
Both have exactly the same nose colour
5389.e: The stone marten has a light, usually flesh-coloured or grey nose, while the pine marten has a darker, often almost black nose. This feature helps tell the two species apart.

a: A non-binding poll of the people on a question
A vote of the cantons only
A secret vote in the Federal Council
A vote that immediately creates a law
5390.e: In a consultative vote the opinion of the population is sought without the result being legally binding. It serves the authorities as a guide.

5391.q: How does the female Alpine newt lay her eggs?
a: One at a time, wrapped in the leaves of water plants
In one big clump on the bottom
5391.e: The female attaches each egg separately to the leaf of a water plant and folds the leaf over it for protection. This keeps the eggs well hidden.
5391.m: Each egg is wrapped in a leaf on its own.

5392.q: Which large dog breed originally comes from the Bernese Oberland?
5392.e: The Bernese Mountain Dog has a black, white and brown coat and used to work on farms as a guard dog and draught dog. It is one of the well-known Swiss mountain dog breeds.
5392.m: The Bernese Mountain Dog comes from Switzerland.

5393.q: Why do people put a little house in a hamster's cage?
a: So that it can hide safely during the day
So that it can swim in it
So that it can climb on it like a tree
So that it only eats in it
5393.e: A little house gives the hamster a safe hiding place to sleep. Without a place to retreat to, it quickly feels unsafe.
5393.m: A little house is a hiding place.

5394.q: What is the technical term for the skin that covers a moose's growing antlers?
5394.e: The growing antlers are covered with hairy skin called velvet. When the antlers are fully grown, it is rubbed off.

5395.q: Which bird family does the grey heron belong to?
5395.e: The grey heron belongs to the heron family, the Ardeidae. This family includes many similar wading birds around the world.
5395.m: Grey herons belong to the heron family.

5396.q: How does a Roman snail lay its eggs?
a: In a hole in the ground
5396.e: The snail digs a small hole in the ground with its foot. There it lays its round, white eggs.
5396.m: The eggs go into a hole in the ground.

5397.q: What is more important to ants than seeing?
5397.e: Ants can smell much better than they can see. With their antennae they pick up smells very precisely.

5398.q: What is special about a koala's fingerprints?
a: They are very similar to human fingerprints
5398.e: A koala's fingerprints look so similar to human fingerprints that they could be mixed up. That is a rather amazing feature.
5398.m: Koala fingerprints are like human ones.

5399.q: What is special about the snow leopard's nostrils?
a: A wide nasal cavity warms the cold air
They can be closed like a seal's
They are very small and have no function
It has no nostrils at all
5399.e: The large nasal cavity warms the icy, thin air before it is breathed in. This helps at high altitudes.
5399.m: The nose warms cold air first.

5400.q: Which body part does a mosquito bite with?
5400.e: The mosquito has a thin, pointed mouthpart that it uses to pierce the skin. It also sucks up blood through it.
5400.m: The mouthpart is used for biting.

5401.q: What is the basic principle of a generator?
a: It converts kinetic energy into electricity using magnetic fields
It stores chemical energy in a cell
It produces light by heating a wire
It turns electricity directly into water
5401.e: If a coil of wire is turned in a magnetic field, a voltage is produced in it. Generators in power stations use exactly this principle to produce electricity.
5401.m: Movement in a magnetic field produces electricity.

5402.q: What colour are the threads of a fresh garden spider web usually?
a: Almost see-through, you can hardly see them
5402.e: The threads are very fine and almost see-through. Only when dew or sunlight falls on them can you really see the web glitter.

5403.q: What covers a seahorse's skin instead of scales?
5403.e: Seahorses do not have normal fish scales, but firm rings of bone under the skin. This makes them tough prey for other animals.
5403.m: Bony plates protect it instead of scales.

5404.q: Why do animal species that only live on one small island die out especially easily?
a: They cannot move elsewhere when their habitat is destroyed
There is never any food on islands
5404.e: The giant earwig lived only on the small island of St Helena in the South Atlantic. When its habitat disappeared, it had nowhere to go and died out.
5404.m: Island animals are especially at risk of dying out.

5405.q: How many toes does a carrion crow have on each foot?
a: four, three forwards and one backwards
5405.e: Like most perching birds, the carrion crow has four toes on each foot, three pointing forwards and one backwards. This lets it sit safely on branches.
5405.m: Carrion crows have four toes on each foot.

5406.q: Which hormone is released in greater amounts by the adrenal glands during stress?
5406.e: Cortisol is the most important stress hormone and is made in the adrenal glands. It increases energy and alertness in the short term.

5407.q: How many toes does a mute swan have on each foot?
5407.e: Like many water birds, the mute swan has four toes on each foot. Three of them are joined by webbing.
5407.m: Four toes, three of them webbed.

5408.q: Does a koala have a long, bushy tail?
a: No, it has almost no visible tail
Yes, a tail like a fox
5408.e: Unlike many other tree animals, the koala has almost no visible tail. It does not need one for climbing either.
5408.m: Koalas have almost no visible tail.

5409.q: How long can a cheetah keep up its top speed?
5409.e: The cheetah can only keep up its full speed for a very short time. After that it has to rest, because it is very exhausted.
5409.m: The cheetah can only keep up full speed briefly.

5410.q: What teeth does a roe deer have at the front of its upper jaw?
a: No incisors, just a hard pad
The same teeth as a lion
No teeth at all in its whole mouth
5410.e: Roe deer have no incisors at the front of the upper jaw, just a hard dental pad. The incisors are only in the lower jaw.
5410.m: Roe deer have no front teeth at the top.

5411.q: What does a queen do after she has founded a new nest?
a: She keeps her wings for ever
5411.e: After the mating flight, the queen no longer needs her wings. She even bites them off herself.

5412.q: What does a lion like to eat most?
a: Large plant eaters such as zebras and wildebeest
5412.e: Lions eat only meat and hunt large animals such as zebras, wildebeest or buffalo. Sometimes they also eat smaller prey.
5412.m: Lions mainly eat large plant eaters.

5413.q: How does the golden eagle usually behave towards people?
a: It is very shy and avoids people
It prefers to live in villages and towns
5413.e: Golden eagles are naturally shy and avoid people, especially in the breeding season. Disturbance at their nest can make them abandon their eggs or chicks.

a: A famine in Ukraine in the 1930s partly caused by the Soviet government
A festival celebrating the October Revolution
A trade agreement between East and West
5414.e: In the early 1930s, millions of people in Ukraine died in a famine. It was made much worse by the forced collectivisation of farming and Stalin’s policies.
5414.m: The Holodomor was a famine in Ukraine.

5415.q: What does a wolf do when it wants to play?
a: It crouches down with its back end in the air
It lies flat on its back and does not move
5415.e: With its back end raised and its front legs crouched, a wolf tells others that it wants to play. Pet dogs do this too.
5415.m: You can tell an invitation to play by the posture.

5416.q: What happens to the number of wood mice when there is lots of food?
a: They have more young and their numbers rise sharply
5416.e: When there is plenty of food, wood mice have more young, and their numbers can rise sharply.
5416.m: Lots of food, lots of mice.

5417.q: Which wild animal does the dog originally come from?
5417.e: The domestic dog is descended from the wolf. People made it a pet a very long time ago.
5417.m: The dog comes from the wolf.

5418.q: What is the most striking feature of the robin?
5418.e: The robin has a bright orange-red breast and an orange-red face. That is how you recognise it straight away.

5420.q: What interests researchers most about garden spider silk?
a: How strong and light the threads are
How brightly the spiders can be painted
How to breed birds from it
5420.e: Spider silk is amazingly strong and at the same time very light. Researchers want to understand how such strong threads could also be made artificially.
5420.m: Spider silk is strong and light.

5421.q: Which continent do llamas originally come from?
5421.e: The llama was domesticated in the Andes of South America. People there have kept llamas for thousands of years.

5422.q: When does the female common earwig usually lay her eggs?
a: In the middle of the night in July
5422.e: The eggs are laid in a nest in the ground during the cold season. The larvae hatch later in spring.
5422.m: The eggs are laid in late autumn or winter.

5423.q: What does the Asian elephant mainly eat?
5423.e: Elephants are plant eaters. They eat lots of different parts of plants.

5424.q: How many young does a guinea pig usually have in a litter?
5424.e: A litter usually has one to six baby guinea pigs. Exactly how many varies from litter to litter.
5424.m: A litter usually has only a few young.

5425.q: What does an otter use its long tail for when swimming?
5425.e: The strong tail helps the otter steer in the water. It makes fast and precise movements possible.
5425.m: The tail steers the otter in the water.

5426.q: Roughly how big is an adult seahorse usually?
a: Often only as big as a hand or smaller
As big as a school bus
5426.e: Most species of seahorse are only a few centimetres long, up to about the size of a hand. Only a few species grow bigger.
5426.m: Most seahorses are the size of a hand.

5427.q: What does an earthworm like to eat most?
5427.e: Earthworms eat dead leaves and plant remains together with soil. In doing so, they turn them into valuable humus.

5428.q: Besides fresh leaves, what else does a Roman snail sometimes eat?
5428.e: As well as fresh leaves, the Roman snail also eats withered, dead plant parts. In this way it helps break down old leaves.

5429.q: What does the World Trade Organization (WTO), based in Geneva, do?
a: It sets rules for international trade
5429.e: The WTO makes sure there are shared trade rules between countries and settles trade disputes. Its headquarters are in Geneva.

5430.q: What does the Roman snail breathe with?
5430.e: The Roman snail has a lung in its mantle. It uses it to breathe air, since it lives on land.
5430.m: Roman snails breathe with a lung.

5431.q: Where do bumblebees like to hide when it rains?
a: In the ground with no air
5431.e: When it rains, bumblebees shelter under leaves or in sheltered flowers. There they stay dry until the weather gets better.

5432.e: Jackals are mostly active at dusk and at night. This way they avoid the worst of the heat.
5432.m: Jackals are often active at night.

5433.q: How quickly does the female cuckoo lay her egg in another bird's nest?
a: Very quickly, in a few seconds
It takes her a whole day
Never, she does not lay eggs at all
5433.e: So that the host birds do not notice the trick, the female cuckoo lays her egg at lightning speed, often in just a few seconds. Then she flies off again at once.
5433.m: Cuckoos lay their eggs at lightning speed.

5434.q: Why are motorway verges and roadsides interesting for kestrels?
a: Lots of mice live in the long grass there
They find drinking water in big puddles there
There are lots of fish to hunt there
5434.e: Long grass often grows on roadsides and verges, and lots of mice live in it. That is why such strips are popular hunting grounds for kestrels.
5434.m: Verges offer lots of mice to hunt.

5435.q: What is the best way to recognise the Asian tiger mosquito?
a: By its black and white stripes
By its long feelers like antennae
5435.e: The tiger mosquito has striking black and white stripes on its body and legs. That is why it is called the tiger mosquito.
5435.m: Stripes make the tiger mosquito easy to recognise.

5436.q: Where does the European tree frog spend most of the year?
a: In bushes and trees away from water
5436.e: Outside the mating season, the tree frog usually lives on land in shrubs and trees. It only goes to water to breed.
5436.m: Mostly on land, not in water.

5437.q: Roughly how tall is a dromedary at the shoulder?
5437.e: A dromedary is usually clearly taller than an adult person at the shoulder. Its head is even higher.
5437.m: Dromedaries are about two metres tall.

5438.q: Which animals are among the marten's enemies in the wild?
a: Large owls such as the eagle owl
5438.e: Large owls such as the eagle owl can be dangerous to young or smaller martens. Foxes are also among their natural enemies.
5438.m: Eagle owls can be dangerous to martens.

5439.q: What have people in the far north traditionally used reindeer for?
5439.e: Reindeer provide meat and hides. In the past they also often pulled sledges.

5440.q: Can Parliament vote a member of the Federal Council out of office during the legislative period?
a: No, the Federal Council is elected for four years and cannot be voted out early
Yes, at any time with a simple majority
Yes, but only by the people
Yes, by the President of the Confederation
5440.e: Unlike other countries, Switzerland has no vote of no confidence against individual members of the Federal Council. They normally stay in office for the whole legislative period.
5440.m: The Federal Council cannot be voted out during its four years.

5441.q: Why should you be careful with jellyfish in the sea?
a: Because their stinging cells can sting
Because they bite like a dog
5441.e: The stinging cells of many jellyfish contain a venom that burns the skin. That is why you should not touch jellyfish on the beach.
5441.m: Jellyfish can sting with their stinging cells.

5442.q: What colour are the grey heron's legs usually?
5442.e: The grey heron's long legs are usually yellowish to brownish. They help it stand even in deeper water.
5442.m: Its legs are long and yellowish.

5443.q: What is typical of a drake's tail?
a: A fan of colourful eye feathers
5443.e: On the drake's tail there are a few special feathers that curl upwards. This makes it easy to recognise a male.

5444.q: How do its stripes help a tiger when hunting?
5444.e: The stripes camouflage the tiger in tall grass and among the shadows of trees. This lets it creep up on its prey unnoticed.

5445.q: Roughly how long do young swifts stay in the nest before they fly for the first time?
5445.e: The young birds grow up in the nest over several weeks and exercise their flight muscles there. Only then do they leave the nest and immediately fly off on their own.
5445.m: Young swifts stay in the nest for weeks.

5447.q: What does the great crested grebe's calm gliding on the water show especially well?
a: How well it is adapted to life on and under the water
5447.e: The great crested grebe is perfectly adapted to life in and on the water, from its lobed feet to its streamlined body. This makes it a skilful swimmer and diver.
5447.m: Its body is perfectly suited to life on the water.

5448.q: What does the lake trout use to take oxygen from the water?
5448.e: Water flows in through the mouth and over the gills. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

5449.q: What does a rhino do when it feels threatened?
a: It charges and attacks with its horn
It hides under the ground straight away
5449.e: When a rhino is scared or threatened, it may attack and use its horn as a weapon. That is why you should not get too close to rhinos.
5449.m: Rhinos defend themselves with their horn.

5450.q: What does a starfish's stomach sometimes do when it eats?
5450.e: The starfish can push its stomach out of its body to digest its prey from the outside. Afterwards it pulls its stomach back in.
5450.m: The stomach turns itself inside out.

5451.q: Where do true buffalo live, which are not the same as bison?
5451.e: The African buffalo lives in Africa, the water buffalo in Asia. Neither of them is a bison.
5451.m: Buffalo live in Africa and Asia.

5452.q: In which municipality in Valais were women the first in Switzerland to take part in a federal vote in 1957, even though their votes did not count?
5452.e: In 1957 the municipal council of Unterbäch let the women vote in a separate ballot box. Their votes were legally invalid, but the action caused a stir across the country.
5452.m: In 1957 Unterbäch was the first municipality to let women vote.

5453.q: What kind of hooves do donkeys usually have?
a: Soft, wide hooves like a frog
5453.e: Their hard, narrow hooves help donkeys walk safely even on stony mountain paths. They need to be looked after regularly.
5453.m: Donkey hooves are hard and narrow.

5454.q: In magpies, who mainly sits on the eggs?
a: Neither the male nor the female
5454.e: In magpies, mostly the female sits on the eggs, while the male often brings food. This is how the pair work together in the breeding season.
5454.m: The female magpie usually sits on the eggs alone.

5455.q: Does the number of spots show how old a ladybird is?
a: No, the number of spots usually shows the species, not the age
Yes, a new spot is added every year
Yes, the more spots, the older the beetle
No, the spots show how hungry it is
5455.e: Many people think more spots mean an older beetle. But that is not true: the number of spots depends on the species of ladybird.
5455.m: Spots show the species, not the age.

5456.q: Roughly how big does an adult great crested grebe get?
a: About 10 centimetres long, like a sparrow
About 2 metres long, like a swan
About 1 metre long, like a goose
5456.e: The great crested grebe is the largest grebe in Europe and reaches a length of around 46 to 51 centimetres. This makes it much smaller than a swan.

5457.q: Why are common toads useful in a garden?
a: they eat lots of pests such as slugs and snails
5457.e: Common toads like to eat slugs, snails and other garden pests. That is why gardeners are often happy when they visit.
5457.m: Common toads get rid of garden pests.

5458.q: Who improved the steam engine so much that it drove industrialisation forward?
5458.e: In the 18th century James Watt improved the steam engine decisively, so that it could power factories economically. Others had invented it before him.
5458.m: James Watt improved the steam engine.

5459.q: Why are mute swans often seen as a symbol of elegance?
a: because of their calm, graceful movements on the water
because of their fast running speed
5459.e: Many people find their calm, smooth movements when swimming especially beautiful. That is why swans are seen as a sign of grace.

5460.q: What does it mean when orcas slap their tail fins loudly on the water?
a: They are sending a signal to other orcas
5460.e: The loud slapping of the tail fin is a sign to other orcas. This is how they communicate over a distance.
5460.m: Tail slaps are signals for orcas.

5461.q: What does a hamster in a cage need so that it can move around enough at night?
5461.e: A big exercise wheel helps the hamster move around a lot at night. In the wild it would otherwise cover long distances.

5462.q: How long does a rhino calf usually stay with its mother?
5462.e: A rhino calf stays with its mother for about two to three years. During this time it learns how to find its way in the wild.
5462.m: Rhino calves stay with their mother for a long time.

5463.q: What is a group of dogs that live closely together with a fixed structure often called?
5463.e: The word pack originally comes from wolf research and is often used for groups of dogs too. Within a pack there are social relationships between the animals.
5463.m: Dogs sometimes live in a pack.

5464.q: What do many cows on Swiss alpine pastures wear around their necks?
5464.e: Many cows wear a big bell so that they can be heard and found easily in the pasture. The ringing is simply part of life on a Swiss alp.

5465.q: What is one of the smallest sharks in the world called?
5465.e: The dwarf lanternshark is tiny compared with other sharks. It almost fits in your hand.
5465.m: The dwarf lanternshark is a very small shark.

5466.q: How are the common frog's front legs different from its back legs?
a: The front legs are much shorter
The front legs are much longer
5466.e: The common frog's back legs are long and muscular for jumping. The front legs, on the other hand, are much shorter and are used more for support.
5466.m: Back legs are longer than front legs.

5467.q: How successful are African wild dogs at hunting compared with lions?
5467.e: Wild dogs are among the most successful hunters in Africa. Their teamwork and stamina pay off.
5467.m: Wild dogs are very successful hunters.

5468.q: What is the instrument called that doctors use to listen to your heart?
5468.e: With a stethoscope doctors can hear the sounds of the heart and lungs more loudly. It has tubes that lead to the ears.
5468.m: With a stethoscope you listen to the heart and lungs.

5469.q: How is the food of a tawny owl in a town often different from that of one in the forest?
a: In town it eats birds more often than mice
In town it only eats fish
In the forest it eats only plants
There is no difference at all
5469.e: Tawny owls living in towns often adapt their prey to what is available and catch more birds or rats. Tawny owls living in forests hunt voles and other rodents more often.
5469.m: Town tawny owls eat more birds than forest ones.

5470.q: Roughly how many different sounds can a common raven make?
5470.e: Common ravens have a very varied range of calls, with over 30 different sounds. With them they can send all kinds of messages.

5472.q: How do males and females differ in some gibbon species?
a: In some species they have different fur colours
They always look exactly the same
5472.e: In some species, such as the crested gibbons, males and females have different fur colours. In others both look similar.
5472.m: Some gibbon species show colour differences between males and females.

5473.q: What makes climate change especially difficult for the Alpine salamander?
a: Drier and warmer conditions harm it
It gets temperatures that are too cold
It makes it bigger and stronger
5473.e: Because the Alpine salamander depends on moisture, rising temperatures and drought cause it problems. This can shrink its habitat.

5474.q: Which larvae also eat lots of aphids?
5474.e: Hoverfly larvae are aphid hunters, and many species feed almost only on aphids. The adult flies, on the other hand, drink nectar.

5475.q: In which Swiss canton are there especially many red deer?
5475.e: The Grisons has large forests and mountains where many red deer live. Deer are often spotted there.
5475.m: Many red deer live in the Grisons.

5476.q: Which wild animal is a close relative of our domestic horses?
5476.e: The Przewalski's horse is one of the last surviving wild horse species and is related to our domestic horses. It used to live wild in Asia.
5476.m: Przewalski's horses are wild relatives of horses.

5477.q: Because it likes eating dead animals, how is the red kite sometimes described?
a: as a kind of natural health patrol for the countryside
as a dangerous pest for people
as a hunter of fish only
as a night hunter like an owl
5477.e: Because the red kite eats dead animals, it helps keep the countryside clean. This important role is sometimes described as being like a health patrol.
5477.m: As a scavenger, the red kite keeps nature clean.

5478.q: What does the mole sometimes do with earthworms it has caught?
a: It stores them alive in a chamber as a food supply
It lets them go again immediately
It dries them in the sun
5478.e: The mole bites worms so that they can no longer move but stay alive. This is how it builds up a food store.
5478.m: Worms are stored as a food supply.

5479.q: How does a budgie learn to repeat words?
a: It hears them often and copies them
It knows them when it hatches
It understands every word like a person
5479.e: Budgies copy sounds they hear often. This is how some learn short words, even though they do not understand what they mean.

5480.q: What does a hedgehog use best to find its food at night?
5480.e: The hedgehog has a very sensitive nose and can even smell insects under the ground. This is how it finds enough to eat in the dark.

5481.q: Apart from food, what does a horse need every day to stay healthy?
a: Plenty of fresh water to drink
5481.e: Horses need large amounts of fresh water every day. A horse can drink several buckets of water a day.
5481.m: Horses need plenty of fresh water.

5482.q: How many body parts does an ant have?
5482.e: An ant has a head, a thorax and an abdomen. This is the same in almost all insects.
5482.m: Head, thorax and abdomen belong together.

5483.q: On which day is World Giraffe Day celebrated?
5483.e: World Giraffe Day is celebrated on 21 June, the longest day of the year. The longest day suits the animal with the longest neck.
5483.m: World Giraffe Day is on 21 June.

5484.q: Is the blackbird a rare or a common bird in Switzerland?
a: One of the most common birds of all
It is only found in zoos
It has died out in Switzerland
5484.e: The blackbird is one of the most common and best-known birds in Switzerland. You can see and hear it in almost every garden.
5484.m: The blackbird is very common in Switzerland.

5485.q: Why are grasshoppers important for many birds?
a: They are an important source of food
They build nests for the birds
They keep the birds' eggs warm
5485.e: Many birds especially like to eat grasshoppers. This makes grasshoppers part of nature's food chain.
5485.m: Many birds like to eat grasshoppers.

5486.q: What sound does a grasshopper often make?
5486.e: In summer, many grasshoppers make a fine chirping sound. You often hear it in meadows.

5487.q: What do lions sometimes do with prey that other predators such as hyenas have killed?
a: They chase the hyenas away and steal the prey
They build a nest out of it
5487.e: Lions are strong enough to drive hyenas or other animals away from a fresh kill. This sometimes saves them from having to hunt themselves.
5487.m: Lions sometimes steal other animals' prey.

5488.q: Can sea turtles sleep underwater too?
a: Yes, they just come up for air now and then
No, they only sleep on land
No, they never sleep at all
5488.e: Sea turtles can rest and even sleep in the water. But they must keep coming up briefly to breathe.

5489.e: Reindeer eat lichens, grasses, herbs and leaves. Like all deer, they chew the cud.

5490.q: How do kestrels typically react to towns and villages?
a: Many cope well and even breed on buildings
They avoid all contact with people completely
They die out at once as soon as people are nearby
They can only survive in completely untouched wilderness
5490.e: The kestrel is one of the more adaptable birds of prey and copes well with towns and villages. It quite often even breeds on tower blocks or industrial buildings in the middle of a city.
5490.m: Kestrels adapt to towns and villages.

5491.q: What colour is the fur on a ring-tailed lemur's back usually?
5491.e: The back and sides are grey to brownish. The belly is much lighter.
5491.m: The back is grey, the belly light.

5492.q: What does the dromedary gain from its tall build with long legs?
a: Its body is further away from the hot ground
5492.e: In the desert, the air close to the ground is the hottest. With long legs, the body sits higher up in cooler air.
5492.m: Long legs keep the body cooler.

5493.q: Why should you never get too close to bison in national parks?
a: They can be dangerous and very fast
5493.e: Bison seem calm, but they attack if they feel threatened. You must always keep your distance.

5495.q: What clearly makes a magpie look different from a carrion crow?
a: The magpie's much longer, graduated tail
5495.e: While the carrion crow has a rather short tail, the magpie has a strikingly long, graduated tail. This feature makes it easy to tell apart.
5495.m: The long tail shows it is a magpie.

5496.q: Roughly how many subspecies of tawny owl are there across its whole range?
a: Several, which differ slightly in size and plumage colour
None, all tawny owls are genetically identical
5496.e: Across the tawny owl's wide range from Europe to Asia, several subspecies have developed. They differ mainly in size and plumage colour.
5496.m: The tawny owl has several regional subspecies.

5497.q: What is the person called who calls people to prayer from the minaret?
5497.e: The muezzin calls out the call to prayer five times a day. In the past he climbed the minaret to do it; today loudspeakers are often used.
5497.m: The muezzin calls people to prayer.

5498.q: What does the wood mouse need its long whiskers for?
a: To feel obstacles in the dark
5498.e: The long whiskers help the wood mouse feel obstacles in the dark without seeing them.

5499.q: What do adult male orangutans often develop on their faces?
5499.e: Dominant males develop broad cheek pads, also called flanges. They often also have a throat sac.
5499.m: Dominant males have striking cheek pads.

5500.q: How much can a very thirsty dromedary drink in a short time?
5500.e: After a long dry spell, a dromedary can drink huge amounts in a few minutes. This quickly tops up its water supply.
5500.m: Dromedaries drink a lot very quickly.

5501.q: What is especially important for young falcons in their first weeks of flying, to learn to hunt?
a: Practising flight manoeuvres and watching their parents
Hunting alone straight away without practice
5501.e: After their first flight, young peregrine falcons practise flight manoeuvres for weeks and watch their parents hunting. This is how they gradually learn to hunt on their own.
5501.m: Young falcons learn by practising and watching.

5502.q: Where does the black-backed jackal get its name from?
a: From the dark, saddle-like marking on its back
5502.e: The animal has a dark marking on its back. It looks a bit like a saddle blanket.
5502.m: A dark saddle on its back.

5503.q: How are a budgie's toes arranged?
5503.e: Budgies have four toes on each foot, two pointing forwards and two backwards. This lets them grip and climb well.

5504.q: Do male sea turtles also come onto the beach to lay eggs?
a: No, only the females come onto land
Only the males come onto land
5504.e: Only female sea turtles leave the sea to lay their eggs on the beach. Males stay in the water their whole lives.
5504.m: Only females come onto land to lay eggs.

5505.q: Roughly how big is a great tit?
5505.e: The great tit is a small bird about 14 centimetres long. It easily fits in a child's hand.
5505.m: The great tit is about 14 centimetres long.

5506.q: How often does a robin usually have young in a year?
5506.e: A robin can usually have young twice in a year. This means it has young more often than some other birds.
5506.m: Robins often breed twice a year.

5507.q: Why do rabbits groom themselves so often?
a: To keep their fur clean and healthy
5507.e: Rabbits groom themselves often so that their fur stays clean, smooth and healthy. It is part of their daily care.

5508.e: The brain sits protected inside your skull. It controls everything you think, feel and do.
5508.m: Your brain lives in your head.

5509.q: Where is the stag beetle found?
5509.e: It is found from southern England to western Asia. In Switzerland it lives mainly in lower, warm areas.
5509.m: The stag beetle lives in large parts of Europe.

5511.q: Why are perches of different thicknesses important for budgies?
a: So that they can talk better
5511.e: Perches of different thicknesses exercise the budgie's feet. This helps prevent foot problems.
5511.m: Different perches keep the feet fit.

5512.q: Does the carp prefer to live alone or in groups?
a: Only with other kinds of fish
5512.e: Carp often swim together in small groups. This gives them a little more protection from danger.
5512.m: Carp like to swim in small groups.

5513.q: Roughly how old can a polar bear get in the wild?
5513.e: Wild polar bears usually live to about 20 to 30. In zoos they can sometimes live a little longer.
5513.m: Polar bears often live to 20 to 30.

5514.q: What does freedom of expression mean?
a: You may say openly what you think.
You must always agree with the government.
You may only talk at home.
5514.e: Freedom of expression means that everyone may express their thoughts freely without being punished. In dictatorships this is often not allowed.
5514.m: Freedom of expression allows open speech.

5515.q: Can a wasp sting more than once?
a: Yes, because its sting is smooth
No, only once in its life
No, it has no sting at all
5515.e: A wasp's sting has no barbs. That is why it can pull it out again and sting again.

5516.q: Which bird of prey can be dangerous to a common buzzard?
5516.e: The stronger goshawk is one of the few predators that can be dangerous to an adult common buzzard. The eagle owl also sometimes catches buzzards.

5517.q: What does a mosquito use to find exactly the right spot to pierce the skin?
5517.e: The mosquito has fine sensory cells on its piercing mouthpart, which it uses to find small blood vessels under the skin. This is how it finds exactly the right spot to bite.

5518.q: How many calves does a red deer hind usually have at once?
5518.e: A hind usually gives birth to just a single calf. Twins are very rare in red deer.
5518.m: There is usually only one calf.

5519.q: What do meerkats most often warn their group about?
a: Birds of prey in the sky
5519.e: Birds of prey such as eagles are dangerous for meerkats. The lookouts have special warning calls for danger from the air.
5519.m: Birds of prey are a big danger.

5520.q: How does a European tree frog usually react when disturbed?
a: It jumps away at lightning speed
5520.e: If a tree frog feels threatened, it escapes with a quick jump. Its powerful jumping helps it a lot.
5520.m: When in danger, it makes a quick jump.

5521.q: What natural enemies does an adult orca have?
a: Practically none, it is the strongest hunter in the sea
5521.e: Adult orcas have hardly any enemies, because they are so strong and clever. That is why they are called apex predators.

5522.q: Which predators can be dangerous to orangutans?
5522.e: On Sumatra there are tigers that can hunt orangutans. Clouded leopards and snakes can also be dangerous.

5524.q: How many young does a tapir mother usually have?
5524.e: Tapirs usually have only one young at a time. The mother looks after it for a long time.
5524.m: Usually only one young per birth.

5525.q: How long can a beaver stay underwater without coming up for air?
5525.e: Thanks to special adaptations, beavers can hold their breath for up to 15 minutes. This helps them travel long distances underwater or hide from enemies.
5525.m: Beavers can dive for up to 15 minutes.

5526.q: Why is the reintroduction of the bearded vulture an international project?
a: Because it lives in several Alpine countries at the same time
Because it is only found in Switzerland
Because it never flies across borders
Because only one country is responsible
5526.e: Because bearded vultures fly huge distances and do not stick to national borders, several Alpine countries work together to protect them. The reintroduction could only succeed as a joint effort.

5527.q: Which close relative of the jackal lives in North America?
5527.e: Like the jackal, the coyote belongs to the genus Canis. In North America it plays a similar role.
5527.m: The coyote is a relative of the jackal.

a: A change in the genetic material of a living thing
