5528.e: A mutation is a random change in the DNA that can be passed on. Mutations are an important reason why living things change and develop over time.

5529.q: What helps a squirrel climb trees so well?
5529.e: The sharp, curved claws dig into the bark and give the squirrel a good grip when climbing.
5529.m: Sharp claws give a grip when climbing.

5531.q: Roughly how many different rabbit breeds are there worldwide?
5531.e: Over time, people have bred more than a hundred different rabbit breeds. They differ in size, colour and fur.
5531.m: There are over a hundred rabbit breeds.

5532.q: What is the stoat's body shape like?
a: Long and slim with short legs
With very long legs like a deer
5532.e: The stoat's body is long and slim, while its legs are short. This build makes it very agile.
5532.m: The stoat has a slim body.

5533.q: What is a male sheep called?
5533.e: A male sheep is called a ram or a tup. Rams often have bigger horns than female sheep.
5533.m: A male sheep is called a ram.

5534.q: Does the barn owl build its own nest out of twigs?
a: No, it uses nooks and hollows
Yes, out of twigs high in a tree
Yes, out of mud like a swallow
Yes, out of reeds by the water
5534.e: The barn owl does not build a proper nest. It simply lays its eggs in dark hollows or nooks in walls.
5534.m: It uses existing nooks as a nest.

5535.q: Does the mole like eating plant roots?
a: No, it eats almost only animals such as worms
Yes, that is its favourite food
It only eats roots in winter
Only very young moles eat roots
5535.e: Contrary to what many people think, the mole does not eat plant roots. It feeds almost entirely on worms and small animals in the soil.

5536.q: How good is the moose's sense of smell?
5536.e: Moose do not see very well, but they smell and hear very well. This lets them notice enemies early.
5536.m: Moose smell and hear very well.

5537.q: What do whitefish use their lateral line for?
a: To sense movements in the water
5537.e: The lateral line is a sense organ along the body. With it the fish senses currents and notices where the others in its shoal are swimming.
5537.m: The lateral line senses water movements.

5538.q: How does the red wood ant defend itself when threatened?
a: With a venomous sting like a bee
With sticky threads like a spider
5538.e: The wood ant can squirt an acidic liquid. This is called formic acid, and it keeps enemies away.

5539.q: Where is the entrance to a beaver lodge usually?
a: On the side above the water
In the forest far from the water
5539.e: The entrance to a beaver lodge is always below the water surface. This makes it harder for land predators such as foxes to get into the lodge.

5540.q: Which diseases can threaten packs of African wild dogs?
5540.e: Diseases such as rabies and distemper can spread quickly in packs. They are often passed on by domestic dogs.
5540.m: Dog diseases put the packs at risk.

5542.q: What are the males' fan-shaped antennae especially for?
5542.e: With their large antennae, males pick up the scent of females. This lets them find partners even over long distances.
5542.m: Males smell females with their antennae.

5543.q: What does an earthworm usually do when you touch it gently?
a: It flinches and pulls itself in a little
5543.e: Earthworms feel touch with their whole skin. When in danger, they quickly pull themselves together a little.

5544.q: What changes in young salmon before they migrate to the sea?
a: They turn silvery and can cope with salt water
5544.e: Before migrating to the sea, the young fish turn silvery. Their bodies adjust to salty water.
5544.m: Young salmon turn silvery before their sea journey.

5545.q: Roughly how long do young red kites stay in the nest before they fledge?
5545.e: The young birds grow up in the nest and after around seven weeks are strong enough to fly on their own. Until then, both parents feed them.
5545.m: Young red kites leave the nest after around 7 weeks.

5546.q: On which continents are wild boar originally found?
a: In Europe, Asia and North Africa
5546.e: Wild boar originally live in large parts of Europe, Asia and North Africa. Today they are also found elsewhere.
5546.m: Wild boar come from several continents.

5547.q: What role does the silverback have in his group?
a: He is the leader and protects the group
He only collects leaves to eat
He builds all the nests for the others
He flies ahead and shows the way
5547.e: The silverback makes important decisions and protects his family from danger. All the other gorillas trust him.
5547.m: The silverback leads and protects everyone.

5548.q: Which bee product do people also love to eat?
5548.e: Honey is sweet and many people love to eat it. People also use wax, for example for candles.

5549.q: What is a big difference between a lion's coat and a tiger's?
5549.e: Tigers have striking black stripes in their fur, while a lion's coat is usually plain sandy brown. Only the lion also has a mane.
5549.m: Lions have no stripes like tigers.

5550.q: What does the blue whale mainly use to push itself along when swimming?
5550.e: The blue whale moves its large tail fin powerfully up and down. This pushes it through the water.
5550.m: The tail fin drives the whale forward.

5551.q: In lake trout, who digs the spawning pit in the gravel?
a: The female, with powerful strokes of her tail
5551.e: The female fans the gravel aside with her tail fin and forms a hollow. She lays her eggs in it.
5551.m: The female digs the spawning pit.

a: Energy obtained from the heat inside the Earth
Energy from the movement of the seas
Energy from the Earth's magnetic field
5552.e: Deep inside the Earth it is very hot. This heat can be used to heat houses or to produce electricity.
5552.m: Geothermal energy uses heat from the Earth.

a: An important leader of the October Revolution who was later exiled by Stalin
The founder of the Berlin Wall
5553.e: Leon Trotsky played a major part in organising the Red Army and the Revolution of 1917. Later Stalin drove him out of the Soviet Union, and he was murdered in Mexico in 1940.
5553.m: Trotsky was later exiled by Stalin.

5554.q: To which faraway country was the European perch introduced, where it is a problem in places?
5554.e: The European perch was introduced to Australia by people. There it can push out native fish and other animals.
5554.m: The perch was introduced to Australia.

5557.q: What is the domestic form of the camel with one hump?
5557.e: The dromedary has one hump and lives mainly in Africa and Arabia. Bactrian camels have two.
5557.m: The dromedary is the domestic camel with one hump.

5558.q: In which area of Switzerland was the last wild brown bear killed?
a: In the canton of the Grisons
5558.e: In 1904, Switzerland's last wild brown bear was killed in the canton of the Grisons. After that, the bear was considered wiped out in Switzerland.
5558.m: In 1904 the brown bear disappeared from Switzerland.

5559.q: Roughly how long do spotted hyenas feed their young with milk?
5559.e: Spotted hyena mothers feed their young with milk for a very long time, often more than a year. The milk is especially nourishing.
5559.m: Hyena mothers give milk for a very long time.

5560.q: What colour are the forehead and throat of a barn swallow?
5560.e: The barn swallow's forehead and throat are a striking rusty red. This makes it easy to tell apart from other swallow species.
5560.m: A rusty red forehead and throat mark it out.

5561.q: Roughly how much can an adult male ibex weigh?
5561.e: Adult males can weigh up to around 100 kilograms. Females are much lighter, at 40 to 50 kilograms.

5562.q: How do young grey herons often look different from adults?
a: They do not yet have a long crest and their colours look duller
They have shorter legs than adults
They are bigger than their parents
5562.e: Young birds start out with less striking plumage and no long crest on their head yet. These features only develop as they get older.
5562.m: Young birds look duller and plainer.

5563.q: What are the sounds made by whales such as the blue whale often called in everyday language?
5563.e: The deep, long calls of whales are often called whale song. To us humans they sound mysterious.
5563.m: The calls are called whale song.

5564.q: Which organ stores extra sugar as glycogen?
5564.e: The liver stores glucose in the form of glycogen. When needed, it turns it back into sugar for energy.
5564.m: The liver stores sugar as glycogen.

5566.q: What does the polar bear mother do while she has her cubs in the den?
a: She eats nothing and lives off her fat reserves
She does not sleep at all
5566.e: During her time in the snow den, the polar bear mother eats nothing. She lives off the fat she built up beforehand.
5566.m: The mother fasts in the den.

5567.q: Why does the white stork fly away in autumn?
a: because it gets too cold here and there is less food
because it wants to go on holiday
because its nest gets too small
5567.e: In winter it gets cold here and many frogs and insects disappear. That is why the stork moves to warmer areas.
5567.m: Cold and little food drive it away.

5568.q: Roughly what is the wingspan of a tawny owl?
5568.e: With its wings spread, the tawny owl has a wingspan of about 95 to 105 centimetres. This allows it to fly nimbly between trees.
5568.m: A tawny owl's wingspan is around 1 metre.

5569.q: How can you tell a particularly happy, playful rabbit?
a: It does little jumps in the air
5569.e: Happy rabbits sometimes suddenly leap into the air and twist as they do it. These jumps show pure joy.
5569.m: Jumps in the air show joy.

5570.q: What happens to an ice cube when you hold it in your hand?
a: It melts because of your body heat
5570.e: Your hand is warmer than the ice, so it gives heat to the ice. This turns the solid ice into liquid water.

5571.q: What are animals at the top of the food chain called?
5571.e: The snow leopard has hardly any natural enemies in its habitat. In this way it keeps the numbers of its prey animals in balance.

5572.q: How heavy can a really big pike get?
a: Only a few grams, like a coin
5572.e: Especially large pike can weigh several kilograms, and some record pike even over 20 kilograms. That is really heavy for a fish.

5573.q: Roughly how much does a robin weigh?
a: About as much as two sugar cubes
About as much as a cat
About as much as a dog
About as much as a brick
5573.e: A robin weighs only about 16 to 22 grams. That is very light, about the same as two sugar cubes.

5574.q: How does a harbour seal move its back flippers when swimming?
a: Together in waves, like a fish's tail fin
Not at all, only the front flippers move
5574.e: The harbour seal's two back flippers move together from side to side like a fish's tail fin. This makes it very powerful and fast in the water.
5574.m: The back flippers drive the seal forward.

5576.q: What does the barn owl's call sound like?
5576.e: The barn owl does not hoot, it makes a screeching cry. Many people find it spooky.

5577.q: In which regions is the European pond turtle found?
a: In Europe, North Africa and western Asia
5577.e: Its range is quite large. In northern Europe, however, it is rare and only found in small numbers.
5577.m: It lives in Europe, North Africa and western Asia.

5578.q: What do professional fishermen on Swiss lakes often use to catch perch?
5578.e: Professional fishermen set nets in the lakes and haul them in later. Perch are also caught with rods by people who fish as a hobby.
5578.m: Professional fishermen catch perch with nets.

5579.q: In mute swans, who usually sits on the eggs?
a: Nobody, the sun keeps them warm
5579.e: Usually the female sits on the eggs. During this time the male guards the nest.
5579.m: The female sits on the eggs.

5580.q: What does the red kite strikingly often do with its nest?
a: it decorates it with plastic or rubbish
it builds a completely new nest every year
5580.e: Red kites like to build bits of plastic, rags or paper into their nest. Researchers think this makes the nest more stable or warns off intruders.
5580.m: Red kites decorate their nest with rubbish.

5581.q: What do you call a group of African wild dogs?
5581.e: Wild dogs live in packs. A pack usually consists of related animals.
5581.m: Wild dogs live in a pack.

5582.q: Where does the name “Bactrian camel” come from?
a: From the region of Bactria in Central Asia
From a mountain in the Alps
5582.e: Bactria was a historical region in Central Asia. Camels were kept there early on.

5583.q: Roughly how long can an emperor penguin stay underwater without coming up for air?
5583.e: Emperor penguins can dive for a very long time, often several minutes at a stretch. This helps them hunt deep down for fish.
5583.m: Emperor penguins dive for minutes without air.

5584.q: Which animal group does the orca really belong to?
5584.e: The orca breathes air and feeds its young with milk. That is why it is a mammal, like us humans.

5585.q: Why do cacti have spines instead of large leaves?
5585.e: Large leaves lose a lot of water through evaporation. Cacti live in dry areas, and thanks to their spines they save precious water.

5586.q: What is one danger for reindeer from climate change?
a: Layers of ice over their food caused by rain in winter
5586.e: Rain in winter can freeze and form a layer of ice over the lichens. Then the animals can hardly get to their food.

5587.q: How many young does a wood mouse usually have in a litter?
5587.e: A wood mouse usually gives birth to between four and seven young at a time.

5588.q: How do okapis often communicate with each other?
a: With quiet sounds that people can hardly hear
5588.e: Okapis also use very low sounds called infrasound. People cannot hear them.

5589.q: How often does a mother rabbit usually feed her young with milk each day?
5589.e: Amazingly, mother rabbits feed their young only once a day. But the milk is especially nourishing.
5589.m: The mother feeds them once a day.

5590.q: What does a rhino eat most?
a: Plants such as grass and leaves
5590.e: Rhinos are plant eaters. They eat grass, leaves and twigs all day long.

5591.q: How do brown bears often mark their territory?
a: By scratching trees and rubbing against them
By stacking stones on top of each other
By digging holes in the ground
5591.e: Brown bears often scratch and rub against trees to leave their scent. This tells other bears that an area is already taken.
5591.m: Bears mark trees with their scent.

5592.q: Which is the heaviest land mammal in Europe?
5592.e: The European bison can weigh over 800 kilograms. It is a close relative of the American bison.
5592.m: The European bison is Europe's heaviest land animal.

5593.q: Which animal is known as the minotaur beetle?
a: A dung beetle whose males have horns
A cow that sounds like a beetle
5593.e: The minotaur beetle is a dung beetle. The males have three horns on the shield behind the head.
5593.m: Minotaur beetles are horned dung beetles.

5594.q: On how many continents is the barn owl found?
a: On almost all of them except Antarctica
5594.e: The barn owl lives on almost every continent in the world, except where it is very cold. It prefers warm and mild areas.
5594.m: It lives almost all over the world.

5595.q: How does a magpie usually move about on the ground?
a: Hopping and walking while looking for food
5595.e: On the ground, magpies usually hop or walk while they look for food. They often seem curious and alert as they do it.
5595.m: Magpies hop when looking for food.

5596.q: Roughly how much does an adult great crested grebe weigh?
5596.e: An adult great crested grebe weighs about a kilogram. Its weight can vary slightly depending on the season and how much food there is.
5596.m: A great crested grebe weighs about a kilogram.

5597.q: Because it is such a keen hunter, what is the pike sometimes called?
5597.e: Because the pike is such a greedy hunter, it is sometimes called the water wolf. It eats almost anything that fits in its mouth in the water.
5597.m: The pike is also called the water wolf.

5598.q: Why does the grass snake have no eyelids to blink with?
a: Its eyes are protected by a see-through scale
5598.e: A see-through scale like a pair of glasses covers the eye. That is why its gaze looks fixed.
5598.m: A spectacle scale protects the eyes.

5599.q: How do many birds react to ladybirds as food?
a: They often avoid them because they taste bitter
They eat them as their favourite food
They never notice them at all
They bring them to their young first
5599.e: Because of the bitter yellow liquid, many birds would rather leave the beetles alone. This protects the ladybird from many predators.
5599.m: A bitter taste protects them from birds.

5600.q: As male ibex get older, what shows their rank most clearly?
a: Bigger horns usually mean a higher rank
The lightest coat colour decides the rank
Only age counts, horns do not matter
There is no ranking among ibex
5600.e: The older and stronger a male is, the bigger his horns often are. Big horns signal strength to the other males and secure a high rank.
5600.m: Big horns show strength and rank.

5601.q: What natural enemies does an adult eagle owl have in the wild?
a: Very few, it has hardly any natural enemies
5601.e: As an apex predator, the adult eagle owl has very few natural enemies in the wild. Human influences such as power line pylons or traffic are usually more dangerous for it.
5601.m: Adult eagle owls have hardly any natural enemies.

5602.q: How many toes does a least weasel have on each paw?
5602.e: Like most members of the marten family, the least weasel has five toes with small claws on each paw. These help it run and climb quickly.

a: A mixture of two or more metals
A building block of biological cells
5603.e: An alloy is made by melting different metals together, for example copper and tin to make bronze. Alloys often have different properties from the pure metals.

5604.q: How do Bactrian camels chew the cud?
a: They bring food back up and chew it again
They store it in their hump
5604.e: Camels are ruminants in the wider sense. After swallowing their food for the first time, they chew it again.

5605.q: What is reproduction without fertilisation, which is common in aphids in summer, called?
5605.e: In summer, female aphids produce young without males. This lets them multiply very quickly.
5605.m: In summer, aphids multiply without males.

5606.q: Which family does the salmon belong to?
5606.e: The salmonids also include trout and char. They are closely related to each other.

5607.q: Is the praying mantis dangerous to people?
a: No, it is harmless to people
5607.e: It only hunts small animals. People can watch it without worrying, but it is better not to touch it.

5608.q: Who discovered the laws of inheritance by crossing pea plants for years?
5608.e: In the 19th century the monk Gregor Mendel studied how features such as flower colour are passed on in pea plants. His laws are the basis of modern genetics.
5608.m: Mendel discovered the laws of inheritance.

5609.q: Which animals are among the kestrel's natural enemies?
a: Larger birds of prey such as the goshawk or eagle owl
5609.e: Larger and stronger birds of prey such as the goshawk or the eagle owl can be dangerous to the kestrel. Young birds are especially at risk.
5609.m: Goshawks and eagle owls are enemies of the kestrel.

5610.q: What is striking about the ears of the African wild dog?
a: They are tiny and hardly visible
5610.e: The large, round ears catch your eye straight away. They help with hearing and also give off heat.

5611.q: How does a caterpillar sometimes protect itself from enemies?
a: With hairs and bristles on its skin
5611.e: Some caterpillars have fine hairs or bristles that prickle or itch. This stops many predators from eating them.

5612.q: What is important before you lift a hamster out of its cage?
a: You should talk to it gently first
You should suddenly throw it up
You should pull it by the tail
You should shout loudly into the cage
5612.e: So that the hamster does not get a fright, you should talk to it calmly first. That way it notices that a hand is coming.
5612.m: Talk calmly to a hamster before lifting it.

5613.q: In which habitats does the magpie feel especially at home?
5613.e: Magpies like living where people live, for example in gardens, parks and fields. They adapt well to different surroundings.

5614.q: How can you often only tell young male chicks after a few weeks?
a: By their growing comb and spurs
By their size straight after hatching
By the colour of the egg
By their feather colour on the very first day
5614.e: In young chicks you often cannot tell whether they are male or female straight away. Only when the comb, wattles and spurs start to grow can you recognise a future cockerel.
5614.m: Combs and spurs show young cockerels.

5615.q: An old story tells of huge swarms of locusts that came over Egypt. What is such a big event called?
5615.e: When lots of locusts come at once, they often eat all the plants bare. Something like that is called a plague.

5616.q: Is there only one species of badger in the world?
a: No, there are several different species of badger
Yes, exactly one in the whole world
There are hundreds of species of badger
There are no badgers alive today
5616.e: Besides our European badger, there are other species of badger around the world, for example in Asia. They look similar to the European badger but differ in the details.
5616.m: There are several species of badger worldwide.

5617.q: What colour are an adult bearded vulture's eyes usually?
5617.e: The bearded vulture's eyes are usually pale yellow to orange-red, which makes them very striking. Together with the red ring around the eye, they give it a piercing gaze.
5617.m: Adult bearded vultures have yellowish to reddish eyes.

5618.q: Why does the robin sometimes sing at night in towns?
a: Because it is warmer at night
Because there are no enemies then
Because it finds more food at night
5618.e: Street lamps and bright windows can fool the robin. It then thinks it is morning again and starts to sing.

5619.q: What does a red fox's face typically look like?
a: A pointed snout with dark ear tips
A round face like a cat with a moustache
A completely flat face with no nose
5619.e: The red fox has a pointed, narrow snout and usually dark ear tips. This look makes it easy to recognise in the forest.
5619.m: The fox has a pointed snout.

5620.q: What is one of the reasons why many dung beetles are declining?
a: Fewer grazing animals and the use of medicines that end up in dung
5620.e: Where there are fewer animals in the pasture, there is less food. Traces of medicine in the droppings can also put the beetles at risk.
5620.m: Less dung and poisons put dung beetles at risk.

5621.q: Why is a dust bath important for hens?
a: It keeps their feathers clean and drives away parasites
5621.e: When dust bathing, hens roll around in dry soil. This removes annoying little parasites from their feathers.

5622.q: What is a young chamois called?
5622.e: The young of a chamois is called a kid. In its first months it usually stays close to its mother.

5623.q: What is especially threatening bumblebees today?
a: Too few flower meadows and pesticides
5623.e: When there are fewer colourful meadows with flowers, bumblebees find less food. Pest poisons can also harm them.

5624.q: What do great tits like to do in summer to keep clean?
a: They roll in the mud like a pig
5624.e: Great tits like to bathe in shallow water or a bird bath. Bathing keeps their feathers clean and healthy.
5624.m: A bird bath keeps the feathers clean.

5625.q: What are the hard, colourful wings that cover a ladybird's back called?
5625.e: The hard wings you see first are called wing cases. They protect the delicate flying wings underneath.
5625.m: The hard wings are called wing cases.

5626.q: How long does a dolphin calf usually stay with its mother?
a: Never, it is alone straight away
5626.e: Dolphin calves often stay with their mother for several years. During this time they learn to hunt and other important behaviour.
5626.m: Dolphin calves stay with their mother for years.

5627.q: Do male and female robins look very similar?
a: Yes, they look almost the same
No, only the male has a red breast
No, the female has a yellow breast
No, the female is much bigger
5627.e: In robins, males and females look almost the same. You can hardly tell them apart from the outside.
5627.m: Males and females look the same.

5628.q: How many legs does a hedgehog have?
5628.e: Like most mammals, the hedgehog has four legs. It uses them to scurry through gardens and meadows at night.

5629.q: How does a mosquito larva move through the water?
a: It swims like a fish with fins
5629.e: The larva jerks its whole body back and forth and wriggles through the water this way. It keeps coming up to the surface to breathe.

5630.q: Can a red deer swim well?
5630.e: Red deer can swim surprisingly well. They even cross rivers and lakes.

5631.q: How many entrances can a fox's den often have?
5631.e: A fox's den often has several entrances and escape routes. That way the fox can quickly escape through another exit when in danger.
5631.m: A fox's den often has several entrances.

5632.q: How do the puma's paws move when it is creeping along?
a: Almost silently, thanks to soft paw pads
5632.e: Soft paw pads muffle its steps. This lets the puma creep up on prey unnoticed.

5633.e: In the wild, giraffes only live in Africa. There they roam across wide savannah landscapes with trees.
5633.m: Wild giraffes only live in Africa.

5634.q: Why does a mosquito bite a person?
a: It needs blood for its eggs
It likes the taste of skin
It is looking for water to drink
5634.e: The female mosquito needs protein from blood so that her eggs can develop. Without blood she could not lay eggs.
5634.m: Blood gives protein for mosquito eggs.

5635.q: How does a red fox usually spend the day before it goes looking for food at night?
a: It plays loud football all day
It flies around like a bird
It swims in the lake all day
5635.e: During the day, the fox usually retreats to its hiding place or den and rests. At dusk it becomes active and goes looking for food.
5635.m: The fox rests during the day.

5636.q: What do you often find in a barn owl pellet?
a: Small bones and bits of fur
5636.e: A pellet contains the parts of the mice that cannot be digested, so small bones and fur. From it you can easily see what the owl has eaten.
5636.m: A pellet shows what it has eaten.

5637.q: Why do alpacas in Switzerland need their feet trimmed regularly?
a: So that their toenails do not grow too long
So that their wool turns blue
5637.e: The toenails keep on growing and must be trimmed when needed. Otherwise the animals find it harder to walk.

5638.q: Does the robin stay in Switzerland in winter, or does it fly away?
a: There are none left at all in winter
5638.e: Some robins stay in Switzerland all year round. Others move to warmer areas in winter.

5639.q: In which Swiss waters can great crested grebes be watched especially well?
a: For example on Lake Constance and Lake Neuchâtel
Only on the Rhine at Basel
5639.e: Larger Swiss lakes such as Lake Constance or Lake Neuchâtel offer good habitats with reeds and plenty of fish. Great crested grebes can regularly be seen there.
5639.m: Large lakes are home to many great crested grebes.

a: Municipalities may regulate many matters themselves
Municipalities must adopt all federal laws word for word
Municipalities may not levy their own taxes
Municipalities are run directly by the canton
5640.e: Municipal autonomy allows municipalities to regulate many matters such as schools, roads or taxes themselves. How much autonomy a municipality has is set by its canton.

5641.q: How do ring-tailed lemurs warn their group about enemies?
5641.e: Ring-tailed lemurs call loudly when they notice danger. The calls can sound different depending on the enemy.

5642.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker like to eat at a bird table in winter?
a: nothing, it does not like bird tables
5642.e: In winter, the great spotted woodpecker likes to visit feeding places in the garden. There it finds valuable fats and nuts.
5642.m: The great spotted woodpecker likes fat in winter.

5643.q: How big can the shell of an adult Roman snail get?
a: About as big as a ping-pong ball
As big as a grain of rice
5643.e: The shell of an adult Roman snail grows to about four to five centimetres wide. That is roughly the size of a ping-pong ball.
5643.m: The shell grows to a few centimetres.

5645.q: What protects your teeth on the outside?
5645.e: Tooth enamel is the hard outer layer of the teeth. It is even harder than bone.

5646.q: What are the bright colours of some frogs, such as the poison dart frog, for?
a: They warn predators about their poison
They help with camouflage in the forest
5646.e: The bright colours of the poison dart frog signal to predators that it is poisonous. These are called warning colours.

5647.q: What does a caterpillar like to eat most?
5647.e: Caterpillars mainly eat the green leaves of plants. They eat a huge amount so that they can grow quickly.
5647.m: Caterpillars eat lots of green leaves.

5648.q: What does a seahorse lack in its body, which is why it has to eat almost all the time?
5648.e: Seahorses have no proper stomach that can store food. That is why they have to keep eating small portions all day long.
5648.m: Without a stomach it has to eat often.

5649.q: What is an adult male cow or buffalo called?
5649.e: In cattle and buffalo, the adult male is called a bull. The female is called a cow.

5650.q: How does a jellyfish's life usually begin?
a: As a tiny polyp on the seabed
As an egg in a nest
As a caterpillar on a leaf
5650.e: Before a jellyfish becomes an adult, it lives as a tiny polyp attached to the seabed. Only later does it break free and swim freely.
5650.m: A jellyfish starts as a polyp on the bottom.

5651.q: How does the male common toad often get to the pond?
a: The female carries him on her back
He carries the female on his back
He hops far ahead of the female
He is always waiting at the pond already
5651.e: The smaller male clings to the back of the bigger female and lets her carry him to the pond.
5651.m: The male rides on the female to the pond.

a: No, it is not a mammal
Yes, it feeds its young with milk
Yes, it breathes with lungs like us
5652.e: The starfish is not a mammal, because it has no fur and does not feed its young with milk. It belongs to a completely different animal group.

5654.q: What colour can the shell of a hen's egg be?
5654.e: Depending on the breed, hens lay white or brown eggs. Some rare breeds even lay slightly greenish eggs.

5655.q: What does a starfish breathe with?
a: Gills like a fish, only on its head
5655.e: Starfish breathe through tiny gills on their skin. This is how they take oxygen from the water.

5656.q: Roughly how big does an adult common frog get?
5656.e: An adult common frog usually measures between 6 and 11 centimetres. Females are often a little bigger than males.
5656.m: Common frogs grow to about the size of a hand.

5657.q: Roughly how long can a Bactrian camel go without water?
5657.e: It can go a long time without drinking, especially in winter. Afterwards it can drink a huge amount of water in a short time.
5657.m: Bactrian camels can go a long time without water.

5658.q: What is the force called that always pulls you towards the ground?
5658.e: The Earth's gravity pulls everything downwards. That is why things fall when you let go of them.

5659.q: What happens when a pond dries up for the Alpine newt?
a: It looks for a new damp hiding place on land
It digs itself deep into dry ground for ever
It dies at once with no way out
5659.e: If a breeding pond dries up, the adult Alpine newt leaves the water in time. On land it can hide in damp places and survive.
5659.m: In a drought it moves onto land.

5660.q: How does a grasshopper protect itself from enemies?
a: It jumps away quickly or hides
It makes itself invisible like a ghost
5660.e: Thanks to its strong legs, it can escape in a flash. Its camouflage colouring also helps it hide.

5661.q: Which country is famous for its road signs showing a moose?
5661.e: In Sweden, signs warn of moose on the road. Collisions with moose are dangerous.
5661.m: In Sweden, signs warn of moose.

5662.q: Which big cat is the only one that usually lives in groups called prides?
5662.e: Lions live in prides with several females, their young and one or a few males. Tigers, leopards and jaguars are loners.
5662.m: The lion is the only big cat that lives in a pride.

5663.q: What was castoreum used for by people in the past?
a: It was used as a medicine and a scent
It was used as a building material
It was used as food for livestock
It was used to dye clothes
5663.e: In the past, people believed castoreum had healing powers and also used it in perfumes. The strong demand helped lead to beavers being hunted and wiped out.
5663.m: Castoreum was once used as a medicine.

5664.q: Why do lions climb trees less often than some other cats?
a: Because they are quite heavy and big for it
Because they are scared of leaves
Because they are not allowed to
5664.e: Lions are big, heavy animals, so they do not climb as skilfully as smaller cats. Some lions still like to rest on strong, low branches.
5664.m: Lions rarely climb because of their size.

5665.q: In mallards, who sits on the eggs?
5665.e: In mallards, only the female looks after the eggs. The drake does not help.
5665.m: Only the female sits on the eggs.

5666.q: What role does the wolf play in the fairy tale “Little Red Riding Hood”?
5666.e: In the well-known fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm, the wolf is shown as a cunning and dangerous villain. Stories like this have shaped the wolf's reputation for centuries.
5666.m: In the fairy tale, the wolf is the villain.

5667.q: Which bird cannot fly but is a brilliant swimmer?
5667.e: The penguin's wings have turned into small flippers. With them it swims very fast through the cold water.

5668.q: What can young geese, called goslings, do shortly after hatching?
a: Nothing, they stay in the nest for weeks
5668.e: Shortly after hatching, goslings can already walk and swim. They follow their mother and leave the nest quickly.

5669.q: What do sheep do to eat grass?
a: They tear it off with their teeth
They dig it up with their hooves
They catch it with their tongue like a frog
They chew the roots out of the ground
5669.e: Sheep tear off the grass with their lower incisors and the hard pad at the top of their mouth. This lets them graze all day long.
5669.m: Sheep tear off grass with their teeth.

5670.q: What is meant by photoperiodism in plants?
a: The response of plants to day length, for example when flowering
The ability to glow in the dark
5670.e: Many plants use day length to tell when to flower. So some species only flower in spring, others not until autumn.
5670.m: Photoperiodism controls flowering by day length.

5671.q: Roughly how long does it take for young carrion crows to fledge and leave the nest?
5671.e: After hatching, young carrion crows stay in the nest for about four to five weeks before they fledge and can fly on their own. After that their parents still help them for a while.
5671.m: Young crows fledge after around four weeks.

5672.q: Which trout originally comes from North America and is now often kept on fish farms?
5672.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. It grows quickly and is therefore often farmed. Brown trout, lake trout and sea trout are native here.
5672.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

5673.q: Roughly how many toes does a common toad have on its back feet?
5673.e: Like many other amphibians, the common toad has five toes on its back feet. They help it crawl and dig a little.
5673.m: A toad's back feet have five toes.

5674.q: How does the badger help the forest?
a: It eats lots of snails and insects
5674.e: The badger eats lots of snails, worms and insects. This keeps everything in the forest in balance.
5674.m: Badgers keep the forest in balance.

5675.e: A seismograph records movements of the ground, for example during an earthquake. From the data scientists can work out the strength and location of the quake.

5676.q: What is the difference between a popular initiative and a referendum?
a: With an initiative you ask for something new, with a referendum you oppose a law that has been passed
Initiatives only apply to cantons, referendums only to municipalities
5676.e: With a popular initiative, the people ask for a new article in the constitution. With a referendum, the people can still stop a law passed by parliament.
5676.m: An initiative demands, a referendum brakes.

5677.q: How long does the shell of an adult European pond turtle usually get?
5677.e: This species is a fairly small to medium-sized turtle. Females usually grow a little bigger than males.
5677.m: The shell usually measures 12 to 20 centimetres.

5678.q: Compared with many other owls, what is a typical feature of the eagle owl?
a: Its striking long tail like a pheasant's
5678.e: Compared with most other European owl species, the eagle owl stands out mainly because of its very large size. Smaller owls such as the long-eared owl look tiny next to it.
5678.m: The eagle owl is much bigger than other owls.

5679.q: What helps the gorilla especially well when climbing?
5679.e: With its strong arms and gripping hands, the gorilla can climb trees well. It needs this, for example, to reach fruit.
5679.m: Strong arms help the gorilla climb.

5680.q: Why does a candle go out when you put a glass over it?
a: It soon runs out of fresh air
5680.e: Fire needs air to burn. Under the glass the air is soon used up, so the candle goes out.

5681.q: Which bird lays its eggs in other birds' nests?
5681.e: The cuckoo does not build its own nest. It lays its eggs in the nests of other birds, which then raise its young.
5681.m: The cuckoo lets other birds hatch its eggs.

5682.q: Why has the cockerel long been a symbol of early morning and waking up?
a: Because it often crows at sunrise
Because it is most active at night
Because it only calls at midday
5682.e: Because cockerels typically crow early in the morning, they were often used as a living alarm clock in the past. That is why the cockerel still stands for the start of the day.
5682.m: The cockerel stands for the morning.

5683.q: Where do most native pond skaters spend the winter?
a: Hidden on land, for example under leaves
Deep in the mud under the ice
5683.e: In autumn the adults look for sheltered hiding places on land. In spring they return to the water.
5683.m: In winter they rest on land.

5684.q: Where does the female wall lizard usually lay her eggs?
a: In loose, warm soil or under stones
5684.e: Warm, loose soil lets enough air and warmth reach the eggs. This helps the embryos develop well.

5685.q: What colour are barn owl eggs?
5685.e: Barn owl eggs are roundish and pure white. They usually lie in a dark nook.
5685.m: The eggs are white and round.

5686.q: One way beavers communicate is to warn of danger. How do they do it?
a: They slap their tail loudly on the water
5686.e: When in danger, a beaver slaps its tail hard on the water surface. The loud bang warns other beavers nearby and makes them dive at once.
5686.m: The tail slap warns other beavers.

5687.q: Which prey does the European tree frog especially like to eat?
5687.e: Mosquitoes, flies and small beetles are among the tree frog's favourite prey. It usually catches them one at a time with its tongue.
5687.m: Small insects are its favourite food.

5688.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult African wild dog get?
5688.e: It is about as heavy as a medium-sized dog. The animals are slim and long-legged.
5688.m: Wild dogs weigh about 20 to 30 kilograms.

5689.q: Why do budgies live in large flocks in the wild?
a: Because it helps them learn to talk
5689.e: In a large flock, lots of eyes watch out for danger. This means predators are spotted more quickly.
5689.m: The flock protects them from enemies.

5690.q: Where in Switzerland are ladybirds found especially often?
a: Only in caves with no light
5690.e: Ladybirds like places with lots of plants and aphids. That is why you often find them in gardens, meadows or fields.
5690.m: Ladybirds live in gardens and meadows.

5691.q: What does it mean for an ant colony when the queen dies?
a: Without a new queen, the colony cannot carry on
5691.e: The queen is the only one who lays eggs. If she dies with no successor, the colony will eventually die out.
5691.m: Without a queen there are no new ants.

5692.q: How does the white stork hold its neck when it flies?
5692.e: In flight, the stork stretches its neck straight out in front. This makes it different from the heron, for example, which pulls its neck in.
5692.m: A stork's neck is stretched out in flight.

5693.q: What is a group of wild boar called?
5693.e: Wild boar live in groups called sounders. They usually consist of females and their young.
5693.m: A group of wild boar is called a sounder.

5694.q: What is left behind on the plant when a dragonfly hatches out of its larval skin?
5694.e: When it hatches, the empty larval skin is left hanging there. Experts call it an exuvia and often use it to identify the species.
5694.m: The empty larval skin is left behind.

5695.q: What colour is the wall lizard normally?
a: Usually brown, grey or greenish with spots
5695.e: The wall lizard's colouring is plain and varies. This helps it hide from enemies.
5695.m: The wall lizard is camouflaged in brown and grey.

5696.q: What is the difference between the Eurasian otter and the sea otter?
a: The Eurasian otter mostly lives in fresh water, the sea otter in the sea
The Eurasian otter only eats plants
The Eurasian otter only lives in Australia
5696.e: The Eurasian otter prefers rivers and lakes, while the sea otter lives in the sea. Both belong to the marten family, but they are different species.
5696.m: The Eurasian otter lives in fresh water, the sea otter in the sea.

5697.q: What colour are a beaver's teeth usually, because of the iron in their enamel?
5697.e: The beaver's tooth enamel contains a lot of iron, which makes it especially hard and orange. This helps the beaver gnaw even thick wood.
5697.m: Beaver teeth are orange because of iron.

5698.q: How can you tell a common buzzard from a red kite?
a: The common buzzard has a rounded tail, the red kite a forked one
The common buzzard has a much longer neck
The common buzzard is tiny, like a sparrow
5698.e: In flight, the common buzzard has a rather round, short tail, while the red kite shows a clearly forked tail. This feature helps to identify the two species.
5698.m: A rounded tail shows it is a buzzard.

5699.q: How is the cuckoo's tail different from a pigeon's?
a: It is longer and looks slimmer
It has colourful feathers like a peacock's
5699.e: The cuckoo has a strikingly long tail, which together with its pointed wings gives it a slim shape in flight. A pigeon looks more compact and rounded by comparison.
5699.m: The cuckoo has a long, slim tail.

5700.q: Which body part helps the lynx hear especially well?
5700.e: The lynx has tufts of hair on the tips of its ears. They improve its hearing and help it hear even quiet sounds.
5700.m: Tufted ears make the lynx an expert listener.

5701.q: What does it mean that the jaguar is an apex predator?
a: It is at the top of the food chain
5701.e: An apex predator has almost no natural enemies in its habitat. The adult jaguar is only seriously threatened by humans.
5701.m: The jaguar has hardly any natural enemies.

5702.q: What does a hen need in her food so that the eggshells get hard?
5702.e: Lime, for example from crushed seashells, makes eggshells firm and hard. Without enough lime the shells would be too soft.

5704.q: What is especially dangerous about the box jellyfish?
5704.e: The box jellyfish has very strong venom in its tentacles. It lives mainly in warm seas, for example off Australia.
5704.m: The box jellyfish is very dangerous.

5705.q: What is the perch's mouth like?
a: Large, with lots of fine little teeth
Small and pointing downwards as a sucking mouth
5705.e: The perch has a large mouth with lots of small, brush-like teeth. It uses them to hold on to slippery prey.
5705.m: A large mouth with a toothbrush.

5706.q: In which season do mosquitoes bite most in Switzerland?
5706.e: In summer it is warm and there are lots of puddles and still water where mosquitoes can breed. That is why mosquitoes bother us most in the warm months.
5706.m: Mosquitoes are especially active in summer.

5707.q: What is the development from egg through caterpillar and pupa to butterfly called?
5707.e: Metamorphosis is the complete change of the body from one stage to the next. In butterflies, each stage looks completely different.
5707.m: The whole transformation is called metamorphosis.

5708.q: On how many toes does a cow walk on each foot?
5708.e: Cows walk on two toes on each foot, which together form the hoof. That is why they are called even-toed hoofed animals.

5709.q: What danger do certain worming treatments for grazing animals pose to dung beetles?
a: Traces in the dung can harm the beetles and their larvae
The treatments make the dung too dry to eat
The treatments attract too many birds
The treatments make the beetles too heavy
5709.e: Some substances, such as avermectins, end up outside in the droppings. There they can poison insects in the dung.
5709.m: Worming treatments in dung harm the beetles.

5710.q: Why should a budgie cage not stand in blazing sun or a draught?
a: The bird could overheat or catch a chill
The bird would become too colourful
The bird would become too quiet
The bird would grow too fast
5710.e: Too much sun can make a budgie overheat, and draughts can make it ill. A sheltered, bright place is best.
5710.m: No cage in a draught or blazing sun.

5711.q: What especially makes ants different from most other insects?
a: Their life in an organised colony
5711.e: Ants do not live alone but in large, well-organised communities. This is called an insect colony.
5711.m: Ants live in an insect colony.

5712.q: What is especially noticeable about many baboons' faces?
5712.e: Baboons have a long snout that looks like a dog's. That is why they are also called dog-faced monkeys.

5713.q: Compared with many other birds, what is typical of where the swift hunts?
a: it mostly hunts high above the ground in the air
it hunts almost only on the ground among the grass
it only hunts in dense forests
5713.e: While many birds look for food on the ground or in trees, the swift stays high up in the air almost all the time. There it finds its favourite food, aerial plankton made up of small insects.
5713.m: Swifts hunt high up in the air.

5714.q: What does a female sparrow look like compared with the male?
a: with a long tail like a peacock's
5714.e: Female sparrows are rather brownish grey and plain. They do not have a black patch on the throat like the males.

a: A strong thinning of the protective ozone layer, mainly over Antarctica
A hole in the Earth’s crust
5715.e: Certain chemicals have greatly weakened the ozone layer over Antarctica. As a result, more dangerous UV radiation reaches the Earth.
5715.m: The ozone hole weakens the atmosphere’s UV protection.

5716.q: Roughly how long do the parents feed young great tits in the nest?
5716.e: The parents feed their young in the nest for about three weeks. Then the young birds are ready to fly and leave the hole.
5716.m: The parents feed them in the nest for three weeks.

5717.q: What often happens to the drones in autumn?
a: They are driven out of the hive
5717.e: In autumn the drones are no longer needed. The workers no longer let them into the hive, so that the honey lasts through the winter.
5717.m: Drones have to leave the hive in autumn.

5718.e: The grubs live underground for several years. There they feed on plant roots.
5718.m: The grubs live in the soil for several years.

5719.q: What is a young reindeer called?
5719.e: Young reindeer are called calves. They are born in spring or early summer.

5720.q: What does a ring-tailed lemur's face look like?
a: White with dark rings around the eyes and a dark nose
5720.e: The face is pale, and the eyes are surrounded by dark rings. The nose is dark too.
5720.m: Ring-tailed lemurs have dark eye rings.

a: A giraffe with a coat pattern like a net
A giraffe with no spots at all
A giraffe with stripes like a zebra
5721.e: The reticulated giraffe is a giraffe from Africa. Its brown patches are separated by fine pale lines, which looks like a net.
5721.m: The reticulated giraffe has a net-like coat pattern.

5722.q: The picture shows a habitat. Where does the brown trout feel most at home?
a: In a cool, clear stream with lots of oxygen
In a swamp with no current
5722.e: The brown trout needs clean, cold water rich in oxygen. It finds such conditions in fast-flowing streams.
5722.m: It loves cool, clear, fast streams.

5723.q: Where do carrion crows most like to build their nests?
5723.e: Carrion crows prefer to build their nests high up in the tops of tall trees. From there they have a good view of their surroundings and are better protected from enemies.
5723.m: Crows' nests are high up in treetops.

5724.q: Which statement about dragonflies stinging is true?
a: Dragonflies have no sting and are harmless to people
They sting with a venomous sting
They squirt venom from their abdomen
5724.e: In theory dragonflies can nip, but they do not sting. Their long abdomen has no sting.

5725.q: What are the tawny owl's legs like compared with many other birds?
a: They are covered with feathers down to the toes
They are completely bare and scaly like a hen's
They are extremely long like a stork's
5725.e: The tawny owl's legs are mostly feathered, which protects it from the cold. This is typical of many owl species from cooler regions.
5725.m: The tawny owl has feathered legs.

5726.q: What does a seed need in order to germinate?
5726.e: A seed needs moisture and warmth to start sprouting. In the soil it also finds support and nutrients.
5726.m: Seeds need water, warmth and soil.

5727.q: What makes the jaguar special among the big cats?
a: It likes swimming and is good at it
5727.e: Unlike many cats, the jaguar goes into the water willingly and swims well. It also hunts in rivers and swamps.

5728.q: Which organisation researches and monitors wolves, among other animals, in Switzerland?
5728.e: The organisation KORA monitors large predators such as the wolf, bear and lynx in Switzerland. It collects data on the numbers, movements and behaviour of these animals.

5729.q: Why can lawnmowers and robot mowers be dangerous for hedgehogs?
a: Hedgehogs lie still in the grass and get injured
5729.e: When a hedgehog hides in the grass, it often lies still instead of running away. This means it can be injured by a lawnmower or robot mower.
5729.m: Robot mowers can injure hidden hedgehogs.

5730.q: Roughly how old can a blue whale get?
5730.e: Blue whales can live a very long time, some almost as long as a person who reaches a hundred. That is a very great age for an animal.
5730.m: Blue whales can live a very long time.

5731.q: How does the pike sense movements in the water?
a: It does not, it only sees
5731.e: The pike has a special line along its side that senses vibrations in the water. This lets it notice when a fish is coming close.
5731.m: The lateral line senses water movements.

5732.q: Roughly how old can orangutans get in captivity?
5732.e: In zoos they can live to over 50. In the wild they usually live a little less long.
5732.m: Orangutans live a very long time.

5733.q: How many nests does a squirrel often build?
5733.e: A squirrel often builds several nests in its territory. That way it always has a safe place to sleep.
5733.m: A squirrel often has several nests.

5734.q: How do golden jackals often hunt?
a: Alone, in pairs or in small groups
Only in packs of a hundred animals
Only with the help of eagles
5734.e: For small prey they usually hunt alone or as a pair. For bigger prey, a small group can work together.
5734.m: They hunt alone, in pairs or in groups.

5735.q: Where do baboons often sleep at night?
5735.e: In trees and on rocks they are better protected from predators such as leopards. There the whole group sleeps close together.
5735.m: They look for safe high places to sleep.

5736.q: Where on their bodies can dogs sweat at all?
a: All over the body like people
Dogs do not sweat at all
5736.e: Dogs have sweat glands mainly on their paw pads, but these do little to cool them down. Their main way of controlling their temperature is panting.
5736.m: Dogs hardly sweat, only on their paws.

5737.q: How many stomachs does a cow have?
5737.e: The cow has four stomachs so that it can digest tough grass well. This lets it get all the nutrients out of its food.

5738.q: What colour is an adult puma's coat usually?
a: Plain yellowish brown to greyish brown
5738.e: The coat of adult pumas is fairly plain, usually sandy to reddish or grey. It has no rosettes or stripes.

5739.q: What are llamas often used for in Switzerland today?
5739.e: In Switzerland there is llama trekking. Llamas go along with people on hikes.
5739.m: There is llama trekking in Switzerland too.

5740.q: What double role does the edible frog play in a pond ecosystem?
a: It is both a hunter of insects and prey for other animals
It is neither hunter nor prey
It alone builds up the whole ecosystem
5740.e: The edible frog eats lots of small insects itself, which makes it a hunter. At the same time it is an important source of food for bigger animals such as storks or snakes.
5740.m: The edible frog is both hunter and prey.

5741.q: What are the two breeds of alpaca?
5741.e: The huacaya has fluffy, woolly fleece. The suri has long, shiny locks that hang down like plaits.
5741.m: Huacaya and suri are the alpaca types.

5742.q: In which of the world's oceans are orcas found?
a: In almost all the world's seas
5742.e: Orcas live almost everywhere in the world, from cold polar seas to warmer waters. They are very widespread.
5742.m: Orcas live in almost all seas.

5743.q: Roughly how long is a llama pregnant?
5743.e: Female llamas carry their young for around 11 months. Then usually a single baby, called a cria, is born.
5743.m: Llamas are pregnant for about eleven months.

5745.q: What do Buddhist monks and nuns often do to find inner peace?
5745.e: When meditating, Buddhist monks and nuns sit still and concentrate on their breathing. In this way they try to calm their thoughts.
5745.m: Meditation helps you find inner peace.

a: The vote of a canton when counting the majority of cantons
The vote of a single citizen
A second vote for Swiss living abroad
5746.e: In votes that need a majority of the cantons, the result in each canton counts as one cantonal vote. The six former half-cantons, such as Obwalden or Basel-Stadt, each have half a cantonal vote.
5746.m: Each canton has one cantonal vote.

5747.q: Which Alpine animal is especially nimble and jumps skilfully over steep rocks?
5747.e: The chamois has small curved horns and, thanks to its hooves, can climb over rugged rocks in a flash. It is much lighter and faster than the ibex.
5747.m: The chamois is a nimble rock climber.

5748.q: Why is the blue whale called the blue whale?
a: Because it only lives in the blue sea
5748.e: Underwater, the whale's grey skin often looks blue. That is why people gave it this name.
5748.m: The water makes it look blue.

5749.q: How many pups are often in an African wild dog litter?
a: Often more than six, sometimes over ten
5749.e: Wild dogs have quite large litters. The number of pups can even be over ten.

5750.q: What do fire salamander larvae do when they finish their metamorphosis?
a: They leave the water and live on land from then on
They stay in the water for ever
5750.e: After metamorphosis, the larvae lose their gills and leave the water. From then on they live on land like the adults.
5750.m: After changing, they move onto land.

5751.q: Which parts of a panda's body are typically black?
5751.e: A panda's ears, legs, shoulders and the patches around its eyes are black. The rest of the body is mostly white.
5751.m: A panda's ears and legs are black.

5752.q: Which country has the most alpacas today?
5752.e: Most alpacas live in Peru. They have been kept there for centuries.

5753.q: What are scientists doing to reduce conflicts between wolves and alpine farming?
a: They encourage the use of livestock guardian dogs and fences
They ban sheep from summer pastures completely
They catch all the wolves and take them to zoos
5753.e: With better fences and livestock guardian dogs, farm animals on alpine pastures can be better protected from wolves. This is meant to help reduce conflicts between farming and wolf protection.
5753.m: Fences and dogs protect the herds.

5754.q: Apart from predators, what is a big danger for chamois in the mountains?
5754.e: In the steep, snowy mountains, avalanches can be a serious danger for chamois. Many animals die because of them every year.
5754.m: Avalanches are a danger in the mountains.

5755.q: Why is the leatherback turtle probably called that?
a: Its shell feels soft like leather
Its flippers are made of leather
5755.e: The leatherback's shell is not hard like that of other species, but rather soft and leathery. That is where its name comes from.
5755.m: Its shell is soft like leather.

5756.q: How does the yellow and black pattern differ between fire salamanders?
a: Each animal has its own unique pattern
All the animals look exactly the same
5756.e: Like a fingerprint, the pattern of spots is unique to each fire salamander. Researchers can use it to recognise individual animals.
5756.m: Each fire salamander has a unique pattern.

5757.q: How do mute swans get plants from the bottom of the water?
a: they put their head under the water
they fly low over the water
5757.e: Swans stretch their long neck underwater to reach plants. Their body stays floating on top.
5757.m: Swans put their head in the water.

5758.e: Fish eggs are called roe. Milt is the name for the males' sperm.

5759.q: Which well-known goldfish variety has a striking double tail fin?
5759.e: The veiltail is a popular variety of goldfish with a long, double tail fin. It was bred especially for aquariums.
5759.m: The veiltail is a bred variety of goldfish.

5760.q: Where can you see real lions in Switzerland?
a: Only in zoos and wildlife parks
Only in the forests in winter
Nowhere, not even in a zoo
5760.e: There are no wild lions in Switzerland. But you can visit them, for example, at Basel Zoo or Zurich Zoo.
5760.m: In Switzerland lions only live in zoos.

5761.q: How well does a rhino see?
a: Very well, better than an eagle
It can see everything in the dark
It only sees colours, not shapes
5761.e: Rhinos do not see very well and can hardly make out things far away. Instead they rely on other senses.
5761.m: Rhinos do not see very well.

5762.q: Which sense mainly helps dragonflies hunt?
5762.e: Dragonflies hunt with their large eyes and spot prey early. They do not use echolocation.

5763.q: What protects the kingfisher's eyes when it dives into the water?
5763.e: When it dives in, a see-through third eyelid closes over the eye. It protects the eye and still lets the bird see well underwater.
5763.m: A third eyelid protects the eyes when diving.

5764.q: How often does a dragonfly larva shed its skin as it develops?
5764.e: To grow, the larva has to shed its stiff skin several times. Usually there are about 10 to 15 moults.
5764.m: Larvae shed their skin several times.

5765.q: What does a wolf often show by the position of its tail?
a: Its mood and its rank in the pack
Whether it is tired and going to sleep
5765.e: A tail held high often shows confidence or dominance, while a tail tucked between the legs shows submission or fear. This is how wolves communicate even without sounds.
5765.m: Tail position gives away the mood.

5766.q: In which of Switzerland's neighbouring countries did the last Alpine ibex survive when they had been wiped out everywhere else?
5766.e: A small group of ibex survived in only one area in Italy, today's Gran Paradiso National Park. Practically all of today's ibex are descended from them.

5767.q: How do mallards often find food underwater?
a: They dabble with their head down and tail up
They always dive right under and stay for hours
They only catch fish with sharp teeth
They jump out of the water
5767.e: When dabbling, the duck puts its head underwater while its tail sticks up in the air. This lets it reach plants and animals on the bottom.
5767.m: Dabbling means searching with your head underwater.

5768.q: Why can the wels catfish track down prey in the water without seeing it?
a: It senses heat like a snake
It has glowing eyes like a cat
5768.e: Its lateral line senses movements in the water. The catfish also tastes with its whole skin.

5769.q: How does the grey heron typically move when creeping up on prey?
a: Very slowly, almost in slow motion
5769.e: When creeping up, the grey heron takes each step extremely slowly and carefully. This way it does not scare the prey in the water.

5770.q: What colour is a honeybee usually?
5770.e: Honeybees have a brownish yellow body with dark stripes. The stripes tell other animals: careful, I can sting.
5770.m: Honeybees have yellow and brown stripes.

5771.q: What does the cuckoo do differently from most birds?
a: It lays its eggs in other birds' nests
5771.e: The cuckoo does not build its own nest, but secretly lays its eggs in the nests of other birds. These other birds then raise its young.
5771.m: The cuckoo lays its eggs in other birds' nests.

5772.q: What is a blue whale's tongue like compared with other animals?
5772.e: The blue whale's tongue is huge and can weigh as much as a whole elephant. Even so, the blue whale only swallows tiny krill.
5772.m: Its tongue is as heavy as an elephant.

5773.q: Why can a housefly bring germs onto our food?
a: Because it has been sitting on rubbish or dung before
5773.e: A fly often sits on rubbish or dung first and then on our food. Germs can get from its feet onto the food.
5773.m: Flies carry germs on their feet.

5774.q: How is the smooth, moist skin of the edible frog usually different from a toad's skin?
a: Toad skin is often drier and wartier
Edible frog skin is completely dry like paper
Toads have no skin at all
There is no difference at all
5774.e: The edible frog's skin is smooth and moist, while toads often have drier, warty skin. This difference helps tell frogs and toads apart.
5774.m: Frog skin is smoother than toad skin.

5775.q: How many calves does a female moose usually have at once?
a: Never more than one in her life
5775.e: Usually one calf is born, and twins too when there is good food. The birth takes place in May or June.
5775.m: Female moose usually have one or two calves.

5776.q: What happens when a pike loses a tooth?
5776.e: The pike's teeth keep growing back when one is lost. This means it has enough sharp teeth to catch prey all its life.

5777.q: What is the Alpine marmot's well-known whistle mainly for?
a: As an alarm call to warn the colony of danger
5777.e: If a marmot spots an enemy such as an eagle or a fox, it gives a loud whistle. The other animals in the colony then flee into their burrows at once.
5777.m: The whistle warns the whole colony.

5778.q: Why do some dragonfly wings shine in rainbow colours?
a: Because of wafer-thin layers, like in soap bubbles
Because of fat in the wing
5778.e: The skin of the wing is very thin. Light is reflected from it in a way that creates bright colours, just like in soap bubbles.
5778.m: Thin wings shimmer like soap bubbles.

5779.q: What does the badger use fixed spots outside its sett for?
a: As toilets to mark its territory
5779.e: Badgers dig small pits that they use as toilets. This shows other badgers where their territory is.
5779.m: Badgers mark their territory with latrines.

5780.q: What did the people of the prairies use bison hides for?
5780.e: Furs and hides were made into clothing and tent covers. Bones and sinews were used too.
5780.m: Almost every part of the bison was used.

5781.q: What do wild rabbits eat in winter when there is little grass?
5781.e: In winter, wild rabbits find less grass, so they also eat bark, twigs and roots. This helps them get through the winter.
5781.m: In winter they eat bark and twigs.

5782.q: How are the barn swallow and the swift related?
a: Despite looking similar, they are not closely related
They are exactly the same species
The swift is a subspecies of the barn swallow
They are the only two bird species in the world
5782.e: Although barn swallows and swifts look similar in flight, they belong to completely different orders of birds. The swift is actually more closely related to hummingbirds than to the swallow.
5782.m: Similar in flight, but not related.

5783.q: Which animals are natural enemies of the reindeer?
5783.e: Wolves hunt reindeer, especially calves and sick animals. Bears and wolverines can also catch reindeer.

5784.q: What is a goat missing at the front of the top of its mouth?
5784.e: Goats have no incisors at the front of the upper jaw, just a hard pad for chewing. That still works well for tearing off plants.
5784.m: Goats have no incisors at the top.

5785.q: What does a stoat sometimes do to get a better view of its surroundings?
a: It stands up on its back legs
It digs itself in at once
5785.e: To scan its surroundings for danger or prey, the stoat sometimes sits bolt upright on its back legs. This lets it see further.

5786.q: What does a wolf often show when it bares its teeth and growls?
a: It is threatening or showing dominance
It is very happy and wants to play
It is showing that it is cold
It is signalling that it is completely relaxed
5786.e: Bared teeth and growling are clear warning signals from a wolf. It is telling another animal that it had better keep its distance.
5786.m: Baring teeth is a warning signal.

5787.q: How does the common raven usually move through the air?
a: with powerful, steady wingbeats and often an outstretched neck
always hopping close to the ground
5787.e: In flight, the common raven typically stretches its neck forwards and beats its wings powerfully. This typical way of flying helps to recognise it from far away.
5787.m: It flies with an outstretched neck and powerful wingbeats.

5788.q: Where does an adult jellyfish release its eggs?
5788.e: Adult jellyfish simply release their eggs and sperm into the open sea. There they meet and new life begins.
5788.m: Jellyfish release eggs into the open water.

5789.q: What is the white patch behind the eye of an orca?
5789.e: Behind its eye the orca has a pale patch. It is part of its typical markings.
5789.m: Orcas have a white eye patch.

5790.q: How does nature help the bearded vulture digest bones?
a: Its stomach acid is especially strong
It cooks the bones in the sun
It lets other animals digest them first
5790.e: Birds have no teeth, but the bearded vulture's stomach acid is extremely strong. It can dissolve even hard pieces of bone within a few hours.
5790.m: Strong acid makes up for missing teeth.

5791.q: Why should children not squeeze a hamster too hard?
a: It is very fragile and can get hurt
5791.e: Hamsters are small, delicate animals. Squeezing them too hard can hurt or injure them.

5792.q: Roughly what speed can a golden eagle reach in a dive?
5792.e: In a steep dive a golden eagle can reach speeds of well over 150 kilometres per hour. This helps it surprise even fast prey.
5792.m: It is extremely fast in a dive.

5793.q: Which bird family does the house sparrow belong to?
5793.e: The house sparrow belongs to the Old World sparrow family, called Passeridae in Latin. This family includes several similar small seed eaters.
5793.m: The house sparrow belongs to the sparrow family.

5794.q: What role does the eagle owl play in its ecosystem?
a: As a top predator it keeps the numbers of many smaller animals in check
It is an important helper that pollinates many flowering plants
It is an important organism that breaks down dead plant material
It mainly carries tree seeds around
5794.e: As a top predator the eagle owl keeps the numbers of many smaller animals such as mice, rats or other birds in check. This helps keep a natural balance in its habitat.
5794.m: As a hunter, the eagle owl regulates the ecosystem.

5796.q: Is an earthworm male or female?
5796.e: An earthworm has both male and female body parts. Animals like this are called hermaphrodites.

5797.q: Why must you not simply put a goldfish into a lake or river?
a: Because it can push out native animals there
Because the water there is too salty
Because it would find nothing to eat
5797.e: Released goldfish can multiply quickly in open waters and upset the balance of nature. That is why it is forbidden to simply set goldfish free.
5797.m: Goldfish do not belong in open waters.

5800.q: Where in Switzerland is the European mantis mainly found?
a: In warm, dry areas, for example in Valais and Ticino
5800.e: It likes warmth and dry conditions. That is why it is found in sunny places such as Valais, Ticino or the Basel region.

5801.q: What colour is a dromedary's coat usually?
5801.e: The pale colour suits the desert. The coat also protects against sun and heat.
5801.m: A sandy coat suits the desert.

5802.q: What does a jellyfish use its tentacles for?
a: To catch prey and defend itself
5802.e: The tentacles carry stinging cells that the jellyfish uses to catch prey and defend itself. They stun small animals.
5802.m: Jellyfish use tentacles to catch prey.

5803.q: What do you call animals that eat dead organic remains?
5803.e: Woodlice are decomposers. Together with other living things they break down dead plant remains.
5803.m: Decomposers eat and recycle dead material.

5804.q: What does a dog need every day to stay fit and happy?
a: Plenty of exercise in the fresh air
Its own room in the house
5804.e: Dogs need daily walks and exercise to stay healthy and not get bored. Playing with people is good for them too.

5806.q: Roughly what is the wingspan of an adult red kite?
5806.e: With a wingspan of almost two metres, the red kite can glide gracefully for a long time. This makes it an impressive flier.
5806.m: Almost two metres of wingspan carry the red kite.

5807.q: Which country has a red circle in the middle of a white flag?
5807.e: The red circle on the Japanese flag represents the rising sun. That is why Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
5807.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

5808.q: What shape is a penguin's beak usually?
a: Long and pointed, good for catching fish
Broad and flat like a duck's
Short and curved like a parrot's
5808.e: A penguin's beak is usually long and pointed. This lets it snap up slippery fish in the water.
5808.m: A pointed beak helps catch fish.

5809.q: Which bird family does the mute swan belong to?
5809.e: The mute swan belongs to the duck family, just like ducks and geese. But it is much bigger than a duck.
5809.m: Swans belong to the duck family.

5810.q: Why are young robins spotted brown?
a: So that they are well camouflaged
5810.e: The brown, spotted colouring protects the young birds from enemies. This way they are hard to see among the leaves.

5811.q: What does the Roman snail do in winter?
a: It rests in the ground over winter
5811.e: In winter the Roman snail buries itself in the ground and rests. This is how it survives the cold.
5811.m: In winter it rests deep in the ground.

5812.q: Which part of a sand lizard's body makes up a large share of its total length?
5812.e: The tail is often longer than the rest of the body. That is why losing the tail looks like such a big loss.
5812.m: The tail is longer than the body.

5813.q: How do African wild dogs often share their food after a hunt?
a: They let pups and weak members eat too
5813.e: Wild dogs are known for their social behaviour. Pups and injured animals are often allowed to eat first or alongside the others.

5814.q: In which season do European perch usually spawn?
5814.e: The spawning season is roughly between March and June, when the water warms up. Then the fish move into the shallow areas near the shore.

5815.q: What is special about the coat of a white tiger?
a: It is white with black stripes
It is completely black with no stripes
It is blue with red spots
It has no stripes at all
5815.e: White tigers have a rare genetic change that makes their coat white instead of orange. The black stripes stay, though.
5815.m: White tigers have white fur with stripes.

5816.q: Which animal is considered the largest land-dwelling member of the weasel family?
5816.e: The wolverine is much bigger and more strongly built than many other members of the weasel family. With its powerful body it can even kill larger prey.
5816.m: The wolverine is the largest land member of the weasel family.

5817.q: Which trees does the great tit especially like?
5817.e: Great tits like to spend time in broadleaved trees such as oaks because there are lots of insects there. But they also feel at home in parks and gardens with different trees.
5817.m: Broadleaved trees like oaks offer lots of food.

5818.q: How do mute swans often react to people who come too close?
a: They always fly away at once
5818.e: Especially during the breeding season, mute swans are very watchful and ready to defend themselves. So you should always keep enough distance.
5818.m: Keep your distance, swans can attack.

5819.q: Roughly how long is a puma without its tail?
a: About one to one and a half metres
5819.e: Its body is about as long as an adult person is tall. Then there is the long tail on top of that.
5819.m: Pumas are about as long as a person is tall.

5820.q: Where does the German name of the adder, ‘Kreuzotter’ (cross viper), probably come from?
a: From the cross-like marking on its head
From the cross on its belly
Because it crosses with other species
5820.e: The marking on its head looks like a cross. That is where the German name ‘Kreuzotter’ comes from.
5820.m: The head marking gave it its name.

5821.q: Which group of animals does the giraffe belong to?
a: The even-toed ungulates, a group of hoofed animals
5821.e: Like cows, sheep and deer, giraffes are even-toed ungulates. This means they have two large toes on each foot.

5822.q: Roughly how long does it take for young kingfishers to fledge?
5822.e: Around three to four weeks after hatching, young kingfishers leave the nest burrow and can fly. After that they must quickly learn to hunt on their own.
5822.m: The young fledge after about four weeks.

5823.q: What happens when a male blackbird spots another male in its territory?
a: It sings loudly and defends its area
5823.e: A male blackbird then sings especially loudly to show clearly that the territory is taken. Sometimes there are even short fights.
5823.m: Blackbirds defend their territory with song.

5824.q: Roughly how long does a goose sit on its eggs?
5824.e: A goose sits on her eggs for about 28 to 30 days. During this time she keeps the eggs warm until the goslings hatch.
5824.m: Geese sit on their eggs for about four weeks.

5825.q: Who played the key role in shaping the idea of the separation of powers?
5825.e: In the 18th century the French philosopher Montesquieu described the separation of the legislature, executive and judiciary. This principle is meant to prevent abuse of power.
5825.m: Montesquieu called for divided state power.

5826.q: Where do chickens usually prefer to sleep at night?
5826.e: At night, chickens like to sit on a raised perch in the coop. This protects them better from enemies such as the fox.

5827.q: What is one use of the European pond turtle's long tail?
5827.e: The tail is almost as long as the shell. When swimming it helps the animal keep its direction.
5827.m: The long tail helps with steering.

5828.q: What do you call the place where chamois often stay in winter?
5828.e: In winter, chamois often retreat to sheltered places called winter refuges. There they find some food and protection from wind and cold.
5828.m: In winter chamois use winter refuges.

5829.q: How many cubs does a lioness usually have at once?
5829.e: A lioness usually gives birth to two to four cubs. She first raises them in hiding before they meet the pride.
5829.m: Lionesses usually have two to four cubs.

5830.q: What happens to the skin of a growing grass snake?
5830.e: The skin does not grow with the snake, so the snake sheds it. The old skin is called a slough.

5831.q: Roughly how long is a cat pregnant?
5831.e: On average a cat carries her young for about nine weeks, so about 63 to 65 days. The kittens are then born blind and deaf.
5831.m: Cats are pregnant for about nine weeks.

5832.q: Why does the great spotted woodpecker drum so loudly on trees?
5832.e: By drumming it tells other woodpeckers that this place belongs to it. It sounds like a fast knocking.
5832.m: Drumming shows who the tree belongs to.

5833.q: What do many dogs wear around their neck on a walk?
5833.e: You can clip the lead to the collar so the dog stays safely by your side. It often has a tag with contact details too.
5833.m: For walks the dog wears a collar.

5834.q: Where does a female sea turtle often swim to lay her eggs?
a: Back to the beach where she hatched herself
Always to a brand new beach
5834.e: After many years, many females find exactly the beach where they hatched. This amazing ability is called homing.
5834.m: Females return to the beach where they were born.

5835.q: Why do dolphins sometimes leap high out of the water?
a: To play and to swim faster
To get closer to the sun
5835.e: Dolphins love jumping; it is fun and helps them swim faster. It also makes it easier for them to breathe.
5835.m: Dolphins leap to play and swim fast.

5836.q: What does an earthworm produce that is a good fertiliser for plants?
5836.e: What the earthworm leaves behind is called worm castings. It contains many nutrients that plants can use well.

a: Yes, it can swim well when it needs to
It can only swim in the rain
5837.e: It may be surprising, but moles really can swim. This helps them when their tunnels are flooded.

5838.q: Which senses are especially good in the beaver, even though it sees poorly?
5838.e: Beavers have rather weak eyes, but a very good sense of smell and sharp hearing. These senses help them notice danger early.
5838.m: Beavers smell and hear very well.

5839.q: Is the elk (moose) a plant eater or a meat eater?
5839.e: The elk feeds only on plants. Like the cow, it is a ruminant.

5840.q: Which small catfish is popular in aquariums and searches the bottom for leftover food?
5840.e: Corydoras catfish stay small and are peaceful. They search the bottom for leftover food.

5841.q: What do young great crested grebes often get from their parents before they can dive themselves?
a: Small fish and insects handed to them
5841.e: At first the parents feed the chicks small fish and insects straight from their beaks. Only later do the young learn to dive themselves.
5841.m: Parents feed the chicks small fish.

5842.q: What does an ant use its antennae for?
5842.e: With its antennae the ant smells scents and feels its way. That is how it finds food and other ants.

5843.q: What is special about the African wild dog's paws compared with many other dogs?
a: They have four toes on the front paws
5843.e: The wild dog has no fifth toe, the so-called dewclaw, on its front paws. So it has four toes there.
5843.m: Wild dogs have only four toes at the front.

5844.q: What does a shark use to smell in the water?
