5844.e: Sharks have nostrils on their snout that let them smell very well. With them they can find prey even from far away.

5845.q: How do great crested grebes usually take off when they want to fly?
a: They run across the water surface flapping their wings
They jump straight up into the air
They let the wind carry them
They first climb onto a rock
5845.e: Because their wings are short, they need a long run-up across the water to build up speed. Only then can they take off.
5845.m: A run-up across the water makes take-off possible.

5846.q: Which region of Switzerland is known for cockchafer swarms?
a: The ice wall of the Jungfraujoch
5846.e: Cockchafers like loose soil and broadleaved woods, so they are common on the Central Plateau. They are absent from the high mountains.
5846.m: Cockchafers live mainly at lower altitudes.

5847.q: What are a harbour seal's eyes especially good at?
5847.e: The harbour seal's big eyes are specially adapted to seeing underwater. This lets it spot fish even in the depths.

5848.q: What do magpies eat especially often in winter?
5848.e: In winter, when insects are scarce, magpies mainly eat carrion, seeds and food scraps. Being so flexible helps them survive the cold season.
5848.m: In winter magpies eat whatever they find.

a: Being unable to digest milk sugar properly
5849.e: With lactose intolerance, an enzyme for digesting milk sugar is missing. This often leads to tummy ache after dairy products.
5849.m: With lactose intolerance, milk sugar is hard to digest.

5850.q: Which bee lays the eggs in the hive?
5850.e: Only the queen lays eggs, often a great many each day. All the other bees look after the hive.

5851.q: Roughly how big can a giant Pacific octopus get?
a: Several metres from arm tip to arm tip
5851.e: The giant Pacific octopus is the largest octopus species in the world. Its arms can span several metres.
5851.m: Giant Pacific octopuses grow very big.

5852.q: How are grubs fought naturally in Swiss meadows?
a: With a fungus that infects the grubs
5852.e: A special soil fungus infects the grubs and kills them. Farmers spread it on meadows on purpose, without any poison.

5853.q: Where does the striped hyena like to rest?
5853.e: During the day, striped hyenas hide in caves or rock crevices. At night they go looking for food.
5853.m: Striped hyenas rest in caves during the day.

5854.q: Why do aphids get so much sugar but little protein when they suck sap?
a: Because plant sap contains a lot of sugar and little protein
5854.e: To get enough protein building blocks, they must take in a lot of sap. They release the extra sugar as honeydew.
5854.m: Lots of sap for little protein, the rest becomes honeydew.

5855.q: What kind of eater is the wild boar?
5855.e: Wild boar eat both plants and small animals. That is why they are called omnivores.
5855.m: Wild boar eat plants and animals.

5856.q: How do geese usually behave towards their partner?
a: They often stay together for life
They have many partners at once
5856.e: Many geese find a partner they stay with for many years. This is called a faithful pair bond.
5856.m: Geese often stay together for a long time.

5857.q: What is the dark stripe below the peregrine falcon's eye, which looks like a moustache, called?
5857.e: The moustachial stripe is a striking feature of the peregrine falcon's face. It helps tell this species apart from other falcons.
5857.m: The moustachial stripe marks the falcon's face.

5858.q: What is a prey animal that relies on flight?
a: An animal that tends to run away from danger
An animal that only hunts at night
5858.e: Animals like alpacas protect themselves by running away quickly. That is why they are often very alert.
5858.m: Such animals run away when in danger.

5859.q: Roughly what is the wingspan of an adult bearded vulture?
5859.e: With its huge wingspan, the bearded vulture is one of the largest birds in Europe. It can glide for hours without flapping its wings.

5860.q: How see-through is the body of many jellyfish?
5860.e: Many jellyfish have an almost glass-clear body that you can nearly see through. This is because they contain so much water.

5861.q: How many claws does a polar bear have on each paw?
5861.e: Each polar bear paw has five sharp claws. They give it a good grip on the ice and help it catch prey.

5862.q: What is the family called that the European tree frog belongs to?
5862.e: The European tree frog belongs to the tree frog family, which includes many tree-dwelling species worldwide. In central Europe it is the only native species of this family.
5862.m: The only native species of its family.

5863.q: How many eyes does a honeybee have in total?
5863.e: A bee has two large compound eyes and three small simple eyes on its head. With them it sees movement and light especially well.

5864.q: What does the common wall lizard do when a person comes near?
a: It usually darts into a crack or under stones
5864.e: Wall lizards are shy and avoid contact with people. When in danger they head straight for the nearest hiding place.
5864.m: In danger the wall lizard flees quickly.

5865.q: What is one way meerkats mark their territory?
5865.e: They have scent glands and rub them on objects. This leaves their scent marks behind.

5866.q: What does a plant need to grow?
5866.e: Plants need light, water and nutrients from the soil to grow. Without these things they cannot thrive.
5866.m: Plants need light, water and soil.

5867.q: Which Swiss dog breed was bred especially for rescue work in the snow?
5867.e: The St Bernard was used on the Great St Bernard Pass to search for and rescue buried travellers. It is a very big, strong dog.
5867.m: The St Bernard rescues people in the snow.

a: Restructuring the economy with more freedom for businesses
5868.e: Perestroika means ‘restructuring’. Gorbachev wanted to reform the weak Soviet economy with it, which in the end also led to big political changes.
5868.m: Perestroika meant restructuring the Soviet economy.

5869.q: Why does an orca sometimes leap right out of the water?
a: To play, communicate or get rid of parasites
5869.e: Orcas often jump for fun or to communicate with others. Sometimes this also cleans their skin.
5869.m: Orcas like to leap out of the water.

5871.q: What does it mean that whitefish are cold-water fish?
a: They feel best in cool water
They need hot water to spawn
5871.e: Cold-water fish do not cope well with warmth. Whitefish need temperatures that would be too cool for many other fish.

5872.q: What is the soft, warm layer of feathers under a duck's large feathers called?
5872.e: Under their large outer feathers, ducks have small, very soft feathers. This down keeps the duck warm, even in cold water.

5873.q: What is the difference between a wasp and a bee when it comes to stinging?
a: A wasp can sting several times, a bee usually only once
5873.e: A bee's sting stays stuck in the skin, and the bee usually dies afterwards. A wasp has a smooth sting and can sting again.
5873.m: Wasps can sting several times, bees usually only once.

5874.e: Meerkats are active by day. At night they retreat into their burrow.
5874.m: Meerkats are active during the day.

5875.q: What is a treaty between two countries?
a: A written agreement that both keep to
5875.e: In a treaty, countries promise, for example, to work together or to avoid disputes. Such treaties are very important for peace.
5875.m: A treaty is an agreement between countries.

5876.q: Which layer protects penguins from the cold?
a: A thick layer of fat under the skin
A fur coat like a bear's
A layer of scales like a fish's
A layer of wax like a bee's
5876.e: Under a penguin's skin is a thick layer of fat called blubber. It keeps the body warm even in icy water.
5876.m: Blubber protects penguins from the cold.

5877.q: What did people in the past want to find out when they counted a cuckoo's calls?
a: How old they would live to be
How many eggs were in the nest
5877.e: In the past, many people believed the number of cuckoo calls told you how old you would become. It was an old folk belief about this herald of spring.
5877.m: Counting cuckoo calls was an old custom.

5878.q: What happens to reindeer fur over the course of the year?
a: They have a summer coat and a winter coat
They always have the same coat
They only have fur in summer
5878.e: In winter the coat is thicker and paler. In summer they change to shorter fur.
5878.m: The coat changes twice a year.

5879.q: How many toes do tapirs have on their front feet?
5879.e: Tapirs have four toes on their front feet. On their back feet they have three.
5879.m: Four toes at the front, three at the back.

5880.q: What is a typical feature of the side-striped jackal?
a: A pale stripe along the side of its body
A striped tail like a tiger's
A stripe of spines on its back
5880.e: The side-striped jackal has a pale stripe along its flanks. That is where its name comes from.
5880.m: The side-striped jackal has pale stripes on its flanks.

5881.q: What does the African wild dog mainly eat?
5881.e: It is a meat-eater and mainly hunts medium-sized antelopes such as impalas. Smaller prey is also on the menu.
5881.m: Wild dogs are meat-eaters and hunt antelopes.

5882.q: What does a red deer hind do when she notices danger?
a: She gives a short, loud call like a bark
5882.e: When a hind notices danger, she gives a short, barking call. This warns the whole group.
5882.m: Hinds warn with a barking call.

5883.q: How many legs does a dragonfly have?
5883.e: Like all insects, a dragonfly has six legs. They are attached to its chest.

5884.q: What role does the male peregrine falcon usually take during the breeding season?
a: It brings food to the female sitting on the eggs
It sits on the eggs entirely alone
It leaves the territory for months
5884.e: While the female mostly sits on the eggs, the male takes care of bringing food. This takes the load off the female so she can stay on the eggs.
5884.m: The male feeds the female on the nest.

5885.q: Why does the protective emblem of the Red Cross show a red cross on a white background?
a: It honours Switzerland with its reversed flag
Red and white are easiest to see in war
It comes from the coat of arms of the city of Geneva
It goes back to the sign of the crusaders
5885.e: The emblem was created in Geneva in 1863. It is the Swiss flag reversed, in honour of the founding country. Worldwide it serves as a neutral protective emblem in war.
5885.m: The Red Cross is the Swiss flag reversed.

5886.q: What is it called when an adder sheds its old skin?
5886.e: Snakes grow and shed their old skin in one piece. This is called shedding.
5886.m: Snakes shed their skin, birds moult.

5887.q: Why does a stag roar so loudly during the rut?
a: To show its strength and attract females
5887.e: With loud roaring the stag shows how strong it is. This keeps other stags away and attracts females.
5887.m: Roaring shows strength during the rut.

5888.q: Why do many older cockerels have especially long spurs on their legs?
a: The spurs keep growing with age
The spurs get shorter over time
The spurs fall off every year
The spurs change colour every year
5888.e: A cockerel's spurs keep growing throughout its life. So older cockerels often have longer spurs than young ones.

5889.q: What separates the habitats of bonobos and chimpanzees?
5889.e: The great Congo River acts like a barrier. Bonobos live to the south of it, chimpanzees to the north.
5889.m: The Congo separates bonobos and chimpanzees.

5890.q: How does the grass snake take in its prey?
5890.e: Snakes have no chewing teeth. They swallow their prey whole, and their jaws stretch wide.

5891.q: How do goose eggs compare with hens' eggs?
5891.e: Geese are bigger animals than hens, so they lay bigger eggs too. One goose egg is enough for a big plate of scrambled egg.
5891.m: Goose eggs are bigger than hens' eggs.

5892.q: How do kangaroos move their back legs when hopping on land?
a: Both together at the same time
Always one after the other, as in walking
They do not move them at all
5892.e: On land, kangaroos jump with both back legs at the same time. In water, though, they can move their legs one at a time.
5892.m: When hopping, both legs move together.

5893.q: What camouflage helps the puma when hunting?
5893.e: The tawny colour matches rocks, grass and the forest floor. This way the puma stays unseen for a long time.

5894.q: What sound does a hedgehog sometimes make when it gets a fright?
5894.e: When a hedgehog is disturbed, it may snort or hiss quietly. Some hedgehogs also smack their lips and grunt while eating.
5894.m: Hedgehogs snort when they get a fright.

5895.q: What do you call an animal that eats almost nothing but meat?
5895.e: The jaguar is a carnivore, a meat eater. Plant eaters are called herbivores.

5896.q: When is the typical spawning season of the alpine newt?
a: Only in the depths of winter
5896.e: Depending on altitude, the alpine newt's spawning season starts in spring. Depending on the climate, it can last into early summer.
5896.m: Spawning is from spring to early summer.

5897.q: Which organisation in Switzerland monitors and protects water birds such as the great crested grebe?
a: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach
5897.e: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach researches and monitors the numbers of many bird species in Switzerland, including the great crested grebe. It provides important data for nature conservation.
5897.m: The institute in Sempach monitors many bird species.

5898.q: What is the name of the beautiful old castle with a large garden near Solothurn?
5898.e: Waldegg Castle stands on a hill near Feldbrunnen and was built long ago for a rich gentleman. Today you can visit the beautiful garden and the rooms.
5898.m: Waldegg Castle stands on a hill near Solothurn.

5899.q: What does a red squirrel like to eat most?
5899.e: Squirrels especially like nuts, seeds and acorns. But they also eat mushrooms and buds.

a: A question from members of parliament to the Federal Council, which it must answer
A law about Swiss living abroad
5900.e: With an interpellation, members of parliament can ask the government for information. The Federal Council must then answer these questions in writing.
5900.m: An interpellation asks the Federal Council for information.

5901.q: What is special about the upper lip of the Bactrian camel?
a: It is split and very mobile
It is horny like a beak
5901.e: The split upper lip helps it grab food such as thorny plants. It is very mobile.
5901.m: A split upper lip helps with eating.

5902.q: How does a jackal often move around when looking for food?
a: By jumping from tree to tree
5902.e: Jackals can cover long distances at a trot. This lets them roam large areas.
5902.m: Jackals trot tirelessly through their territory.

5903.q: What does ‘cumulating’ mean in an election?
a: Writing a name twice on the ballot paper
5903.e: When cumulating, you give a person twice the weight by writing their name twice. This way the person gets more votes.
5903.m: Cumulating doubles the vote for one person.

5904.q: How can you roughly tell the age of an Alpine ibex?
a: By the ridges (rings) on its horns
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its tail
By the number of its teeth alone
5904.e: Each year visible ridges form on the horns, much like the growth rings of a tree. Counting them lets you estimate the animal's age.

5905.q: What are the legs and feet of the barn swallow like compared with other birds?
a: Rather short and weak, not much good for walking
Very long and strong like a stork's
With sharp talons like an eagle's
5905.e: The barn swallow's legs and feet are rather short and weak. So they are not much good for walking on the ground, and the swallow prefers to perch on wires or branches.
5905.m: Short, weak legs, poor for walking.

5906.q: What colour is the fur on a badger's body usually?
5906.e: A badger's body is usually grey; only the face has the black and white markings. This camouflages it well in the woods.

5907.q: Which pattern typically decorates the adder's back?
5907.e: A dark zigzag band runs along its back. It is an important way to recognise the species.
5907.m: The zigzag band gives the adder away.

5908.q: What makes the wild dog a good long-distance runner?
5908.e: It can chase its prey over long distances. This tires out the prey animals.
5908.m: Wild dogs hunt with lots of stamina.

5909.q: How many cubs does a mother polar bear usually have?
5909.e: A mother polar bear normally has one or two cubs. That is rather few compared with other animals.
5909.m: She usually has one or two cubs.

5910.q: What colour are the pelvic and anal fins of the European perch usually?
5910.e: The fins on the underside are usually a striking red to orange. The back, on the other hand, is greenish to dark.
5910.m: The perch usually has red lower fins.

5911.q: When does the tawny owl call especially often to mark its territory?
a: Never, it does not call at all
5911.e: In autumn and winter, tawny owls defend their territory especially hard by calling, before the breeding season starts in spring. This is how they secure their hunting ground.
5911.m: The tawny owl calls a lot in autumn and winter.

5912.q: What are the young of a duck called?
5912.e: Little ducks are called ducklings. They can swim soon after hatching.

5913.q: Where does the name hippopotamus, meaning ‘river horse’, come from?
a: It lives in rivers and people compared it to a horse
It can run as fast as a horse
It eats the same food as horses
It neighs loudly like a horse
5913.e: The hippopotamus got its name because it spends a lot of time in rivers. Long ago people compared it to a horse.

5914.q: What special shape is the barn owl's face?
5914.e: The barn owl's face looks like a white heart. This shape helps it hear sounds better.
5914.m: The barn owl has a heart-shaped face.

5915.q: How does the ladybird survive the winter?
a: It goes into a winter rest in a sheltered hiding place
It builds a nest in the water
It stores up a supply of meat
5915.e: In autumn the ladybird looks for a sheltered spot, for example under bark or leaves. There it falls into a kind of winter sleep until it gets warmer.
5915.m: Winter rest protects it from the cold.

5916.q: What is the so-called ‘magic formula’ in Swiss politics?
a: A fixed sharing of Federal Council seats among the largest parties
The name of the Federal Constitution
5916.e: The magic formula describes how the seats on the Federal Council are traditionally shared among the largest parties.
5916.m: The magic formula shares out Federal Council seats.

5917.q: What do European pond turtles do in winter?
a: They rest in the mud at the bottom of the water
They climb trees and sleep there
They stay active and keep hunting
5917.e: When it is cold they slow their body processes right down. They survive the cold season in the water, often buried in the mud.
5917.m: They spend winter resting in the mud.

5918.q: How does a tapir usually behave when in danger?
a: It flees into thick undergrowth or into the water
5918.e: Tapirs are shy and usually flee into dense bushes or into the water. Their thick skin gives them extra protection.
5918.m: Tapirs flee into undergrowth or water.

5919.q: Roughly how many subspecies of tiger still exist today?
5919.e: Today there are still about six different subspecies of tiger. Each lives in a different part of Asia.
5919.m: There are about six tiger subspecies.

5920.q: Which bird cannot fly but is the biggest bird in the world?
5920.e: The ostrich lives in Africa and can run very fast, even though it cannot fly. It lays the biggest eggs of all birds.
5920.m: The ostrich runs instead of flying.

5921.q: Roughly how long does it take for a chick to hatch from a budgie egg?
5921.e: After about 18 days of incubation, a little budgie chick hatches from the egg. Before that the female keeps it warm.

5922.q: How does the fur of Alpine marmots change over the year?
a: It is replaced once a year
It falls out completely during hibernation
5922.e: Like many mammals, marmots change their fur once a year. In summer they get a new, thick coat for the cold months.
5922.m: New fur comes once a year.

5923.q: Which owl has striking ear tufts and orange eyes and is the largest owl in Europe?
5923.e: The eagle owl is easy to recognise by its ear tufts, orange eyes and size. The tawny owl and the little owl have no ear tufts.
5923.m: Ear tufts and orange eyes: that is the eagle owl.

5924.q: Do polar bears usually live alone or in large groups?
5924.e: Polar bears are loners and usually roam on their own. Only mothers with their cubs stay together longer.

5925.q: How does a llama usually react to strangers who approach quickly?
a: It is cautious and moves away
It always greets them at once
5925.e: Llamas are animals that flee and are shy of hasty movements. A calm manner helps to win their trust.

5926.q: How clever are chimpanzees compared with other animals?
a: They are among the cleverest animals in the world
They are the least clever animals
5926.e: Chimpanzees can think, solve problems and use tools. That is why they count as one of the cleverest animals of all.
5926.m: Chimpanzees are among the cleverest animals.

5927.q: Roughly how old can an edible frog get in the wild?
5927.e: In the wild, edible frogs usually reach an age of about five to ten years. Disease, enemies and traffic often shorten their lives.
5927.m: Edible frogs usually live several years.

5928.q: What does a giraffe do when it has swallowed leaves and is resting?
a: It brings the food back up and chews it again
It spits it onto the grass and leaves it
It feeds it to its calf
5928.e: Giraffes are ruminants. They bring their food back from the stomach into the mouth and chew it a second time, thoroughly.
5928.m: Giraffes chew their food a second time.

5929.q: What is an adult male horse called?
5929.e: An adult male horse is called a stallion. A female horse is called a mare.
5929.m: A male horse is called a stallion.

5930.q: What is the skin above a budgie's beak called?
5930.e: Above the beak, budgies have a small patch of skin called the cere. Its colour tells you whether the bird is male or female.
5930.m: The cere shows whether it is male or female.

5931.q: What do young Roman snails look like when they hatch from the egg?
5931.e: Young Roman snails hatch with a small shell already. They look like miniature versions of the adults.
5931.m: The young look like mini snails.

5932.q: Where is the asteroid belt in our solar system?
a: Between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter
Between the Earth and the moon
5932.e: The asteroid belt contains countless rocks of different sizes. It lies between the orbit of Mars and the orbit of Jupiter.
5932.m: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

5933.q: In which season are most roe deer fawns born?
5933.e: Most roe deer fawns are born in late spring, in May or June. Then there is plenty of fresh green food.
5933.m: Roe deer fawns are born in spring.

5934.q: Why are plastic rubbish and fishing nets dangerous for seals?
a: They can get tangled up in them
Seals like to eat plastic as a treat
It disturbs them when they sleep on land
5934.e: Seals can get tangled in discarded nets or bits of plastic and hurt themselves. That is why it is important to keep the sea clean.
5934.m: Rubbish in the sea endangers seals.

5935.q: How many tentacles can a jellyfish have, depending on the species?
a: Depending on the species, very many, sometimes over a hundred
5935.e: The number of tentacles varies greatly among jellyfish. Some species have only a few, others over a hundred fine threads.
5935.m: Jellyfish have different numbers of tentacles.

5936.q: Where does the chacma baboon live?
5936.e: The chacma baboon is found in South Africa, Namibia, Botswana and neighbouring countries. It is at home there in savannahs and mountains.
5936.m: Chacma baboons live in the south of Africa.

5937.q: Which big cat sometimes hunts Malayan tapirs in Asia?
5937.e: In Southeast Asia the tiger can prey on tapirs. The jaguar and the puma live in the Americas.
5937.m: In Asia the tiger is an enemy.

5938.q: How many finger-like tips does the African elephant's trunk have?
5938.e: At the tip of its trunk the African elephant has two small extensions. With them it can grab very small things, such as little fruits.
5938.m: The tip of the trunk has two fingers.

5939.q: Why does a sheep chew so often, even when it is not eating?
a: It is chewing its food again
It is playing with its teeth
5939.e: Sheep are ruminants. They bring their food back up and chew it a second time so they can digest it better.

5940.q: You see a brown trout. Which family of fish does it belong to?
5940.e: The brown trout belongs to the salmon family. Its relatives include the salmon and the rainbow trout.
5940.m: The brown trout is in the salmon family.

5941.q: Roughly how long does it take for a young fish to hatch from a brown trout egg?
5941.e: Depending on the water temperature, it takes several weeks to months for a little fish to hatch from the egg. In colder water it takes longer.
5941.m: Trout eggs take weeks to hatch.

5942.q: What is the slowest pace of a horse called?
5942.e: At a walk the horse moves very calmly, one leg after the other. It is the quietest way it moves.
5942.m: The walk is the slowest pace.

5943.q: What are young tawny owls called that have left the nest but cannot fly properly yet?
5943.e: Young tawny owls often leave the nest hole before they can fly and climb onto nearby branches using beak and claws. This stage is called the brancher stage.
5943.m: Young tawny owls are called branchers.

5944.q: What does a baboon show when it yawns with its mouth wide open?
a: It can show its canine teeth as a threat
5944.e: Yawning by males can be a threatening gesture. It shows off the large canine teeth.

5945.q: What does an orangutan mainly eat?
5945.e: Ripe fruit makes up most of its diet. It also eats leaves, bark and insects.

5946.q: Where do magpies usually build their nest?
a: In tall trees or thick bushes
5946.e: Magpies prefer to build their big nests in tall trees or dense shrubs, where they are safe from enemies. From there they also have a good view of the surroundings.
5946.m: Magpie nests sit high in trees.

5947.q: Why are whitefish seen as a sign of good water quality?
a: They need cool water rich in oxygen
They clean the water with chlorine
They live only in dirty water
5947.e: Where whitefish do well, the water is usually clean and rich in oxygen. Pollution can quickly drive them away.

5948.q: Which tiger has especially thick fur for cold winters?
5948.e: The Siberian tiger lives in the cold region of Russia and so has especially thick, warm fur. This helps it survive the icy winters.
5948.m: The Siberian tiger has thick fur.

5949.q: On which islands do wild orangutans live?
5949.e: Wild orangutans are found only on Borneo and Sumatra in Southeast Asia. There they live in tropical rainforests.
5949.m: Wild orangutans live only on Borneo and Sumatra.

5950.q: How is a baby bonobo usually carried at first?
a: The mother carries it on her body
It walks on its own straight away
The father carries it in his mouth
It is left behind in a nest
5950.e: Newborns cling to their mother's belly. Later they also ride on her back.
5950.m: Baby bonobos cling to their mother.

5951.q: Where does the Humboldt penguin live?
5951.e: The Humboldt penguin lives on the coasts of Chile and Peru in South America. Cold sea water full of fish flows there.
5951.m: The Humboldt penguin lives in South America.

5952.q: Why can a Roman snail crawl over a sharp razor blade without getting hurt?
a: It has hard skin like leather
5952.e: The snail's sticky slime lays a protective layer over the ground. This lets it glide over rough or sharp spots without getting hurt.

5953.q: Why does a mosquito bite usually itch?
5953.e: When it bites, the mosquito puts a little saliva into the skin so the blood does not clot. This saliva irritates the skin and causes the itching.
5953.m: Mosquito saliva makes the skin itch.

5954.q: How do males and females differ in many baboon species?
a: Males are much bigger and heavier
5954.e: In baboons there is a clear difference between the sexes. Males are often almost twice as heavy as females.

5955.q: How does the call of the common raven usually differ from that of the carrion crow?
a: It sounds much higher and squeakier
The raven never makes a sound
Both calls are exactly the same
5955.e: The call of the larger raven usually sounds deeper and fuller than the hoarse caw of the carrion crow. With a little practice you can tell the two species apart by ear.
5955.m: The raven calls deeper than the carrion crow.

5956.q: What is one difference between a leopard and a jaguar?
a: The jaguar is more powerfully built
The leopard lives in South America
5956.e: The jaguar looks bulkier and has a bigger head. It also lives in America, while the leopard lives in Africa and Asia.
5956.m: The jaguar is stockier, the leopard slimmer.

5957.q: Roughly how much does a typical gibbon weigh?
5957.e: Most gibbons are light; the large siamang reaches about 10 to 14 kilograms. Being lightweight helps with swinging.

5958.q: What protects a giraffe's eyes from dust and sun?
5958.e: Giraffes have very long eyelashes that protect their eyes from dust, thorns and bright sunlight. This helps them see well even in the wind.
5958.m: Long eyelashes protect a giraffe's eyes.

5959.q: Why does a cat's tongue feel so rough?
a: Because it has tiny hooks for grooming
Because it has lots of teeth
5959.e: A cat's tongue is covered with tiny hard hooks. It uses them to comb its fur like a brush.
5959.m: The rough tongue works as a fur brush.

5960.q: Why does the female European pond turtle choose a sunny spot for her eggs?
a: The warmth is important for the young developing inside
So that the eggs dry out faster
So that enemies can see the eggs better
So that the eggs never get wet
5960.e: The eggs are not sat on; they are warmed by the sun and the ground. If it is too cool, the young develop poorly.

5961.q: How did Enver Hoxha rule Albania during the Cold War?
a: As an isolated, very strict Stalinist dictatorship
As an open market economy on the Western model
5961.e: Enver Hoxha ruled Albania with an iron fist from 1944 to 1985 and cut the country off almost completely from the rest of the world. He even broke with the Soviet Union and China.
5961.m: Hoxha cut Albania off under a strict dictatorship.

5962.q: Why are there so many different kinds of whitefish in Swiss lakes?
a: They have adapted to different habitats in the lake
They were brought from the sea
Each river brings a new species
5962.e: Many whitefish species developed from a few ancestors. Some live deep down, others near the surface, and they eat different food.
5962.m: Whitefish adapted to different habitats in the lakes.

5963.q: What does the grey heron mainly eat?
5963.e: The grey heron is a versatile hunter. Besides fish, it also eats amphibians, small mammals and insects.

5964.q: How long is a female elephant pregnant before the calf is born?
5964.e: Elephants have the longest pregnancy of all mammals. The calf takes almost two years before it is born.
5964.m: Elephant calves take a very long time to be born.

5965.q: What is the legal status of the wolf in Switzerland?
5965.e: In Switzerland the wolf is protected, but under certain conditions its numbers may be controlled. These rules are set out in the Hunting Act.
5965.m: The wolf is protected in Switzerland.

5966.q: How do mute swans get going before they take off into the air?
5966.e: Because swans are so heavy, they first have to run across the water to gain enough speed. Then they slowly lift off.
5966.m: Swans run across the water to take off.

5967.q: How does an eagle owl usually fly when hunting, so its prey cannot hear it?
5967.e: The soft edges of the eagle owl's flight feathers mean it makes hardly any noise in flight. This lets it approach its prey unnoticed.
5967.m: Soft feathers let the eagle owl fly almost silently.

5968.q: Which birds are among the peregrine falcon's favourite prey in cities?
5968.e: In cities the peregrine falcon mainly hunts feral pigeons, which live there in large numbers. It usually strikes them in flight.
5968.m: Pigeons are popular prey in cities.

5969.q: Which rhino has folds of skin that look like armour?
5969.e: The Indian rhinoceros has large, thick folds of skin that look like a suit of metal armour. In German it is even called the ‘armoured rhino’.

5970.q: What does a domestic pig's tail usually look like?
a: Long and bushy like a fox's
There is no tail at all
5970.e: The typical curly tail is a well-known feature of many domestic pigs. Wild boar, on the other hand, tend to have a straighter tail.
5970.m: Domestic pigs often have a curly tail.

5971.q: Which fable tells of a cunning fox who tricks a crow out of its piece of cheese?
5971.e: In the famous fable, the fox flatters the crow so that it starts to sing and drops the cheese. This story shows the fox as especially clever and cunning.
5971.m: In the fable the fox outwits the crow.

5972.q: Where is the stone marten found in Switzerland?
a: All over the country, from the lowlands to the mountains
Only in high mountain areas above 3,000 metres
Nowhere, it does not live in Switzerland
5972.e: The stone marten is found all over Switzerland, both in the lowlands and higher up. It is especially common near villages.
5972.m: Stone martens live all over Switzerland.

5973.q: In which habitats does the golden eagle feel most at home?
a: In open mountain landscapes with rocks
5973.e: Golden eagles prefer open, rocky mountain landscapes where they can hunt and nest well. They usually avoid dense forests because they cannot see far enough there.
5973.m: Open mountain landscapes are its habitat.

5974.q: What is one difference between a housefly and a bee?
a: The fly has only one pair of wings, the bee has two
The fly lives in a beehive
5974.e: Bees have two pairs of wings, whereas houseflies have only one. Also, flies do not collect nectar or make honey.
5974.m: Flies have fewer wings than bees.

5975.q: What is a baby ladybird called before it becomes a fully grown beetle?
5975.e: A small larva hatches from the egg first, looking like a tiny crocodile. Only later does it turn into a beetle.

5976.q: Which body part does the lynx use to find its way better in the dark?
5976.e: The whiskers on its face give the lynx important information about its surroundings. They help it sense obstacles even in the dark.

5977.q: What are newborn red squirrels like when they are born?
a: Already with thick fur and able to see
5977.e: Young squirrels are born without fur and with their eyes closed. They need their mother to survive.

5978.q: What do red foxes do to mark their territory?
a: They mark it with scents such as urine
They lay stones in a circle
5978.e: Foxes mark their territory with urine and scent glands so that other foxes notice the area is taken. This often helps them avoid a direct fight.
5978.m: Foxes mark their territory with scent.

5979.q: What shape is our galaxy, the Milky Way?
a: A flat disc with no structure
5979.e: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy with several arms winding round a centre. Our solar system is in one of these arms.
5979.m: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.

5980.q: What is the longest a harbour seal can stay underwater?
5980.e: Seals can hold their breath for a long time and often dive for several minutes. On especially long dives they manage up to 30 minutes.
5980.m: Seals dive for a surprisingly long time.

5981.q: How many arms does an octopus have?
5981.e: An octopus has eight arms that it uses to swim, feel and catch prey. Each arm is very flexible and strong.

5982.q: What does the skin of the Alpine salamander normally feel like?
5982.e: Amphibian skin is typically smooth and moist, and so is the Alpine salamander's. This clearly sets it apart from scaly reptiles.
5982.m: Its skin is smooth and moist.

5983.q: Which season is the main breeding season for the great tit?
5983.e: The great tit's main breeding season begins in spring. Then there are lots of insects to feed the young.
5983.m: The great tit breeds in spring.

5984.q: What is root pressure in plants?
a: The pressure that pushes water up from the root
The pressure roots exert on stones
The air pressure in the soil
The pressure of rainwater on roots
5984.e: Active uptake of minerals in the root creates osmotic pressure. This pushes water a little way up into the plant’s vessels.
5984.m: Root pressure helps move water upwards in the plant.

5985.q: What do rabbits absolutely need for healthy teeth?
5985.e: Hay is the most important food for rabbits. Chewing it wears down their teeth and keeps them healthy.

5986.q: Which habitat suits the pine marten best?
a: Flat sandy beaches by the sea
5986.e: The pine marten is a good climber and prefers forests with old trees, where it finds tree holes to shelter in. It moves much more skilfully there than on the ground.

5987.q: How many thumbs does a koala have on each front paw?
5987.e: Koalas have two thumbs on each front paw that can press against the other fingers. This helps them grip branches especially well.
5987.m: Koalas have two thumbs per paw.

5988.q: What is the layer called that protects the Earth from dangerous UV radiation?
5988.e: The ozone layer is high up in the atmosphere and filters out a large part of the sun’s harmful UV radiation. Without it, life on Earth would be much harder.
5988.m: The ozone layer protects against UV radiation.

5989.q: What colour are a robin's legs?
5989.e: The robin's legs are thin and brownish. They go well with the rest of its plumage.
5989.m: The legs are thin and brownish.

5990.q: In some jackals, who helps the parents raise the pups?
5990.e: Young jackals from the year before sometimes stay with their parents. They help look after the new pups.
5990.m: Older siblings help raise the young.

5992.q: What colour is an adult chimpanzee's fur usually?
5992.e: Most adult chimpanzees have black fur. Only their face is often almost hairless.

5993.q: How fast can a harbour seal swim in the water?
5993.e: In the water the seal is much faster and more agile than on land. With its strong flippers it reaches up to 35 kilometres per hour.
5993.m: In the water the seal is lightning fast.

5994.q: Which animal is often mistaken for the harbour seal but has a longer snout?
5994.e: The grey seal looks similar to the harbour seal but has a longer snout and is usually bigger. Both belong to the seals.
5994.m: Grey seals have a longer snout.

5995.q: Where is the European perch naturally found?
a: In Africa south of the Sahara
5995.e: The perch's original range stretches across Europe into northern Asia. People have introduced it to other continents.
5995.m: The perch is native to Europe and northern Asia.

5996.q: How can you tell adult praying mantises apart from young ones?
a: They no longer have grasping arms
5996.e: Young ones have only wing buds. The wings are only complete after the last moult.

5997.q: Why is the carrion crow's varied diet seen as a survival advantage?
a: It finds something to eat almost anywhere and depends less on the seasons
It means it no longer needs any food
It automatically makes it bigger than other birds
It means it can never get ill
5997.e: Because carrion crows are omnivores, they find some kind of food in almost every season, whether carrion, insects or plant remains. This makes them very adaptable and successful.
5997.m: Crows eat everything and always find food.

5998.q: Which disease was defeated in Switzerland with vaccine baits for foxes?
5998.e: From 1978, vaccine baits for foxes were put out in Switzerland. Rabies disappeared, and since 1999 Switzerland has been considered rabies-free.
5998.m: Vaccine baits stopped rabies in foxes.

a: Yes, it swims well and likes to
No, brown bears avoid water completely
5999.e: Brown bears swim well and use this skill, for example, when fishing in rivers. Some bears even cover quite long distances while bathing.

6000.q: Where does the cuckoo fly when autumn comes to Switzerland?
6000.e: The cuckoo is a migratory bird and spends the winter in warm Africa south of the Sahara. In spring it comes back to Switzerland.
6000.m: The cuckoo spends winter in Africa.

6001.q: What is the hollow called where bison roll around?
6001.e: A wallow is a hollow for rolling in, in dust or mud. Wild boar use wallows too.
6001.m: A wallow is a hollow for rolling in.

6002.q: Roughly how many teeth does a rabbit have?
6002.e: An adult rabbit has about 28 teeth. With them it can grind up tough grass and hay well.

6003.q: Why are trees and bushes along a stream good for trout?
a: They give shade and keep the water cool
They provide fruit for the trout to eat
They hold back water so the stream dries up
6003.e: Shade stops the water from warming up too much. The roots also provide hiding places.
6003.m: Trees on the bank keep streams cool.

6004.q: What colour is the kingfisher's back mainly?
6004.e: The kingfisher's back shimmers an intense blue to turquoise. This blue makes it one of the most striking birds by our rivers and lakes.
6004.m: The kingfisher's back shines bright blue.

6005.q: What is it called when a cow eats grass straight from the pasture?
6005.e: When a cow eats grass outside in the field, it is called grazing. It moves slowly across the pasture as it does so.

6006.q: What are the teeth called that an elephant uses to grind plants?
6006.e: With its large molars the elephant grinds tough grass and branches. These teeth are very important for eating every day.

6007.q: What does a caterpillar often do right after hatching from its egg?
a: It often eats its own eggshell first
It turns into a pupa at once
It sleeps for a whole week
6007.e: The empty eggshell still contains valuable nutrients. That is why many caterpillars eat it as their first meal.
6007.m: Caterpillars often eat the eggshell first.

6008.q: Apart from hibernation, which time of day does the edible dormouse mainly spend asleep?
6008.e: On top of its long hibernation, the edible dormouse also sleeps in its hiding place during the day. It only becomes active when it gets dark.
6008.m: It sleeps by day and is active at night.

6009.q: In the photo a leopard is lying on a branch. What does it often do with its prey in the tree?
a: It hides it and eats it there
It throws it into the water
6009.e: Leopards are strong climbers and drag their prey up trees. This protects it from lions and hyenas.
6009.m: Leopards take their prey up trees.

6010.q: What does a fox sometimes do instead of digging its own den?
a: It takes over a badger's abandoned sett
It builds a nest high up in a tree
It moves into an empty birdhouse
It always lives in the water
6010.e: Foxes do sometimes dig for themselves, but they also like to use abandoned badger setts. This saves them a lot of work building a shelter.
6010.m: Foxes also use old badger setts.

6011.q: Why is it important that all adults are allowed to have a say?
a: So that decisions are fair for everyone
So that there are more holidays
So that nobody has to work
So that everyone looks the same
6011.e: When many people are allowed to help decide, decisions become fairer. Every vote counts the same.

6012.q: What happens when an alpine newt in its water phase finds a pond with lots of fish?
a: It tends to avoid such waters, because fish eat eggs and larvae
It makes friends with the fish
It turns into a fish itself
Fish are completely harmless to it
6012.e: Fish are among the greatest enemies of newt eggs and larvae. That is why small ponds without fish are especially valuable for alpine newts to breed in.
6012.m: Ponds without fish are safer for alpine newts.

6013.q: Which large group of animals does the Roman snail belong to?
6013.e: The Roman snail belongs to the group of molluscs. It has no bones and no hard skeleton inside.

6014.q: Which fish family does the lake trout belong to?
6014.e: The lake trout belongs to the salmon family, just like salmon and brown trout. One way to recognise this family is the adipose fin.
6014.m: Lake trout belong to the salmon family.

6015.q: What is the stoat's white winter coat useful for?
a: To scare enemies with bright colours
6015.e: The white coat in winter helps the stoat blend in with the snow. This makes it harder for prey and enemies to spot.

6016.q: Which teeth are important for the way the least weasel hunts?
a: Sharp canines for a precise killing bite
It has no teeth at all
Only grinding teeth like plant eaters
6016.e: With its pointed canines, the least weasel usually kills its prey with a precise bite to the neck. This is typical for predators of its size.
6016.m: Sharp canines for the killing bite.

6017.q: What does a female mosquito really need to be able to lay eggs?
6017.e: Only with the protein from blood can the eggs develop properly inside the female's body. That is why she bites people and animals.

6018.e: The male does not look after the young. The mother feeds them milk, protects them and teaches them to hunt.
6018.m: The puma mother raises the young alone.

6019.q: Eawag is a Swiss research institute. What does it mainly study?
6019.e: Eawag is the water research institute of the ETH Domain. It studies, for example, water quality and the fish in Swiss lakes.
6019.m: Eawag studies lakes and their fish.

6021.q: What shows that orangutans have a good memory?
a: They remember fruit trees in the forest
6021.e: Researchers have seen them return to particular trees on purpose. This helps them find food in a large area.

6022.q: In most martens, who raises the young?
6022.e: In most marten species the female raises the young alone, without help from the male. She feeds them milk and protects them in the den.
6022.m: Female martens usually raise their young alone.

a: Signals are passed from one nerve cell to the next
6023.e: At the synapse, a nerve cell uses messenger substances to pass a signal to the next cell. This is how communication in the nervous system works.

6024.q: What happens when an enemy takes a common toad in its mouth?
a: It releases a bitter poison from its skin
6024.e: The common toad protects itself with a bitter skin poison. Many enemies then prefer to leave it alone.

6025.q: What makes a badger look very different from a fox?
a: The badger is stockier and has a black and white striped face
The badger has a bushier red tail
The badger is much bigger than a horse
The badger has wings like a bird
6025.e: While the fox is slim and reddish brown, the badger looks stockier and grey. Its striped face is also unmistakable.
6025.m: Face and build tell a badger from a fox.

6026.q: What is the basic difference between nuclear fusion and nuclear fission?
a: In fusion light nuclei merge, in fission a heavy nucleus splits
Fusion only happens on Earth, fission only in space
6026.e: In nuclear fusion, hydrogen nuclei, for example, merge into helium, as in the Sun. In nuclear fission, a heavy nucleus such as uranium is split into smaller parts, as in nuclear power stations.
6026.m: Fusion merges atomic nuclei, fission splits them.

6027.q: What does a pig use its flexible snout for?
a: To root in the ground for food
6027.e: With their sensitive snout, pigs dig in the ground for roots, worms and other treats. The snout is full of nerves and very sensitive.
6027.m: The pig uses its snout for rooting.

6028.q: What is typical of the common buzzard's plumage?
a: Its colour varies a lot, from light to dark
It is exactly the same colour in every bird
6028.e: Common buzzards show a great variety of colours, from almost white birds to very dark brown ones. These colour variations are called colour morphs.

6029.q: Which large predator was wiped out in Switzerland for a long time and has occasionally wandered back in from Italy in recent years?
6029.e: The brown bear was wiped out in Switzerland for a long time. In 2005, for the first time in almost a hundred years, a bear came from Italy into the Engadine.

6030.q: Why do ibex prefer to move around on very steep, rocky ground?
a: Because they are safe from many enemies there
Because that is where most food grows
Because they can run fastest there
6030.e: On steep rocky ground, ibex can climb where most larger predators cannot follow. This protects them from lynx and wolves.

6031.q: How does a male stag beetle find a female?
a: By scent and by searching flights
6031.e: Females attract the males with scent. The males then fly around in the evening.

6032.q: How does the grass snake protect its body from drying out?
a: With its skin of horny scales
With a layer of slime like a frog
By always staying in the water
6032.e: The grass snake is a reptile. Its dry skin of horny scales stops it from drying out. Frogs, by contrast, have moist skin.
6032.m: Horny scales protect against drying out.

6033.q: What do two stags often do when they fight in autumn?
a: They kick each other with their back legs
6033.e: In a fight, stags lock their antlers together. Then they push and shove against each other.

6034.q: How many fawns does a roe deer doe usually have?
6034.e: A roe deer doe usually has one or two fawns at a time. Sometimes there are three.
6034.m: Roe deer usually have one or two fawns.

6035.q: Who looks after the little larvae in an ants' nest?
6035.e: Some workers have the job of feeding and caring for the larvae. This way they grow up safely.

6036.q: Which small relative of the great tit often comes to the bird feeder with it?
6036.e: The blue tit is smaller and has a blue cap. You often see it at the bird feeder together with great tits.
6036.m: Blue tits and great tits are often together.

6037.q: What are young Alpine marmots like when they are born?
a: With full fur and open eyes
Already as big as their parents
6037.e: Newborn marmots are tiny, naked and cannot see yet. Only after a few weeks do they open their eyes and grow fur.

6038.q: How does a housefly maggot move, even though it has no legs?
a: It wriggles and squeezes its body together
6038.e: A maggot has no legs, but it can move by squeezing and stretching its body. That is how it slowly crawls forwards.

6039.q: What is a young wild boar called?
6039.e: Young wild boar are called piglets. They have a striped coat.
6039.m: A baby wild boar is a piglet.

6040.q: How many eggs does a white stork usually lay?
6040.e: A mother stork usually lays three to five eggs in her nest. The young storks hatch from them.
6040.m: A white stork usually lays three to five eggs.

6041.q: Why does the eel turn silvery before its migration?
a: It is getting ready for life in the sea
6041.e: In the silver eel, the eyes, skin and body change for life in the sea. It also stops eating.
6041.m: Silver eels get ready for the sea.

6042.q: Who mainly builds the nest in mute swans?
6042.e: Both parents help to build the nest. The male often brings reeds and twigs.
6042.m: Both parents build the nest together.

6043.q: Where does a female ladybird usually lay her eggs?
6043.e: The mother looks for leaves with lots of aphids on them. That way the larvae have plenty to eat as soon as they hatch.

6044.q: Which trees does the great spotted woodpecker prefer for its nest hole?
6044.e: Rotten wood is much easier to chip out than hard, fresh wood. That is why it picks old trees.
6044.m: Old trees are softer for pecking.

6045.q: Why does the European pond turtle have webbed feet with claws?
6045.e: The webbing helps it move forwards in the water. With its claws it climbs onto logs and digs.

6046.q: From what kind of lookout does the common buzzard typically watch its surroundings?
a: From fence posts, branches or electricity pylons
Only from the bottom of a river
Only from the air above the sea
6046.e: Common buzzards like to sit up high on fence posts, pylons or branches to scan the area for prey. From there they can launch an attack quickly.
6046.m: Raised lookouts are used for hunting.

6047.q: When does the common raven's breeding season usually begin?
a: Early in the year, often in February
In midwinter, fully out in the freezing cold
6047.e: Ravens breed comparatively early, often before winter is completely over. This gives the young time to become independent.
6047.m: The breeding season starts as early as February.

6048.q: Which animals do some birds rub on their feathers to protect themselves against parasites?
6048.e: Some monkeys and birds rub themselves with millipedes. Their defensive chemicals can keep insects away.

6049.q: Which threat is especially hard on the common wall lizard in Switzerland?
a: The loss of natural, stony habitats
6049.e: When dry stone walls and banks disappear, the wall lizard loses important habitats. This makes survival hard for it.
6049.m: Losing walls puts it at risk.

6050.q: In some Asian countries, jellyfish are also eaten as food. Is that true?
a: No, jellyfish must never be eaten
6050.e: In countries such as China or Japan, certain kinds of jellyfish are eaten. They are specially prepared for this.

6051.q: How do adult roe bucks usually live in summer?
a: Each defends its own area alone
They always stay with their mother
6051.e: In summer each roe buck usually keeps to itself and guards its own area. Other bucks are driven away.
6051.m: Roe bucks have their own area in summer.

6052.q: What is the female of the cockerel called?
6052.e: A cockerel is the male chicken and the hen is the female. Together they form a flock of chickens.
6052.m: The hen is the cockerel's partner.

6053.q: How many stomach chambers does a giraffe have, just like cows?
6053.e: Giraffes are ruminants, just like cows. They have four stomach chambers so they can digest their food well.

6055.q: Roughly how many years can a common frog live in the wild?
6055.e: In the wild, common frogs can live several years, some even up to about 8 years. But many are eaten by enemies before they get that old.
6055.m: Common frogs can live several years.

6056.q: What is the Federal Constitution, explained very simply?
6056.e: The Federal Constitution contains the most important rules about how Switzerland is organised. It can only be changed by the people.
6056.m: The constitution is the most important rule book.

6057.q: What role does the wolf play as a predator in the ecosystem?
a: It keeps the numbers of hoofed animals such as deer in balance
It has no effect at all on other animals
It only creates more forest by eating trees
All other animals avoid it, so it does not matter
6057.e: As a top predator, the wolf mainly hunts weak or sick hoofed animals and so helps keep populations healthy. Its mere presence also changes how other animals in the forest behave.
6057.m: The wolf keeps hoofed animal numbers in balance.

6058.q: Why does the slow worm often stay under stones or boards in summer?
a: It is warm, damp and sheltered there
It builds nests for birds there
6058.e: Under flat objects the ground warms up and stays damp. It is also safe from enemies there.
6058.m: Under stones it finds warmth and shelter.

6059.q: What happens if a hamster does not get enough to gnaw on?
a: Its teeth can grow too long
6059.e: Without enough to gnaw, a hamster's teeth can grow too long. This can then cause it pain.
6059.m: Without gnawing, teeth grow too long.

6060.q: Roughly when does the kestrel's breeding season begin in central Europe?
a: Only in high summer in August
6060.e: Kestrels usually start breeding in April. This lets the young grow up in summer, when there is enough food.
6060.m: The breeding season starts in spring.

6061.q: Does a hippopotamus have sweat glands like a human?
a: No, it has no normal sweat glands
Yes, but only on its back
6061.e: Hippos do not sweat the way we humans do. Instead, their skin gives off the well-known reddish liquid.

6062.q: What is the protein in red blood cells that picks up and carries oxygen called?
6062.e: Haemoglobin contains iron and picks up oxygen in the lungs. It also gives blood its red colour.

6063.q: What is typical of the underside of a common frog?
a: It is often paler, sometimes yellowish or whitish
6063.e: While the common frog's back is usually brown, its belly is often paler, sometimes yellowish or whitish. Sometimes it also has dark spots.

6064.q: Why are leaves under a colony of aphids often sticky?
a: The aphids give off sugary honeydew
The plant sweats resin out of fear
The aphids put down glue as traps
6064.e: Aphids suck lots of sugary plant sap and get rid of the excess as honeydew. This drips onto the leaves below and makes them sticky.

6066.q: How does the grey heron's beak colour often change in the courtship season?
a: It turns a more intense orange to reddish
6066.e: During the courtship season the beak takes on a stronger orange to reddish colour. This shows the bird is ready to pair up.
6066.m: In the courtship season its beak glows brighter.

6067.q: Why is the kingfisher probably called ‘Eisvogel’ (ice bird) in German?
a: Probably from ‘Eisenvogel’ (iron bird), because of its metallic plumage
Because it only lives on ice
Because it can only be seen in winter
Because its song sounds like breaking ice
6067.e: The name probably comes from the old word ‘Eisenvogel’ (iron bird), because its plumage has a metallic shine. So the name actually has nothing to do with real ice.

6068.q: What role do aphids play in making forest honey?
a: They provide the honeydew that bees collect
6068.e: Bees collect honeydew from aphids on trees such as firs and spruces. This becomes the dark forest honey.
6068.m: Aphids provide the raw material for forest honey.

6069.q: Which language, besides English, is often also spoken at many international conferences?
6069.e: Besides English, French is one of the most important languages at international meetings, partly because Geneva is a French-speaking city. The UN has six official languages in total.
6069.m: French is often an important conference language.

6070.q: What shape is the salmon's body?
6070.e: The streamlined shape helps it swim fast. This lets it make headway even against the current.

6071.q: Which butterfly flies especially far on its migration?
6071.e: The painted lady covers thousands of kilometres on its migrations, sometimes from Africa to Switzerland. This is one of the longest journeys made by any insect.
6071.m: The painted lady travels very far.

6072.q: What role does the common raven often play alongside wolves?
a: It follows wolf packs and eats leftovers from their prey
It hunts large prey together with wolves
6072.e: Ravens sometimes follow wolf packs to get leftovers after a successful hunt. That is why some people call it the wolf bird.

6073.q: What does a beaver mainly eat?
6073.e: The beaver is a pure plant eater and feeds on bark, leaves, twigs and water plants. In winter it mainly eats the bark of trees such as willows and poplars.

6074.q: What colour is the fluffy down of a newly hatched gosling usually?
6074.e: Little goslings are covered with soft, yellowish grey down. Only later do they grow the firmer feathers of an adult goose.
6074.m: Goslings first have yellowish grey down.

6075.q: What do you call a group of elephants made up of cows and their young?
6075.e: Elephant herds are made up of related females and their young. Usually an experienced older cow leads the herd.
6075.m: An experienced matriarch leads the herd.

6076.q: What do bumblebees do to pollinate flowers such as tomato flowers?
a: They shake the flower so the pollen falls out
They simply wait for the wind
6076.e: Some flowers only release their pollen when they are shaken hard. Bumblebees can do this with their flight muscles; it is called buzz pollination.
6076.m: Bumblebees shake pollen loose from flowers.

6077.q: What colour is the cere of an adult female budgie usually?
6077.e: In female budgies the cere is usually brown or brownish. This is how you can tell males and females apart.
6077.m: Females often have a brown cere.

6078.q: Where does the common swift prefer to build its nest?
a: In cracks in walls and in nooks on tall buildings
6078.e: Swifts nest in cracks in house walls, in towers or under roofs. Such nesting places are becoming rarer and rarer.
6078.m: Swifts breed in cracks in buildings.

6079.q: In which fairy tale does a wolf try to eat seven young goats?
a: The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids
6079.e: In this Grimm fairy tale the wolf sneaks up to the kids several times until he eats almost all of them. In the end the mother goat saves her children with a clever trick.
6079.m: In the fairy tale a wolf hunts seven kids.

6080.q: Who began a period of ‘de-Stalinisation’ after Stalin’s death?
6080.e: In 1956 Nikita Khrushchev criticised Stalin’s crimes in a famous speech. After that, some rules in the Soviet Union were relaxed a little.

6081.q: What is mainly stored in a dromedary's hump?
6081.e: The hump holds a store of fat that the animal can live on when food is scarce. When the animal is hungry, the hump goes floppier.
6081.m: The hump stores fat, not water.

6082.q: What is at the very start of the food chain that the blue whale lives on?
6082.e: Tiny plankton is eaten by krill, and the krill in turn by the blue whale. So the biggest giant depends on the smallest living things.
6082.m: Big whales need tiny living things.

6083.q: What does a kangaroo like to eat most?
6083.e: Kangaroos are plant eaters. They mainly eat grass, herbs and leaves.

6084.q: What is the part of the cow called that the milk comes from?
6084.e: The cow's milk comes from the udder, which hangs under her belly. Calves drink their milk straight from it.

6086.q: What is it called when a grasshopper sheds its old skin?
6086.e: When moulting, the grasshopper sheds its skin that has become too small. Underneath, a new, bigger skin appears.

6087.q: What is special about the way woodlice moult?
a: The shell is shed in two halves
They moult only once in their life
The skin is eaten and never shed
6087.e: First the back half of the body comes loose, then the front half. You can see this clearly in woodlice.

6088.q: What does a white stork like to eat most?
6088.e: Storks are skilful hunters and mainly eat frogs, mice and insects. They look for prey in meadows and wetlands.

6089.q: Why is releasing pet terrapins into ponds a bad idea?
a: They can push out native species and spread diseases
They build dams that are too big
They pollute the water with oil
They drive away all the birds
6089.e: Foreign species compete for food and sunbathing spots. They can also bring in germs that cause disease.

a: The loss of natural gardens, and traffic
Too many insects in the garden
Water in ponds that is too cold
6090.e: Tidy gardens without hiding places and heavy traffic make it hard for hedgehogs to survive today. Hedgehog-friendly gardens with hedges and leaves help them a lot.
6090.m: Tidy gardens and traffic endanger hedgehogs.

6091.q: Which land animal is one of the heaviest in the world after the elephant?
6091.e: After the elephant, the white rhinoceros is one of the heaviest land animals on Earth. It can weigh more than two tonnes.
6091.m: Rhinos are huge, heavy land animals.

6092.q: Who usually leads a group of wild boar?
6092.e: The group is usually led by a clever, experienced sow. She knows her way around the forest well.
6092.m: A lead sow leads the group.

6093.q: How high can a cat jump compared with its body length?
a: Several times its own body length
Hardly more than a few centimetres
Only as high as its paw
Not at all, cats cannot jump
6093.e: Thanks to strong back legs, a cat can jump several times its own body length from a standing start. This helps it climb onto furniture or trees, for example.
6093.m: Cats jump several times their body length.

6094.q: Which animals are among a tiger's most important prey?
6094.e: Tigers mainly hunt large plant eaters such as deer and wild boar. These animals live in the same forests as the tiger.
6094.m: Tigers hunt deer and wild boar.

6095.q: What does a cow do when it rests?
a: It lies down and chews the cud
6095.e: Cows often lie down to rest and chew their cud at the same time. They do this several times a day.

6096.q: Why can a standing horse fall asleep without falling over?
a: Its legs can lock at the joints
It has suction cups on its hooves
It is stuck to the ground
It holds on with its tail
6096.e: Horses have a special mechanism in their legs that can lock the joints. This lets them rest standing up without falling over.
6096.m: Horses' legs can lock while standing.

6097.q: What do tapirs like doing in the water?
6097.e: Tapirs swim well and even dive. In the water they cool down and can escape enemies.

6098.q: Roughly when does the sand lizard's winter rest begin?
a: Never, it is active all year
6098.e: As soon as temperatures drop, the lizard looks for a safe winter shelter. Only in spring, when it gets warmer again, does it become active again.
6098.m: From autumn it withdraws for its winter rest.

6099.q: Roughly how heavy can a fully grown cow get?
6099.e: A fully grown cow often weighs several hundred kilograms, more for some breeds. That makes it much heavier than a person.

6100.q: What is the flesh of the European perch like?
a: Firm, white and delicate in taste
6100.e: Perch have firm, white flesh that is considered a delicacy. The fillets have only a few bones.

6101.q: How long can the biggest seahorse grow?
a: About as long as a ruler
Only as long as a fingernail
6101.e: The biggest seahorses can grow up to about 35 centimetres long. That is about as long as a school ruler.
6101.m: Large species grow up to 35 cm long.

6103.q: What role does the sense of smell play for martens when looking for food?
a: It is very important for detecting prey and territory borders
It plays no role at all
Martens only use their eyes, never their nose
6103.e: Martens rely heavily on their good sense of smell to track down prey and recognise other martens' scent marks. This also helps them find their way reliably at night.
6103.m: Martens smell prey and territory borders.

6104.q: What does an octopus's skin colour often show when it is stressed?
a: It glows blue like the night
6104.e: When an octopus feels threatened or stressed, its skin can turn darker or reddish. This is a sign of its mood.
6104.m: Stress shows in the skin colour.

6105.q: Why is a pike so good at surprising its prey?
a: Because its camouflage makes it almost invisible
Because it calls out loudly before it snaps
Because it always raises the alarm first
6105.e: Thanks to its green and yellow camouflage colours, the pike almost blends in with the water plants. So its prey often notices it too late.
6105.m: Camouflage makes the pike a surprise hunter.

6106.q: How long does an adder usually grow?
6106.e: It is a fairly small, sturdy snake. Females usually grow a little longer than males.
6106.m: Adders are usually under one metre.

6107.q: The scientific name of the Alpine marmot is Marmota marmota. What does the word Marmota refer to?
6107.e: Marmota is the scientific genus name for all marmot species worldwide. The Alpine marmot's full species name is Marmota marmota.
6107.m: Marmota is the name of the genus.

a: An underground system of tunnels with several chambers
A nest high up in a tree
A floating nest on a pond
A hole the badger never digs itself
6108.e: A badger sett is a complex system of tunnels and chambers underground. Such setts can be used and extended over many generations.

6109.q: What does the barn owl cough up after eating?
a: A pellet of bones and fur
6109.e: The barn owl cannot digest bones and fur. It brings them back up as a small package called a pellet.

6110.q: Which amphibian family does the common frog belong to?
6110.e: The common frog belongs to the true frog family. This family includes many different frog species all over the world.
6110.m: The common frog is one of the true frogs.

6111.q: Which animals are among the predators of many millipedes?
6111.e: Ground-dwelling animals such as hedgehogs, toads and blackbirds eat them. Some species, though, are protected by poisons.
6111.m: Hedgehogs and toads like eating them.

6112.q: What does a torch need to shine?
6112.e: The battery supplies the electricity that makes the small bulb or LED light up. Without electricity the torch stays dark.
6112.m: No torch shines without a battery.

6113.q: What are young meerkats like when they are born?
a: With fully developed fur and open eyes
6113.e: Newborn meerkats are helpless. Their eyes only open after about two weeks.
6113.m: Young meerkats are blind at first.

6114.q: Which teeth are especially long and pointed in the jackal, as a predator?
6114.e: Like the wolf and the dog, the jackal has long, pointed canines. It uses them to grab and hold its prey.
6114.m: The jackal grabs prey with its canines.

6115.q: Roughly how many degrees can an eagle owl turn its head?
6115.e: Thanks to special neck bones, an eagle owl can turn its head up to 270 degrees. This lets it keep almost its whole surroundings in view.
6115.m: The eagle owl turns its head up to 270 degrees.

6116.q: What does a secret police do in a dictatorship?
a: It secretly watches people who think differently.
6116.e: A secret police searches in secret for people who criticise the ruler. This makes many people afraid, and they no longer dare to speak freely.
6116.m: Secret police secretly watch the people.

6117.q: What do you call animals that play an important role for many other species in an area?
6117.e: The elephant is considered a keystone species. Its behaviour affects many other animals and plants.

a: Only if they have a boat
6118.e: Foxes are surprisingly good swimmers and will cross streams or small rivers if they need to. Mostly, though, they prefer to avoid water.

6120.q: When are you most likely to see fire salamanders in the wild?
a: After rain, when they come out of their hiding places
Only at midday in the blazing sun
Only in the depths of winter on snow
6120.e: After rain the air is damp enough for fire salamanders to leave their hiding places and look for food. That is why you often meet them on damp days.

6121.q: Which animal is the national symbol and heraldic animal of the USA?
6121.e: The bald eagle was declared the national symbol of the USA in 1782 and appears on the country's Great Seal. It stands for strength and freedom.
6121.m: The USA has the bald eagle as its symbol.

6122.q: When is the least weasel active?
6122.e: Least weasels hunt at different times of day, depending on when their prey is around. So they are not purely night animals.
6122.m: Least weasels are active round the clock.

6123.q: What is the jaguar's job in the ecosystem?
a: It keeps prey numbers in balance
6123.e: As a predator it stops particular prey animals from multiplying too much. This helps the whole habitat.

6124.q: What do you call a group of bison living together?
6124.e: Bison usually live in herds. Cows and calves form the core groups.

6125.q: How is a wolf pack usually made up?
a: A pair of parents with their young
Lots of unrelated wolves with no order
6125.e: A wolf pack typically consists of a pair of parents and their offspring from the last one or two years. Together they hunt and defend their territory.
6125.m: A wolf pack is usually a family.

6126.q: How important is moisture for where the Alpine salamander is found?
a: Only areas that are damp enough give it a habitat
Moisture does not matter to it
It lives only where it never rains
6126.e: Because its skin and its breeding need moisture, the Alpine salamander depends on habitats that are damp enough. It cannot survive in areas that are too dry.

6127.q: Why does the kingfisher need especially clear water?
a: To see fish clearly when hunting
Because it can only swim there
6127.e: Only in clear water can the kingfisher spot fish well from its perch. Murky water makes hunting much harder for it.
6127.m: Clear water helps it find fish.

6128.q: What does a roe deer often use to detect danger first?
6128.e: Roe deer have a very good sense of smell. They can smell a person or a predator from far away.
6128.m: Roe deer smell danger from far away.

6129.q: Where do the threads come out of a spider?
a: At the back end of its body
6129.e: At the end of its abdomen the spider has small spinnerets. The fine threads come out of these.
6129.m: The threads come out of the back of the body.

6130.q: Which animal family does the Alpine marmot belong to?
6130.e: Like the red squirrel, the Alpine marmot belongs to the squirrel family. It is part of the marmot genus, Marmota in Latin.

6131.q: What are roe deer especially good at with their ears?
a: Hearing very well and locating sounds
6131.e: Roe deer have big, mobile ears. With them they hear very well and notice early when danger is near.
6131.m: Roe deer hear very well with big ears.

6132.q: How does an adder usually react when people come near?
a: It rolls up into a ball
6132.e: Usually it tries to hide. It only bites if it feels cornered or is trodden on.

6133.q: How does a male leopard usually differ from a female?
a: It has stripes instead of spots
6133.e: Male leopards are usually much heavier than females. They can weigh about 60 to 90 kilograms.

6134.q: Where does the red fox like to live?
a: In forests, fields and even in cities
Only on high mountains above 4,000 metres
6134.e: The red fox is very adaptable and finds food almost everywhere. In Switzerland it even lives in the middle of cities such as Zurich or Bern.
6134.m: Foxes live in forests, fields and cities.

6135.q: What colour is the abdomen of the European garden spider usually?
a: Brown or reddish with pale spots
6135.e: The garden spider's abdomen is usually brown to reddish. It has pale spots on it that form the cross pattern.
6135.m: Brown with pale spots is typical.

6136.q: How wide can a hippopotamus open its mouth?
a: About as wide as a dog
About as wide as a person
6136.e: Hippos can open their mouths extremely wide. They often do this to look strong and dangerous.
6136.m: Hippos open their mouths hugely wide.

6137.q: What colour is the coat of many reindeer calves at birth?
a: Fairly plain, light to reddish brown
6137.e: Reindeer calves are usually a plain brownish colour. They lack the white spots of young roe deer or red deer.

a: A state insurance that pays a pension in old age and is partly funded by working people
A private savings insurance for children
A health insurance for young people
6138.e: AHV (old-age and survivors' insurance) is Switzerland's state pension insurance. All working people pay into it during their working life so that pensions can be paid out later.
6138.m: AHV provides a pension in old age.

6139.q: In which season do female fire salamanders usually release their larvae into the water?
6139.e: The females carry the eggs inside their bodies for months. In spring they release the fully formed larvae into cool streams.
6139.m: In spring the larvae go into the water.

6140.q: Why do rabbits have to gnaw all the time?
a: So that their teeth do not get too long
6140.e: Because their teeth keep growing, rabbits must wear them down by gnawing. Otherwise the teeth would get too long and get in the way of eating.

6141.q: Why were many blue whales hunted in the past?
a: Because they ate up the fish
6141.e: People hunted blue whales to get oil from their blubber and to eat their meat. That is why huge numbers were killed in the past.
6141.m: Whales were heavily hunted in the past.

6142.q: What must a hamster never eat because it harms it?
6142.e: Chocolate is poisonous for hamsters, just as it is for many other pets. It must never go in its bowl.

6143.q: What is the Hindu place of worship called?
6143.e: In a Hindu temple there are statues of different gods. People pray there and bring flowers and offerings.

6144.q: What mainly sets the mute swan apart from other swan species?
a: The black knob on its beak
6144.e: Other swan species such as the whooper swan have no knob on their beak. This feature makes the mute swan especially easy to recognise.
6144.m: The knob is its identifying mark.

6145.q: What is another name for the orca?
6145.e: Orca is another word for killer whale. Both names mean the same animal.
6145.m: The orca is also called the killer whale.

6146.q: Why does a carp have a swim bladder in its belly?
a: So that it neither sinks nor rises in the water
6146.e: The swim bladder is filled with gas. It helps the carp hover at a certain depth without having to swim all the time.
6146.m: The swim bladder keeps the carp hovering.

6147.q: What is complete metamorphosis in insects?
a: Larva and then straight to egg
6147.e: In complete metamorphosis an insect goes through four very different stages. The butterfly is a well-known example.
6147.m: The four stages are egg, larva, pupa and insect.

6148.q: Which animals make up Africa's “Big Five”?
6148.e: The Big Five were originally the most dangerous animals for hunters. Today the term is best known from safaris.
6148.m: The buffalo is one of the Big Five.

6149.q: Apart from the Alps, in which European mountains is the chamois also found?
6149.e: Besides the Alps, the chamois also lives in the Carpathians in eastern Europe. There is even a subspecies of its own there.
6149.m: Chamois also live in the Carpathians.

6150.q: Which animals does the barn owl eat besides mice?
6150.e: Besides mice, the barn owl sometimes eats small birds or rats. But mice remain its favourite food.
6150.m: Small birds are on the menu too.

6151.q: How do meerkats communicate with each other?
6151.e: They have a wide range of calls for different situations. Scent and body posture also play a part.

6153.q: Is an old wasps' nest used again the following year?
a: No, a new nest is usually built
No, it is burnt straight away
6153.e: A wasps' nest is normally used for only one year. The next spring a new queen builds a fresh nest.
6153.m: A new nest is made every year.

6154.q: What colour is a roe deer's coat usually in summer?
6154.e: In summer a roe deer's coat is reddish brown. In winter it turns greyish brown.
6154.m: In summer the roe deer is reddish brown.

6155.q: Where in Switzerland is the great spotted woodpecker common?
a: In forests, parks and gardens all over the country
Only high in the mountains above 3,000 metres
Only in the city of Zurich
6155.e: The great spotted woodpecker feels at home wherever there are enough trees. That is why you see it all over Switzerland.
6155.m: It lives wherever there are trees.

6156.q: Which Swiss organisation does a lot for swifts and nest boxes?
a: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach
6156.e: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach monitors and protects many Swiss bird species, including the swift. For example, it encourages people to put up nest boxes on houses.
6156.m: The institute in Sempach protects the swift.

6157.q: What is one of the most common large earthworm species in Switzerland called?
6157.e: The lobworm is a large earthworm species often found in gardens and meadows. It digs deep, vertical tunnels.
6157.m: The lobworm is a large earthworm.

6159.q: What else does a fox use to feel its way in the dark?
6159.e: Like many other mammals, the fox has sensitive whiskers on its face. With them it can sense what is near it even in the dark.

6160.q: Which part of the body helps you grab and hold things?
6160.e: With your fingers you can grab, hold and feel things. Your hand is very skilful.

a: A disease in which bones lose density
A vision problem in old age
6161.e: With osteoporosis the bones lose density and break more easily. Older people in particular are affected more often.
