6161.m: Osteoporosis makes bones break more easily.

6162.q: Roughly how long can a kangaroo live in the wild?
6162.e: In the wild, kangaroos usually live 6 to 8 years. In captivity they can live longer.

6163.q: How can you tell individual leopards apart in camera trap pictures?
a: By the spot pattern, which is different for each one
By the size of their ears
By the colour of their eyes
6163.e: Every leopard's spot pattern is unique, a bit like a fingerprint. Researchers use this to count the animals.

6164.q: What type of water does the wels catfish prefer to live in?
6164.e: The wels catfish likes warm water with little current, for example in big lakes and the lower parts of rivers. It avoids fast, cold mountain streams.
6164.m: The wels loves warm, calm water.

6165.q: What colour are many native woodlice?
6165.e: Many species are grey or brown. This camouflages them well among stones and leaves.
6165.m: Many woodlice are grey or brown.

6166.q: What is an earthworm's long body made of?
6166.e: An earthworm's body is made up of lots of small rings. There are more than a hundred of them.
6166.m: The worm has many body rings.

6167.q: How does an edible frog develop?
a: From egg to tadpole to frog
From egg straight to a finished frog
From caterpillar to pupa to frog
It is born alive as a little frog
6167.e: Tadpoles hatch from the frogspawn and live in the water. Over time they grow legs, the tail disappears and a little frog forms.

6168.q: What do whitefish usually look like from the outside?
6168.e: Whitefish have a slim body with silvery scales. This helps them move well in open water.

6169.q: Which four breeds are the Swiss mountain dogs?
6169.e: The four Swiss mountain dog breeds were traditionally used on farms as guard dogs, herding dogs or draught dogs. The St Bernard is also a Swiss dog, but not a mountain dog of this group.
6169.m: Four mountain dog breeds come from Switzerland.

6170.q: Where does the carp prefer to live?
a: In calm ponds and lakes with plants
6170.e: Carp like warm, calm water with lots of plants. There they find enough food and hiding places.
6170.m: Carp love calm waters full of plants.

6171.q: What do people sometimes use duck down for?
6171.e: Down feathers are very light and keep you warm. That is why they are sometimes used in jackets or duvets.
6171.m: Down keeps you warm in jackets too.

6172.q: What colour is a European tree frog typically?
6172.e: The green colour helps the tree frog hide among leaves. Its colour can vary slightly depending on the situation.
6172.m: Green like the leaf it sits on.

6173.q: What does the grey heron use to spread the powder from its powder down through its plumage?
a: A comb-like claw on its middle toe
6173.e: On its middle toe the grey heron has a serrated grooming claw. It uses it to comb the powder through its feathers and clean them thoroughly.
6173.m: Its grooming claw helps care for its feathers.

6174.q: On which continents is the Eurasian otter naturally found?
a: In Europe and large parts of Asia
6174.e: The Eurasian otter is found in large parts of Europe and Asia. In some regions it is missing, though, because it was wiped out there.
6174.m: Otters live in Europe and Asia.

a: The scientific name of the wels catfish
6175.e: A scientific name is made up of the genus and the species. For the wels catfish it is Silurus glanis.
6175.m: Silurus glanis is the wels catfish.

6176.q: What do bees collect from flowers?
6176.e: Bees fly from flower to flower and suck up the sweet nectar. In doing so they help the plants to reproduce.

6177.q: Which season is best for polar bears to hunt on the sea ice?
6177.e: In winter and spring there is a lot of solid sea ice. That is when polar bears can hunt seals best.
6177.m: Winter and spring are the best hunting time.

6178.q: Why are overhead power lines especially dangerous for eagle owls?
a: The birds can get an electric shock when landing or fly into the lines
Because eagle owls eat metal and choke on it
Because the lines change the colour of their feathers
Because the lines stop the owl from flying at all
6178.e: On overhead lines, eagle owls can get an electric shock when they land or collide with the wires. Special protective devices on pylons are meant to prevent such accidents.
6178.m: Overhead lines are dangerous for eagle owls.

6179.q: Where on the pasture do alpacas most often come together to eat?
a: At the feeding place or in the field as a herd
6179.e: Alpacas like to graze together as a herd. This makes them safer and lets them keep each other in sight.
6179.m: Alpacas like to eat as a herd.

6180.q: What does the koala eat almost exclusively?
6180.e: Eucalyptus leaves are poisonous to many animals, but the koala can digest them thanks to a special digestive system. Because the leaves are not very nourishing, it sleeps more than 18 hours a day.
6180.m: Koalas eat almost only eucalyptus leaves.

6181.q: What can happen when praying mantises mate?
a: Sometimes the female eats the male
The male always eats the female
Neither eats anything for a week afterwards
The pair builds a nest together
6181.e: It does happen, but not every time. It happens more often in a terrarium than in the wild.
6181.m: The female sometimes eats the male.

6182.q: How does the grey heron typically hunt?
a: It stands motionless in the water and waits for prey
It swims and dives like a duck
It catches prey in the air
It digs in the ground for prey
6182.e: The grey heron often stands patiently without moving in shallow water for minutes on end. As soon as a fish swims by, it strikes like lightning.
6182.m: Patience is its best hunting weapon.

a: The group that runs a country, a canton or a municipality
6183.e: A government makes important decisions and makes sure laws are carried out. In Switzerland there are governments at federal, cantonal and municipal level.
6183.m: The government runs the country, canton or municipality.

6184.q: How does a herd of elephants protect its young from danger?
a: The adults form a circle around the young
6184.e: When danger threatens, the adult elephants surround their young to protect them. In the middle, the calves are safe from enemies.
6184.m: Adults protect the young in a circle.

6185.q: What is especially dangerous for young otters?
a: Road traffic near rivers and lakes
6185.e: Because otters often have to cross roads to move between waters, young animals are especially at risk from cars. Many conservation projects try to prevent this.
6185.m: Roads are a big danger for young otters.

6186.q: Some pond skaters live in a place that is very unusual for insects. Where?
6186.e: Most pond skaters live on ponds and streams. But a few species even dart about on the surface of the oceans.
6186.m: Some pond skaters live on the sea.

6187.q: What protection status does the sand lizard have in Switzerland?
a: It is a protected and endangered species
It may be kept and sold as a pet
It is not at risk at all and very common
6187.e: The sand lizard is protected in Switzerland because its numbers have fallen. You must not catch it, disturb it or destroy its home.
6187.m: The sand lizard is protected by law.

6188.q: Which sound is typical of tapirs?
6188.e: Tapirs communicate with high whistling sounds. This is how mother and young keep in touch.

6189.q: Is the snow leopard a subspecies of the leopard?
a: No, it is a separate species
Yes, a subspecies from the Himalayas
Yes, a subspecies with light fur
No, it belongs to the lynxes
6189.e: The snow leopard is called Panthera uncia and is a separate species. It is related to the leopard, but it is not the same animal. It is not a lynx either.
6189.m: The snow leopard is a separate species.

6190.q: Which wing shape is typical of the kestrel in flight?
a: Very short, round wings like a sparrow's
Huge, broad wings like a vulture's
6190.e: In flight you can recognise the kestrel by its long, pointed wings and long tail. This shape makes fast, nimble flying possible.
6190.m: Pointed wings and a long tail mark it out.

6191.q: What does the song you often hear from great tits in spring sound like?
6191.e: The great tit's typical song sounds like “tea-cher, tea-cher” or “zi-za-zi-za”. You can hear it from late winter and in spring.

6192.e: Jaguars are skilful climbers and sometimes lie in wait on branches. From there they can surprise prey.

6193.q: Which group of animals does the gorilla belong to?
6193.e: The gorilla is a great ape, just like the chimpanzee and the orangutan. Great apes have no tail and are very clever.

6194.q: Why are hippos dangerous, even though they only eat plants?
a: They fiercely defend their territory and their young
They have poison in their teeth
6194.e: Hippos defend their territory and their young very fiercely. That is why they are considered dangerous animals, despite eating plants.

6195.q: In which of these countries is the alpine newt common?
6195.e: The alpine newt is one of the most common newt species in Switzerland. It is missing from islands such as Iceland or Malta and from the far north.
6195.m: The alpine newt is widespread in Switzerland.

6196.q: What is the fire salamander's skin poison for?
a: It keeps it warm in winter
6196.e: The poison comes out of glands in the skin. That is why many predators leave the fire salamander alone.
6196.m: The skin poison protects against predators.

6197.q: What is a baby rhinoceros called?
6197.e: A young rhino is called a calf, just like a young cow. It stays with its mother for a long time.
6197.m: A baby rhino is a calf.

6198.q: How do young garden spiders spread out once they have hatched?
a: They let the wind carry them away on fine threads
They stay in the same place all their lives
The mother carries each one away
They swim away in the water
6198.e: The tiny spiders spin a long thread that flies in the wind like a sail. This carries them far away so they find new places to live.
6198.m: The wind carries the little spiders away.

6199.q: What does the German name ‘Wasserläufer’ (water runner) of the pond skater mean?
a: It runs on the surface of the water
It runs along the bottom of the water
It only runs in the rain
6199.e: The name describes the way it moves so strikingly. The pond skater looks as if it is walking on water.
6199.m: The name describes running on water.

6200.q: What is a typical feature of the male alpine newt's breeding colours?
a: A low, smooth ridge along its back
A tall, jagged crest like the great crested newt's
6200.e: Unlike the great crested newt, the male alpine newt grows only a low, smooth ridge along its back. Even so, this is a typical feature in its water phase.
6200.m: The back ridge stays low and smooth.

6201.q: What are the long black feathers on the back of the grey heron's head called?
6201.e: The nape plumes are a typical feature of the grey heron. They often hang down long over the neck.
6201.m: The plumes sit on the back of the head.

6202.q: What is typical of young otters before they learn to swim?
a: At first they are afraid of water
They stay on land for ever
6202.e: Surprisingly, young otters are wary of water at first. Their mother has to teach them to swim patiently.
6202.m: Young otters avoid water at first.

6203.e: Leopards usually hunt at dusk and at night. During the day they often rest in the shade or in trees.

6204.q: Why does the great spotted woodpecker sometimes peck holes in house walls?
a: Because it suspects insects are there
Because it wants to annoy people
Because it wants to eat the wood
Because it wants to bathe there
6204.e: If woodworm or other insects live in the wall, the woodpecker hears them and pecks after them. Sometimes it also pecks just to mark its territory.
6204.m: It is looking for insects in the wood.

6205.q: Which group of animals does the roe deer belong to?
6205.e: Roe deer give birth to live young and feed them milk. That is why they are mammals.
6205.m: Roe deer are mammals like us.

6206.q: What do you call the person who looks after a flock of sheep?
6206.e: A shepherd watches over the flock and makes sure the animals are well. Often a dog helps.
6206.m: The shepherd looks after the sheep.

6207.q: What does a rhinoceros mainly use its horn for in the wild?
6207.e: The horn helps the rhino defend itself against enemies and hold its own in fights over territory. It is like a natural weapon.

6208.q: When are badger cubs usually born?
a: In winter, between January and March
They are never born in the sett
6208.e: Badger cubs are usually born in late winter in the safe, warm sett. They are well protected there.
6208.m: Badger cubs are born in winter.

6209.q: How do peregrine falcon parents react when an enemy comes near their nest?
a: They often attack the intruder noisily
They leave the nest at once for ever
They call other bird species for help
6209.e: Peregrine falcons defend their nest very bravely, often attacking enemies with loud calls and fast flying. This is how they protect their eggs and young.
6209.m: The parents defend the nest bravely.

6210.q: What do you call a wolf that roams without a fixed pack?
6210.e: Some wolves leave the pack they were born into and roam alone to find their own territory and a partner. Such animals are called lone wolves.
6210.m: Some wolves live as lone wolves.

6211.q: What can the pike do in a well-known Russian fairy tale?
a: It breathes fire like a dragon
It walks on legs on land
6211.e: In an old Russian fairy tale, a magic pike grants the hero all his wishes. This story is very well known in eastern Europe.
6211.m: A fairy tale tells of a magic pike.

6212.q: What do you call the way of life of a brown bear that, apart from raising young, mostly goes about alone?
6212.e: Brown bears are typical loners. Only mothers with their cubs form a fixed group for a longer time.

6213.q: What is the purpose of gibbons' calls early in the morning?
a: They tell other groups: this place is taken
They are meant to bring rain
6213.e: Gibbon groups announce their territory with song. This helps them avoid quarrels with neighbouring groups.

6214.q: What is the great spotted woodpecker looking for when it pecks into tree bark?
6214.e: Many insects and larvae live under the bark and in the wood. The great spotted woodpecker pecks holes to get at them.

6215.q: What makes the bright colours on a butterfly's wings?
6215.e: The wings are covered with thousands of tiny scales. These scales give them their beautiful colours and patterns.
6215.m: Tiny scales make the wings colourful.

6216.q: Which kind of trout has a pinkish red stripe along its side?
6216.e: The rainbow trout has a striking, colourful stripe along its side. It sometimes shimmers like a little rainbow.
6216.m: Rainbow trout have a colourful stripe.

6217.q: Because of its coat, what else is the African wild dog called?
6217.e: The name hyena dog comes from its spotted appearance and its hunched walk, which is reminiscent of hyenas. But it is not related to hyenas.
6217.m: Hyena dog is another name for it.

6218.q: How do adult African wild dogs often bring food to the young?
a: They bring meat back up from their stomach
They carry live prey to the den in their mouth
They feed them milk from fruit
6218.e: Pack members bring up partly digested meat so that pups and the dogs looking after them can eat it. This way even animals that do not hunt get fed.
6218.m: Meat is brought back up for others.

6219.q: Why do you see a cuckoo less often than you hear it?
a: It likes to hide in dense trees
6219.e: The cuckoo likes to sit hidden in trees and bushes, so you rarely get to see it. But you can hear its call from far away.
6219.m: You hear a cuckoo more often than you see it.

6220.q: Why is a polar bear's black nose easy to spot?
a: It stands out against the white fur
6220.e: The black nose stands out clearly against the white fur. That is why a polar bear sometimes covers its nose with its paw when it wants to hide.
6220.m: The black nose is easy to see.

6221.q: In which surroundings does the stone marten especially like to live?
a: Only high above the tree line
6221.e: Stone martens often seek out places near people, because they find plenty of food and sheltered hiding places there. Barns, lofts and gardens are popular spots.
6221.m: Stone martens love being near people.

6222.q: Where do orangutans spend most of their lives?
6222.e: Orangutans are the largest animals in the world that live mainly in trees. There they find food and sleep.

6223.q: What are lion cubs like when they are just born?
a: They are as big as a dog
6223.e: Little lions are born blind, with their eyes still closed. In the first weeks they are very helpless.

6224.q: How much can a big bull elk (moose) weigh?
6224.e: Big bulls reach over 500 kilograms, even more in Alaska. That is much heavier than a roe deer.

6225.q: How do ducks often sleep so that they still notice danger?
a: With one eye open and part of the brain awake
6225.e: Some ducks sleep in such a way that one half of the brain stays awake and one eye stays open. This lets them notice enemies even while resting.
6225.m: Ducks sometimes sleep with one eye open.

6226.q: How do dogs see colours compared with humans?
a: They see fewer colours, mainly blues and yellows
They see all colours just like humans
They see only black and white
They see more colours than humans
6226.e: Dogs are dichromats and can mainly tell apart shades of blue and yellow; reds and greens look more alike to them. People with normal colour vision, by contrast, see three primary colours.
6226.m: Dogs see fewer colours than humans.

6227.q: Do wild boar live in Switzerland too?
a: Yes, they are found in many Swiss forests
No, there are no wild boar in Switzerland
No, they live only in Africa
6227.e: Wild boar are native to Switzerland and live especially in well-wooded areas. They are cautious animals and usually avoid contact with people.
6227.m: Wild boar also live in Swiss forests.

6228.q: What is special about the tree kangaroo?
a: It digs holes in the ground
6228.e: Most kangaroos hop across the ground. The tree kangaroo, however, lives in the rainforest and climbs trees skilfully.

6229.q: What does it show when great tits are already singing loudly in January?
a: Spring and the breeding season are coming
It is very cold and they are freezing
6229.e: Male great tits often start singing as early as January to mark a territory and attract a female. This shows that spring will soon be here.

6230.q: What is the force called that keeps an aeroplane in the air when it flies?
6230.e: The shape of the wings makes the air flow faster over the wings than underneath. This creates a difference in pressure that carries the aeroplane upwards.
6230.m: Lift keeps the aeroplane in the air.

6231.q: How do roe deer eat compared with cows?
a: They carefully pick out tender buds and herbs
They eat large amounts of grass without choosing
They mainly eat moss and stones
6231.e: Roe deer choose their food carefully. They prefer tender leaves, buds and herbs instead of just lots of grass.
6231.m: Roe deer choose their food carefully.

6232.q: Why do red foxes also live in the middle of Swiss cities such as Zurich or Bern?
a: Because they easily find food in gardens and bins there
Because there are no people in cities
Because it always snows in cities
Because cities are forbidden to foxes
6232.e: In cities, foxes can often find food easily, for example in gardens, compost heaps or bins. That is why many foxes have adapted well to city life.

6233.q: How do ants get aphids to release honeydew?
a: They stroke them with their antennae
6233.e: Ants tap the aphids' abdomen with their antennae. This makes the aphids release a drop of honeydew.

6234.q: Which animal is a natural enemy of young, still small brown bears?
a: Mainly older brown bears from outside the family
6234.e: Young brown bears can be in danger mainly from adult bears that are not their family. That is why the mother stays especially watchful near her cubs in their first years.
6234.m: Unrelated bears can be dangerous to cubs.

6235.q: How are baby baboons usually carried at first?
a: They cling to their mother's belly
6235.e: Newborns hold on to the fur on their mother's belly. Later they ride on her back.

6236.q: In which part of Africa does the African wild dog mainly live today?
a: In the middle of the Sahara
6236.e: The African wild dog lives mainly in the savannahs south of the Sahara, for example in Botswana, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Today it is only found in small areas.
6236.m: The wild dog lives in Africa's savannahs south of the Sahara.

6237.q: Roughly how many young does a slow worm have?
6237.e: A female usually gives birth to several young in late summer. The number depends on her age and size.
6237.m: Several young usually arrive in late summer.

6238.q: Is the chimpanzee a good swimmer?
a: Yes, it swims better than a fish
6238.e: Most chimpanzees cannot swim well and avoid deep water. They feel much more at home in the trees.

6239.q: What do you call a red deer stag whose antlers have twelve points?
6239.e: The points on antlers are called tines. A stag with twelve points is traditionally called a royal.
6239.m: A royal has twelve antler points.

6240.q: What does the African buffalo mainly eat?
6240.e: The African buffalo is a plant eater and mainly eats grasses. It is a ruminant.

6241.q: Which family of rodents does the edible dormouse belong to?
6241.e: The edible dormouse belongs to the dormouse family. This family is known for its long hibernation.
6241.m: The edible dormouse belongs to the dormouse family.

6242.q: What do the eggs of the common wall lizard look like?
a: Whitish with a soft, leathery shell
Hard and colourfully speckled like birds' eggs
6242.e: Reptile eggs such as those of the wall lizard have a soft, parchment-like shell. They lie well hidden in warm soil.
6242.m: Lizard eggs have a soft shell.

6243.q: What does a male bonobo's rank depend on a lot?
6243.e: The mother supports her son in the group. If she has a high rank, that helps him too.
6243.m: The mother affects her son's rank.

6245.q: Roughly how long does the fire salamander's larval stage in the water last?
6245.e: Depending on water temperature and food, the larvae need two to six months before they become land animals. Then they leave the water.
6245.m: The larval stage lasts several months.

6246.q: What is celebrated on World Bee Day?
a: The protection and importance of bees
6246.e: On World Bee Day, people all over the world remember how important bees are for nature and farming. It takes place every year on 20 May.

6247.q: On which continents do tapirs live in the wild?
a: South America, Central America and Asia
6247.e: Wild tapirs are found in South and Central America and in Southeast Asia. None live in Europe or Africa.
6247.m: Tapirs live in the Americas and Asia.

6248.q: Which group of animals does the Alpine salamander belong to?
6248.e: The Alpine salamander is an amphibian. This group of animals usually depends on damp habitats.

6249.q: What happens to a tadpole's tail as it turns into a frog?
a: It drops off whole at once
6249.e: During metamorphosis the tadpole's tail is broken down step by step while legs grow at the same time. In the end a little frog without a tail is left.

6250.q: What role do whitefish play in a lake's food chain?
a: They eat plankton and are prey for predatory fish
They live independently of other animals
They eat only plants on the shore
6250.e: Whitefish link the plankton to the larger predatory fish. This way they pass energy along the food chain.
6250.m: Whitefish link plankton and predatory fish.

6251.q: How many eggs does a female tawny owl usually lay in a clutch?
6251.e: A female tawny owl usually lays between two and six white, round eggs. The exact number often depends on how much food there is.
6251.m: Tawny owls usually lay two to six eggs.

6252.q: What colour are newly hatched young sand lizards usually?
6252.e: The little lizards are at first a fairly plain bronze colour and only change colour as they get older. This gives good protection from enemies.
6252.m: The young are bronze brown at first.

6253.q: How big is a donkey usually compared with a large horse?
a: A donkey is always much bigger
Donkeys and horses are exactly the same size
Donkeys are as big as elephants
6253.e: On average, donkeys are smaller than large horse breeds. But there are also bigger donkey breeds that can grow taller.
6253.m: Donkeys are usually smaller than horses.

6254.q: What is the mating position called in which dragonflies form a typical heart shape?
6254.e: The male holds the female by the neck. The female bends her abdomen forwards, which forms a wheel or heart.
6254.m: The mating wheel looks like a heart.

6255.q: What is the male of the cow called?
6255.e: The male of the cow is called a bull. Bulls are often bigger and stronger than cows.
6255.m: The male cow is called a bull.

6256.q: What happens when a kestrel catches more mice than it eats straight away?
a: It can hide the extra prey for later
It lets them go again at once
It always shares them at once with other birds
It never eats more than one mouse a day
6256.e: Kestrels can hide extra prey and fetch it later, especially when hunting is going very well. This helps them have enough food even in harder times.

6258.q: What do elephants often do when a member of the herd dies?
a: They show grief and often stay by it
6258.e: Elephants are considered very social, feeling animals. Scientists have seen them stay for a long time with dead family members and even touch them.

6259.q: Why are kangaroos well adapted to dry, hot weather?
a: They need only a little water to survive
6259.e: Kangaroos can go a long time without much water. This helps them survive in the dry parts of Australia.

6260.q: What role does the fire salamander play in the forest ecosystem?
a: As a predator it keeps the numbers of insects and other small animals in check
6260.e: As a hunter of insects, worms and slugs, the fire salamander helps keep the forest floor in balance. It is an important part of the food chain.
6260.m: It keeps small animals in balance.

6261.q: How does the blue whale usually catch its food?
a: It swims through swarms of krill with its mouth open
It digs for it in the sand
It collects plants from the sea floor
6261.e: The blue whale swims into a swarm of krill with its mouth wide open. Then it pushes the water out through its baleen plates and keeps the krill.
6261.m: The blue whale swims through krill clouds with its mouth open.

6262.q: Great apes belong to the Old World monkeys and apes. Which way do their nostrils point?
6262.e: In Old World monkeys and apes, including the great apes, the nostrils are close together and point downwards. In the New World monkeys of the Americas, they point sideways.
6262.m: Old World primates have downward-pointing nostrils.

6263.q: What teeth does an orca have?
a: Large, pointed teeth for gripping prey
6263.e: Orcas have many pointed, cone-shaped teeth. They use them to grip their prey firmly.

6264.q: What does the eel prefer to eat?
6264.e: The eel is a predatory fish and eats small animals on the bottom of the water. These include worms, insect larvae, crayfish and small fish.
6264.m: The eel is a predatory fish.

6267.q: What do you usually hear shortly after a flash of lightning?
6267.e: Lightning and thunder happen at the same time, but light is much faster than sound. That is why you see the lightning first and only hear the thunder afterwards.
6267.m: After the lightning comes the thunder.

6269.q: How big can the giant isopod from the deep sea get?
6269.e: Giant isopods of the genus Bathynomus live in the deep sea and can grow over thirty centimetres long. They mainly eat carrion.
6269.m: Giant isopods grow over 30 centimetres long.

6270.q: What is the main colour of the United Nations flag?
6270.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world on a light blue background. The colour stands for peace.
6270.m: The UN flag is light blue with a map of the world.

6271.e: Meerkats dig a widely branching system of tunnels with several entrances. They sleep there, safe from heat and enemies.

6272.q: What does a well-known English rhyme say about the number of magpies you see?
a: The number is supposed to predict good or bad luck
The number tells the magpie's age
6272.e: In England there is the old rhyme “One for sorrow, two for joy”, which links the number of magpies seen to good or bad luck. It is a folk belief with no scientific basis.
6272.m: The number of magpies is said to predict luck.

6273.q: What is the name of the well-known monastery in the canton of Solothurn that many pilgrims visit?
6273.e: Mariastein Abbey lies in the canton of Solothurn near the border with Basel and France. Many people make pilgrimages there because it has a famous chapel of grace.
6273.m: Mariastein Abbey is in the canton of Solothurn.

6274.q: How do experts track the flight paths of released bearded vultures?
a: With small transmitters on the bird
With glowing paint on the wings
Not at all, it is impossible
6274.e: Released bearded vultures often carry small GPS transmitters. This shows where they fly and whether they survive.
6274.m: Transmitters help researchers follow the birds.

6275.q: How does a lynx mark its territory?
a: With scent marks and scratch marks on trees
With mounds of earth like a mole
6275.e: Lynx leave urine, droppings and scratch marks in noticeable places. This shows other lynx that the area is taken.

6276.q: Which statement about grass snakes and people is true?
a: They are shy and usually flee
6276.e: It usually disappears as soon as it notices someone. You should not touch it.

6277.q: How does a foal recognise its mother soon after birth?
a: By the colour of her coat
By the sound of her hooves
6277.e: A foal recognises its mother soon after birth by her smell and her voice. This bond is very important for the foal.
6277.m: Foals recognise their mother by smell.

6278.q: What were goose feathers especially often used for in the past?
6278.e: Long ago, people carved a point on a large goose feather and dipped it in ink. This let them write with it.
6278.m: Goose feathers were made into quill pens.

6279.q: How long does an adult housefly usually live?
6279.e: An adult housefly usually lives only a few weeks. But in that short time it already lays lots of eggs.
6279.m: Adult flies live only a short time.

6280.e: Insects breathe through fine tubes called tracheae. They open in small holes, the spiracles, along the sides of the body.

6281.q: Which material does light shine through well?
6281.e: Glass is transparent, so light gets through almost unhindered. Wood or stone blocks the light.
6281.m: Glass lets light through, stone does not.

6282.q: How big is a golden jackal compared with a wolf?
6282.e: The golden jackal is much smaller and lighter than a wolf. It looks more like a slim, small dog.
6282.m: The golden jackal is smaller than the wolf.

6283.q: How quickly can an egg become a fully grown housefly?
6283.e: In warm weather a housefly develops from egg to adult fly in just a few weeks. That is why flies can multiply so fast.

6284.q: Why are its front paws so important to the mole?
a: So that it can dig tunnels quickly
So that it can climb trees
So that it can swim well
So that it can crack nuts
6284.e: Without its strong digging paws, the mole could not build its home underground. They are its most important tool.
6284.m: Its paws are its most important tool.

6285.q: How does the European tree frog protect itself from predators during the day?
a: It sits well camouflaged among green leaves
It sprays a cloud of poison
6285.e: Thanks to its green colour, the tree frog blends in well with the leaves. This makes it hard for predators to spot.

6286.q: When does the nictitating membrane slide over the eye in some sharks?
6286.e: When biting, the prey could injure the shark's eye. The protective membrane then slides across in front of it.
6286.m: When biting, the membrane protects the eye.

6287.q: Which group of animals do millipedes belong to?
6287.e: Millipedes have a segmented body and jointed legs. So, like insects and spiders, they count as arthropods.

6288.q: How does a stork hold its neck when it flies?
6288.e: In flight the stork stretches its neck straight out in front. A heron, by contrast, pulls it in. This is how you can tell the two birds apart in the sky.
6288.m: The stork flies with its neck stretched out.

6289.q: Where is the fin you see sticking out of the water when a dolphin swims at the surface?
6289.e: The dorsal fin sits on top of the back. It helps the dolphin swim steadily in the water.
6289.m: The dorsal fin keeps the dolphin steady.

6290.q: Which bird family does the great tit belong to?
6290.e: The great tit belongs to the tit family. It is the largest tit species in Europe.
6290.m: The great tit is the largest tit.

6291.q: How do some praying mantises move to look like a leaf in the wind?
a: They sway gently back and forth
6291.e: This rocking fools both enemies and prey. It looks as if a leaf or twig were wobbling in the wind.

6292.q: Which body parts help the badger especially well with digging?
a: The long, strong claws on its front paws
The webbing on its back feet
6292.e: The badger has strong, long claws on its front paws that let it dig out earth very well. With them it builds its large underground tunnels.
6292.m: Strong claws help the badger dig.

6294.q: What does the badger regularly do with the bedding in its sett?
a: It brings in fresh leaves and grass
6294.e: The badger keeps carrying fresh leaves and dry grass into its sett. This gives it a clean, warm place to sleep.

6295.q: What can happen to your skin when you touch some large millipedes?
a: Their secretion can irritate the skin
You become immune to cold at once
Nothing, because they are made of stone
6295.e: Some species give off substances that irritate the skin or eyes. That is why you should wash your hands after touching them.
6295.m: Wash your hands after touching them.

6296.e: A molecule is formed when two or more atoms join together. Water, for example, consists of one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms.

6297.q: Roughly how old can a lion get in the wild?
6297.e: In the wild, lions usually live between 10 and 14 years. In a zoo, where they face no dangers, they can live a little longer.
6297.m: Wild lions live about 10 to 14 years.

6298.q: Which teeth are missing at the front of a sheep's upper jaw?
a: It has no incisors there, just a hard pad
It has no teeth at all
It has especially long teeth there
It has fangs there like a wolf
6298.e: Sheep have no incisors at the front of the upper jaw, but a hard dental pad instead. They tear off grass between this pad and their lower teeth.
6298.m: Sheep have no teeth at the top front.

6299.q: Why does a bumblebee look rounder and fatter than a wasp?
a: Because of its thick, fluffy hair
6299.e: The bumblebee's thick coat of hair makes its body look rounder. Wasps, on the other hand, look smooth and almost hairless.
6299.m: Thick hair makes bumblebees look round.

6300.q: How does a mosquito find a person in the dark?
6300.e: Mosquitoes can smell the carbon dioxide in our breath and so sense that someone is nearby. This way they find us even without good light.

6301.q: How small can the smallest seahorse be?
a: About as small as a fingernail
6301.e: Some pygmy seahorses are only a few centimetres long. They easily fit on a fingertip.

6302.q: What was the stoat's white winter fur often used for in history?
6302.e: The fine white winter fur of the stoat, called ermine, was once used as precious fur for the robes of kings and judges. You can still see this trimming in old paintings today.

6303.q: How many young does a female dromedary usually have?
6303.e: Usually only a single calf is born. Twins are very rare.
6303.m: Usually only one calf is born.

6304.q: What does the common wall lizard mainly eat?
6304.e: Wall lizards are skilful hunters of small animals. Insects, spiders and other arthropods are at the top of their menu.

6305.q: Why does a donkey sometimes just stop and refuse to go on?
a: It is carefully checking whether the way is safe
6305.e: Donkeys are often thought of as stubborn, but they are actually very careful. Before heading into possible danger, they prefer to think first.

6306.q: Who feeds the blackbird chicks in the nest?
6306.e: Both parents take turns flying off to fetch food for the chicks. This keeps the hungry young well fed.
6306.m: Both blackbird parents feed the chicks.

6307.q: Roughly how much krill does a blue whale eat in a day?
a: None at all, it only eats once a week
6307.e: A blue whale needs huge amounts of krill to fill up. On some days it eats several tonnes of it.
6307.m: A blue whale eats a lot of krill.

6308.q: What does the carp do in winter, when the water gets cold?
a: It becomes sluggish and hardly eats
It swims to the warm sea
6308.e: When it gets cold in winter, the carp hardly moves. It retreats to deeper, calm spots and eats almost nothing.
6308.m: In winter the carp becomes very still.

6309.q: How does the diet of most gorillas differ from that of many predators?
a: Gorillas eat almost only plants, no prey animals
6309.e: Unlike lions or tigers, gorillas do not hunt other animals. They feed almost entirely on plants.
6309.m: Gorillas are almost pure plant eaters.

6310.q: In stoats, which is usually bigger, the male or the female?
a: Both are always the same size
It depends only on the season
6310.e: Male stoats are usually bigger and heavier than the females. This difference is called sexual dimorphism.

6311.q: How do swan parents react when their cygnets are threatened?
6311.e: Swan parents are very caring and brave. If necessary they defend their cygnets even against bigger animals.

6312.q: How does an octopus swim especially fast?
a: It pushes water out through a funnel
It swims backwards with its tail
6312.e: The octopus sucks water into its body and then squeezes it out again through a funnel. This pushes it forwards like a rocket.
6312.m: A water funnel drives the octopus forwards.

6313.q: Where do bonobos usually sleep in the wild?
a: In nests they build in trees
On the open ground of the savannah
6313.e: Bonobos bend branches and twigs together into a nest. They usually build a new one every evening.
6313.m: Bonobos build sleeping nests in trees.

6314.q: When is the housefly especially active?
6314.e: Houseflies like warmth and are especially active in summer. When it is cold they become sluggish and hide.

6315.q: Why can a mallard stand in icy water without freezing?
a: Its feet stay cool and lose hardly any heat
It grows feathers on its feet in winter
6315.e: The blood in a duck's legs passes its warmth back to the body before it flows into the feet. So the feet stay cool and the duck loses hardly any heat.
6315.m: Cool feet keep the duck warm.

6316.q: What does the giant panda like to eat most?
6316.e: The panda eats almost nothing but bamboo. It spends many hours a day eating.
6316.m: The panda loves bamboo above all.

6317.q: Which famous shark is one of the biggest predatory fish in the sea?
6317.e: The great white shark is a big, powerful hunter. It often appears in films and stories.
6317.m: The great white is a big predatory fish.

6318.q: What does a ladybird do when it gets a fright?
a: It gives off a smelly yellow liquid
6318.e: When a ladybird is in danger, it lets a yellow liquid ooze from its legs. It smells nasty and tastes bitter, which puts enemies off.
6318.m: A yellow liquid protects against enemies.

6319.q: How do gibbons such as the pileated gibbon move through the trees?
a: They swing from branch to branch with their long arms
They glide with a flap of skin
They hop on their back legs like kangaroos
They only climb slowly up the trunk
6319.e: Gibbons have very long arms and swing hand over hand through the treetops. The pileated gibbon lives in Southeast Asia and has dark fur on its head like a cap.
6319.m: Gibbons swing through the trees with long arms.

6320.q: What does a butterfly use its antennae for?
6320.e: With its antennae the butterfly can sense scents and find its way. It drinks nectar, on the other hand, with its proboscis.
6320.m: Antennae help with smelling and feeling.

6321.q: Which bird family does the common buzzard belong to?
6321.e: The common buzzard belongs to the hawk and eagle family. This family includes many birds of prey with broad wings.
6321.m: The buzzard belongs to the hawk and eagle family.

6322.q: In the European pond turtle, what decides whether males or females hatch?
6322.e: At higher temperatures, more females tend to hatch; at cooler ones, more males. This is called temperature-dependent sex determination.

6323.q: What is special about the llama's upper lip?
a: It is hard like a beak
6323.e: The split upper lip helps it grab plants. Llamas can move it very well.
6323.m: Llamas have a split upper lip.

6324.q: Why are sheep important for the alpine pastures in Switzerland?
a: They keep the grass short and look after the landscape
6324.e: By eating the grass, sheep keep the alpine pastures short and open. This helps rare flowers and herbs grow better there.
6324.m: Sheep look after the alpine pastures.

6325.q: Where does the name “lemur” come from?
a: From the Latin “lemures”, the spirits of the dead
6325.e: The naturalist Linnaeus named the animals after the ghosts of Roman legend. The reason was probably their calls at night and the glowing eyes of some species.

6326.q: Which large forest animal does a robin sometimes follow to find insects?
a: A wild boar rooting up the ground
6326.e: When wild boar root up the ground with their snouts, insects and worms come to light. The robin likes to take advantage of this.

6327.q: What does the Antarctic Treaty lay down?
a: That Antarctica may only be used for peaceful and scientific purposes
That only Switzerland may do research in Antarctica
That Antarctica will be sold to a single country
That wars may be fought in Antarctica
6327.e: Several states agreed to keep Antarctica free of military activity and to use it only for research. The treaty shows how countries can make rules for an area together.
6327.m: Antarctica is for peace and research.

6328.q: What behaviour does the grey heron often show towards possible partners during courtship?
a: Bowing, calling and raising its feathers
6328.e: In the courtship season the grey heron performs striking bows and calls and raises its ornamental feathers. This is how it woos the female near the nest.
6328.m: Courtship shows in bowing and calling.

6329.q: Where does the house sparrow like to build its nest?
6329.e: Sparrows like to nest in small holes in houses, for example under roof tiles. Their eggs are well protected there.
6329.m: Sparrows like to nest on houses.

6330.q: How do lionesses usually hunt their prey?
a: Together, with a plan, as a team
6330.e: Lionesses work well together when hunting. Some drive the prey while others wait in hiding and pounce.
6330.m: Lionesses hunt together as a team.

6331.q: What does the pupil of an adder look like?
6331.e: The pupil is a vertical slit, similar to a cat's. The grass snake, by contrast, has round pupils.
6331.m: Adders have a vertical slit pupil.

6332.q: What is the time called when a hen sits on her eggs to hatch them?
6332.e: During the incubation period the hen sits on her eggs almost without a break. She leaves the nest only briefly to eat and drink.
6332.m: During incubation the hen sits on the eggs.

a: Only in the middle of the night
6333.e: Most butterfly species fly around in sunlight. They need the warmth of the sun to be able to fly.

6334.q: What danger do young marmots face when they leave the burrow?
a: They can easily be caught by predators
The snow melts them at once
They cannot breathe outside the burrow
They lose their fur at once
6334.e: When young marmots leave the safe burrow for the first time, they are especially at risk. Eagles and other predators take advantage of the young ones' inexperience.
6334.m: Young marmots are especially at risk.

6335.q: What is different about the great crested grebe's wings compared with the rest of its body?
a: They are fairly short and make taking off from water hard work
They are huge and allow effortless gliding
They are longer than its whole body
6335.e: The fairly short wings suit swimming well but make take-off and flying harder. That is why the bird needs a long run-up.

6336.q: Which animal lives on Swiss farms and gives us milk?
6336.e: The cow eats grass and hay and gives milk in return. Milk is also used to make cheese and yoghurt.

6337.q: What do young whitefish eat first?
6337.e: Young whitefish are very small and can only take in tiny food. That is why they eat fine plankton.

6338.q: Why do you slip more easily on a smooth wooden floor in socks than in trainers?
a: The friction between socks and floor is smaller
6338.e: The rubber sole of trainers grips the floor well. Smooth fabric on smooth wood creates only a little friction, so you slip easily.

6339.q: What colour is the fur of a red kangaroo often?
6339.e: The red kangaroo usually has reddish brown fur, especially the males. Females can also be a little greyer.

6340.q: How heavy can a large lake trout get?
6340.e: Lake trout can grow much bigger than brown trout. Some weigh several kilograms, especially in big lakes.
6340.m: Lake trout can weigh several kilos.

6341.q: What are the soft cushions under a dog's paws called?
6341.e: The pads under the paws protect the dog when it walks and help it grip the ground. It can also sweat a little through its pads.
6341.m: Under the paws are the pads.

6342.q: Why should you not simply take lots of wild Roman snails home in Switzerland?
a: Because it is protected and should stay in nature
6342.e: The Roman snail is protected in Switzerland. So you should leave it in nature and not just take it away.

6343.q: Why is it important to separate young male guinea pigs early from their mother and sisters?
a: Because they can be able to breed at a very young age
Because otherwise they eat too little
Because otherwise they do not learn to talk
Because otherwise they lose their fur
6343.e: Young male guinea pigs can be able to breed within their first weeks of life. That is why they are separated in good time, so there are no unwanted babies.
6343.m: Young males can breed very early.

6344.q: What is the biggest penguin in the world called?
6344.e: The emperor penguin is the biggest and heaviest penguin species. It can grow over a metre tall.
6344.m: The emperor penguin is the biggest penguin.

6345.q: How does a mosquito larva breathe underwater?
a: Through a breathing tube at the water surface
Through its skin in the mud
6345.e: The larva often hangs upside down in the water and pokes a small breathing tube up to the surface. This is how it gets air even though it lives in water.

6346.q: Why do some red kites now spend the winter in Switzerland instead of flying south?
a: Milder winters give them enough food
They can no longer fly in winter
6346.e: Because of milder winters and extra food sources such as compost heaps, more and more red kites stay in Switzerland in winter. In the past, almost all of them left.
6346.m: Milder winters let some red kites stay.

6347.q: Where does the goldfish originally come from?
6347.e: The goldfish was bred in China more than a thousand years ago from the wild Prussian carp. Since then it has come in many colours.
6347.m: The goldfish originally comes from China.

6348.q: Which animals are the “Big Five” in Africa?
6348.e: The Big Five are the lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo. They used to be seen as especially hard to hunt; today they are mostly photographed.
6348.m: The leopard is one of the Big Five.

6349.q: How does the wood mouse move when it flees?
6349.e: When in danger, the wood mouse bounds away in quick leaps to reach its hiding place fast.

a: Living far from home because you are not safe there.
A big party in the palace.
A kind of prison just for children.
6350.e: People who are persecuted in their country sometimes flee abroad into exile. There they are safer from the dictatorship.
6350.m: In exile you live far from home.

6351.q: In which habitat does the fire salamander feel most at home?
a: In damp, shady broadleaved woods with streams
6351.e: Fire salamanders need damp, cool woods with clean streams nearby. There they find hiding places and water for their larvae.

6352.q: What size are most of the prey animals a common buzzard hunts?
a: Fairly small animals such as mice and insects
Almost always big animals such as deer
Only huge fish over a metre long
6352.e: Common buzzards usually catch small animals they can carry easily, mainly mice, small birds or insects. They lack the strength needed for larger animals such as deer.
6352.m: Prey is usually small and light.

6353.q: What does a least weasel do in winter, when it is cold?
a: It stays active in its territory and keeps hunting
It buries itself for months and sleeps
It travels high up into the Alps
6353.e: Because it has no big fat reserves, it must find food regularly even in the cold. Retreating for a long time would be too risky for the least weasel.
6353.m: It stays active even in winter.

a: Personality cult, political purges and mass terror against supposed enemies
Free elections and freedom of the press
An open market economy without state control
6354.e: Stalin had millions of people persecuted, deported or executed, often on invented charges. At the same time he was worshipped as an infallible leader.
6354.m: Stalinism was marked by terror and a personality cult.

6355.q: What does a budgie need every day besides its food?
6355.e: Like all animals, the budgie needs fresh drinking water every day. Without water it quickly gets ill.
6355.m: Budgies need fresh water every day.

6356.q: What role does the lynx play in the ecosystem?
a: As a predator it keeps the numbers of roe deer and other hoofed animals in check
It pollinates flowers like a bee
It spreads seeds in its fur
It has no important role because it is too rare
6356.e: As a natural predator, the lynx keeps the numbers of roe deer and other plant eaters in balance. This also benefits the forest, because fewer young trees are eaten.
6356.m: The lynx keeps the forest in balance.

6357.q: What does a least weasel mainly eat?
6357.e: Its German name ‘Mauswiesel’ (mouse weasel) comes from its love of mice, which it even follows into their tunnels. It kills its prey with a precise bite to the neck.
6357.m: The least weasel mainly hunts mice.

6358.q: What lets a red squirrel climb head first down a tree trunk?
a: Back feet that can turn round
6358.e: The squirrel's back feet can turn round almost 180 degrees. This lets it hold on well when climbing down, even head first.
6358.m: Turning feet help with head-first climbing.

6359.q: Why do banks sometimes charge fees for an account?
a: Because the bank has costs for running the account and its services
Because otherwise accounts would give out unlimited money for free
Because fees automatically go into the savings account
6359.e: Banks offer services such as cards, online banking or advice, and these cost money. Part of this is covered by account fees.
6359.m: Bank fees cover the cost of services.

6360.q: What is the best way to tell female and male great spotted woodpeckers apart?
a: Only the male has a red nape
Only the female has a red belly
6360.e: The female has no red patch on the back of the head. This makes it easy to tell the two apart.
6360.m: Only the male shows a red patch.

6361.q: How does an eagle owl mark its territory?
a: Mainly with scent marks like a fox
6361.e: Eagle owls mainly use their loud, deep calls to mark off their territory from other eagle owls. This often lets them settle disputes from a distance.
6361.m: The eagle owl marks its territory by calling.

6363.q: Which insect, whose larva lives in streams, is a favourite food of trout?
6363.e: Larvae of mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies live in streams. They are important food for trout.

6364.q: What happens to a beaver dam when it is damaged?
a: The beavers usually repair it the same night
6364.e: Beavers react very quickly to damage to their dam and usually fix leaks the same night. This shows how important a steady water level is to them.

6365.q: What does a hamster usually do during the day?
6365.e: During the day a hamster spends most of its time asleep in its sheltered nest. Only at dusk does it become really active.
6365.m: Hamsters sleep a lot during the day.

6367.q: Roughly what is the wingspan of a grey heron?
6367.e: With its wings spread, the grey heron measures almost two metres. That makes it one of the largest native birds.
6367.m: Its wings span almost two metres.

6368.q: What often makes a wasp look different from a bee?
a: The wasp is slimmer and shinier
The wasp is much smaller than an ant
6368.e: Wasps have a smooth, shiny body without much hair. Bees are usually furrier and rounder.
6368.m: Wasps are smooth, bees are furry.

6369.q: What sounds does a red squirrel make when it is upset or giving a warning?
a: It barks loudly like a dog
6369.e: When in danger, squirrels give short, scolding or chattering calls. This warns other squirrels.

6370.q: What exactly is a dust or sand bath for, for a sparrow?
6370.e: In a dust bath the sparrow spreads sand through its feathers, which helps against tiny parasites. Afterwards it shakes the dust off again and its feathers are in good condition.
6370.m: A dust bath keeps sparrow feathers in shape.

6371.q: What is it called when a trout swims from the sea back into a river to lay eggs?
6371.e: Some trout, such as the sea trout, swim back into rivers from far away to spawn there. This journey is called a spawning migration.
6371.m: The journey to spawn is a spawning migration.

6372.q: What does a starfish use to sense light?
a: Small light spots at the tips of its arms
It cannot see or sense anything
6372.e: At the tips of its arms the starfish has small light-sensing organs. This lets it tell light from dark.

6373.q: What is the body shape of a typical marten like?
a: A long, stretched body with short legs
A short, round body with long legs
A broad body with a shell
6373.e: Martens have a slim, long body and fairly short legs. This shape helps them squeeze skilfully through narrow gaps, burrows and holes in trees.

6374.q: What is it called when you teach a dog, for example, to sit or lie down?
6374.e: In dog training the dog learns new commands and behaviours. This is done with patience and rewards.
6374.m: The dog learns commands in training.

6375.q: How does the IUCN classify the threat to orangutans?
6375.e: All three species are considered critically endangered. Their habitat is shrinking fast.
6375.m: All orangutan species are severely threatened.

6376.q: Where does the banded demoiselle live?
a: On glaciers in the high mountains
6376.e: The banded demoiselle lives by gently flowing streams and rivers with plants on the banks. You can recognise the male by a dark blue band on its wings.

6377.q: Can a blue whale make loud sounds?
a: Yes, it is one of the loudest animals in the world
No, it can only whisper softly
6377.e: Blue whales give very deep, loud calls. Other whales can hear these sounds many kilometres away.

6378.q: How many countries in the Alpine region are home to Alpine ibex again today?
a: Several, for example Switzerland, Italy, Austria and France
None any more, the species is extinct everywhere
6378.e: Thanks to planned reintroductions, ibex live again in several Alpine countries, including Switzerland, Italy, Austria and France. All of today's populations go back to the animals saved in Gran Paradiso.
6378.m: Ibex live again in many Alpine countries.

6379.q: Which body feature do gibbons lack, unlike many other monkeys?
6379.e: Gibbons have no tail, just like the great apes and humans. Many monkeys, on the other hand, have a long tail.

6380.q: Where does a red squirrel usually build its nest?
a: High up in the fork of a branch
In a hole in the rock
6380.e: Squirrels like to build their nests high up in trees, often in the fork of a branch. There they are well protected from enemies.
6380.m: The nest is high up in the tree.

6381.q: Why do many months pass in martens between mating in summer and birth?
a: The embryo rests for a long time before it grows on
The mother goes into a long hibernation
The young hatch late from eggs
6381.e: After mating, the embryo rests for some months; this is called delayed implantation. So the young are only born in spring, when there is enough food.
6381.m: Delayed implantation pushes back the birth.

6382.q: In fly fishing for trout, an artificial fly is often used. What is it made of?
a: Feathers and thread, copying an insect
Shiny metal, shaped like a spoon
6382.e: Fly fishers tie small copies of insects out of feathers, hair and thread. They use them to fool hungry trout.

6383.q: What does a carp sense with the lateral line on its body?
a: Movements and currents in the water
6383.e: The lateral line is a row of fine sensory cells along the carp's body. With it the carp senses the tiniest movements and currents in the water.
6383.m: The lateral line senses water movements.

6384.q: Which monkey has a long silver-grey mane around its head and shoulders in the male?
6384.e: Male hamadryas baboons wear a silver-grey cape of long hair. In German that is where its name ‘Mantelpavian’ (cape baboon) comes from.
6384.m: The hamadryas baboon wears a cape of hair.

6385.q: What is the group of insects called that the wasp belongs to?
6385.e: Wasps, bees and ants belong to the Hymenoptera. This is a large group of insects with many species.

6386.q: What are a dog's babies called?
6386.e: Little dogs are called puppies. They are fed milk by their mother.

6387.q: What pattern does the coat of a red deer calf have?
a: Brown with a white stripe on the belly
6387.e: Calves have white spots on their coat. This camouflages them well in the sunlight between the leaves.
6387.m: Calves have white spots on their coat.

6388.q: What job does the lymphatic system have in the body?
a: It carries tissue fluid and supports the immune defences
It pumps blood around the body
6388.e: The lymphatic system collects extra fluid from the tissues and filters it in the lymph nodes. Germs are caught along the way.
6388.m: The lymphatic system supports your defences.

6389.q: Why are hyenas often rivals of lions?
a: They hunt similar prey and fight over meat
They live in trees like birds
6389.e: Hyenas hunt the same animals as lions and often fight over a kill. That is why there is often conflict between the two species.
6389.m: Hyenas and lions fight over prey.

6390.q: What happens to a penguin's feathers once a year?
a: It replaces all its feathers, which is called moulting
It gets a new beak colour
6390.e: Once a year a penguin loses its old feathers and grows new ones. This time is called the moult, and during it the penguin cannot swim.
6390.m: Penguins change their feathers every year.

6391.q: How does a robin usually fly between branches?
a: Over very long distances without a break
Not at all, it only hops
6391.e: The robin usually flies in short, quick hops from branch to branch. This is how it moves nimbly through the bushes.

6392.q: Roughly how long do young storks stay in the nest before they can fly?
6392.e: Young storks stay in the nest for about two months until their wings are strong enough to fly. Then they dare their first flight.
6392.m: Young storks fly after about two months.

6393.q: What does a female butterfly lay on leaves?
6393.e: The female lays her eggs on exactly the plants that the caterpillars will later be able to eat. This way the caterpillars find food as soon as they hatch.

6394.q: What do the tunnels of dung beetles do to the soil?
a: The soil becomes hard as concrete
Water can no longer soak in
6394.e: The tunnels let air and water get deeper into the earth. This helps plant roots and creatures living in the soil.
6394.m: Tunnels loosen and air the soil.

6395.q: What has the peregrine falcon been especially valued for by people for centuries?
a: For falconry, hunting with trained falcons
As an animal for pulling carts
6395.e: Because of its speed and hunting skills, the peregrine falcon has been used in falconry for a very long time. This tradition continues today.
6395.m: Falconry uses the falcon's hunting skills.

6396.q: What does an orca mother do when her calf is swimming?
a: She stays very close to it and protects it
She leaves it alone in the open sea
6396.e: The mother always swims right next to her calf. This lets her protect it from danger.
6396.m: The mother stays close to the calf.

6397.q: What is it called when ducklings follow their mother everywhere straight after hatching?
6397.e: Soon after hatching, ducklings remember the first moving creature they see. Usually it is their mother, whom they then follow everywhere.
6397.m: Ducklings imprint on their mother early.

6398.q: When do panda cubs open their eyes for the first time?
6398.e: Panda babies are born blind. Only after several weeks do their eyes slowly open.
6398.m: Panda babies open their eyes late.

6399.q: Where does the great spotted woodpecker usually sleep at night?
a: In a hole in a tree
6399.e: Even outside the breeding season it often sleeps in a hole in a tree. There it is well protected from wind and enemies.
6399.m: At night it sleeps in a tree hole.

6400.q: What happens when an unknown marmot enters a colony's territory?
a: The residents usually drive it away
It is welcomed at once as a new family member
It may take over the colony's burrow
The colony moves away at once
6400.e: Marmot colonies defend their territory against outsiders of their own kind. Intruders are usually driven off with threats or attacks.

a: A separate, small species of hippo
A horse that lives in a river
6401.e: The pygmy hippo is much smaller than the common hippo. It is a separate, rare species from West Africa.
6401.m: There is also a pygmy hippo.

6402.q: Which seal family does the harbour seal belong to?
6402.e: The harbour seal belongs to the true seal family. Eared seals such as the sea lion, by contrast, have small visible ears.

6403.q: Roughly how many bison lived in North America before they were heavily hunted in the 19th century?
6403.e: It is estimated that there were many millions of bison before the great hunt. Then their numbers dropped dramatically.
6403.m: Millions of bison once lived in North America.

6404.q: Which shark often lies quietly on the sea floor and is active at night?
6404.e: The nurse shark likes to rest on the bottom during the day. At night it goes hunting for small animals.
6404.m: The nurse shark rests on the sea floor by day.

6405.q: Which statement about the weight of peregrine falcons is true?
a: The female is much heavier than the male
Both weigh only a few grams
6405.e: A female weighs about one kilogram, a male only about 600 to 750 grams. In many birds of prey the females are bigger than the males.

6406.q: Roughly how big does an adult koala grow?
6406.e: An adult koala usually grows between 70 and 80 centimetres long. Males are often a little bigger than females.

6407.q: Which combination of colours does the fire salamander's typical pattern usually show?
6407.e: The black skin is patterned with bright yellow spots or stripes. Every animal has a unique pattern.
6407.m: Black with yellow spots is typical.

6408.q: How do roe deer usually live in winter?
a: Always alone deep in the forest
In huge herds of a hundred animals
6408.e: In winter, roe deer often join up in small groups. In German such a group is called a ‘Sprung’.
6408.m: In winter roe deer form small groups.

6410.q: Apart from plant food, what does the edible dormouse sometimes eat?
6410.e: Besides nuts, seeds and fruit, the edible dormouse sometimes eats insects or birds' eggs. This adds protein to its diet.
6410.m: Sometimes it eats insects and eggs too.

6411.q: Why is direct democracy an important difference between Switzerland and the EU?
a: In Switzerland citizens can vote directly on laws
In the EU all citizens vote directly on every law
6411.e: In Switzerland the people and the cantons can have a direct say through initiatives and referendums. The EU does not have this kind of direct participation in this form.
6411.m: Switzerland has direct popular votes, the EU does not.

6412.q: What are jaguars with almost black fur called?
6412.e: Dark jaguars are often called black panthers. Their rosettes can usually still be faintly seen in the dark fur.
6412.m: Black jaguars are called black panthers.

6413.q: Where are houseflies found especially often?
a: Where food or rubbish is lying around
High up in the mountains on glaciers
6413.e: Houseflies feel at home wherever they find food or rubbish. That is why you often find them near people.

a: So that it keeps longer and gets more flavour
So that it loses its colour
6414.e: Smoking preserves the fish and gives it a rich flavour. Smoked salmon is often eaten in thin slices.

6415.q: What is a debt advice centre in Switzerland for?
a: It helps people with debts get an overview and make a plan to pay them off
It gives loans to people in debt itself
6415.e: Debt advice centres help people who have lost track of their finances to sort out and reduce their debts. There are such centres in many cantons and municipalities.
6415.m: Debt advice helps you out of the debt trap.

6416.q: What is a fully scaled carp?
a: A carp with lots of small scales all over its body
A carp with almost no scales
A carp with only a few big scales
A carp with scales only on its head
6416.e: The fully scaled carp has lots of small scales all over its body. This makes it look different from mirror carp or leather carp.
6416.m: The fully scaled carp has small scales everywhere.

6418.q: What have researchers found out using small transmitters on the backs of swifts?
a: That outside the breeding season they almost never land
That they sleep on the ground every night
That they only fly very short distances
That they spend the winter in Switzerland
6418.e: Thanks to small transmitters, researchers could follow how swifts fly in detail. This showed that some birds do not land at all for months.
6418.m: Transmitters showed that swifts hardly land.

6419.q: Which helpful insect is often encouraged in organic gardens, for example with insect hotels?
6419.e: Lacewings like to spend the winter in sheltered hiding places. Their larvae eat lots of aphids.
6419.m: Insect hotels help lacewings in the garden.

6420.q: Is a Roman snail male or female?
6420.e: The Roman snail is a hermaphrodite. This means it has both male and female organs in one body.

6421.q: Do common toads croak as loudly as some frogs?
a: No, they make rather quiet sounds
Yes, very loudly like a frog
6421.e: Common toads are much quieter than many frog species. At most you hear a quiet peep or creak from them.
6421.m: Common toads are rather quiet animals.

6422.q: What does an octopus like to eat most?
6422.e: The octopus likes to hunt crabs, shellfish and small fish. With its hard beak it can even crack tough shells.
6422.m: The octopus eats crabs and shellfish.

6423.q: Who are bonobos most closely related to?
6423.e: Bonobos and chimpanzees are humans' closest living relatives. This shows, for example, in their genes.

6424.q: Why can fish that live deep down in a lake die out?
a: Because the deep water has too little oxygen
Because the water there is too salty
Because it is too bright there
Because there are too many waves there
6424.e: When too many nutrients get into a lake, a lot of oxygen is used up at the bottom. This is how a whitefish species of Lake Constance, the Bodenseekilch, died out.
6424.m: Without oxygen, fish in the depths die.

6425.q: Roughly how long do fox cubs grow inside their mother?
6425.e: The cubs grow inside the mother fox for almost two months. Then they are born in the fox's den.
6425.m: Fox cubs grow inside their mother for almost two months.

6426.q: What do you call programmed, natural cell death in the body?
6426.e: Apoptosis is a controlled process in which old or damaged cells die off in an orderly way. This is important for the growth and renewal of the body.

6427.q: What is it called when several male toads cling to one female?
6427.e: Sometimes several males cling to one female. This is called a toad ball. It can be exhausting for the female.

6428.q: Roughly how many species of isopods (woodlice and their relatives) live worldwide?
6428.e: There are several thousand species of isopods worldwide. Most live in the sea, some in fresh water and on land.
6428.m: There are thousands of isopod species.

6429.q: Which animal family does the badger actually belong to, even though many people would not think so?
6429.e: Scientifically, the badger belongs to the weasel family, also called Mustelidae. It looks different from a stone marten, but it is related to it.
6429.m: Badgers actually belong to the weasel family.

6430.q: What do ants do with aphids?
a: They milk them for sweet honeydew
They build their nest out of them
They carry them into the sky
6430.e: Aphids give off a sweet juice called honeydew. Ants stroke them with their antennae so they release this juice.

6431.q: What is a domesticated Bactrian camel also called?
6431.e: The domesticated Bactrian camel is also called the domestic camel. People have kept it for thousands of years.
6431.m: The tame form is called the domestic camel.

6432.q: What is the mating season of reindeer called?
6432.e: The mating season of deer is called the rut. In reindeer it takes place in autumn.
6432.m: The rut is the mating season.

6433.q: What are the elk's (moose's) long legs especially useful for?
a: For walking through deep snow and water
6433.e: With its long legs the elk gets through snow, bog and water. It can also reach higher branches.
6433.m: Long legs help in snow and bog.

6434.q: Where does a starfish feel most at home?
a: On the sea floor among stones and sand
In dry sand on the beach
6434.e: Starfish prefer to live on the sea floor, where there are stones, sand and rocks. They also find their food there.
6434.m: The sea floor is their home.

6435.q: How can you help slow worms in the garden?
a: With piles of leaves, stones and branches as hiding places
By mowing the lawn often during the day
6435.e: In such piles they find shelter and food. Poison would also harm their food and the slow worms themselves.

6436.q: What shape is the Alpine salamander's tail?
6436.e: The Alpine salamander's tail is round and not flattened at the sides like that of some water-dwelling amphibians. This suits its life on land.
6436.m: Its tail is round in shape.

6437.q: Roughly how long does a red squirrel's body grow (without the tail)?
6437.e: A squirrel's body is about 20 to 25 centimetres long. The tail adds almost the same length again.
6437.m: The body is about 20 to 25 centimetres long.

6438.q: How long is the lynx's tail compared with other cats?
a: The same length as a house cat's
It has no tail at all
6438.e: The lynx has a strikingly short tail with a black tip. This clearly sets it apart from other cats with long tails.
6438.m: The lynx has a short tail with a black tip.

6439.q: In which season are many native dung beetles especially active?
6439.e: When it is warm enough, the beetles fly and look for dung. In winter they withdraw because they are sensitive to cold.

6440.q: What is the yellow flower dust that bees collect called?
6440.e: Pollen is the fine dust from flowers that bees need as protein food. When it is stored in the hive it is also called bee bread.

6441.q: How many hoof parts does a goat have on each foot?
a: Two, it is an even-toed ungulate
One big hoof like a horse
6441.e: The goat is an even-toed ungulate and has two hoof parts on each foot. With them it walks safely even on uneven rocky ground.
6441.m: Goats have two hoof parts per foot.

6442.q: Which group of animals does the cockerel belong to?
6442.e: The cockerel is a bird, just like the hen. Birds have feathers and lay eggs.

6443.q: Which senses are especially good in the hedgehog, even though it sees poorly?
6443.e: Hedgehogs have poor eyesight, but they smell and hear very well. This is how they find their food in the dark.
6443.m: Hedgehogs smell and hear especially well.

6444.q: How does the colour of its coat help the lion when hunting?
a: To blend in with tall dry grass
6444.e: The sandy coat makes the lion almost disappear in dry grass. This lets it creep up on its prey unnoticed.
6444.m: Its colour camouflages the lion in the grass.

6445.q: What does the panda need its very strong molars for?
6445.e: Bamboo is hard and tough. That is why the panda has strong teeth and jaws to chew it well.

6446.q: What does the sand lizard mainly eat?
a: Insects, spiders and other small invertebrates
6446.e: The sand lizard is a meat eater and mainly hunts small arthropods such as grasshoppers, beetles and spiders. It grabs its prey with its mouth.
6446.m: Sand lizards hunt insects and spiders.

6447.q: Which group of animals does the guinea pig belong to?
6447.e: Despite its name, the guinea pig is not a pig but a rodent. Rabbits, on the other hand, belong to a different group with the hares.

6448.q: What is a delegation at the UN?
a: A group of people who represent a country at meetings
A sum of money for poor countries
A flag flying in front of the UN
6448.e: Every country sends a delegation to UN meetings so that it can give its opinion. The delegation is usually made up of diplomats.
6448.m: A delegation represents a country at meetings.

6449.q: What do a marmot's different whistles reveal?
a: They can point to different dangers
They always mean the same thing
6449.e: Researchers have seen that marmots give different-sounding alarm calls depending on the kind of danger, for example a bird or an animal on the ground. This lets the others react in the right way.

6450.q: What does a cow do when she calls her calf?
6450.e: A cow moos to keep in touch with her calf or to call it. This way mother and calf recognise each other even from a distance.

6451.q: What sound does the female cuckoo make?
6451.e: While the male calls “cuckoo”, the female makes a completely different, bubbling call. This lets you tell the two apart by their voices.
6451.m: The female sounds quite different from the male.

6452.q: What is the hard part at the bottom of a horse's foot called?
6452.e: The hoof is like a big, hard nail that protects the horse's foot. It keeps growing throughout its life.
6452.m: The hoof protects the horse's foot.

6453.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
6453.e: A little kangaroo is called a joey. At first it lives for a long time in its mother's pouch.

6454.q: What does it mean when an alpaca lays its ears back?
a: It is annoyed or warning others
It wants to play like a dog
6454.e: Ears laid back are a warning signal. Often spitting follows if the other animal does not back off.
6454.m: Ears laid back are a warning sign.

6455.q: What is the largest cat species in the Americas?
6455.e: The jaguar is the biggest cat on the American continent. The puma is smaller and more slimly built.
6455.m: The jaguar is the biggest cat in the Americas.

6456.q: Which element has the chemical symbol O?
6456.e: In the periodic table O stands for oxygen, a gas we need to breathe. It is one of the most common elements on Earth.

6457.q: How does the wood mouse move through tall grass or undergrowth?
a: It digs its way through stones
6457.e: In tall grass the wood mouse uses narrow paths it has made itself, so that it stays unseen.

6458.q: In which habitat does the okapi feel most at home?
6458.e: Okapis live in dense rainforest, where they are well hidden. You would hardly find them in the open savannah.

6459.e: Although the octopus lives in the sea, it is not a fish. It is a mollusc, more precisely a cephalopod.
6459.m: The octopus is not a fish.

6460.q: What does a budgie mainly eat?
6460.e: Budgies love pecking at small grass seeds and grains. Their beak is perfectly shaped for cracking them.

6462.q: What do ring-tailed lemurs mainly eat?
a: Plant parts such as fruit, leaves and flowers
6462.e: Ring-tailed lemurs mostly eat plants. Now and then they add insects to their diet.

6463.q: How does the common wall lizard usually move?
a: Quickly, wriggling on four short legs
6463.e: On its four short legs the wall lizard moves lightning fast with a slight wriggling motion. This lets it escape danger quickly.
6463.m: Fast and wriggling on the move.

6464.q: Which feature of the brown trout can you see particularly well in the photo?
a: Red spots with a pale ring
A big black spot on the tail
6464.e: The brown trout has red and black spots on its skin. The red spots are often surrounded by a pale ring.
6464.m: Red spots with a pale ring

6465.q: Why are bumblebees important for wildflower meadows?
a: Without pollination many flowers could not make seeds
They drive away all other insects
6465.e: Many wildflowers need insects such as the bumblebee to pollinate them. Without this help the plants could not reproduce.

6466.q: In which well-known fairy tale does a golden goose play the main role?
6466.e: In this fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm, a goose has golden feathers. Anyone who touches it gets stuck to it.
6466.m: A goose with golden feathers in a fairy tale.

6467.q: Where does a brown trout like to live?
a: In clear, cool streams and rivers
In the salt water of the ocean
6467.e: The brown trout needs clean, cool water to feel at home. That is why you often find it in mountain streams.
6467.m: Brown trout love cool, clear streams.

6468.q: Which predators can steal prey from African wild dogs?
6468.e: Lions and spotted hyenas sometimes steal the prey or kill wild dogs. That is why the packs often eat very quickly.

6469.q: What are the Alpine salamander's eyes like compared with its body?
6469.e: The Alpine salamander has fairly large, bulging dark eyes. They help it see well even when the light is poor.

6470.q: What does a bumblebee do when it gets too hot?
a: It flies into the blazing sun
It lies on a warm stone
6470.e: When the bumblebee gets too hot, it looks for cooler, shady places. This lets its body cool down again.
6470.m: Bumblebees look for shade in the heat.

6471.q: How is a donkey's tail different from a horse's tail?
a: A donkey's tail ends in a tuft of hair and is not hairy all along
A donkey's tail is exactly like a horse's
Donkeys have no tail at all
A donkey's tail is made of feathers
6471.e: A donkey's tail usually has short hair except for a tuft at the tip, whereas horses have a completely bushy tail. This is a good way to tell them apart.
6471.m: A donkey's tail has just a tuft.

6472.q: Do sparrows sometimes bathe in water too?
6472.e: Besides dust baths, sparrows also like a bath in a puddle now and then. This keeps their feathers clean and fresh.
6472.m: Sparrows sometimes bathe in water too.

6473.q: What kind of living thing are aphids in the food web?
6473.e: Aphids are food for many animals, such as beetles, fly larvae and birds. This makes them an important link in the food chain.
6473.m: Aphids are important prey in the food web.

6474.q: Why does it sometimes look as if a sea turtle is crying?
a: It gets rid of extra salt through its eyes
It has sand in its eyes
6474.e: Special glands help the turtle get rid of the extra salt from sea water. A salty liquid runs out of its eyes that looks like tears.

6475.q: Roughly how long are baboons pregnant?
