6475.e: Pregnancy lasts about 180 days, roughly half a year. Then usually one baby is born.
6475.m: Baboon pregnancy lasts about half a year.

6476.q: Roughly how big does a house sparrow grow?
6476.e: A sparrow is about as long as a hand, about 15 centimetres. That is quite small for a bird.
6476.m: A sparrow is about the size of a hand.

6477.q: What is one feature of the African wild dog's coat?
a: Each animal has a different pattern
It is the same plain colour on all of them
6477.e: The patches of black, yellow, brown and white are different on every animal. This makes it possible to recognise individual animals.
6477.m: No two wild dogs look the same.

6478.q: In what form is eel a well-known speciality in northern Germany?
6478.e: Smoked eel is considered a delicacy and is especially well known in northern Germany and Denmark. The fish is very rich in fat.
6478.m: Smoked eel is a well-known speciality.

6479.q: What is the rough hair on a wild boar’s back called?
6479.e: Stiff, rough hairs called bristles grow on the wild boar’s back. They can stand up when the animal is excited.
6479.m: The rough hair is called bristles.

6480.q: What is the umbrella-shaped part of a jellyfish called?
6480.e: The soft upper part of a jellyfish is called the bell. It looks like an umbrella or a bell.
6480.m: That body part is called the bell.

6481.q: Which bird is often confused with the common swift but belongs to a completely different bird family?
6481.e: Swallows look similar to swifts, but they are more closely related to perching birds. Swifts belong to their own order of birds, the swifts.
6481.m: Swallows and swifts are not related.

6482.q: Where does a sea turtle such as the olive ridley turtle lay its eggs?
a: In the sand on a beach
In a nest in a tree
In a rocky cave under water
6482.e: Sea turtles come ashore to lay their eggs. They dig a hole in the sand on the beach and lay their eggs in it.
6482.m: Sea turtles lay their eggs in the sand.

6484.q: What do you call animals that cannot control their own body temperature?
6484.e: The adder depends on the temperature around it. That is why it often basks in the sun.
6484.m: Cold-blooded means the warmth comes from outside.

6485.q: What is the largest kangaroo in the world called?
6485.e: The red kangaroo is the largest kangaroo species. Males can be almost two metres tall when they stand upright.
6485.m: The red kangaroo is the biggest.

6486.q: Apart from protecting them, what job does a cockerel have in a group of hens?
a: He shows them where food is
6486.e: When a cockerel finds food, he often calls the hens over and shares it with them. Sitting on the eggs, on the other hand, is usually done by the hens.
6486.m: The cockerel shares food with the hens.

6487.q: What are spiders that specialise in hunting woodlice called?
6487.e: Woodlouse hunters have very large fangs. They use them to pierce the hard shell of woodlice.
6487.m: Some spiders hunt woodlice on purpose.

6488.q: Roughly how many eggs does a female lay in one nest?
6488.e: A female often lays around a hundred eggs in the sand at once. That way, despite many dangers, a few young have a chance to survive.
6488.m: Usually about a hundred eggs per nest.

6489.q: Why is a penguin’s white belly useful in the water?
a: From below it looks like bright light from the sky
6489.e: Seen from below, the white belly blends in with the bright light at the surface of the water. This is called camouflage and it protects the penguin from enemies.
6489.m: A white belly hides the penguin from below.

6490.q: How many calves does a female elephant usually have at one time?
6490.e: Normally only one calf is born. Twins are very rare.
6490.m: Usually only one calf is born.

6491.q: What are the hard front wings of a cockchafer called?
6491.e: The hard front wings are called wing cases. They protect the delicate back wings, which are used for flying.
6491.m: Wing cases protect the back wings.

6492.q: When does a lion prefer to hunt?
6492.e: Lions see very well in the dark and take advantage of this. In the evening and at night their prey cannot see as well.

6493.q: What colour are the vocal sacs of many male pool frogs?
6493.e: The vocal sacs at the corners of the males’ mouths are often greyish or whitish. They puff up a lot when the frog calls.
6493.m: Vocal sacs are usually greyish white.

6494.q: Which planet is called the “red planet” because of its colour?
6494.e: Mars looks reddish because there is a lot of rusty iron oxide on its surface. It is the fourth planet from the sun.
6494.m: Mars glows red because of iron dust.

6495.q: What covers a goldfish’s skin and protects its body?
6495.e: A goldfish’s skin is covered with small scales that protect its body. The skin also gives off slime, which protects it too.

6496.q: What does a silverback do when it feels threatened?
a: It beats its chest with its hands
It lies flat on the ground
6496.e: Chest beating is a loud warning signal. With it, the silverback shows that it is strong.

6497.q: Where does the edible dormouse usually spend its hibernation?
a: In burrows deep in the ground
At the tops of tall trees
6497.e: For hibernation the edible dormouse digs deep into the ground or uses existing burrows. There it is well protected from frost.
6497.m: It hibernates deep in the ground.

6499.q: How can an edible dormouse escape from an attacker that has grabbed its tail?
a: It sheds the skin of its tail
It bites off its own tail
6499.e: When in danger, the skin of the dormouse’s tail can come loose so that it can escape. The bare end of the tail usually heals afterwards.
6499.m: The tail skin can come off in danger.

6501.q: Which striking feature does the tawny owl lack, unlike the long-eared owl?
6501.e: The tawny owl has no tufts of feathers on its head that look like ears. The long-eared owl, however, has clearly visible ear tufts.
6501.m: The tawny owl has no ear tufts.

6502.q: How does a chamois’s coat change over the year?
a: It becomes thicker and darker in winter
It falls out completely in winter
6502.e: The chamois’s coat adapts to the changing seasons. In winter it is thicker and darker, in summer short and reddish.
6502.m: Chamois have a summer coat and a winter coat.

6503.q: How do meerkats react to an alarm about a bird of prey?
a: They run quickly into the nearest burrow
6503.e: When the alarm sounds, the animals run to the nearest entrances and disappear into the burrow. There they are safe from birds.
6503.m: When the alarm sounds, it’s into the burrow.

6504.e: Even newborn adders have working venom glands. But they are very small and well hidden.

6505.q: Roughly how long do reindeer live in the wild?
6505.e: Wild reindeer usually live to about ten to fifteen years. Predators and harsh winters often shorten their lives.

6506.q: What often happens when two bearded vulture chicks hatch?
a: Usually only the stronger chick survives
Both chicks always grow to the same size
The parents feed only the weaker one
6506.e: Because food can be scarce, the chick that hatched first and is stronger often wins. The weaker sibling then usually dies.

6507.q: Roughly how old can a wild badger get?
a: A few years, often eight to ten
6507.e: In the wild, badgers reach an age of several years, and some even live over ten years. It also depends on luck in surviving dangers.
6507.m: Wild badgers often live for several years.

6508.q: How does a bonobo’s build compare with a chimpanzee’s?
a: With shorter legs and flaps of skin for gliding
6508.e: Bonobos look more delicate than chimpanzees. They have narrower shoulders and slightly longer legs.

6509.q: What was the South Vietnamese city of Saigon renamed after the communist victory in 1975?
6509.e: After the end of the Vietnam War, the victorious communists renamed Saigon after their late leader Ho Chi Minh. Today the city is Vietnam’s economic centre.
6509.m: Since 1975 Saigon has been called Ho Chi Minh City.

6510.q: What happens when there is a lot of food at bird feeders in winter?
a: More great tits survive the winter
The great tits fly away at once
6510.e: When there is enough food, great tits have a better chance of surviving the winter. Extra feeding helps especially in cold, snowy winters.
6510.m: Enough food helps great tits in winter.

6511.q: What are spotted hyenas especially good at thanks to their strong teeth?
6511.e: Their powerful jaws and teeth can even break thick bones. That way they get at the nutritious marrow.
6511.m: Hyenas crack bones with their strong teeth.

6512.q: Why do tigers often go into the water?
a: To cool down on hot days
Because they are afraid of water
Because other cats do it too
6512.e: Tigers like water and enjoy using it to cool down when it is hot. Sometimes they even hunt in the water.
6512.m: Tigers cool down in the water.

6513.q: What is the scientific name of the wolf?
6513.e: The wolf belongs to the dog family and its scientific name is Canis lupus. All pet dogs are descended from it.
6513.m: The wolf’s scientific name is Canis lupus.

6514.q: How can you sometimes tell a male barn swallow from a female?
a: By its longer outer tail feathers
By a completely different body colour
By the fact that it has no tail
6514.e: Male barn swallows often have slightly longer outer tail feathers than females. Long tail feathers are seen as especially attractive when choosing a partner.
6514.m: Males often have longer tail feathers.

6515.q: In pool frogs, which is usually bigger, the male or the female?
a: Both are always exactly the same size
It depends only on the weather
6515.e: Female pool frogs usually grow a little bigger than males. Males, on the other hand, can often be recognised by their vocal sacs.
6515.m: Females are usually bigger than males.

6516.q: How does seawater get into a starfish’s system of tubes?
a: Through a small sieve plate on its back
Through the eyes at the tips of its arms
6516.e: On its upper side the starfish has a small sieve plate. Seawater gets into its system of tubes through it, and this moves its tiny feet.
6516.m: A sieve plate lets water in.

6517.q: How often a year does a stoat change its coat?
6517.e: The stoat changes its coat twice a year, once in spring and once in autumn. That way it adapts to the seasons.
6517.m: The coat changes twice a year.

6518.q: What does a kangaroo do when it notices danger?
6518.e: When a kangaroo senses danger, it thumps its back foot loudly on the ground. This warns other kangaroos nearby.
6518.m: Kangaroos thump when there is danger.

6519.q: What does the stone marten especially like to eat as well in autumn?
a: Sweet fruit such as cherries and apples
6519.e: In autumn the stone marten changes its diet and eats more ripe fruit. This gives it important energy for the coming winter.
6519.m: In autumn the stone marten likes to eat fruit.

6520.q: What do you call animals like the wood mouse that mainly eat plants but sometimes insects too?
6520.e: The wood mouse mostly eats plants, but sometimes small insects too. That is why it is called an omnivore.
6520.m: The wood mouse is an omnivore.

6521.q: How can you recognise a wood mouse?
a: By its large eyes, large ears and pale belly
6521.e: The wood mouse has strikingly large eyes and ears, a long tail and a pale belly. Its back is brown.
6521.m: The wood mouse has large eyes and ears.

6522.q: A stone lies at the top of a cliff. What kind of energy does it mainly have there?
6522.e: The stone is not moving, but because of its height it has potential energy. If it falls, this turns into energy of movement, kinetic energy.
6522.m: Movement is kinetic, position is potential.

6523.q: What does the edible dormouse especially like to eat in autumn to build up fat reserves?
6523.e: In autumn the edible dormouse collects energy-rich beechnuts and nuts. These help it store enough fat for hibernation.
6523.m: Beechnuts provide energy for the winter.

6524.q: What special feature of cats’ eyes also helps the jaguar?
a: A reflective layer that uses leftover light
6524.e: Behind the retina there is a layer that reflects light (tapetum lucidum). This helps the jaguar see better at night and makes its eyes shine in headlights.
6524.m: Cats’ eyes make the most of faint light.

6525.q: How do gibbons usually move compared with orangutans?
a: Much faster and with more swing
Much more slowly, they hardly climb
6525.e: Gibbons are very fast, agile swingers. Orangutans move more carefully in the trees.
6525.m: Gibbons are the gymnasts of the forest.

6526.q: What happens if you put washing-up liquid in water that a pond skater is standing on?
a: It sinks because the water’s skin gets weaker
6526.e: The pond skater is held up by surface tension, a kind of skin on the water. Washing-up liquid weakens this skin and the insect sinks.
6526.m: The water’s skin carries the pond skater.

6527.q: Do sea turtles have visible ears like us humans?
a: No, they have no outer ears
Yes, big ears like a hare
6527.e: Sea turtles have no outer ears. Even so, they can sense sounds and vibrations in the water.

6528.q: What is a baby red deer called?
6528.e: A young red deer is called a calf, just like a young cow. It is usually born in early summer.
6528.m: Young red deer are called calves.

6529.q: What does the red kite eat?
a: Only large mammals such as roe deer
6529.e: The red kite is not fussy. It eats small mammals, dead animals, earthworms, insects and sometimes small birds.
6529.m: The red kite eats almost anything it finds.

6530.q: How does the red kite typically hunt over fields, compared with the hovering of many other birds of prey?
a: It glides elegantly and nimbly and rarely hovers
It hovers all the time like a kestrel
It hunts by walking on the ground
It dives into the water like a kingfisher
6530.e: While the kestrel often hovers in one spot in the air, the red kite soars and glides elegantly and nimbly over the fields. Only rarely does it hover briefly to get a better look at prey.
6530.m: The red kite glides elegantly instead of hovering.

6531.q: On which continent do mountain gorillas live?
6531.e: Mountain gorillas live high up in mountain forests in Africa. It is cool and often misty there.
6531.m: Mountain gorillas live in the mountains of Africa.

6532.q: How does a praying mantis sometimes react when threatened?
a: It rears up and spreads its catching legs and wings
6532.e: This makes it look bigger and more dangerous. It is meant to scare enemies away.
6532.m: A threat pose is meant to scare enemies away.

6533.q: What does “cold-blooded” mean for the slow worm?
a: Its body temperature depends on its surroundings
It changes colour depending on the weather
It has warm fur in winter
It always produces 37 degrees of body heat
6533.e: Cold-blooded animals can hardly control their own temperature. For example, they warm up in the sun.
6533.m: For the cold-blooded slow worm, the surroundings set its body temperature.

6534.q: What danger do poisoned mouse baits pose to red kites in particular?
a: They can be poisoned by the poison in the mice
They lose their feathers because of it
They stop laying eggs because of it
They grow too fast because of it
6534.e: If red kites eat poisoned mice, they can die of the poisoning. This so-called secondary poisoning is one of the biggest dangers to the species.
6534.m: Poison baits also put the red kite in danger.

6535.q: What does the great tit do when a bigger bird comes into its territory?
a: It immediately builds a new nest
6535.e: When there is danger, the great tit gives loud alarm calls. This also warns other birds nearby.
6535.m: Alarm calls signal danger in the territory.

6536.q: What does a jellyfish lack compared with a fish?
6536.e: A fish has scales and fins, but a jellyfish does not. Instead, the jellyfish moves by squeezing its bell.
6536.m: A jellyfish has no scales or fins.

6537.q: How do bonobos often behave when eating?
a: They sometimes share food with each other
They only eat alone at night
They fight over every single fruit
6537.e: Bonobos often share food, for example with group members they know well. This strengthens their life together.

a: A body of ice and dust in space with a tail
6538.e: Comets are made of frozen water, dust and rock and travel round the sun on a long path. Near the sun their surface melts a little and a glowing tail forms.
6538.m: Comets are made of ice and dust and have a tail.

6539.q: What does it mean when a plant or animal species is on the Red List?
6539.e: The Red List names species whose numbers have fallen sharply or that are threatened with extinction. It helps to plan protection measures.
6539.m: The Red List shows threatened species.

6540.q: Does a centipede such as the stone centipede really have a hundred legs?
a: No, usually only 15 pairs of legs
No, only eight legs like a spider
Yes, even over a thousand legs
6540.e: Adult stone centipedes have 15 pairs of walking legs, so 30 legs. The name centipede only means that they have many legs.
6540.m: The name and the number of legs don’t match exactly.

a: Yes, it has thin wings under its wing cases
No, it jumps a long way instead
6541.e: Under its hard, colourful wing cases the ladybird has delicate flying wings. With them it can fly from leaf to leaf or even further.

6542.q: Which country was united under communist rule after a long war?
6542.e: In the Vietnam War, the communist North fought against the South. In 1975 the North won and the country was united.

6543.q: Why do some gardeners get annoyed with moles?
a: Because the molehills make the lawn bumpy
6543.e: Molehills bother some gardeners because they make a nice lawn look bumpy. But the hills don’t harm the soil itself.

6544.q: What colour is the iris, the ring around the pupil, of the common toad often?
6544.e: The common toad’s iris often shimmers gold or copper. You can see this especially well if you look very closely.

6545.q: Roughly how old can a European tree frog get in the wild?
6545.e: In the wild, tree frogs can live up to ten years in good conditions. In captivity some have lived even longer.
6545.m: They can live up to ten years.

6546.q: What is a beaver’s dam mainly for?
a: To raise the water level and protect the lodge entrance
6546.e: The dam raises the water level so that the entrance to the beaver lodge always stays under water. This protects the beavers from enemies on land.
6546.m: Dams protect the entrance to the lodge.

6547.q: Why do jackals sometimes come into conflict with farmers?
a: They can kill lambs or poultry
6547.e: Jackals take easy prey, including farm animals. That is why farmers often protect their herds with fences or dogs.
6547.m: Farm animals are sometimes easy prey.

6548.q: Which organ do you need to breathe?
6548.e: When you breathe in, the lungs take oxygen from the air, and when you breathe out they give off carbon dioxide. We have two lungs in our chest.

6549.q: Where does the Amur leopard you see in the photo live?
a: In the east of Russia and the north-east of China
6549.e: The Amur leopard lives in forests in the Russian Far East and neighbouring China. It is one of the rarest big cats in the world.
6549.m: Amur leopards live in the Far East.

6550.q: What happens to the female after she has laid her eggs?
6550.e: Most females die after laying their eggs. They do not look after their young.
6550.m: Females die after laying their eggs.

6551.q: How do donkeys groom each other to show affection?
a: They nibble each other’s backs and necks
They wash each other in a lake
They comb each other with their hooves
They shake water over each other
6551.e: Donkeys that are friends often nibble and rub each other on the neck and back. This mutual grooming strengthens their friendship.

6554.q: Which group of animals does the beaver belong to?
6554.e: The beaver is a rodent, like mice and squirrels. Typical of this group are front teeth that keep growing all the time.

6555.q: Which animal lives in the sea but breathes with lungs like you?
6555.e: Whales are mammals and have to come up to the surface to breathe air. Fish, on the other hand, breathe with gills.

6556.q: Who usually leads a wolf pack?
6556.e: In a wolf pack it is usually the parents, the leading pair, who take charge. All the other animals are their offspring.
6556.m: The parent pair leads the pack.

6557.q: The green woodpecker is a relative of the great spotted woodpecker. What does it like to eat most?
6557.e: The green woodpecker often searches the ground in meadows for ants. It uses its long tongue to pull them out of their tunnels.

6558.q: At what time of day do barn swallows usually migrate?
a: During the day, as they hunt along the way
Only at night in the dark
6558.e: Unlike many other migratory birds, barn swallows migrate during the day. That way they can hunt insects at the same time on their journey.
6558.m: They migrate by day and hunt as they go.

6559.q: What colour are a common raven’s feathers typically?
6559.e: The common raven’s feathers are jet black and often shimmer bluish purple in the sunlight. This sheen comes from the structure of the feathers.
6559.m: Black feathers with a metallic sheen.

6560.q: How many young does a rabbit usually have per litter?
6560.e: A litter usually has four to eight baby rabbits. Sometimes there are a few more or fewer.

6561.q: What does the henhouse protect the hens from at night?
6561.e: A well-secured henhouse keeps predators such as the fox away at night. That way the hens are safe while they sleep.
6561.m: The henhouse protects against the fox.

6562.q: What do hens do when a bird of prey is circling in the sky?
a: They warn each other and run for cover
They stay lying calmly in the sun
They fly onto the roof of the henhouse
6562.e: When hens spot danger from the air, they give a special alarm call. All the hens then quickly look for shelter.
6562.m: Hens warn each other of danger from the air.

6563.q: Which ape is the chimpanzee’s closest relative?
6563.e: The bonobo looks similar to the chimpanzee and belongs to the same genus. Both are close relatives of humans.
6563.m: The bonobo is the chimpanzee’s closest relative.

6564.q: How does a bison clear away snow in winter to get to the grass?
a: With swinging movements of its head
By using its horns as a shovel in the air
With its mouth like a digger
6564.e: Bison swing their heads from side to side and push the snow aside. Underneath they find grass.
6564.m: Bison shovel snow with their heads.

6565.q: What is the name of the mosquito species that has also been found in southern Switzerland for some years?
6565.e: The tiger mosquito originally comes from Asia and was brought here through travel. It feels especially at home in warm Ticino.
6565.m: The tiger mosquito came from Asia.

6566.q: Roughly how far can a tiger jump?
6566.e: Tigers can jump a very long way, which helps them when hunting. One leap can be several metres long.
6566.m: Tigers can jump a long way.

6567.q: What does an Alpine marmot mainly eat?
6567.e: Marmots are plant-eaters and feed on the grasses, herbs and flowers of Alpine meadows. Sometimes they also eat roots or seeds.
6567.m: Marmots eat plants from Alpine meadows.

6568.q: What position do meerkats often take when warming up in the sun?
a: They stand upright with their belly towards the sun
They roll up into a ball
6568.e: With their bellies facing the sun they soak up warmth. It often looks as if they are sunbathing.

6569.q: What is the time before Christmas called, when one more candle is lit every Sunday?
6569.e: During Advent Christians look forward to Christmas. On the Advent wreath one more candle burns each Sunday.
6569.m: Advent is looking forward to Christmas.

6570.q: What does the pond skater’s remarkable ability show in physics?
6570.e: The pond skater is a good way to explain how water can form a surface that carries weight. Scientists also study how it moves.
6570.m: It shows the effect of surface tension.

6571.q: Why has Pluto no longer counted as a full planet since 2006?
a: It has not cleared its orbit of other objects
It has no moon of its own
It is too close to the Sun
It is not made of rock
6571.e: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union defined new criteria for planets. Because Pluto does not fully meet them, it was declared a dwarf planet.
6571.m: Since then Pluto has counted as a dwarf planet.

6572.q: What do rabbits like to eat most?
6572.e: Rabbits are plant-eaters and especially like fresh grass and hay. Herbs and some vegetables are also part of their diet.

6573.q: Which people used to keep many llamas in the Andes?
6573.e: The Inca used llamas for transport and wool. They were also important as sacrificial animals.
6573.m: The Inca relied heavily on llamas.

6574.q: What kind of animal is a moray?
a: An eel-like sea fish with powerful jaws
6574.e: Morays are eel-like fish and live in warm seas. They often hide in cracks in the rocks.

6575.q: What does the female need her ovipositor for?
a: To lay eggs in the soil
To defend herself like a sting
6575.e: With her ovipositor the female pushes the eggs carefully into the ground. There the eggs are well protected.

6576.q: Roughly how many different colours and shapes are there in bred goldfish?
a: Very many, for example orange, white, black and spotted
6576.e: Thanks to centuries of breeding, goldfish today come in many colours and with different fin shapes. Some look very different from their wild ancestor.

6577.q: Why did the ancient Romans keep edible dormice in special clay pots?
a: To fatten them up and eat them
To give them away as lucky charms
To use them as guard animals
6577.e: The Romans fed edible dormice in special clay pots until they were nice and fat. They were then considered a special delicacy.
6577.m: Romans fattened dormice in clay pots.

6578.q: In which country do most kangaroos live?
6578.e: Kangaroos originally come from Australia. There are many different species there.

6579.q: Roughly how far can a snow leopard jump?
6579.e: With its powerful back legs it can make very long leaps. This helps it in rugged terrain.
6579.m: It jumps up to about 15 metres.

6580.q: How do male and female great crested grebes differ in appearance?
a: Hardly at all, they look very alike
Only the male has a crest
The female is twice as big
6580.e: Male and female great crested grebes hardly differ in appearance. Both have the same crest and ruff.
6580.m: Both sexes look almost the same.

6581.q: Why can you see through a window pane but not through a wall?
a: Glass lets light through, a wall does not
Glass is colder than a wall
Glass is always cleaner than a wall
A wall is always a darker colour
6581.e: Glass is transparent, which means light can shine through it almost unhindered. A stone wall is opaque and lets no light through.

6582.q: What do you call people whose job is training dogs?
6582.e: Dog trainers teach dogs good behaviour and commands together with their owners. They often work at dog training schools.

6583.q: What do most woodlice breathe with?
a: With modified legs that work like gills
With breathing holes on the head
6583.e: Woodlice have gill-like breathing organs on their back legs. These must stay moist, which is why woodlice need damp places.

6585.q: What do you only very rarely see blue whales do?
a: Jump right out of the water
Show their back at the surface
6585.e: Some whales like to jump right out of the water. But blue whales are so huge and heavy that you only rarely see them do it.
6585.m: Blue whales rarely jump out of the water.

6586.q: What does it mean that the snow leopard is endangered?
a: There are only a few animals left and the number is falling
6586.e: The species is on the Red List and is considered threatened. Poaching and loss of habitat are the reasons.
6586.m: The snow leopard is under threat.

6587.q: What are the kingfisher’s legs like compared with its body?
a: It has no visible legs at all
6587.e: The kingfisher’s legs are strikingly short and reddish. It hardly uses them for walking, as it spends most of its time perching or flying.
6587.m: The kingfisher has very short legs.

6589.q: What shape is the pupil in a European tree frog’s eye?
6589.e: The tree frog’s pupils are horizontal and oval. This gives it a wide field of view so that it can spot predators early.
6589.m: Horizontal pupils give a good overview.

6590.q: Which coat pattern do lion cubs have that adult lions no longer have?
6590.e: Lion cubs often have spots in their fur to protect them from enemies. These fade as they get older.
6590.m: Lion cubs have spots at first.

6591.q: How often does a mallard usually breed per year?
a: Usually once, sometimes there is a replacement brood
6591.e: Normally a mallard raises its ducklings once a year. If the first clutch is lost, it sometimes tries again.
6591.m: There is usually one brood per year.

6592.q: Why should a budgie never be kept completely alone?
a: Because it is a sociable flock bird
Because otherwise it flies too fast
Because otherwise it grows too big
Because it is afraid of water
6592.e: In the wild, budgies live in large flocks and need company. On their own they feel very lonely.
6592.m: Budgies need the company of other budgies.

6593.q: What does the mother earwig do with her eggs?
a: She buries them deep and goes away
6593.e: The female stays with the eggs and defends them. By cleaning them she also protects them from fungi.
6593.m: Earwig mothers look after their eggs.

6594.q: How is the African wild dog classified by the IUCN?
6594.e: According to the IUCN Red List, the species is endangered. There are only a few thousand animals left.

6595.q: What does a robin’s song usually sound like?
a: Clear and melodic, like a string of pearls
6595.e: The robin sings with many different notes that sound clear and beautiful. Many people find its song especially lovely.

6596.q: How fast can a giraffe run?
6596.e: Despite their size, giraffes can run surprisingly fast. Over short distances they almost reach the speed of a car in town.

6597.q: Roughly how big does an adult Alpine newt get?
6597.e: The Alpine newt is one of the smaller newt species in Europe. Fully grown, it reaches a length of about 7 to 12 centimetres.
6597.m: Alpine newts grow to about 10 centimetres.

6598.q: What are the small horns on a giraffe’s head called?
6598.e: The small, fur-covered horns are called ossicones. Almost all giraffes have them, whether male or female.

6599.q: How long is a ring-tailed lemur’s tail compared with its body?
a: Longer than its head and body together
About half as long as its body
6599.e: At over 50 centimetres, the tail is longer than the head and body. That is why it catches the eye straight away.
6599.m: The tail is longer than the body.

6600.q: Which sense organ does a cockerel mainly use to spot danger early?
6600.e: Cockerels have very good eyes and use them to spot movement and danger from far away. The sense of smell plays a smaller role in chickens.
6600.m: The cockerel sees danger with his eyes.

6601.q: How does a rhinoceros usually move when it is not running?
6601.e: Normally a rhino walks slowly and leisurely to save energy. Only when it senses danger does it start running fast.
6601.m: Rhinos usually walk slowly and calmly.

6602.q: Where do chimpanzees sleep at night?
a: In nests made of branches in trees
6602.e: Every evening chimpanzees build a new nest of branches high in the trees. There they are safe from enemies.
6602.m: Chimpanzees build a new nest every night.

6603.q: Where does the pike most like to hide while lying in wait?
a: In the middle of the open lake
High above the water on a branch
6603.e: Among thick water plants the pike can camouflage itself well. From there it watches the fish swimming past.
6603.m: Water plants are the best hiding place.

6604.q: Apart from nuts, what else does a squirrel eat?
a: Mushrooms, buds and sometimes birds’ eggs
6604.e: Squirrels are omnivores. Besides nuts they also eat mushrooms, buds, fruit and occasionally birds’ eggs.
6604.m: Squirrels also eat mushrooms and buds.

6605.q: What do ducks like to eat most in the wild?
a: Water plants, small insects and snails
6605.e: Ducks are not fussy and eat lots of things around the water. They like plants, small animals and seeds.
6605.m: Ducks eat plants and small animals.

6606.q: What often happens when a young wolf grows up?
a: It leaves the pack to look for its own territory
It immediately becomes leader of its own pack
It stays with its parents for ever
It loses its ability to hunt
6606.e: Many young wolves move away once they are fully grown to find their own territory and a partner. This also allows wolves to spread over large areas.
6606.m: Young wolves often leave the pack.

6607.q: When is the jaguar usually most active?
6607.e: The jaguar mainly hunts at dusk and at night. During the day it often rests in the shade.

6608.q: How many young does a female llama usually have at one time?
6608.e: A female llama usually gives birth to one young. Twins are very rare.
6608.m: Usually only one young is born.

6609.q: In which habitat are slow worms often found in Switzerland?
a: In gardens, at the edges of woods and in meadows
6609.e: It is widespread in Switzerland, mostly in the lowlands and in mountain areas. It needs cover and moisture.
6609.m: Gardens and woodland edges are its home.

6610.q: What can you often see as a shiny trail after a Roman snail has crawled past?
6610.e: The snail leaves a shiny trail of slime on the ground. That is how you can tell a snail has been there.
6610.m: The trail shines because of the slime.

6611.q: What makes the European tree frog especially different from many other European frog species?
a: It lives much more in trees and bushes than on the ground
6611.e: While most native frogs live on the ground or in the water, the tree frog often stays in bushes and trees. This makes it an exception among European frogs.
6611.m: A tree-living frog among the European species.

a: A particularly small breed of rabbit
A baby rabbit of any breed
A wild rabbit from the desert
6612.e: Dwarf rabbits are a breed of their own that stays very small even when fully grown. They are popular pets with children.

6613.q: Where are carp often bred in large numbers?
6613.e: For carp farming, special ponds are made; this is called pond farming. There the carp grow up in large numbers.

6614.q: How do jackal parents feed their pups once they need solid food?
a: They put seeds in their mouths
6614.e: The parents carry food in their stomachs to the den and bring it back up there. That way the pups can eat it easily.
6614.m: Parents bring up food for the pups.

6615.q: How does a red deer calf call for its mother?
a: With a growl like a bear
6615.e: A calf calls its mother with a high, soft sound. This sound is called a bleat.
6615.m: Calves call with a soft squeak.

6616.q: Why are ticks important for health in Switzerland?
a: They can pass on diseases such as Lyme disease
6616.e: Ticks are small arachnids that feed on blood and can pass on germs while doing so. Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis are well-known diseases spread by ticks.

6617.q: What kind of coat does a red fox wear in winter compared with summer?
6617.e: In winter the fox grows a thicker and warmer coat so that it doesn’t freeze in the cold. In summer its coat is thinner.
6617.m: The winter coat is thicker and warmer.

a: A planet outside our solar system
A particularly small planet in our solar system
6618.e: Exoplanets orbit stars other than our Sun and have only been discovered regularly since the 1990s. Thousands of these distant planets are now known.

6619.q: What does a common toad often do with its old skin?
a: It builds a nest with it
It lets it float in the water
It buries it in the soil
6619.e: After shedding, the common toad usually eats its old skin itself. That way the valuable substances in it are not lost.

6620.q: What does Faraday’s law of induction basically state?
a: A changing magnetic field produces a voltage in a loop of wire
An electric current always produces light
Magnets automatically lose their strength over time
6620.e: If a magnet moves near a coil of wire or the magnetic field changes, a voltage is produced in the coil. Generators use this principle to turn motion into electric current.

6621.q: How does an orca move through the water?
a: With powerful up-and-down strokes of its tail
It is carried by the water
6621.e: The orca beats its tail fin up and down to move forwards. That way it can swim very fast.
6621.m: Orcas swim with their tail fin.

6622.q: How do moose usually behave in everyday life?
a: As a pack with a leader
6622.e: Moose mostly live alone. Only cows with calves stay together.

6623.q: In which month does the tawny owl’s breeding season usually begin?
a: Already in early spring, often in March
Only in the middle of high summer
Only in the depths of winter, in January
Never, it breeds all year round
6623.e: Tawny owls start breeding comparatively early in the year, often in March. That gives the young enough time to become independent by autumn.
6623.m: The tawny owl breeds from early spring.

6624.q: What do many people link with the cuckoo’s call in spring?
a: It is seen as a sign that spring has begun
It is seen as a sign of snow
It is seen as a sign of the harvest
It is seen as a sign of a thunderstorm
6624.e: Many people are happy when they hear the first cuckoo call in spring, because it has long been seen as a herald of spring. In the past there were many customs around this first call.
6624.m: The cuckoo’s call is a herald of spring.

6625.q: Why is the slow worm scientifically called “the fragile one”?
a: Because its tail breaks off easily
Because its bones are made of glass
Because its eggs are very thin
6625.e: When in danger, the slow worm’s tail breaks off easily. That is where its Latin name “fragilis” comes from, which means fragile.

6626.q: When did the wolf return to Switzerland after a long absence?
6626.e: After the wolf had been wiped out in Switzerland for a long time, single wolves came back from Italy in the 1990s. Since then the population has slowly grown.
6626.m: Wolves have lived here again since the 1990s.

6627.q: What colour is an adult male blackbird?
6627.e: The male blackbird is completely black. Only its beak is a bright different colour.

6628.q: Is the red squirrel protected in Switzerland?
a: Yes, it must not be caught or hunted
No, there are no rules about it
No, it may even be sold
6628.e: The red squirrel is protected in Switzerland. You must not catch, injure or kill it.

6629.q: What is one of the puma’s jobs in the ecosystem?
a: It keeps numbers of hoofed animals in balance
6629.e: As a predator, the puma mainly catches hoofed animals such as deer. This stops them from becoming too numerous.
6629.m: Pumas keep prey numbers in check.

6630.q: How does the barn swallow catch its food?
a: In flight with its beak wide open
It digs for it in the ground
It waits quietly on a branch
It dives under water for it
6630.e: The barn swallow hunts insects in flight and opens its beak wide while doing so. That way it can catch many small insects at once.

6632.q: Roughly how much does an adult squirrel weigh?
6632.e: An adult squirrel usually weighs between 250 and 400 grams. That makes it quite light.
6632.m: A squirrel weighs only a few hundred grams.

6633.q: What can happen if a wolf and a dog have young together?
a: Mixed offspring, called hybrids, can be born
There is always one sterile pup without fur
6633.e: Wolves and dogs belong to the same species and can in theory have young together. In Europe, however, this rarely happens in the wild and is closely monitored by experts.
6633.m: Wolves and dogs can in theory interbreed.

6634.q: How many young does a female alpaca normally have per birth?
6634.e: Alpacas usually have only one young at a time. Twins are very rare.
6634.m: Usually only one cria is born.

6635.q: In which country outside Africa do a few wild cheetahs still live?
6635.e: In Iran there is a small group of Asiatic cheetahs. They are especially rare and critically threatened.
6635.m: Wild cheetahs still live in Iran.

6636.q: On which Indonesian island does the siamang live?
6636.e: The siamang is found on Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula. It lives in rainforests there.

6638.q: Roughly how big does a cockchafer get?
6638.e: Cockchafers grow to about 2 to 3 cm long. That makes them one of the bigger native beetles.
6638.m: Cockchafers grow to about 2 to 3 cm long.

6639.q: How do carrion crows often behave when a bird of prey appears in their territory?
a: They circle and attack it noisily
They hide quietly in the nest
6639.e: Carrion crows often show so-called mobbing behaviour towards birds of prey. Several crows circle and noisily attack the intruder to drive it away.
6639.m: Crows mob birds of prey together.

6640.q: Apart from fish, which small animals are also part of the grey heron’s diet?
6640.e: The grey heron is very flexible when looking for food and also eats frogs, small rodents and insects. That way it finds enough food even far from water.
6640.m: It eats much more than just fish.

6641.q: In which habitat does the jaguar feel especially at home?
a: High mountains above the tree line
6641.e: Jaguars like to live in damp forests, swamps and by rivers. But they are also found in savannahs and scrubland.

6642.q: Which animal is our domestic pig descended from?
6642.e: Our domestic pigs were bred from the wild boar a long time ago. That is why they look a little alike.
6642.m: Domestic pigs come from the wild boar.

a: Giving money freely to someone who needs it, without asking for anything in return
6643.e: When you donate, you give money to help others, for example a charity. You get nothing back for it.
6643.m: Donating helps others without anything in return.

6645.q: What colour are a hedgehog’s spines usually?
6645.e: A hedgehog’s spines are usually striped brown and white. This helps it camouflage itself well among the leaves.
6645.m: Hedgehog spines are banded brown and white.

6646.q: What is meant by the ‘Cold War’?
a: The decades-long political rivalry between the USA and the Soviet Union without a direct war between them
A real war with many battles in Europe
A period of extreme cold in Russia
A trade war between China and Japan
6646.e: In the Cold War, the capitalist West led by the USA faced the communist Eastern Bloc led by the Soviet Union. There was no direct armed war between the two.
6646.m: In the Cold War, two powers were rivals without fighting each other directly.

6647.q: Which sense organ is especially good in the polar bear?
6647.e: The polar bear has a very keen nose. With it, it can smell seals from a great distance.
6647.m: The polar bear has a powerful nose.

6648.q: What is the strongest stag called, the one that has many females to himself during the rut?
6648.e: The master stag is the strongest stag in an area. He drives weaker rivals away from the females.
6648.m: The strongest stag is called the master stag.

6649.q: Why does the lake trout have sharp teeth in its mouth?
a: To hold on to prey fish
6649.e: It uses its teeth to grab slippery prey and hold it tight. Then it usually swallows it whole.

6650.q: What is the koala’s big nose especially important for?
a: For smelling which leaves are good
6650.e: With its keen nose the koala can sniff out which eucalyptus leaves taste good and are less poisonous. That way it chooses its food carefully.
6650.m: The nose helps it choose its leaves.

6651.q: Why are quarries important replacement habitats for the eagle owl today?
a: Because they offer rock features similar to natural gorges
Because there is particularly a lot of water to drink there
Because no plants grow there and the eagle owl avoids plants
Because quarries are always very noisy and busy
6651.e: Quarries offer the eagle owl rock ledges and steep walls similar to those in natural gorges. That is why it often uses them today as a replacement habitat for breeding.
6651.m: Quarries serve eagle owls as a replacement habitat.

6652.q: Where do you think the cuckoo clock gets its name from?
a: From a figure that calls like a cuckoo
6652.e: The cuckoo clock gets its name from the little bird figure that comes out every hour and calls like a cuckoo. Such clocks originally come from the Black Forest.
6652.m: The cuckoo clock copies the bird’s call.

6653.q: How does a jellyfish’s bell move when it swims?
a: It opens and closes like an umbrella
6653.e: When swimming, the jellyfish opens and closes its bell again and again. This pushes water out and moves it forwards.
6653.m: A jellyfish swims by opening and closing.

6654.q: How does an eel often react when you try to grab it with your bare hands?
a: It wriggles and slips away easily
6654.e: Its layer of slime makes it very slippery. That is why it is hard to hold.
6654.m: Eels are slippery and escape easily.

6655.q: In which habitat do many jaguars live in South America?
6655.e: In the Amazon basin many jaguars live in the tropical rainforest. The Amazon is one of the rivers with the most water on Earth.
6655.m: Many jaguars live in the Amazon region.

6656.q: Why do butterflies often sit in the sun with their wings open?
6656.e: The dark areas of the wings soak up the sun’s warmth. That way the butterfly can warm up and then fly.

6657.q: Who likes to eat small young pike?
a: Nobody, they are never in danger
Only other small pike of the same size
6657.e: Young pike are still small and weak. Bigger fish and fish-eating birds often catch them as prey.

6658.q: What does a hedgehog do when it is scared?
a: It rolls up into a prickly ball
It immediately digs itself deep into the ground
It bites loudly all around it
6658.e: When in danger, the hedgehog rolls up so that only its spines can be seen. This protects its soft belly from enemies.
6658.m: When in danger, the hedgehog rolls up.

6659.q: How can you tell that two budgies get on well?
a: They feed and groom each other
They bite each other all the time
6659.e: Budgies that are friends scratch each other with their beaks and sometimes feed each other. This shows that they like each other.

6660.q: How does the call of the male eagle owl usually differ from the female’s?
a: There is no difference, both sound identical
The male never calls, only the female
6660.e: The male eagle owl’s call usually sounds deeper than the female’s. Both sexes use their calls to communicate and defend their territory.
6660.m: Male eagle owls call more deeply than females.

6661.q: How many babies can a male seahorse have at once?
6661.e: Several hundred tiny young can come out of the belly pouch at once. Only a few of them survive later.
6661.m: Hundreds of babies come at once.

6662.q: How many toes does a hamster usually have on its front paws?
6662.e: A hamster usually has four toes on its front paws. On its back paws, however, it has five.
6662.m: Hamsters have four toes at the front.

6663.q: The species name cristatus fits the English name great crested grebe. What does it mean?
6663.e: Cristatus is Latin and means crested or crowned. This fits the great crested grebe’s crest of feathers.

6664.q: How does a cat mainly mark its territory?
a: With scent glands on its head and paws and with scratch marks
With bright colours in its fur
6664.e: Cats have scent glands, for example on their cheeks and paws. When rubbing and scratching they leave scent marks that show other cats whose territory it is.
6664.m: Cats mark their territory with scent glands.

6665.q: What sound do meerkats often make when they are relaxed and looking for food in groups?
6665.e: While foraging they exchange soft sounds. That way they stay in touch even when their heads are in the sand.

6666.q: Is there a duty to take part in votes in Switzerland?
a: No, except in the canton of Schaffhausen
Yes, in all cantons, with a fine
Yes, but only for constitutional amendments
No, not in a single canton
6666.e: In Switzerland, taking part in votes is basically voluntary. Only the canton of Schaffhausen has compulsory voting; anyone who does not take part pays a small fine.
6666.m: Voting is voluntary, except in Schaffhausen.

6667.q: What does a Roman snail use to smell its surroundings?
6667.e: A snail’s tentacles are used not only for seeing but also for smelling. With them it finds fresh food, for example.

6668.q: Where does a polar bear mother give birth to her cubs?
6668.e: In winter the polar bear mother digs a den in the snow. There she gives birth to her cubs safely.
6668.m: Polar bear cubs are born in a snow den.

6669.q: The gelada is a monkey from the highlands of Ethiopia. What does it mainly eat?
6669.e: The gelada is closely related to baboons. It sits on the ground a lot and plucks grasses, which is very rare for monkeys.
6669.m: The gelada is a grass-eater from Ethiopia.

6670.q: How do orangutans build their sleeping places?
a: They bend branches into a nest in the trees
They dig caves in the ground
They always sleep on the ground
They weave nets out of grass
6670.e: Every evening they build a new nest of branches and leaves. They often choose tall trees for it.
6670.m: Orangutans build a new nest every evening.

6671.q: Which scientist worked especially hard to protect mountain gorillas?
6671.e: Dian Fossey lived with mountain gorillas in Africa for many years and helped to protect them. She made the animals known around the world.
6671.m: Dian Fossey protected the mountain gorillas.

6672.q: What do most millipedes feed on?
a: Dead plant material such as leaves
6672.e: Most millipedes eat rotting leaves and wood. In this way they help break down plant remains.
6672.m: Millipedes break down dead plant material.

6673.q: What does the badger rely on most to find food?
6673.e: The badger has a very keen nose. With it, it sniffs out worms and insects deep in the ground.
6673.m: Badgers smell better than they see.

6674.q: What does the magpie’s flight look like compared with small songbirds?
a: Rather heavy, with short, rounded wings
Very elegant and fast like a falcon
6674.e: The magpie has fairly short, rounded wings, which makes its flight look a little heavy. Even so, it can manoeuvre well, especially thanks to its long tail.

6675.q: What colour is an adult African buffalo’s coat usually?
6675.e: The coat is usually dark and rather thin. In forest buffalo it is often more reddish.
6675.m: African buffalo are dark brown to black.

6677.q: Roughly how old can a domestic goat get?
6677.e: Domestic goats usually live between 10 and 15 years, some even longer. It also depends on good care.

6678.q: In eagle owls, which is usually bigger and heavier, the male or the female?
a: It depends only on the season
6678.e: In eagle owls the females are usually bigger and heavier than the males. This difference in size is found in many owl and bird of prey species.
6678.m: Female eagle owls are bigger than males.

6679.q: Which reptile family does the common wall lizard belong to?
6679.e: The common wall lizard belongs to the family of wall lizards, the Lacertidae. This family also includes the sand lizard and the green lizard.

6680.q: What makes an orca different from a fish?
a: The orca breathes air and suckles its young, fish don’t
The orca has scales like a fish
6680.e: Fish breathe with gills and lay eggs, but the orca does not. It is a mammal that breathes air.
6680.m: The orca is not a fish but a mammal.

6681.q: What advantage does the pond skater get from hunting on the water?
a: It finds insects that have fallen into the water
It is safe from all enemies there
6681.e: Many insects land on the water and struggle there. The pond skater can reach them quickly.
6681.m: The water’s surface is its hunting ground.

6683.q: How many young does a harbour seal usually have per year?
6683.e: A harbour seal mother usually gives birth to just one pup. She takes very good care of this one baby.
6683.m: Harbour seals usually have only one pup.

6684.q: How many colours does a rainbow usually have?
6684.e: When sunlight passes through raindrops, it is bent and split into its colours. This makes a rainbow with seven colours.

6685.q: Roughly how big is an adult meerkat, not counting the tail?
6685.e: Its body is about as long as a ruler. On top of that comes a tail of about 20 centimetres.

6686.q: What happens if a Roman snail is kept dry for a very long time?
a: It withdraws into its shell and waits for moisture
6686.e: Without moisture, the snail withdraws into its shell and seals it. It waits like this until it rains again.
6686.m: In dry weather it waits in its shell.

6687.q: Roughly how long does an adult common wall lizard get, including its tail?
6687.e: With its long tail, the common wall lizard is about as long as a ballpoint pen. Without the tail it is much shorter.

a: A sanctuary for orphaned bonobos near Kinshasa
A mountain range in the Congo
6688.e: At Lola ya Bonobo orphaned animals are cared for, often young ones whose mothers were hunted. The project was founded by Claudine André.
6688.m: Lola ya Bonobo protects orphaned bonobos.

6689.q: Where does the name “jaguar” probably come from?
a: From an indigenous language of South America
6689.e: The word goes back to languages of the indigenous peoples of South America, for example Tupi-Guarani. It roughly means “the one who kills with one leap”.
6689.m: The name jaguar comes from South America.

6690.q: How soon after hatching can ducklings swim?
6690.e: Ducklings can swim almost from the start. Shortly after hatching they follow their mother into the water.

6691.q: Which sense organ does a fox use especially to detect prey or danger?
6691.e: The fox has an excellent sense of smell and can use it to detect prey or other foxes from far away. This sense is especially important for it.
6691.m: Foxes have a particularly good sense of smell.

6692.q: What does a penguin do when it jumps out of the water to breathe?
a: It leaps in an arc like a dolphin
6692.e: This leaping way of swimming is called porpoising. It lets penguins swim fast and still keep breathing.
6692.m: Penguins leap out of the water as they swim.

6693.q: What do a roe deer’s eyes look like in the dark when light shines on them?
a: They light up when light falls into them
They turn completely black and dark
6693.e: As in many nocturnal animals, a roe deer’s eyes shine in headlights. This helps them see well even in low light.
6693.m: Roe deer eyes shine when light hits them in the dark.

6694.q: What often happens to leaves that are badly infested with aphids?
a: They curl up or roll up
6694.e: The sucking makes the leaves change shape. They curl or roll up, and the plant grows less well.

6695.q: Where does the Alpine newt mainly live during the breeding season?
6695.e: To breed, the Alpine newt looks for calm, still water. That is where mating and egg-laying take place.
6695.m: Alpine newts lay their eggs in calm pools.

6696.q: What is a ballot box in a vote?
a: A container into which you put your ballot paper
A computer in the Federal Palace
6696.e: If you go to the polls, you put your ballot paper into a special container. That way your vote is counted.
6696.m: The ballot paper goes into the ballot box.

6697.q: Which small crustacean, living under stones in streams, is eaten by brown trout?
6697.e: The freshwater shrimp is only about 1 to 2 centimetres long. It lives in clean streams and is common prey.
6697.m: The freshwater shrimp is a popular food.

6698.q: Apart from a piggy bank, where else can you keep saved money safe?
a: In a savings account at the bank
Under your pillow at holiday camp
In your trouser pocket while playing
6698.e: Money in a savings account at the bank is safe and does not get lost so easily. Many children have their own savings account.

6699.q: How do kangaroos often stand when they are resting?
a: They lean back on their tail
6699.e: When resting, kangaroos like to prop themselves up on their thick tail. That way they can sit or stand comfortably.
6699.m: Kangaroos prop themselves up on their tail.

6700.q: Which tapir species lives high up in the Andes?
6700.e: The mountain tapir lives in the mountain forests and highlands of the Andes. Its thick coat protects it from the cold.
6700.m: The mountain tapir lives in the Andes.

6701.q: What happens when a young lynx becomes independent?
a: It leaves its mother’s territory and looks for its own
It stays in the same territory with its mother for ever
It goes back to its father’s territory
6701.e: After about 10 months young lynxes move away to find their own territory. They can travel very long distances while doing so.
6701.m: Young lynxes set off on a long journey.

6702.q: What noise does a hen often make after laying an egg?
6702.e: After laying an egg the hen often cackles quite loudly. That way she draws attention to herself.
6702.m: Hens cackle after laying an egg.

6704.q: What colour is the great spotted woodpecker under its tail?
6704.e: Under its tail the great spotted woodpecker has a red patch. You can see it especially well when it climbs a tree.
6704.m: It is red under the tail.

6705.q: How does the garden spider repair its damaged web?
a: It eats the old threads and spins new ones
It gets help from other spiders
6705.e: The spider eats the old threads because they contain valuable material. It then uses this to make new threads.

6706.q: Roughly how much does an adult ring-tailed lemur weigh?
6706.e: A ring-tailed lemur weighs about as much as a small to medium-sized pet cat. So it is quite a light animal.
6706.m: Ring-tailed lemurs weigh only a few kilograms.

6707.q: Roughly how long are most perch that are caught?
6707.e: Most perch measure between 15 and 35 centimetres. Very large ones can be well over 40 centimetres.
6707.m: A typical perch is about as long as a ruler.

6708.q: What does the male mute swan do while the female is sitting on the eggs?
6708.e: While the female sits on the eggs, the male swims nearby and guards the nest. If anyone comes too close, he chases them away.

6709.q: The brook trout looks similar to the brown trout. Where does it originally come from?
6709.e: The brook trout came to Europe from North America. It is a char and does not belong to the trout genus.
6709.m: The brook trout comes from North America.

6710.q: Which is the only country in the world with the outline of an assault rifle on its national flag?
6710.e: The flag of Mozambique shows an AK-47 on a hoe and a book as symbols of defence, work and education. It is the only national flag in the world with a modern firearm.
6710.m: Mozambique is the only country whose flag shows an assault rifle.

6711.q: What do antibodies do in the immune system?
a: They recognise and fight foreign invaders
6711.e: Antibodies recognise germs such as viruses or bacteria. They help the body to make them harmless.

6712.q: Roughly how long can an adder live in the wild?
6712.e: In the wild some adders live for more than ten years. How long they live depends a lot on predators and winters.
6712.m: A good ten years is possible.

6713.q: What does a curious goat often do with unfamiliar things?
6713.e: Goats are very curious and examine unfamiliar things with their nose and mouth. That way they find out whether something can be eaten.

6714.q: When does a tiger prefer to hunt?
6714.e: Tigers mostly hunt at night or at dusk. At this time they see well and their prey notices them less quickly.

6715.q: Apart from its latrines, what else does the badger use to mark its territory?
a: Scratch marks on trees like a bear
6715.e: The badger has special scent glands on its body. With them it leaves a smell that other badgers recognise.

6716.q: What does a mute swan show when it raises its wings over its back?
6716.e: When a swan raises its wings and puffs itself up, it is warning other animals or people. This is called a threat display.

6717.q: When does the wels catfish usually spawn?
a: In early summer when the water is warm
In the middle of winter under the ice
6717.e: The wels catfish spawns from about May to July, when the water is warm enough. It needs temperatures of about 20 degrees for this.
6717.m: Wels catfish spawn in warm early summer.

6718.q: What helps a harbour seal swim quickly through the water?
6718.e: A harbour seal’s body is long and smooth, which helps it glide easily through the water. On land, however, it looks rather clumsy.
6718.m: A smooth body makes seals fast.

6719.q: Which large yellow and black butterfly has long points on its hind wings?
6719.e: The swallowtail is easy to recognise by its yellow and black wings and the long points on its hind wings. It is one of the largest butterflies in Switzerland.
6719.m: The swallowtail has wing points like a swallow’s tail.

6721.q: How often a year can rabbits have young?
6721.e: Rabbits can breed very quickly and have young several times a year. That is why there are so many wild rabbits.

6722.q: How does a pool frog usually react when you approach the edge of a pond?
a: It jumps into the water with a powerful leap
It digs itself into the sand in a flash
6722.e: When in danger, the pool frog typically jumps into the water with a long leap in a flash. It then often dives down into the mud or among plants.
6722.m: In danger it jumps straight into the water.

6723.q: How does a marmot’s behaviour in spring differ from its behaviour in late autumn?
a: In spring it is active, in late autumn it withdraws to hibernate
In spring it sleeps, in autumn it is active
It behaves exactly the same all year
In spring it leaves the Alps completely
6723.e: After waking up in spring, marmots are active, mate and eat a lot. In late autumn they then withdraw into their burrow to hibernate.
6723.m: The seasons shape the marmot’s life.

6724.q: What is meant by fish spawn?
6724.e: Spawn is the name for the eggs that fish have laid. Laying them is called spawning.

6725.q: What can scientists often tell from a whale’s blow?
a: Which species of whale it is
What the whale had for breakfast
How many friends the whale has
6725.e: Each whale species has a slightly different shape of blow. That way scientists can tell from far away which whale is surfacing.
6725.m: The blow gives away the whale species.

6726.q: What is typical of a chamois’s horns?
a: They are bent backwards into a hook at the end
They grow back new every year
6726.e: The chamois’s horns are slender and curve backwards at the tip like a small hook. This shape is typical of the species.
6726.m: Chamois horns are hooked at the tip.

6727.q: How does the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) classify the jaguar?
6727.e: The jaguar is listed on the Red List as near threatened. Its habitat is shrinking and it is hunted.

6728.q: Where does a female grasshopper usually lay her eggs?
6728.e: With her ovipositor she pushes the eggs into the ground. There they are well protected.
6728.m: The eggs are hidden in the ground.

6729.q: Which body parts especially help the chamois stand safely on rocks?
6729.e: The chamois’s hooves are perfectly shaped to grip on narrow rock ledges. This makes it a sure-footed climber.

6730.q: Where is the wels catfish in the food chain of its waters?
a: It is a scavenger on land
It is a filter feeder like a mussel
6730.e: Large wels catfish have hardly any natural enemies in the water. They are at the top of the food chain.
6730.m: Large wels catfish are top predators.

6731.q: How heavy should a hedgehog be before hibernation?
6731.e: For a hedgehog to survive hibernation, it needs enough fat reserves. That is why it should weigh at least about 500 grams before winter.
6731.m: Hedgehogs need enough fat for the winter.

6732.q: What especially hinders eels in rivers on their migration?
6732.e: Dams block the way. In the turbines of hydroelectric power stations, eels migrating downstream are often injured or killed.
6732.m: Power stations and weirs endanger eels.

6733.q: Roughly how long is a jaguar pregnant?
6733.e: The jaguar mother carries her young for about three to three and a half months. Then she usually gives birth to them in a hidden place.
6733.m: The pregnancy lasts about three months.

6734.q: How does the Alpine salamander spend the winter?
a: It crawls underground and rests through the winter
It simply lies down in the water
6734.e: During the cold season the Alpine salamander hides in holes in the ground, under stones or in cracks in the rock. There it waits for the winter to pass.

6735.q: What is special about the mountain tapir?
6735.e: The mountain tapir has thicker fur than the other species. This helps it survive the cold at high altitude.
6735.m: Thick fur protects against the mountain cold.

6736.q: How does the sand lizard move when it flees from danger?
a: It runs away very fast on four legs
It rolls up and tumbles away
6736.e: With its strong legs it can sprint surprisingly fast and quickly disappear into the bushes or under stones. It cannot fly or jump.
6736.m: Running fast saves it from enemies.

6737.q: What happens to whitefish eggs in fish hatcheries?
a: They are hatched and the young fish are released into lakes
They are made into caviar for cats
They are washed into the Rhine
6737.e: Fishermen collect the spawn and let the larvae hatch. Later the young fish are released into the lake to support the population.

6738.q: Which insect with colourful wings collects nectar from flowers?
6738.e: Butterflies use their long proboscis to suck sweet nectar from flowers. In doing so they also help the plants with pollination.

6739.q: What does a bonobo sometimes eat in addition to plants?
6739.e: Bonobos are not pure plant-eaters. Sometimes they eat insects or small animals, but meat is only a small part of their diet.
6739.m: Animal food is only an extra.

6740.q: Why should you empty old water butts and tyres regularly?
a: So that no mosquito larvae develop there
So that the garden looks nicer
So that no leaves fall in
6740.e: Mosquitoes like to lay their eggs in still water. If you tip the water away regularly, no mosquito larvae can develop there.

6741.q: How heavy can an adult Bactrian camel get?
6741.e: Bulls can weigh about half a tonne to a tonne. Females are usually a little lighter.
6741.m: Up to about a tonne in weight.

6742.q: Why can the common buzzard be found in many different landscapes in Switzerland?
a: Because it can adapt well to different habitats
Because it finds exactly the same prey everywhere
Because it lives in only one Swiss municipality
6742.e: The common buzzard is a very adaptable bird that is found in the lowlands as well as in mountain areas. As long as there are trees for nesting and open land for hunting, it feels at home.

6743.q: When are ring-tailed lemurs mainly active?
6743.e: Ring-tailed lemurs are active during the day. They look for food by day and rest in the trees at night.
6743.m: Ring-tailed lemurs are active by day.

6744.q: Why can’t a harbour seal walk properly on land?
a: Its back flippers always point backwards
It has no bones in its flippers
6744.e: A harbour seal’s back flippers always point backwards and cannot be turned forwards like legs. That is why it wriggles along on its belly on land.

6745.e: Young dolphins are called calves, like the young of other large sea mammals. They stay with their mother for a long time.

6746.q: How do adult gorillas often communicate with each other?
6746.e: Gorillas often make deep grunting sounds to talk to each other. That way the animals in the group know where the others are.

6747.q: What does a butterfly use to drink nectar from flowers?
6747.e: The proboscis is like a thin straw. With it the butterfly sucks the sweet nectar out of the flowers.
6747.m: A butterfly drinks nectar with its proboscis.

6748.q: What time of activity is typical of the snow leopard?
6748.e: It is active mainly at dusk. This is called being crepuscular.

6749.q: Which animal has black and white stripes and lives in Africa?
6749.e: Every zebra has a unique stripe pattern, almost like a fingerprint. Zebras live in herds on the savannah.
6749.m: Zebras have black and white stripes.

6750.q: Roughly how long does it take for a pool frog tadpole to turn into a young frog?
a: Several weeks to a few months
6750.e: It usually takes a few weeks to months from tadpole to finished little frog. The exact time depends on water temperature and food.
6750.m: The change takes weeks to months.

6751.q: How does the badger usually move?
6751.e: The badger usually moves at a calm, waddling trot. But it can also run faster for a short time if necessary.

6752.q: Roughly how much can an adult male chamois weigh?
6752.e: An adult male chamois usually weighs between 30 and 50 kilograms. That makes it much lighter than a red deer, for example.
6752.m: A male chamois weighs about 30 to 50 kilos.

6753.q: Roughly how many teeth can a bottlenose dolphin have?
6753.e: Bottlenose dolphins have many small, pointed teeth, often more than 80. They use them to grab their slippery prey.

6754.q: What do you call a large group of penguins living together?
6754.e: Penguins often live in huge groups called colonies. Some colonies have thousands of animals.

6755.q: How many calves does a female reindeer usually give birth to?
6755.e: Usually only one calf is born per year. Twins are very rare.

6756.q: What do the eggs of the European pond turtle look like?
a: White, elongated and with a hard chalky shell
Green and perfectly round with soft skin
Brown and as big as a hen’s egg
6756.e: The eggs have hard shells and are long and oval. They are much smaller than hens’ eggs.
6756.m: The eggs are white, elongated and hard-shelled.

6757.q: Which of the cheetah’s body parts are especially large so that it can take in lots of air?
6757.e: The cheetah’s heart and lungs are very large compared with its body. That way it can get enough oxygen when running fast.
6757.m: Big lungs and heart help with sprinting.

6758.q: Roughly how fast can a spotted hyena run?
a: Up to about 60 kilometres per hour
6758.e: Spotted hyenas can run at up to about 60 km/h for short periods. They also have great stamina over long distances.
6758.m: Spotted hyenas are fast and have stamina.

6759.q: What kind of weather do common toads especially like for their migration?
6759.e: Common toads feel most comfortable on their migration in warm rain. The moisture protects their sensitive skin from drying out.
6759.m: Rain and warmth get toads moving.

6760.q: What makes pond skaters important for ponds?
a: They are predators and food for other animals
They clean the water with gills
They fertilise the pond with honey
6760.e: They eat small insects and are themselves eaten by fish and birds. That makes them part of the food chain.
6760.m: They are hunters and prey at the same time.

6761.q: Why is it wise not to spend all your pocket money straight away?
a: So you can afford something bigger later
So that your parents take the money back
6761.e: If you do not spend everything at once, over time you can afford more expensive things too. Saving takes patience.
6761.m: Saving makes bigger wishes come true.

6762.q: What can you do to help stag beetles?
a: Leave dead wood and old tree stumps in the forest
6762.e: Leaving dead wood creates breeding sites. There are even artificial oak posts that larvae can live in.
6762.m: Leaving dead wood helps the stag beetle.

6763.q: Which other name is also used for the puma?
6763.e: The puma is also called the silver lion or mountain lion. In North America people often say “mountain lion”.
6763.m: The puma is also called the silver lion.

6764.q: Which animal lives in close family groups that are usually led by an experienced older female?
6764.e: Elephant herds are usually led by an experienced older female, the matriarch. She knows where the waterholes and feeding places are and leads the family safely through the area.
6764.m: The oldest female leads the elephant herd.

6765.q: How do the calls of male and female tawny owls differ?
a: The female calls a sharp “ke-wick”, the male more of a “hoo-hoo-hooo”
Only the male calls, the female is always silent
Only the female calls, the male is always silent
6765.e: Males and females have different calls that are easy to tell apart. The two calls together are used for communication and marking their territory.

6766.q: How does a goose usually move on land?
a: Rather waddling and a little slowly
It can’t walk on land at all
6766.e: On land a goose’s walk often looks a little wobbly and slow. In the water, however, it moves much more skilfully.
6766.m: On land a goose waddles along.

6767.q: What does the photoelectric effect describe, for whose explanation Einstein received the Nobel Prize?
a: Light can knock electrons out of a metal
Light produces heat in every material
6767.e: If light with enough energy hits a metal, it can knock individual electrons out of the surface. This effect showed that light also behaves like individual packets of energy called photons.
6767.m: Light can release electrons from metal.

6768.q: What does it mean that the cockchafer can be a pest?
a: It passes diseases on to people
6768.e: By eating leaves and roots it damages forests, meadows and crops. It is not dangerous to people, however.
6768.m: The damage is done to plants.

6769.q: What is the equipment on a horse’s head that you use to steer it called?
6769.e: With the bridle and reins the rider can show the horse which direction and speed to go. It is put over the horse’s head.
6769.m: A bridle helps you steer the horse.

6770.q: How are an orangutan’s feet built?
6770.e: Their feet can grip like hands too. This helps when climbing in the branches.
6770.m: Orangutans grip with their feet as well.

6771.q: How many toes does a dromedary have on each foot?
6771.e: Dromedaries belong to the tylopods and have two toes on each foot. Both rest on a shared pad.

6772.q: Why do elephants usually stay near rivers or waterholes?
a: They have to drink many litres every day
They lay their eggs in water
6772.e: An adult elephant needs several dozen litres of water every day. Elephants also like to bathe and shower.
6772.m: Elephants need lots of water every day.

6773.q: Does the mole hibernate in winter?
a: No, it is active all year round
It only sleeps on very cold days
6773.e: The mole does not hibernate. It stays active underground in winter too and keeps looking for food.
6773.m: Moles don’t sleep through the winter.

6774.q: What does the beaver use to mark its territory?
6774.e: Beavers leave scent marks with castoreum on small mounds of earth on the bank. That way they show other beavers that the area is already taken.

6775.q: How big is a pike’s mouth compared with its head?
a: Very big, almost the whole head
It has no mouth at all
As small as a gnat’s mouth
6775.e: The pike has a very big mouth that takes up almost its whole head. That way it can swallow even bigger prey fish.

6776.q: Roughly how long does a young bearded vulture stay in the eyrie before it learns to fly?
6776.e: The young bearded vulture grows slowly and only leaves the eyrie after around 120 days. Then it practises flying near the nest.
6776.m: It leaves the eyrie only after months.

6777.q: Roughly how many toes does a hippopotamus have on each foot?
6777.e: Each of the hippo’s feet has four toes with small hooves. This helps it grip on the muddy river bed.
6777.m: Hippos have four toes per foot.

6778.q: How does a mute swan often behave when you approach its nest?
a: It may attack to protect the eggs
It is happy and joins in the play
6778.e: Swan parents are very protective. If someone comes too close to their nest, they may hiss or even attack.

6779.q: Which animals are close relatives of the jellyfish?
6779.e: Like the jellyfish, corals and sea anemones belong to the cnidarians. They all have similar stinging cells.

6780.q: Where does a female cheetah hide her cubs in their first weeks of life?
a: In a deep cave under the ground
6780.e: In the first weeks the mother hides her cubs in tall grass. That way they are better protected from enemies.
6780.m: Cheetah cubs hide in tall grass.

6781.q: What were the “Great Purges” under Stalin?
a: A wave of persecution against real and suspected opponents of Stalin.
6781.e: In the 1930s Stalin had hundreds of thousands of people arrested, deported or shot. Many were innocent but were labelled as supposed enemies.
6781.m: The purges killed many innocent people.

6782.q: What does a trout do when the water gets too warm in summer?
a: It looks for cooler, deeper water
6782.e: When the water gets too warm, the trout gets less oxygen. That is why it then looks for cooler and deeper spots in the water.
6782.m: Trout look for cooler spots in the heat.

6784.q: How is the fox often described in stories and sayings?
6784.e: In many stories and sayings the fox is seen as especially clever and crafty. For example, people say “as sly as a fox”.
6784.m: The fox is seen as very clever.

6785.q: What happens if an earthworm lies in the blazing sun for too long?
a: It dries out and can die
It gets a suntan and is happy
6785.e: Without damp protection the worm’s skin quickly loses water. That is why it can quickly dry out in the sun.

6786.q: How wide can a golden eagle spread its wings?
6786.e: Depending on whether it is male or female, a golden eagle’s wingspan is about 1.9 to 2.3 metres. Females are usually bigger than males.
6786.m: The wingspan reaches over two metres.

6787.q: What else is the snow leopard called?
6787.e: Irbis is another name for the snow leopard. It comes from the Turkic languages.

6788.q: Why does the roe deer change its coat in spring and autumn?
a: So that it suits the season
Because the old coat is too small
So that it can run faster
6788.e: In spring the roe deer gets a thinner, reddish-brown summer coat. In autumn a thicker, greyish-brown winter coat grows.
6788.m: Roe deer change their coat with the seasons.

6789.q: What makes the brown trout different from the Atlantic salmon?
a: It usually stays in fresh water and in the stream
It always lives in the sea
6789.e: The salmon migrates to the sea to feed and returns to spawn. The brown trout usually spends its life in the stream.
6789.m: The brown trout usually stays in the stream.

6790.q: What makes the Roman snail different from a slug?
6790.e: The Roman snail carries a hard shell on its back. Slugs, on the other hand, have no such house.
6790.m: The Roman snail has a shell, the slug does not.

6791.q: What colour are a cuckoo’s feathers usually?
a: Grey on top and barred on the belly
6791.e: The cuckoo usually has grey feathers on its back and a barred underside. This colouring also helps it look like a bird of prey.

6792.q: What does a pig often show when it feels comfortable?
a: It grunts contentedly and lies relaxed
6792.e: Contented pigs make calm, even grunting sounds. They then often lie down comfortably to sleep or doze.

6793.q: What is an octopus’s hard mouth called?
6793.e: The octopus has a hard beak, similar to a parrot’s. With it, it can even crack hard shells.
6793.m: The octopus has a hard beak.

6795.q: What is special about the common swift’s feet?
a: They have no toes at all
They are webbed like ducks’ feet
They have only two toes like ostriches
6795.e: In the common swift all four toes point forwards. This helps it cling well to vertical walls.

6796.q: What do you call it when a wild boar searches for food in the forest?
a: It digs a tunnel under the ground
6796.e: When wild boar churn up the ground with their snouts, this is called rooting. You can easily see the marks in the forest.
6796.m: Churning up the ground is called rooting.

6797.q: What shows that chimpanzees are very social animals?
a: They live in groups and help each other
They fight each other all the time
