6797.e: Chimpanzees live together in groups, look after each other and play together. This shows how social they are.

6798.q: Which of the beaver’s teeth keep growing throughout its life?
6798.e: Like all rodents, the beaver has front teeth that keep growing. Gnawing wood regularly wears them down at the same time.
6798.m: A beaver’s front teeth keep growing.

6799.q: What do people do at a seal rescue centre?
a: They nurse orphaned seal pups back to health
They catch fish for the market
6799.e: At seal rescue centres people look after young seals that have lost their mother. When the animals are big enough, they go back to the sea.
6799.m: Seal rescue centres help orphaned pups.

6802.q: What food does a brown bear often catch in rivers in autumn when fish are swimming upstream?
a: Only trout and no other fish
6802.e: In North America brown bears like to catch salmon in autumn as they swim upstream to spawn. The bears often stand at waterfalls and catch the leaping fish.
6802.m: Brown bears often catch salmon in autumn.

6803.q: What does the term territory mean for male dragonflies?
a: They defend a stretch of water against rivals
They build a burrow in the ground
6803.e: Many males claim a stretch of the bank and chase competitors away. That way they secure chances to mate.
6803.m: Males defend their territory by the water.

6805.q: What is typical of the Eurasian otter’s claws?
a: They are as long as its whole body
6805.e: Unlike cats, otters cannot pull their claws in. The claws help the otter hold on to slippery prey.

6806.q: How are the fish usually given to the young?
6806.e: The parents always give the fish to the young head first. That way the chicks can swallow them more easily.

6807.q: Which group of animals does the edible dormouse belong to?
6807.e: The edible dormouse is a small rodent with gnawing teeth that keep growing. It belongs to the dormouse family.
6807.m: The edible dormouse is a true rodent.

6809.q: When do wolf pups start eating solid food instead of just drinking milk?
6809.e: After a few weeks the pups start to eat meat that the adults have chewed or brought back up, as well as their mother’s milk. That way they are slowly weaned.
6809.m: After a few weeks pups eat solid food.

6810.q: What prey can a stoat kill despite its small size?
a: Rabbits that are bigger than itself
6810.e: Although stoats are small themselves, they can overpower surprisingly large rabbits. Their speed and skill help them do this.

6811.q: What does a sheep look like shortly after shearing?
a: It has little wool and looks thinner
It looks exactly the same as before
It has more wool than before
It has no wool only on its head
6811.e: After shearing, a sheep has much less wool and looks much thinner than before. The wool then slowly grows back.

6812.q: Does a squirrel’s fur change between summer and winter?
a: Yes, it gets thicker in winter
No, it stays exactly the same all year
6812.e: In winter the squirrel gets thicker fur so that it doesn’t freeze. In summer the fur is thinner.
6812.m: The fur is thicker in winter.

6813.q: Why are hedgehogs sometimes not afraid of venomous snakes?
a: They are somewhat more resistant to some snake venoms
They can’t see snakes at all
Hedgehogs are faster than any snake
6813.e: Hedgehogs can even eat smaller snakes because they are more resistant to some venoms than other animals. Their spines also protect them in a fight.
6813.m: Hedgehogs cope better with some snake venoms.

6814.q: At what age does a mute swan usually have its first young?
6814.e: Mute swans need a few years before they are old enough to breed. Only at about three to four years do they have their first cygnets.
6814.m: The first young come at about 3 years.

6815.q: Why are eyes that move independently useful for the seahorse?
a: It can look in two directions at once
So that it can glow in the dark
So that it sees more colours
6815.e: Because its two eyes can move separately, the seahorse can look forwards and sideways at the same time. That way it spots prey and enemies better.
6815.m: Two directions of view at once.

a: A rapidly spinning column of air
A kind of cloud without wind
6816.e: A tornado is a funnel-shaped whirlwind that can form during thunderstorms. It can produce very strong winds and cause great damage.
6816.m: A tornado is a powerful whirlwind.

6817.q: Apart from drinking, what role does water play for elephants?
a: They like to bathe and swim in it
6817.e: Elephants love water not just for drinking. They like to bathe, swim and squirt each other with their trunks.

6819.q: Where in Switzerland are you most likely to find the adder?
a: In moors and in the mountains
In the middle of big cities
6819.e: It prefers damp, cool habitats such as moors, woodland edges and Alpine slopes. In Switzerland it is found mainly in the Prealps and the Alps.

6820.q: What is typical of the diet of domestic pigs on a farm?
a: They get a mix of grain, vegetables and feed
6820.e: On a farm, domestic pigs usually get a balanced mix of grain, vegetable scraps and special feed. That way they get all the important nutrients.

6821.q: What shows that orangutans can use tools?
a: They use sticks to get insects or seeds
6821.e: Some orangutans use sticks to fish food out of holes. This is seen as a sign of high intelligence.

a: A colourful bred form of the carp
A completely different fish from the carp
6822.e: Koi are colourful ornamental fish that were bred from the carp. They are often kept in garden ponds.
6822.m: Koi are colourful carp from Japan.

6823.q: In which habitats does the robin feel especially at home?
6823.e: The robin likes places with bushes and undergrowth, such as woods, gardens and hedges. There it finds good hiding places and food.
6823.m: Robins like woods, gardens and hedges.

6825.q: At roughly what age is a bearded vulture old enough to breed?
6825.e: Bearded vultures need a long time to grow up and be able to raise young themselves. Only after several years do they start looking for their own territory.
6825.m: They only become old enough to breed late.

6826.q: How does the badger usually move compared with many other members of the marten family?
a: Rather leisurely and on the ground
6826.e: Compared with nimble relatives such as the pine marten, the badger moves rather slowly and mostly stays on the ground. It relies less on a quick escape than on its safe sett.

6827.q: Thanks to its long body, what can an eel do that most fish can hardly do?
6827.e: Thanks to its snake-like body, the eel can swim forwards and backwards. This helps it hide in pipes and cracks.

6828.q: What does a housefly have on its head to smell with?
6828.e: A housefly has two short antennae on its head. With them it can sense smells around it.

6829.q: What does a goat usually do when it gets a fright?
a: It lies flat in the grass
6829.e: Goats are very alert and flee to safe ground in a flash when in danger, often onto rocks. That way they escape enemies.

6830.q: How is the magpie’s diet different from that of pure meat-eaters like foxes?
a: It also eats many plant parts
It eats no meat at all
6830.e: Unlike pure meat-eaters, the magpie is an omnivore and also eats fruit, seeds and other plant parts. This variety makes it very adaptable.
6830.m: Magpies also eat many plant parts.

6831.q: What is the name of the big church that is the landmark of the town of Solothurn?
6831.e: St Ursus Cathedral stands in the middle of Solothurn's old town and can be seen from far away. It is the town's main church and was built several hundred years ago.
6831.m: St Ursus Cathedral is the landmark of Solothurn.

6832.q: How do adult otters usually react to other otters in their territory?
a: They always greet them in a friendly way
They leave the territory at once
6832.e: Otters are territorial and usually don’t tolerate strange otters in their own territory. Meetings can therefore lead to fights.

6833.q: What is a mute swan’s nest usually made of?
6833.e: The nest is built from reeds, grasses and other plants. It is large and often lies on the bank.
6833.m: The nest is made of reeds and grass.

6834.q: Are guinea pigs good at jumping or climbing?
a: No, they prefer moving on the ground
Yes, they love climbing tall trees
Yes, they jump metres high like kangaroos
6834.e: Guinea pigs are ground-living animals and are not good climbers or jumpers. Their enclosure should therefore be large and flat rather than tall.
6834.m: Guinea pigs prefer to stay on the ground.

6835.q: In which habitat does the African wild dog mainly live?
a: In high mountains above the snow line
6835.e: The wild dog needs open country where it can chase its prey well. Savannahs and open woodland therefore suit it.

6836.q: What is special about the skin of a beaver’s tail?
a: It is covered with scaly skin instead of fur
It is completely covered with thick fur
6836.e: Unlike the rest of its body, the beaver’s tail is covered with scaly, hairless skin. This makes it especially tough and good as a rudder.

6837.q: What is the mutual fur care among monkeys and apes often called?
6837.e: When grooming, monkeys and apes search each other’s fur for dirt and parasites. This is important for holding the group together.
6837.m: Grooming is fur care among primates.

6838.q: When do baby hedgehogs get their first hard brown spines?
a: Just a few hours after birth
6838.e: The soft white spines of baby hedgehogs are replaced by the first hard spines after just a few hours. Over time more and more brown spines grow through.
6838.m: Hard spines grow after just hours.

a: A partnership of a fungus and an alga
A kind of moss without a fungus
A kind of fungus without an alga
6839.e: Lichens are made of a fungus and an alga or a cyanobacterium. The two live in a close partnership.

6840.q: Which feature helps tell the European tree frog apart from other frogs?
a: A dark stripe along its sides
A yellow spot on its back
6840.e: A typical feature is the dark stripe that runs along the side from the eye to the back legs. This stripe helps with identification.
6840.m: A dark stripe gives the tree frog away.

6841.q: Which butterfly has black wings with red bands and white spots?
6841.e: The red admiral has black wings with red bands and white spots. It is well known in Switzerland and migrates here from the south every year.
6841.m: The red admiral has red bands.

6842.q: Can a starfish live in a lake?
a: No, only in the salty sea
6842.e: Starfish need salty seawater to live. They cannot survive in fresh water such as lakes or rivers.

6843.q: How does the common wall lizard’s behaviour change in high summer when it is very hot?
a: It retreats into the shade so as not to overheat
It becomes completely inactive until winter
6843.e: Too much heat can harm the common wall lizard. That is why it moves into the shade or cool hiding places when it is very hot.

6844.q: How do adult male chamois usually live outside the rutting season?
a: Only in pairs with a female
6844.e: Outside the mating season, male chamois usually live alone or in small groups. Only during the rut do they seek out the females.

6845.q: Which group of animals does the ladybird belong to?
6845.e: Ladybirds belong to the beetles, a huge group of insects. They have a hard shell and six legs.

6846.q: Why does the barn owl fly almost silently?
a: Because its feathers are very soft
6846.e: The edges of the barn owl’s feathers are especially soft and fine. This means it makes hardly any noise when flying.

6847.q: Does the European pond turtle also eat dead animals?
a: No, it only eats living plants
6847.e: The species is not fussy and also uses dead animals in the water as food. That way it makes use of what it finds.
6847.m: Carrion is on the menu too.

6848.q: Into which three parts is a dragonfly’s body divided?
6848.e: Like all insects, the dragonfly has a head, thorax and abdomen. In dragonflies the abdomen is long and slender.
6848.m: Insects have a head, thorax and abdomen.

6849.q: Why doesn’t the cuckoo build its own nest?
a: Because it prefers to lay its eggs in other birds’ nests
Because it can’t find any twigs
Because it lives in the water
6849.e: Over time the cuckoo has developed in such a way that it no longer has to build its own nest. Instead it uses other birds’ nests for its eggs.
6849.m: The cuckoo doesn’t need its own nest.

6850.q: On which continents are wolves found naturally?
a: In North America, Europe and Asia
6850.e: The wolf is one of the mammals with the widest natural range and lives in various subspecies in North America, Europe and Asia. It is not found naturally in Australia or Antarctica.
6850.m: Wolves live on three large continents.

6851.q: Where does a female octopus usually lay her eggs?
a: In a cave on the seabed
On a rock above the water
6851.e: The female octopus finds a sheltered cave or crack and hangs hundreds of eggs there. She guards them very carefully.
6851.m: Octopus eggs lie in a cave.

6852.q: Where are a kangaroo’s eyes placed to help it see enemies?
a: On the sides of its head
6852.e: A kangaroo’s eyes are on the sides of its head. This means it can see almost everything around it and spot danger quickly.
6852.m: Eyes on the sides see far around.

6853.q: What is the underground hole that a fox lives in called?
6853.e: A fox’s earth is an underground den with several entrances. Sometimes the fox digs it itself, sometimes it takes over a badger’s sett.
6853.m: The fox lives in an earth.

6854.q: How does a magpie defend its territory?
a: It noisily chases off other magpies all year round
It always shares its territory willingly
6854.e: Magpies defend their territory all year round, often with loud calls and threatening gestures towards intruders. The territory is important for food and a nesting site.
6854.m: Magpies defend their territory all year.

6855.q: How high above sea level can golden eagles be found in the Alps?
6855.e: Golden eagles in the Alps often hunt and breed at great heights, frequently above 2000 metres above sea level. There they find suitable rocks and open hunting grounds.
6855.m: It often lives high above 2000 metres.

6856.q: How many planets does our solar system have?
6856.e: Our solar system has eight planets, from Mercury to Neptune. The Earth is the third planet from the Sun.

6857.q: Where does a salmon swim to breed?
a: Back to the river where it was born
6857.e: Salmon live in the sea, but to spawn they return to exactly the fresh water where they hatched themselves. This ability is called homing.

6858.q: What does the red kite show in spring when it wants to find or defend a partner?
6858.e: During courtship, red kites show impressive flight manoeuvres with loops and dives. With them they impress their partner or defend their territory.
6858.m: Red kites court with acrobatic flights.

6859.q: What do a male mosquito’s antennae often look like?
6859.e: Male mosquitoes have strikingly bushy antennae, which they use to hear the hum of the females. Females, on the other hand, have smoother, thinner antennae.

6860.q: How do the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems differ?
a: The sympathetic activates the body, the parasympathetic relaxes it
Both are parts of the brain with no function in the body
6860.e: These two parts of the autonomic nervous system work in opposite ways. The sympathetic prepares for effort, the parasympathetic promotes rest and recovery.
6860.m: The sympathetic activates, the parasympathetic relaxes.

6861.q: At what altitude does the snow leopard often live in summer?
a: Above the tree line, up to over 4000 metres
By the sea at sea level
6861.e: In summer it climbs to high altitudes. In winter it often follows its prey down to lower areas.
6861.m: In summer it lives very high up.

6862.q: What is an important difference between a cockerel’s call and a hen’s cackling?
a: The cockerel’s crowing is much louder
Both calls sound exactly the same
6862.e: A cockerel’s crowing is a very loud sound that carries far, while the hens’ cackling sounds much quieter. So you can often tell cockerel and hen apart just by the sound.
6862.m: A cockerel’s crowing is very loud.

a: An amount you want to save to buy something particular
6863.e: A savings goal is what you are putting money aside for, for example a new bike. It helps you stay motivated to save.
6863.m: A savings goal keeps you motivated to save.

6864.q: Is the Alpine newt protected in Switzerland?
a: It is bred as a pet
6864.e: Like most amphibian species, the Alpine newt is protected by law in Switzerland. It must not simply be caught or disturbed.
6864.m: The Alpine newt is protected in Switzerland.

6865.q: Roughly how long is a Bactrian camel pregnant?
6865.e: The female carries her young for about 13 months. Usually only one calf is born.
6865.m: A Bactrian camel’s pregnancy lasts about 13 months.

6866.q: How well does a wild boar see?
6866.e: A wild boar’s eyes are not particularly good. Its nose and ears, however, are much better.

6867.q: What does the common frog have on its back feet for swimming?
6867.e: The common frog has webbing between the toes of its back feet. This helps it move well through the water.
6867.m: Webbed feet help the frog swim.

6868.q: What horns do many rams (male sheep) have?
a: A single straight horn like a unicorn
6868.e: Many rams have large, spiral-curled horns on their heads. But some breeds of sheep have no horns at all.

6869.q: What especially helps a goat notice enemies from far away?
a: Its sense of touch in its hooves
6869.e: Goats have very good hearing and ears that can move. That way they often hear enemies from far away.

6870.q: Into which three body sections is a cockchafer divided?
6870.e: All insects have a head, thorax and abdomen. The legs and wings are attached to the thorax.
6870.m: An insect’s body is divided into head, thorax and abdomen.

6871.q: Roughly how long does it take for a red kite’s eggs to hatch?
6871.e: The red kite’s incubation lasts a good month. During this time it is mainly the female that sits on the eggs.
6871.m: The red kite incubates for a good month.

6872.q: In which habitats is the kestrel typically found?
a: In open country such as fields, but also in towns
Only high above the tree line in eternal snow
Only over wide stretches of sea far from land
6872.e: The kestrel prefers open land such as meadows, fields and roadsides, where it can hunt mice well. But it also copes well with towns and breeds on tall buildings.
6872.m: Open country and towns are its home.

6873.q: Roughly how heavy is an adult llama?
6873.e: A llama usually weighs 100 to 150 kilograms. So it is much lighter than a horse.

6874.q: What does a plant need the green pigment chlorophyll for?
6874.e: Chlorophyll captures the sunlight that the plant needs for photosynthesis. This produces sugar as a source of energy, and it also makes the leaves look green.

6875.q: How fast can a rhinoceros run despite its size?
6875.e: Although rhinos are so heavy, they can run surprisingly fast. They can reach up to 45 kilometres per hour.

6876.q: What does a trout use to steer skilfully through the water?
6876.e: Trout have several fins on their body, for example on the back, the belly and the tail. With these fins they steer and move skilfully in the water.

6877.q: What is the difference between heat conduction and heat radiation?
a: Conduction needs contact, radiation also works through a vacuum
6877.e: In heat conduction, energy is passed on through direct contact, for example from a hot pan to its handle. Heat radiation travels as a wave, which is how the sun's heat reaches us through empty space.

6878.q: The picture shows a rainbow trout with a pink band. Where does it originally come from?
6878.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. The brown trout, on the other hand, is native to Europe.
6878.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

6879.q: Roughly how much time does a cat spend cleaning itself each day?
a: A whole day without a break
6879.e: Cats are very clean animals and often spend several hours a day grooming their fur. That way their fur stays clean and shiny.
6879.m: Cats groom themselves for many hours a day.

6880.q: Why shouldn’t a llama be kept alone?
6880.e: Llamas are herd animals and need company. That is why they are kept at least in pairs.

6881.q: Where does the Alpine salamander like to hide during the day?
a: Under stones and in cracks in the rock
In the middle of open meadow paths
6881.e: It looks for damp, dark hiding places to protect itself from drying out and from predators. Stones and cracks in the rock offer exactly these conditions.
6881.m: Stones and cracks are its hiding place.

6882.q: Since which event has Switzerland officially been permanently neutral?
a: Since the Congress of Vienna in 1815
Since the founding of the EU
6882.e: At the Congress of Vienna in 1815, the great powers of Europe recognised Switzerland’s permanent neutrality. Since then Switzerland has tried to stay out of military conflicts.
6882.m: Switzerland has been permanently neutral since 1815.

6883.q: Why do wild boar piglets have striped fur?
a: So that they are easier to find
6883.e: The stripes help the little piglets hide among leaves and bushes. That way enemies don’t spot them so easily.

6884.q: What is an example of a symbiosis or close relationship with aphids?
a: Ants get honeydew and protect the aphids
6884.e: In the relationship between ants and aphids, both sides benefit. The ants get food and the aphids get protection.
6884.m: Ants and aphids help each other.

6885.q: What is the famous reindeer with the red nose called?
6885.e: Rudolph is a character from a Christmas song and a story. His red nose glows in the dark.

6886.q: Why does the Roman snail urgently need damp surroundings?
a: Because otherwise its body would dry out
Because otherwise it would grow too fast
Because otherwise it would lose its colour
6886.e: The snail’s soft body dries out quickly without moisture. That is why it usually lives in damp, shady places.
6886.m: Moisture protects it from drying out.

6887.q: Why is the house sparrow seen as especially adaptable?
a: Because it can live almost anywhere people are
Because it can fly especially fast
Because it migrates south in winter
Because it eats only one kind of food
6887.e: The sparrow can live in towns, villages and on farms because it adapts well to different habitats. This makes it one of the most successful birds in the world.

6888.q: What often helps common toads get safely across a road?
a: A toad fence with buckets or a tunnel
A toad taxi with an engine
6888.e: Along many roads, toad fences are put up in spring. They guide the animals to safe crossings or into buckets.
6888.m: Toad fences protect animals on roads.

6889.q: Which little town in the canton of Solothurn lies at the foot of the Jura?
6889.e: Balsthal lies in the Thal, a beautiful valley in the canton of Solothurn at the foot of the Jura mountains. Burgdorf and Langenthal belong to Bern, Zofingen to Aargau.
6889.m: Balsthal lies in the Thal at the foot of the Jura.

6890.q: How many species of tapir are there today?
6890.e: Four species live today: the lowland tapir, the mountain tapir, Baird’s tapir and the Malayan tapir. All belong to the tapir genus.
6890.m: There are four tapir species today.

6891.q: Why have rabbits become a problem in Australia?
a: They became very numerous and strip the fields bare
6891.e: In Australia rabbits have hardly any natural enemies, so their numbers have become huge. As a result they damage fields and nature.
6891.m: Without enemies, rabbits become too many.

6892.q: Roughly how much does a meerkat weigh?
6892.e: Meerkats are quite light, about like a bag of sugar. So they weigh less than a kilogram.
6892.m: Meerkats weigh less than a kilo.

a: So that your eyes stay moist and clean
So that your nose stays clear
6893.e: When you blink, tear fluid spreads over the eye. That keeps it clean and stops it drying out.

6894.q: What is the mother kangaroo’s pouch mainly for?
a: As a safe place for the baby to grow
As a hiding place for food
For the mother to sleep in
6894.e: In the pouch the tiny baby is protected and warm. There it drinks milk and grows until it is big enough for the outside world.
6894.m: The pouch protects the baby kangaroo.

6895.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult male orangutan get?
6895.e: Males are much heavier than females, which often weigh 35 to 50 kilograms. They are the heaviest tree-living mammals.
6895.m: Males weigh up to about 100 kilograms.

6896.q: What is in a goldfish’s throat to break up food?
6896.e: Goldfish have no teeth in their mouth, but special throat teeth further back in the throat. With them they can break up their food.

6897.q: What protection status does the barn swallow have in Switzerland?
a: It is protected and must not be disturbed
It is seen as a pest and may be controlled
It has no special protection at all
6897.e: The barn swallow is a protected bird species in Switzerland. Its nests must therefore not simply be removed.
6897.m: Barn swallows are protected by law.

6898.q: Which bird family does the great crested grebe belong to?
6898.e: The great crested grebe belongs to the grebe family, which is known for its lobed feet and diving skills. This family is not closely related to ducks.
6898.m: Grebes are the great crested grebe’s family.

6899.q: Put simply, what is the principle of energy conversion in a thermal power station?
a: Chemical or nuclear energy is converted via heat and motion into electrical energy
Electrical energy is obtained directly from coal without intermediate steps
Heat is converted completely into electricity without any loss
A thermal power station produces energy entirely without fuel
6899.e: In a thermal power station, burning fuel heats water into steam, which drives a turbine. The turbine turns a generator that produces electricity, and some of the energy is always lost as waste heat.
6899.m: Thermal power stations turn heat into electricity via steam.

6900.q: Which family does the adder belong to?
6900.e: The adder belongs to the vipers. It is related to the asp viper and the nose-horned viper.

6901.q: How do young male blackbirds in their first year differ from adult males?
a: They have white spots all over
6901.e: In their first year young males still have brownish feathers, similar to the female. Only later do they become properly black.
6901.m: Young males are brown at first.

6902.q: What does the cuckoo usually do during the day when it isn’t calling?
a: It sits hidden and hunts for insects
It digs tunnels under the ground
6902.e: During the day the cuckoo often sits quietly hidden on a branch and keeps a lookout for caterpillars and other insects. Only when it calls does it give itself away to people.
6902.m: The cuckoo hunts insects while hidden.

6905.q: What might the Alpine salamander’s black colour mean in relation to its mountain habitat?
a: It might help it absorb warmth better
It makes it invisible to birds
It makes it glow in the dark
6905.e: Some scientists think the dark colour helps the Alpine salamander absorb the sun’s warmth more efficiently in the cooler mountain areas. This is an advantage at cold altitudes.
6905.m: Black might help it warm up.

6906.q: What does a dromedary sometimes spit when it feels threatened?
6906.e: The animal brings up contents from its stomach and spits them out. This is unpleasant but not poisonous.
6906.m: The spit is stomach contents, not hump water.

6907.q: What are a gibbon’s eyes like?
a: They face forwards and help it judge distances
They are on the sides of its head like a horse’s
They glow in the dark like a cat’s
6907.e: As is usual in primates, the eyes face forwards. This lets gibbons judge distances well when leaping.
6907.m: Good depth vision helps with swinging.

6908.q: How do a spotted hyena’s front legs compare with its back legs?
6908.e: The front legs are longer than the back legs. This makes the back slope downwards towards the rear.
6908.m: Hyenas have longer front legs than back legs.

6909.q: What colour is a trout’s back usually compared with its belly?
a: The back is darker, the belly lighter
The back is white, the belly black
6909.e: A trout’s back is usually darker, while its belly is lighter. This is the case in many fish.
6909.m: Trout have a dark back and a light belly.

6910.q: What does it mean that the pool frog is a cold-blooded animal?
a: Its body temperature adapts to its surroundings
It can change its colour as it likes
It changes its habitat every year
It is male and female in turn
6910.e: Cold-blooded animals like the pool frog cannot keep their body temperature constant themselves. That is why they often bask in the sun to warm up.
6910.m: The pool frog is cold-blooded like other amphibians.

6911.q: Do robin chicks have a red breast straight away?
a: No, at first they are speckled brown
Yes, but only on the tail
6911.e: Young robins look speckled brown at first. Only after their first moult do they get their lovely red breast.
6911.m: Young robins are speckled brown at first.

6912.q: What colour is a mole’s fur usually?
6912.e: The mole’s velvety fur is usually dark grey or black. That way it is well camouflaged in the dark soil.

6913.q: How do snow leopards leave messages for other snow leopards?
a: With scent marks and scratch marks
6913.e: They mark rocks with urine, droppings and scratch marks. That way other snow leopards learn who has been passing by.

6914.q: How does the great spotted woodpecker protect its brain when hammering?
a: A special skull structure cushions the blows
It wears a kind of helmet made of feathers
It has no brain in its head at all
6914.e: In the great spotted woodpecker’s head there is a cushion that absorbs the blows. That way it doesn’t hurt itself when hammering.

6915.q: How many toes do meerkats have on their front and back paws?
6915.e: Meerkats have four toes on all their feet. This is a feature that sets them apart from some other mongooses.
6915.m: Meerkats have four toes per foot.

6916.q: What is the behaviour called in which the mute swan raises its wings over its back like a sail?
6916.e: When busking, the swan raises its wings to look bigger and stronger. With it, it often shows its power in its territory.
6916.m: Raised wings like this are called busking.

6917.q: What is the main aim of the Paris climate agreement?
a: To limit global warming to well below 2 degrees
To ban all fossil fuels immediately
To commit only Switzerland to climate protection
To lower the sea level artificially
6917.e: In the 2015 Paris climate agreement almost all countries in the world committed to limiting global warming, if possible, to 1.5 degrees. To do this, greenhouse gas emissions are to be reduced worldwide.
6917.m: The Paris agreement aims to keep warming well below 2 degrees.

6918.q: What is characteristic of how wolves move over long distances?
a: Constantly leaping from branch to branch
6918.e: Over long distances, wolves usually move at a steady, energy-saving trot. This lets them cover many kilometres without a long break.
6918.m: Wolves trot tirelessly over long distances.

6919.q: What were llamas mainly used for in the Andes in the past?
6919.e: Llamas carry loads on mountain paths. They can carry about a quarter of their body weight.
6919.m: Llamas are the classic pack animals of the Andes.

6920.q: What does the compass jellyfish have on its bell?
a: Brown stripes that look like rays
6920.e: The compass jellyfish has brown stripes on its bell that look like the points of a compass. It is often found on European coasts.
6920.m: The compass jellyfish has a striped pattern.

6921.q: Why are mute swans good swimmers?
a: Their body is streamlined and their feet are webbed
They have a fin on their tail
6921.e: Its slim body and webbed feet make the mute swan a skilful swimmer. That way it glides elegantly over the water.
6921.m: Its shape and feet make it a swimmer.

6922.q: What does it mean that the lake trout is cold-blooded?
a: Its body temperature depends on the water temperature
It can keep its body temperature constant itself
It changes its colour every year
It switches between fresh and salt water
6922.e: Fish produce hardly any body heat of their own. Their temperature follows that of the water around them.
6922.m: In the cold-blooded lake trout, body temperature adjusts to the water.

6923.q: What does the fur of newborn baboons often look like?
6923.e: The young are usually dark when they are born. The fur becomes lighter as they get older.

6924.q: What do wood mice do when danger threatens?
a: They flee into their burrow in a flash
6924.e: When in danger, the wood mouse runs into its safe burrow under the ground in a flash.
6924.m: In danger, quickly into the burrow.

6925.q: What job does the spleen have in the body?
a: It filters out old blood cells and helps with defence
It cleans urea out of the blood
6925.e: The spleen sorts old or damaged blood cells out of the blood. It also plays a part in the immune defences. Urea is filtered by the kidneys, and bile is made by the liver.

6926.q: Roughly how much weight can a brown bear put on in a few months before winter?
a: None, the weight stays the same
6926.e: In autumn a brown bear eats so much that it often puts on several dozen kilograms of fat within a few months. This fat serves as an energy reserve for its winter rest.
6926.m: Bears put on a lot of fat before winter.

6927.q: Why does a cow chew so often and for so long?
6927.e: Cows bring their food back up and chew it again; this is called chewing the cud. That way they can digest the tough grass better.

6928.e: Jellyfish have no bones and no skeleton. Their soft body is supported by the water.

6929.q: How does the snow leopard move around in the mountains?
a: It climbs skilfully over steep rocks
6929.e: It is an excellent climber. With its paws and tail it keeps its balance even on steep ground.

6930.q: What colour is an Alpine newt’s belly?
6930.e: The Alpine newt has a bright orange belly without spots. Its back is dark, and in the male it turns bluish in the breeding season.
6930.m: Alpine newts have an orange belly.

6931.q: In which direction does the shell of most Roman snails coil?
6931.e: In most Roman snails the shell coils to the right. This is called right-handed coiling.
6931.m: The shell usually coils to the right.

6932.q: What does the saying “a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush” mean?
a: Something certain is better than something uncertain
Birds in bushes are worth less
You should never hold on to anything
6932.e: This old saying means that you should take a small, certain thing rather than hope for something bigger that you might not get at all. The bird in the hand stands for something small but certain.
6932.m: Something small and certain beats something uncertain.

6933.q: Which river flows right through the town of Solothurn?
6933.e: The Aare flows through the old town of Solothurn and is important for the town. Many bridges cross the river.
6933.m: The Aare flows right through Solothurn.

6934.q: When did the great variety of whitefish species in Alpine lakes probably begin to develop?
a: In the time of the dinosaurs
A million years ago in the sea
6934.e: When the glaciers melted, the lakes filled with water. In them, many whitefish species developed within a few thousand years.
6934.m: The variety arose after the Ice Age.

6935.q: How does a housefly eat its food?
a: It sucks it up with a proboscis
It licks it with a tongue like a dog
6935.e: The housefly has no teeth for chewing. That is why it sucks up its food with a special proboscis.

6936.q: Who feeds the young in barn swallows?
6936.e: In barn swallows, the male and female feed the young together. That way they can satisfy the chicks’ great hunger.

6937.q: Roughly how old can a dromedary get?
6937.e: Dromedaries live to quite an old age if they are well looked after. That is well above the life expectancy of many domestic animals.
6937.m: Dromedaries live up to about 50 years.

6938.q: When is the common toad mainly active?
6938.e: Common toads are nocturnal and mostly hide during the day. At dusk and at night they go looking for food.

6939.q: From which neighbouring country do brown bears occasionally wander into Switzerland today?
6939.e: From the Trentino region in Italy, where brown bears have been reintroduced in recent decades, single animals occasionally wander into Switzerland. They usually cross into the canton of the Grisons.
6939.m: Bears often wander into Switzerland from Italy.

6940.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult Asian elephant get?
6940.e: Fully grown animals weigh about two to five tonnes, depending on whether they are male or female. The bulls are heavier than the cows.

6941.q: What do you call energy produced by flowing water?
6941.e: Flowing water can drive a water wheel or a turbine. This turns the movement of the water into electricity.

6942.q: What is a jellyfish’s body made of almost entirely?
6942.e: A jellyfish’s body is made almost entirely of water. That is why it is so soft and sometimes almost see-through.

6943.q: What is it called when part of a bee colony moves out with a queen?
6943.e: This moving out is called swarming. The bees often hang in a thick cluster on a branch until they find a new home.

6944.q: Does the kestrel build its own nest?
a: No, it mostly uses other birds’ abandoned nests or rock ledges
Yes, it builds an elaborate new nest of twigs every year
Yes, it digs a hole in soft soil
No, it lays its eggs straight onto bare rock without any protection
6944.e: Kestrels don’t build their own nests. They breed in old crows’ nests, rock ledges, holes in walls or special nest boxes.
6944.m: The kestrel doesn’t build its own nest.

6945.q: How do chimpanzees often look for food?
a: Only at night in the dark
Never, they would rather go hungry
6945.e: Chimpanzees often roam the forest together in small groups. That way they find fruit and other food more easily.
6945.m: Chimpanzees often look for food together.

a: A band of strong wind high in the atmosphere
An ocean current in the deep sea
A type of radiation from the sun
6946.e: The jet stream is a narrow band of very fast winds about 10 kilometres up. It has a big influence on how weather systems move over Europe.
6946.m: The jet stream is a band of strong wind high up.

6947.q: What does a lion use to hold and kill its prey?
6947.e: The lion holds its prey with its sharp claws and kills it with its powerful teeth. These tools make it a good hunter.
6947.m: Claws and teeth help with hunting.

6948.q: How many young does a female snow leopard usually have per litter?
6948.e: Litters usually have two to three young. They are born in a sheltered rocky cave.
6948.m: There are usually two to three young.

6949.q: What does the expression “goldfish memory” wrongly suggest about goldfish?
a: That they can supposedly only remember things for a few seconds
That they are the best at maths of all animals
6949.e: The expression “goldfish memory” is actually wrong, because goldfish can remember things for weeks. They even learn where food is hidden.
6949.m: Goldfish have a better memory than people think.

6950.q: How many different stages of development does a ladybird go through from egg to adult beetle?
a: Six: six different kinds of larva
One, it always stays the same
6950.e: A ladybird develops in four steps. First it is an egg, then a larva, then a pupa and finally an adult beetle.
6950.m: The ladybird goes through four stages: egg, larva, pupa and beetle.

6951.q: In which parts of Europe is the fire salamander widespread?
a: In large parts of central and southern Europe
6951.e: The fire salamander is widespread in central and southern Europe, from Spain to the Balkans. It is also found in many forests in Switzerland.
6951.m: It lives in large parts of Europe.

6952.q: What is a baby chimpanzee called?
6952.e: A baby chimpanzee is simply called an infant. It stays with its mother for a long time.
6952.m: A baby chimpanzee is called an infant.

6954.q: Roughly how old can domestic geese get?
6954.e: Well-kept domestic geese can live to a surprisingly old age. Some reach 15 to 20 years.
6954.m: Domestic geese can live up to 20 years.

6955.q: What colour is an adult bearded vulture’s head usually?
a: Pale, often whitish with a black stripe through the eye
6955.e: An adult bearded vulture’s head is usually pale, with a striking black stripe over the eye. This stripe gives it a distinctive look.
6955.m: Pale head with a black eye stripe.

6956.q: Roughly how many spines does an adult hedgehog have?
6956.e: A hedgehog has thousands of small spines on its back. They protect it from enemies like armour.
6956.m: Hedgehogs have thousands of sharp spines.

6957.q: How is the common buzzard population doing in Switzerland?
a: It is not threatened and is common
It was only discovered last year
6957.e: The common buzzard is a common, unthreatened species in Switzerland. It benefits from the open farmland with fields and meadows.
6957.m: The common buzzard is common and not threatened.

6958.q: Which country is especially well known for large carp ponds?
6958.e: In the Czech Republic there have been large carp ponds for centuries. Carp farming has a long tradition there.
6958.m: The Czech Republic is famous for its carp ponds.

6959.q: Why can the least weasel follow mice right into their narrow tunnels?
a: Because its body is very slim and long
Because it has very short, stocky legs
Because it has big digging paws
Because it has no fur tips on its legs
6959.e: Its slim, worm-like body lets the least weasel get into the narrowest mouse tunnels. There the prey has hardly any chance to escape.
6959.m: A slim body fits into mouse tunnels.

6960.q: In which Swiss waters is the wels catfish found?
a: In larger lakes such as Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Murten
6960.e: In Switzerland the wels catfish lives mainly in lower, warmer waters, for example in the Jura lakes region. High mountain waters are too cold for it.
6960.m: In Switzerland it lives in warm lakes.

6961.q: What helps hedgehogs travel from garden to garden?
a: Small gaps or holes in fences
A swimming pool in the garden
6961.e: Hedgehogs travel long distances every night to find food. Small holes in fences help them move from garden to garden.
6961.m: Holes in fences help hedgehogs get around.

6962.q: What happens when a pond dries up in summer?
a: Winged pond skaters can fly to other waters
All pond skaters walk across the land
They dig themselves in and become pupae
6962.e: Animals with wings can look for new water. Wingless ones have a harder time.
6962.m: Wings help in the search for water.

6963.q: What are badger cubs like when they are born?
a: Blind and with very little fur
Able to see and with thick fur
Already as big as their mother
6963.e: Badger cubs are blind at birth and have only fine, thin fur. Only after a few weeks can they see.

6964.q: How does a blue whale breathe?
a: With lungs, it has to come to the surface
6964.e: The blue whale is a mammal and has lungs. That is why it has to keep coming up to breathe air.
6964.m: Blue whales breathe air like us.

6965.q: What colour is a female blackbird usually?
6965.e: The female is brown and less striking than the male. That way she is better camouflaged while sitting on the eggs.

6966.q: What does the brown bear stand for as a symbol in Russia?
a: It is often seen there as a symbol of strength and of the country itself
It is seen there as a symbol of weakness
It is only seen there as a pest
It is seen there as a symbol of cold deserts
6966.e: In Russia the brown bear is often used as a symbol of strength, size and the country itself. It appears in coats of arms, stories and even as a sports mascot.
6966.m: In Russia the bear stands for strength.

6967.q: How many foals does a female donkey usually have at one time?
6967.e: A female donkey normally has only one foal at a time. Twins are very rare in donkeys.
6967.m: Female donkeys usually have one foal.

6968.q: How many legs does a starfish have?
a: A starfish has no legs, only tiny feet
Exactly as many as a beetle
6968.e: Starfish have no real legs, but many tiny tube feet under their body. That is something quite different from legs.
6968.m: Starfish have tiny feet instead of legs.

6969.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female pike lay?
6969.e: A female pike can lay many thousands of eggs at once. But not all eggs and young fish survive to adulthood.
6969.m: Pike lay a great many eggs.

6970.q: What makes aphids different from spiders?
a: Aphids have six legs, spiders eight
Aphids have eight legs, spiders six
Both have the same number of legs
6970.e: Aphids are insects with six legs and three body sections. Spiders are arachnids with eight legs.
6970.m: Insects have six legs, spiders have eight.

6971.q: In what form does the stag beetle spend most of its life?
a: As a larva in rotting wood
As an egg in the water
As a pupa in a leaf
6971.e: The larva lives for several years in wood under the ground. The adult beetle, on the other hand, lives for only a few weeks.
6971.m: Most of its life is spent as a larva.

6972.q: How does a magpie behave towards larger groups of its own kind outside the breeding season?
a: It may join up in small groups
It then always lives completely alone
It immediately attacks every other magpie
6972.e: Outside the breeding season, magpies can sometimes gather in small groups, for example when looking for food together. During the breeding season, however, they are usually territorial.

6973.q: How does the snow leopard usually live?
a: In herds of a hundred animals
6973.e: Adult snow leopards normally live alone. Only during the mating season and as mothers with young are they together.

6974.q: How does a baby gorilla get attention when it is hungry?
6974.e: Baby gorillas make different sounds, for example squeaking. That way the mothers know their baby needs something.
6974.m: Babies squeak when they are hungry.

6975.q: How big do most native woodlice get?
6975.e: Native woodlice are usually only about one to two centimetres long. So they are small but easy to see.
6975.m: Native woodlice are about 1 to 2 cm long.

6976.q: What do newly hatched salmon feed on in their first weeks?
a: The yolk sac on their belly
6976.e: Newly hatched salmon still carry a yolk sac on their belly. They feed on it in their first weeks.
6976.m: The yolk sac feeds newly hatched salmon.

6977.q: In which habitats do meerkats live?
a: In dry areas such as savannahs and semi-deserts
In the moors of northern Europe
6977.e: They live in open, dry areas, for example in the Kalahari. The ground there is good for digging.
6977.m: They live in dry, open areas.

a: A sticky resin for sealing the beehive
The wax the honeycombs are made of
6978.e: Propolis is a sticky tree resin that bees collect and process. They use it to seal cracks in the hive and protect it from germs.

6979.q: What is it called when a goat brings its food back up and chews it again?
6979.e: Goats bring their food back from their stomach into their mouth and chew it thoroughly again. This is called chewing the cud.

6980.q: Do all Swiss kestrels fly south in winter?
a: No, many stay all year, others move a little further away
Yes, they all fly to South Africa
Yes, they all spend the winter in the Arctic
No, they all spend the winter under water
6980.e: The kestrel is a partial migrant. Some birds stay in Switzerland in winter too, while others move to milder parts of southern and western Europe.
6980.m: The kestrel is only partly a migratory bird.

6981.q: Which organisation works especially hard to protect chimpanzees?
6981.e: The Jane Goodall Institute was founded to protect chimpanzees and their habitat. It works for nature conservation all around the world.
6981.m: The Jane Goodall Institute protects chimpanzees.

6982.q: Roughly how long is a female lynx pregnant?
6982.e: After about ten weeks the female lynx gives birth to her young. This is similar to the pregnancy of many medium-sized mammals.
6982.m: A female lynx gives birth after about ten weeks.

6983.q: What is the force called with which a body presses straight down on a surface?
6983.e: Weight is caused by gravity acting on the mass of a body. It presses the body onto the surface it is standing or lying on.

6984.q: Which danger caused by people threatens tawny owls especially badly today?
a: Road traffic and collisions with windows
Too much food in the forests
6984.e: Many tawny owls die in collisions with cars, as they often fly low over roads when hunting. Windows are sometimes fatal for them too.
6984.m: Road traffic is a big danger to tawny owls.

6985.q: What do pigs like to do when you give them lots of straw?
a: Root around in it and build a nest
Eat it and spit it out again
6985.e: Pigs love rooting around in straw and making themselves a soft nest. This is part of their natural behaviour.
6985.m: Pigs love rooting around in straw.

6986.q: Because of what it eats, which larger group of animals does the stoat belong to?
6986.e: Because it mainly eats mice and other small animals, the stoat counts as a carnivore. Its sharp teeth are perfect for hunting.

6987.q: How long does a snow leopard usually feed on a large prey animal such as a wild sheep?
6987.e: Large prey provides food for several days. The snow leopard keeps coming back to it.
6987.m: One large prey animal lasts several days.

6988.q: Which animal family does the Eurasian otter belong to?
6988.e: The otter belongs to the mustelid family. So it is related to the badger, the stoat and the stone marten.
6988.m: Otters belong to the mustelid family.

6989.q: What colours is the flag of the canton of Solothurn?
6989.e: The flag of Solothurn is red at the top and white at the bottom. You can see it on many buildings in the canton.
6989.m: Solothurn's flag is red and white.

6990.q: What do perch parents do after spawning?
a: They don’t look after the spawn
They guard the eggs for months
They build a nest of stones
They carry the young in their mouths
6990.e: Perch don’t care for their young. The spawn is left to itself.
6990.m: Perch don’t look after their young.

6991.q: What kind of water does the carp especially like?
6991.e: Carp feel most comfortable in warm, calm water. In cold water they become sluggish.

6992.q: What colour is the back of many sharks compared with the belly?
6992.e: From above, a shark looks like the dark water. From below, it hardly stands out against the bright sky. That way it is well camouflaged.
6992.m: Sharks are dark on top and light underneath.

6993.q: What colour are ladybird eggs usually?
6993.e: The female lays small yellow eggs on the underside of leaves. There they are well hidden and protected.

6994.q: How are perch fillets often prepared in Switzerland?
a: Fried or breaded, usually with lemon
6994.e: Perch fillets are a popular restaurant dish in Switzerland. They are usually served crispy fried or breaded.
6994.m: Fried perch fillets are a classic.

6995.q: How does the wels catfish usually swallow its prey?
a: After soaking it in slime for days
Only after spearing it on the bank
6995.e: Wels catfish usually swallow their prey whole. They have a mouth that can stretch very wide for this.
6995.m: The wels catfish swallows prey whole.

6996.q: Where does the female lay her eggs?
a: In the middle of the sea
6996.e: Female sea turtles leave the water and dig a hole in the sand for their eggs. Then they go back to the sea.
6996.m: The eggs are buried in the sand.

6998.q: Which instruments play the wolf in “Peter and the Wolf”?
6998.e: In Sergei Prokofiev’s Peter and the Wolf, each character has its own instrument. Three horns play the wolf, the flute is the bird, the oboe the duck and the clarinet the cat.
6998.m: In the piece Peter and the Wolf, horns play the wolf.

6999.q: Is a dolphin a fish or a mammal?
6999.e: Dolphins give birth to live young and feed them milk, so they are mammals. Fish usually lay eggs.

7000.q: How big are newborn brown bear cubs compared with their mother?
a: Very small and light, weighing only a few hundred grams
Almost as big as their mother
7000.e: Newborn brown bear cubs are surprisingly small and often weigh only a few hundred grams. Only over their first years do they grow into strong animals.
7000.m: Bear cubs are tiny at birth.

7001.q: Roughly how long does a single worker wasp live?
7001.e: Workers usually live only a few weeks. Then they die and new wasps take over the work.

7002.q: What happens at the entrance to the nest hole while the young are growing up?
a: Droppings build up and it starts to smell bad
The hole stays completely clean and odourless
The parents carry the droppings far away every day
7002.e: Because the young leave lots of droppings in the nest, the hole gets very dirty over time and smells unpleasant. Even so, it stays in use until the young fly off.
7002.m: The nest chamber gets very dirty over time.

7003.q: Which beaver is native to Europe, and so also to Switzerland?
7003.e: The Eurasian beaver lives in Europe, while a separate species, the Canadian beaver, is found in North America. The two species look similar but are genetically different.
7003.m: The Eurasian beaver lives in Europe.

7004.q: What kind of coat does a roe deer fawn have in autumn after its first moult?
7004.e: In autumn the fawn loses its white spots. It then gets a plain coat like an adult roe deer.
7004.m: In autumn the fawn’s spots disappear.

7005.q: What is the area that a gorilla group usually moves around in called?
7005.e: A gorilla group wanders around within a particular area of the forest to find food. This area is called its home range.
7005.m: Gorilla groups have their own home range.

7006.q: Which animal changes its fur colour to white in winter for camouflage?
7006.e: The mountain hare lives in the mountains and swaps its brown summer coat for a white winter coat. That way it is well camouflaged in the snow.
7006.m: In winter the hare wears white.

7007.q: How does the European tree frog move about especially skilfully?
a: It jumps and climbs in bushes and trees
It mostly digs itself into the ground
7007.e: Thanks to its long back legs and sticky toe pads, the tree frog can climb and jump skilfully. This sets it apart from many other frog species.
7007.m: Jumping and climbing are its strengths.

7008.q: What does it mean that the giraffe is the tallest land animal in the world?
a: No other land animal naturally grows so tall
It is the heaviest animal in the world
It is the smallest animal in the world
7008.e: At up to six metres tall, the giraffe towers over all other land animals. Its long neck and long legs make this possible.
7008.m: The giraffe is the tallest land animal.

7009.q: What can young common wall lizards already do shortly after hatching?
a: Move about on their own and catch prey
Only be fed by their mother
7009.e: As soon as the little wall lizards hatch, they are completely independent. They immediately hunt small insects of their own.
7009.m: The young are independent straight away.

7010.q: When is the eel usually active?
a: It is active all the time without a break
7010.e: Eels are mainly active at dusk and at night. During the day they often hide in holes or in the mud.

7011.q: Which animals are among a squirrel’s enemies?
7011.e: Birds of prey such as the goshawk and martens hunt squirrels. That is why these animals are always alert in the forest.
7011.m: Birds of prey and martens are enemies.

7012.q: Roughly how long do young barn swallows stay in the nest before they fledge?
7012.e: Young barn swallows stay in the nest for about three weeks before they fly for the first time. After that their parents feed them for a while longer.
7012.m: Around three weeks until they fly.

7013.e: International means that something involves several countries, for example a partnership or a meeting. The opposite would be national, meaning involving only one country.
7013.m: International means that something involves several countries.

7014.q: What is the most striking feature at the rear end of an earwig?
7014.e: At the end of its abdomen the earwig has two strong appendages that look like pincers. They are the reason it is easy to recognise.
7014.m: The pincers at the rear are typical.

7015.q: In which country is the story “The Jungle Book” set?
7015.e: In The Jungle Book, Rudyard Kipling tells of the boy Mowgli, who grows up with wolves in the Indian jungle. There he meets Baloo, Bagheera and the tiger Shere Khan.
7015.m: The Jungle Book is set in India.

7016.q: Which group of animals do dung beetles belong to?
7016.e: Dung beetles have six legs and a body made of head, thorax and abdomen. These are typical features of insects.
7016.m: Dung beetles are insects with six legs.

7017.q: How much does a mole have to eat every day compared with its weight?
a: Almost as much as its own body weight
Nothing at all, it lives on air
7017.e: Because the mole uses a lot of energy digging, it has to eat large amounts every day. Without food it would starve after just a few hours.
7017.m: Moles have to eat all the time.

7018.q: How does a jellyfish catch its prey?
a: It paralyses it with stinging threads from its tentacles
It catches it with its fins
It scares it with loud calls
7018.e: When a small animal touches the jellyfish’s tentacles, tiny venomous threads shoot out. These paralyse the prey so that the jellyfish can eat it.
7018.m: A jellyfish paralyses prey with stinging threads.

7019.q: What is typical of a puma’s footprint in the ground?
a: No claw marks can be seen
7019.e: Pumas pull their claws in when walking. That is why you usually see no claws in the track, unlike with dogs.

7021.q: How do migrating reindeer cross rivers?
a: They jump over in one leap
They wait until the river dries up
7021.e: Reindeer are good swimmers. Their coat with its air-filled hairs helps them stay afloat in the water.

7022.q: What is the full name of the squirrel that lives here in Switzerland?
7022.e: The Eurasian red squirrel lives in Switzerland; its scientific name is Sciurus vulgaris. It can be found in many forests and gardens.
7022.m: The Eurasian red squirrel lives in Switzerland.

7023.q: Which senses help orangutans find ripe fruit?
7023.e: They recognise ripe fruit by its colour and smell. They also remember where and when trees bear fruit.
7023.m: They find fruit with their eyes and nose.

7024.q: Which international court can convict individual people of crimes against humanity?
a: The European Court of Human Rights
7024.e: Since 2002 the International Criminal Court in The Hague has prosecuted individuals for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. The International Court of Justice, by contrast, settles disputes between states.
7024.m: The ICC convicts individuals of the most serious crimes.

7025.q: What does a harbour seal do with its nose when it dives?
a: It keeps breathing through its nose
It holds it shut with its flipper
7025.e: When diving, the harbour seal closes its nostrils so that no water gets in. Only when it comes up does it open them again to breathe.
7025.m: When diving, the seal closes its nose.

7026.q: How does the octopus often communicate with other animals?
7026.e: As the octopus can hardly make any sounds, it often uses the colour of its skin to express something. That way it can warn or camouflage itself.

7027.q: Why does an eagle owl have to turn its whole head when it wants to look to the side?
a: Because its eyes are fixed in their sockets
Because its neck is especially long
Because otherwise it would lose its balance
7027.e: The eagle owl’s eyes are firmly fixed in their sockets and cannot move. That is why it turns its head when it wants to look in another direction.
7027.m: Eagle owl eyes are fixed, so the head turns.

7028.q: What often happens to the colour of a male trout’s body at spawning time?
a: It becomes stronger and more colourful
It becomes as white as snow
7028.e: During the spawning season some male trout change in appearance. Their colours often become stronger to attract females.
7028.m: Male trout become more colourful at spawning time.

7029.q: What colour are the red kite’s feathers mainly?
7029.e: Its rusty red feathers gave the red kite its name. Its head looks paler than its body.
7029.m: Reddish-brown feathers gave the red kite its name.

7030.q: What is typical of soil centipedes, a group of centipedes?
a: They have a long, very narrow body with many pairs of legs
They have only a few pairs of legs
7030.e: Soil centipedes are as thin as threads and live in the soil. They have many pairs of legs and hunt in cracks in the ground.
7030.m: Soil centipedes are long and narrow.

7031.q: How do adult wild boar males usually live outside the mating season?
7031.e: Apart from the mating season, adult male wild boar usually live alone. The females, on the other hand, stay together with their young.
7031.m: Male wild boar often live alone.

7032.q: What colour do male sand lizards often turn in the mating season in spring?
7032.e: In spring, males turn bright green on their sides and sometimes all over their body to impress females. This colour fades again after the mating season.
7032.m: Males turn bright green in spring.

7033.q: How can experts estimate the age of a perch?
a: By annual rings on its scales or ear stones
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its barbels
By the number of its fins
7033.e: As it grows, rings form like in trees, because the fish grows more slowly in winter. They are counted under a microscope.
7033.m: Annual rings give away the age.

7035.q: How many horns do most African rhinos have?
7035.e: African rhinos such as the white rhino usually have two horns one behind the other on their nose. The front one is often bigger.

7036.q: What is a big danger for koalas in Australia?
7036.e: In Australia large forests often burn. Many koalas lose their home and their food as a result.
7036.m: Bushfires are a danger for koalas.

7038.q: What role do reindeer play in the Arctic ecosystem?
a: They are prey for predators and eat plants
7038.e: As plant-eaters, reindeer affect the vegetation. At the same time they are important prey for wolves and other predators.
7038.m: Reindeer are part of the food chain.

7039.q: What does the great tit use to crack hard seed shells?
7039.e: The great tit has a short, strong beak. With it, it can peck open the hard shells of seeds and nuts.
7039.m: Its strong beak opens hard seeds.

7040.q: What does the garden spider make its silk threads from?
a: From a liquid that hardens in the air
7040.e: A sticky liquid is produced inside the spider’s body. As soon as it meets the air, it becomes a solid thread.
7040.m: The liquid hardens in the air.

7041.q: How does a spotted hyena protect itself in a fight over food?
a: It bites and threatens as part of the pack
7041.e: In a pack, hyenas defend their prey together. Calls and threatening gestures also play a part.
7041.m: Hyenas defend prey as a pack.

7042.q: When is the European tree frog mainly active?
7042.e: During the day the tree frog usually sits quietly hidden among leaves. It actively looks for food mainly at dusk and at night.

7043.q: How long does an adult butterfly usually live?
7043.e: Many butterflies live only a few weeks as adult insects. Before that, however, they often spend much longer as an egg, caterpillar and pupa.
7043.m: As an adult, a butterfly lives only a short time.

7044.q: What kind of eyes does a squirrel have?
a: Large, round eyes with good eyesight
Very small eyes, it is almost blind
It has no eyes at all
7044.e: Squirrels have large, round eyes that they can see well with. This helps them spot enemies in time.

7045.q: Which animal are all dog breeds originally descended from?
7045.e: Many thousands of years ago wolves were tamed by people. Over time all of today’s dog breeds developed from them.
7045.m: All dogs are descended from the wolf.

7046.e: Adders that are coloured black are called hell adders (Höllenottern in German). Their zigzag band is hardly visible.
7046.m: A black adder is called a hell adder.

7047.q: What did the bonobo Kanzi become famous for?
a: He learnt to use symbols to communicate
He learnt to play the piano
7047.e: Kanzi understood symbols on a board and could use them to communicate with researchers. He showed how clever bonobos are.

7048.q: What does the fox need its pointed canine teeth for?
a: To grab and hold on to prey
7048.e: With its pointed canine teeth the fox can grab a mouse and hold it tight. Like a dog, an adult fox has about 42 teeth.
7048.m: Pointed canines hold the prey tight.

7049.q: How heavy can a big male gorilla get?
7049.e: Male gorillas are very heavy and muscular. They can weigh as much as two to three adult humans.

7050.q: Is a red deer bigger than a roe deer?
7050.e: The red deer is much bigger and heavier than the roe deer. It is one of the largest wild animals in Switzerland.
7050.m: The red deer is much bigger than a roe deer.

7051.q: What is the funniest way a penguin moves on land?
a: It waddles or slides on its belly
7051.e: On land penguins waddle with little steps. On snow and ice they like to slide on their bellies, which is much faster.
7051.m: Penguins waddle or slide on the ice.

7052.q: Roughly how often does a gorilla mother have a new baby?
a: Only once in her whole life
7052.e: Gorilla mothers look after each baby for a very long time before they become pregnant again. That is why several years usually pass between two babies.
7052.m: Gorilla babies come rarely, every few years.

7053.q: What happens if two adult golden hamsters are put together in one cage?
7053.e: Adult golden hamsters are loners and don’t get on well with each other. Together in a cage they can have serious fights.
7053.m: Adult golden hamsters quickly start fighting.

7054.q: What colour is a chamois’s summer coat usually?
7054.e: In summer the chamois has a short, reddish-brown coat. It is lighter than the thick winter coat.
7054.m: In summer the chamois wears a reddish-brown coat.

7055.q: What job does the mute swan’s beak do when it is feeding?
a: It plucks plants and sieves them out of the water
It digs deep holes in the ground
7055.e: The broad beak helps the swan grab plants and sieve out the water. That way it can feed efficiently.
7055.m: The beak sieves plants out of the water.

7056.q: How many eggs does a female emperor penguin usually lay per year?
7056.e: The female emperor penguin lays only one single egg. Then she hands it over to the male to keep warm and goes to look for food in the sea.
7056.m: Emperor penguins lay only one egg.

7057.q: What is the pterostigma on a dragonfly?
a: A dark spot near the wing tip
A hole in the middle of the wing
A spike on the edge of the wing
7057.e: The pterostigma is a small, thicker and often dark patch at the front near the wing tip. It helps stop the wing from fluttering in fast flight.
7057.m: The pterostigma sits near the wing tip.

7058.q: What does a mosquito do after it has drunk enough blood?
a: It flies away to develop its eggs
It stays on the skin for ever
7058.e: As soon as the mosquito has drunk enough blood, it flies away to rest. During this time the eggs develop inside its body.

7059.q: What is special about how stoats have young?
a: The fertilised egg only settles in the womb much later
7059.e: Stoats have what is called delayed implantation. The fertilised egg waits several months before it settles in the womb and develops further.

7060.q: How does a hamster usually react to loud noises?
a: It comes closer out of curiosity
7060.e: Hamsters have sensitive hearing and are quickly frightened by sudden noise. That is why you should be quiet near them.

7061.q: What is carbon dioxide (CO2) largely responsible for?
7061.e: CO2 is a greenhouse gas that holds heat in the atmosphere. Burning coal, oil and gas increases the amount of CO2 and so strengthens global warming.

7062.q: How does a grasshopper’s camouflage colour help it in everyday life?
a: Birds can’t see it as well in the grass
7062.e: Green or brown colours make the grasshopper almost disappear in the grass. That way it sometimes escapes hungry birds.

7063.q: Why do kangaroos have such big, strong back legs?
7063.e: The strong back legs let the kangaroo make long, fast leaps. This also helps it escape from enemies.

7064.q: What is the best way for countries to solve a big problem like climate change?
7064.e: Many problems, such as climate change, affect the whole world. That is why countries work together in organisations like the UN to find shared solutions.
7064.m: Big problems are solved together with other countries.

7065.q: Where in the sea do seahorses often live?
7065.e: Seagrass meadows give the seahorse lots of plants to hold on to and hide in. It also finds enough small prey there.

7066.q: What does a hamster’s tail look like?
a: As long as its whole body
7066.e: The hamster has only a very short, small tail. This makes it different from a mouse, for example, with its long tail.

7067.q: What is the dance called that bees use to show food sources far away?
7067.e: In the waggle dance the bee moves in a figure of eight and waggles its abdomen. That way it shows the direction and distance of a meadow full of flowers.
7067.m: The waggle dance shows long distances.

7068.q: Roughly how long does the larval stage last in many native dragonflies?
a: Several months to a few years
7068.e: Depending on the species and the water temperature, the larva lives in the water for a few months up to several years. The adult, on the other hand, usually lives only weeks to months.
7068.m: Larvae often live longer than adult dragonflies.

7069.q: What happens to mosquito larvae when the water they live in dries up?
a: They swim to the next pond
7069.e: Mosquito larvae absolutely need water to live and breathe. If their water dries up, they cannot survive.

7070.q: How do carrion crow pairs normally live together?
a: They usually stay together for life
They only live together for a day
7070.e: Carrion crows are monogamous birds and often stay with the same partner for many years, sometimes for life. Together they defend their territory.
7070.m: Carrion crows often stay a pair for life.

7071.q: Who has the big antlers in red deer?
7071.e: Only male red deer have antlers. The hinds have none.

7072.q: Why do you feel a headwind when cycling fast, even when there is no wind?
a: You are moving through the air, and you feel this as resistance
Your bike makes its own wind
7072.e: When you move, you have to push the air in front of you out of the way. You feel this air resistance as wind in your face.

7073.q: Which group of animals does the mole actually belong to?
7073.e: Although it looks like a small rodent, the mole belongs to a separate group of insect-eaters. It is closely related to shrews and hedgehogs.

7075.q: What is an otter’s den called?
7075.e: An otter’s den is called a holt. The entrance is often under water so that it is well hidden.
7075.m: An otter’s den is called a holt.

7076.q: How old can donkeys get compared with horses?
a: Donkeys often live about as long or even longer
Donkeys only live for one year
Donkeys never get older than a month
7076.e: With good care, donkeys can live just as long as horses or even longer. Some donkeys live to over thirty.

7077.q: What job does the spinal cord have in the nervous system?
a: It carries signals between the brain and body and controls reflexes
7077.e: The spinal cord connects the brain and body and carries nerve signals in both directions. It also controls simple reflexes directly.
7077.m: The spinal cord connects the brain and body.

7078.q: When is a hamster most active?
a: In the evening and at night
7078.e: Hamsters are active at dusk and at night. During the day they usually sleep deep in their nest.

7079.q: How many legs does a wasp have?
7079.e: Like all insects, the wasp has six legs. Wasps are insects.

7080.q: What are the small, hard grains of ice called that can fall from the sky in a thunderstorm?
7080.e: Hail forms in thunderclouds when water droplets freeze and are carried up and down again and again. The ice grains get bigger as this happens.
7080.m: Hailstones are hard grains of ice from thunderclouds.

7081.q: In which season do you most often hear grasshoppers chirping?
7081.e: When it is warm, grasshoppers are especially active. In summer you can hear their chirping in many meadows.

7082.q: At what altitude do Alpine marmots typically live?
a: In Alpine meadows above the tree line
In deep forests in the valley
7082.e: Alpine marmots live on open grassland high in the mountains. There they find enough plants to eat and can easily spot danger.
7082.m: Marmots live high in the Alps.

7083.q: Which bird is a close relative of the carrion crow?
7083.e: Like the carrion crow, the magpie belongs to the crow family. The jay and the common raven are also part of it.
7083.m: Magpies and carrion crows are both crows.

7084.q: What colour is the kingfisher’s belly usually?
7084.e: While its back shines blue, the kingfisher’s underside is a strong orange. This contrast makes it easy to recognise.

7085.q: How does the housefly survive the winter?
a: In sheltered, warm places, for example as a pupa
It builds a nest of twigs
7085.e: In winter the housefly hides in sheltered, warm places. Sometimes it also spends the winter as a pupa before hatching in spring.
7085.m: In winter the fly hides away.

7086.q: What does the stoat use to mark its territory?
7086.e: Stoats have scent glands whose strong secretion warns other stoats and marks their own territory. The smell can also scare off enemies.

7087.q: What is baleen in the blue whale?
7087.e: Baleen plates are fine, comb-like plates in the whale’s mouth. They are made of the same material as our fingernails.

7088.q: How many young does a female ring-tailed lemur usually have at one time?
7088.e: Usually only one young is born, sometimes twins. The female then takes very good care of the little one.
7088.m: Usually one lemur baby is born.

7089.q: What is the smallest working unit of a living thing?
7089.e: Every living thing is made of cells, which can carry out all the important functions of life. Some living things consist of only a single cell, others of trillions.
7089.m: The cell is the building block of life.

7090.q: What is the young stage of the mosquito that lives in water called?
7090.e: A larva hatches from the mosquito egg; it lives and moves around in the water. Later it turns into a pupa.
7090.m: The mosquito larva lives in water.

7091.q: Which animal is especially dangerous for a small roe deer fawn?
7091.e: Small fawns can’t run away well yet. That is why foxes are a big danger for them.

7092.q: What is the biggest risk threatening gorillas’ habitats today?
a: Lakes that are too big nearby
7092.e: When people clear the rainforest for fields or wood, gorillas lose their home. This is one of the biggest dangers for them.

7093.q: What is the suborder of dragonflies with strong, broad bodies that usually hold their wings spread out at rest called?
7093.e: True dragonflies usually perch with their wings spread out to the sides. They are more strongly built than damselflies.
7093.m: True dragonflies spread their wings out.

7094.q: How do baboons usually move on the ground?
7094.e: Baboons mainly live on the ground and walk on hands and feet. They walk on the palms of their hands and the soles of their feet.
7094.m: Baboons mostly walk on all fours.

7095.q: Can an octopus also swim backwards through the water?
7095.e: With its water funnel the octopus can choose the direction in which it shoots off. That way it can also escape backwards.

7096.q: What job do ring-tailed lemurs do in the forest when they eat fruit?
a: They fertilise the soil with feathers
7096.e: Seeds from the fruit get back into nature in their droppings. That way new plants can grow in other places.

7097.q: Roughly how long can a slow worm live in human care?
7097.e: Slow worms can live to a great age. In human care some have lived for over 30 years.
7097.m: Slow worms can live very long.

7098.q: What do some adult mosquitoes do in winter in Switzerland?
a: They spend the winter hidden in sheltered places
They all die immediately in the cold
They build a nest like birds
7098.e: Some female mosquitoes hide in winter in sheltered places such as cellars or barns and become very still. As soon as it gets warm again, they fly off again.
7098.m: Some mosquitoes spend the winter hidden away.

a: More than half have decided the same way
7099.e: In a majority, more than half of the people vote for the same thing. This is how votes decide what applies.

7100.q: What does a red deer like to eat most?
7100.e: The red deer is a plant-eater. It eats grass, herbs, leaves and also buds.

7101.q: What does it mean if you see a hedgehog walking around during the day?
a: It can be a sign that it is ill
That is quite normal for hedgehogs
It means the hedgehog likes to play
It shows that it will rain soon
7101.e: As hedgehogs are really nocturnal, a hedgehog out during the day is often ill or weak. In that case you should tell a wildlife rescue centre.
7101.m: A hedgehog out in the day is often ill.

7102.q: Roughly how big does an adult mole get?
a: About as long as a hand, around 15 cm
As long as a fox, over 60 cm
7102.e: An adult mole measures about 12 to 17 centimetres. That means it fits well into narrow tunnels in the ground.
7102.m: Moles are about the size of a hand.

7103.q: How long do robins usually live in the wild?
a: Often only one to two years
7103.e: Many robins only live to one or two years in the wild. But a few manage much longer.
7103.m: Robins usually live only a short time.

7104.q: Roughly how long is an otter including its tail?
a: About one to one and a half metres
7104.e: Including its tail, an otter reaches a length of about one to one and a half metres. The tail makes up a large part of this length.
7104.m: Otters grow up to 1.5 metres long.

7105.q: What is a leopard especially good at?
7105.e: With strong legs and claws, the leopard climbs trees skilfully. It can even climb up with prey in its mouth.

7106.q: How does an otter mark its territory?
7106.e: Otters leave their droppings, called spraint, in easily visible places such as stones on the bank. That way they show other otters that this is their territory.
7106.m: Spraint on stones marks the territory.

7107.q: How many pairs of legs does a wasp have?
7107.e: Insects like the wasp always have three pairs of legs. That makes six legs altogether.
7107.m: Wasps have three pairs of legs.

a: No, it is active in winter too
Yes, it sleeps through the whole winter
No, it migrates south in winter
7108.e: Least weasels have to hunt all year round because they can’t build up big fat reserves. A long hibernation would be dangerous for them.
7108.m: Least weasels don’t sleep through the winter.

7109.q: How many eyes does an octopus have?
7109.e: The octopus has two large eyes that it sees very well with. They are on the left and right of its head.

7110.q: Can a brown bear pull in its claws like a cat?
a: No, its claws are always visible
7110.e: Unlike cats, bears cannot pull their claws in. The strong, blunt claws help the bear above all when digging for roots and insects.

7111.q: Roughly how old can wild golden eagles get?
7111.e: In the wild, golden eagles can reach an age of around 25 to 30 years. In human care some live a little longer.
7111.m: Golden eagles live up to 30 years.

7112.q: What happens to the chicks shortly after they hatch?
a: They soon leave the nest with their mother
