They stay in the nest for a whole year
Their mother leaves them at once
They fly away alone at once
7112.e: Shortly after hatching, the chicks leave the nest together with their mother. From then on they look for food by the water together.

7113.q: Where does the name wall lizard probably come from?
a: From its liking for walls and cracks in rocks as a habitat
Because it only lives in houses
7113.e: The common wall lizard especially likes to stay on stone walls and rocks. That is where its name comes from.
7113.m: The name comes from its life on walls.

7114.q: Roughly how old does a wild moose get?
7114.e: In the wild, moose usually live 12 to 15 years. Predators, diseases and harsh winters shorten their lives.

7115.q: In which South American country are guinea pigs still traditionally kept as farm animals today?
7115.e: In Peru and some neighbouring countries, guinea pigs have been kept for food for a very long time; there they are called cuy. In Europe, on the other hand, they are mainly popular pets.
7115.m: In Peru guinea pigs are also farm animals.

7116.q: Why are martens skilful hunters despite their small size?
a: Because they are fast, agile and good climbers
Because they are much bigger than their prey
Because they are slow but have stamina
Because they only hunt in water
7116.e: Despite their small size, martens are very agile, fast and skilful climbers. These qualities help them catch even nimble prey such as mice or birds.
7116.m: Martens are small but very agile.

7117.q: Which animal family does the cheetah belong to?
7117.e: The cheetah belongs to the cat family, just like lions and pet cats. But it forms its own genus with only one species.
7117.m: The cheetah belongs to the cat family.

7118.q: Which two parts make up the central nervous system?
7118.e: The central nervous system processes and passes on all the signals in the body. It consists of the brain and spinal cord.
7118.m: The brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system.

7119.q: Which animals are among the barn swallow’s enemies?
a: Cats and small birds of prey such as the sparrowhawk
7119.e: The barn swallow’s enemies include cats, martens and small birds of prey such as the sparrowhawk. Young birds and eggs are especially at risk.

7120.q: Which animal is a well-known competitor of the puma in South America?
7120.e: Pumas and jaguars share their habitat in parts of the Americas. The jaguar is bigger and stronger.

7121.q: Why do people release young eels into rivers and lakes?
7121.e: The European eel is critically endangered. That is why young eels, called stocking eels, are released into waters so that they can grow up there.

7122.q: What is the name of the well-known viewpoint mountain above the town of Solothurn?
7122.e: From the Weissenstein, in good weather, you can see many Alpine peaks and the town of Solothurn looking tiny from above. You can ride up by cable car.
7122.m: The Weissenstein is Solothurn's local mountain.

7123.q: How can you tell which end of an earthworm is the front and which the back?
a: By the saddle, which is closer to the head
7123.e: The pale band called the saddle, or clitellum, is closer to the head end than to the tail end. That way you can tell the direction.
7123.m: The saddle shows the front end.

7124.q: What are budgies especially good at?
a: Diving for a very long time
7124.e: Budgies are nimble fliers and can change direction in a flash. In the wild this helps them escape enemies.

7125.q: Which country is home to large parts of the Pantanal, where many jaguars live?
7125.e: The Pantanal is a huge wetland that lies mainly in Brazil. There are especially many jaguars there.
7125.m: The Pantanal lies mainly in Brazil.

7126.q: Why don’t ducks simply sink in the water?
a: Air in their feathers makes them light and able to float
They have fins like a fish
Their bones are made of cork
7126.e: Lots of air is trapped in a duck’s thick feathers. This air carries the duck on the water like a life jacket.
7126.m: Air in the feathers keeps the duck afloat.

7127.q: Which country's national flag has the same colours as Ireland's, but in mirror-image order (orange, white, green)?
7127.e: The flag of the Ivory Coast shows the same colours as Ireland's, but mirrored: orange, white and green. This is pure coincidence with no historical connection.
7127.m: The flag of the Ivory Coast is the mirror image of the Irish flag.

7128.q: What do aphids mainly feed on?
7128.e: Aphids pierce the tubes that carry sap in plants and suck the sugary sap from the sieve tubes. This is also called phloem sap.

7129.q: What else is a male hippopotamus called?
7129.e: An adult male hippopotamus is sometimes called a bull, as with other large animals. Males are often bigger than females.
7129.m: A male hippo is called a bull.

7130.q: Apart from the lungs, what can the pool frog’s moist skin do?
a: It takes in some oxygen from water or air
It keeps growing back like fur
It stores large amounts of fat
7130.e: The pool frog’s skin is thin and moist and can help with breathing as well as the lungs. This is called skin breathing.
7130.m: The skin helps the pool frog breathe.

7131.q: Which surroundings does the common earwig like best?
a: Damp, sheltered places with lots of hiding places
7131.e: It is found in gardens, forests and at woodland edges. There it has hiding places under stones, leaves and bark.
7131.m: It likes hiding places in gardens and forests.

7132.q: What does a hunter call the tracks a roe deer leaves in the ground?
7132.e: The tracks of deer in soft ground are called slots. You can see the shape of the hooves in them.

7133.q: Which animal does not truly hibernate in winter but only has a winter rest, waking up now and then?
7133.e: In winter the badger goes into a winter rest, but wakes up now and then and even leaves its sett. True hibernators such as the marmot lower their body temperature much more.
7133.m: The badger often wakes up in winter.

7134.q: How do giraffes usually move in everyday life, fast or leisurely?
a: Usually leisurely at a calm walk
7134.e: Giraffes only run when there is danger or they want to reach a goal. In everyday life they usually move slowly through the savannah.

7135.q: How many calves does a female bison normally have per year?
7135.e: Usually only one calf is born. It stands up soon after birth.
7135.m: Usually only one calf is born.

7137.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of the pool frog?
7137.e: Birds such as storks and herons and snakes such as the grass snake like to hunt pool frogs. Fish can also eat small frogs and tadpoles.
7137.m: Storks, herons and grass snakes hunt pool frogs.

7138.q: What happens to a ball that you throw up?
7138.e: Gravity keeps pulling the ball back towards the ground. That is why it comes down again after a short time.
7138.m: What goes up comes back down.

7139.q: Roughly how much time does an elephant spend eating each day?
7139.e: Elephants need huge amounts of food. That is why they are busy eating almost all day.

7140.q: What pattern do many sand lizards have on their back?
a: Black and white stripes like a zebra
No pattern at all, just pure white
7140.e: The dark spots help the lizard camouflage itself on soil and dry grass. The exact pattern differs a little from animal to animal.
7140.m: Rows of dark spots usually decorate the back.

7141.q: What role does the praying mantis play in the garden?
a: It eats many other insects, including pests
7141.e: As a hunter it keeps insect numbers in check. But it also eats useful animals, so it is not a targeted pest controller.
7141.m: It is a hunter, not a plant-eater.

a: It protects the skin from sunburn
It makes you tanned without sun
It cools the body from the inside
7142.e: Sun cream protects the skin from dangerous UV rays. That way you avoid painful sunburn.

7143.q: What does a grasshopper like to do on a warm day?
7143.e: On warm days the grasshopper likes to sit in the sun. In between it nibbles on grasses and leaves.

7144.q: How many young does a female lynx usually have at once?
7144.e: A litter usually has one to four young. Not all of them survive the first months of life.
7144.m: One to four young per litter.

7145.q: Which statement about the meerkat is correct?
a: It is a land carnivore and mainly eats small animals
It is a rodent with big front teeth
7145.e: Meerkats belong to the carnivores, more precisely to the mongooses. They are mammals and not rodents.

7146.q: What do ants mainly use to communicate with each other?
7146.e: Ants mostly communicate with scents and touch. With their antennae they smell what other ants are telling them.

7147.q: How tall can an adult male gorilla be when standing?
7147.e: Male gorillas are very big and strong. They can be almost as tall as an adult human.
7147.m: Male gorillas are almost two metres tall.

7149.q: What is the main difference between the mouths of the blue whale and the sperm whale?
a: The blue whale has baleen, the sperm whale has teeth
Both have the same number of teeth
The blue whale has teeth, the sperm whale doesn’t
7149.e: The blue whale filters its food with baleen. The sperm whale, on the other hand, has real teeth to catch bigger prey.
7149.m: Baleen or teeth, that is the difference.

7150.q: What does the grass snake often do when it feels threatened?
7150.e: Some grass snakes go limp and play dead. While doing so they can also give off a smelly secretion.
7150.m: Playing dead is a defence trick.

7151.q: Why can llamas live well at high altitude?
a: Their blood takes up oxygen well
7151.e: Their blood can take up a lot of oxygen even when there is little of it. That way they are adapted to the thin air of the Andes.
7151.m: Llamas are adapted to mountain air.

7152.q: What does a hamster do when it enjoys being stroked?
7152.e: A hamster that feels safe stays sitting calmly when stroked. That is how it shows it feels comfortable.

7153.q: How can you help the barn owl?
a: With grain in a bird feeder
7153.e: People can hang special nest boxes in barns or on towers. There barn owls find a safe place to breed.
7153.m: Nest boxes help the barn owl.

7154.q: What are guinea pigs especially good at?
7154.e: Guinea pigs have a very good sense of smell and use it to recognise other guinea pigs and tasty food. Their hearing is also quite sharp.

7155.q: Which old story is often told to children about the stork?
7155.e: In the past, children were told that the stork brought babies to families. That is just an old story, not a fact.

7157.q: What does the female cuckoo sometimes remove from the other bird’s nest?
a: One of the host bird’s eggs
7157.e: Before she lays her own egg, the female cuckoo sometimes takes away one of the host bird’s eggs. That way it is less noticeable that there is an extra egg in the nest.
7157.m: The cuckoo sometimes removes a host egg.

7158.q: What is the narrow part between a wasp’s thorax and abdomen called?
7158.e: The wasp waist is the thin section between the thorax and the abdomen. It makes wasps easy to recognise.
7158.m: The waist is narrow and thin.

7159.q: At roughly what age does a young hen lay her first eggs?
a: On the first day after hatching
7159.e: Young hens usually only start laying eggs after a few months. Before that they still have to grow.
7159.m: Hens only lay eggs after a few months.

7160.q: What is it called when an animal like the common wall lizard cannot control its own body temperature?
7160.e: Cold-blooded animals adjust their body temperature to their surroundings. That is why the common wall lizard deliberately looks for warm places.

7161.q: Roughly how long do llamas live?
7161.e: Llamas usually live to about 20 years. With good care, sometimes a little longer.

7162.q: What do storks such as the white stork have?
a: Long legs and a long beak
Short legs and a curved beak
Webbed feet and a flat beak
Short legs and a short beak
7162.e: Storks have long legs and a long, pointed beak. With them they stalk through wet meadows and catch frogs.
7162.m: Storks have long legs and a long beak.

7163.q: What does a barn swallow do when an enemy appears near the nest?
7163.e: When in danger, the barn swallow gives sharp, loud alarm calls. With them it warns other swallows and its family.
7163.m: Alarm calls signal danger to the nest.

7164.q: What was the Enabling Act of 1933?
a: A law that gave Hitler almost unlimited power.
7164.e: With the Enabling Act the government under Hitler could pass laws without asking parliament. It was an important step towards dictatorship.
7164.m: The law gave Hitler almost all power.

7165.q: How big can an adult male orca get?
7165.e: Male orcas are often bigger than females. They can be almost as long as a bus.
7165.m: Male orcas grow up to 10 metres long.

7167.q: Why is the slow worm useful for gardeners?
a: It loosens the soil with its wings
7167.e: Slugs often eat lettuce and other garden plants. The slow worm helps reduce their numbers.
7167.m: Slow worms eat garden pests such as slugs.

7168.q: Roughly how long does an adult kingfisher get?
7168.e: At around 17 centimetres, the kingfisher is only a little bigger than a sparrow. Despite its small size, its colours make it very noticeable.
7168.m: A kingfisher is about the size of a palm.

7169.q: What is a capacitor mainly used for in electronics?
a: For storing electric charge for a short time
For storing large amounts of energy permanently like a rechargeable battery
7169.e: A capacitor consists of two conducting plates separated by an insulator that can collect charge. It charges and discharges quickly, which is used, for example, to smooth voltage in circuits.
7169.m: Capacitors store charge for a short time.

7170.q: In which city is the Federal Palace, where the National Council and the Council of States work?
7170.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Palace with the parliament is there.
7170.m: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.

7171.q: Which landscape does the lynx prefer as a habitat?
a: Large, unbroken forests with lots of cover
7171.e: The lynx needs large forest areas where it can hide and hunt. It tends to avoid open, treeless areas.
7171.m: Large forests give the lynx shelter.

7172.q: Does the great tit fly to warm countries in winter?
a: It flies to the South Pole
7172.e: The great tit is a resident bird, which means it usually stays in its home area all year. Only in a very harsh winter does it sometimes move a little further.
7172.m: Great tits usually stay here all year.

7173.q: How many young does a jaguar mother usually have per litter?
7173.e: Usually one to four young are born. Often there are two.

7174.q: What do Bactrian camels sometimes do when they feel threatened or annoyed?
7174.e: Camels can bring up the contents of their stomach and spit it out. They do this to defend themselves.

7175.q: Why does the red deer have a thicker coat in winter?
a: So that it does not get cold
So that it can run faster
So that it can hear better
7175.e: The winter coat is much thicker and warmer than the summer coat. This helps the deer get through cold days in the snow.
7175.m: The thick winter coat keeps the deer warm.

7176.q: What makes a lynx track in the snow especially easy to recognise?
a: Round prints with no visible claw marks
Long trailing marks like those of a snake
7176.e: Because the lynx pulls in its claws when it walks, its paws leave round prints without claw marks. This makes them different from dog tracks.
7176.m: A lynx track is round and shows no claw marks.

7177.q: What colour is the fur of bonobos usually?
7177.e: Bonobo fur is usually black. Their face and skin are dark too.

7178.q: What does a jellyfish use as its mouth and also as its exit?
7178.e: In a jellyfish, a single opening leads into the stomach. It takes in food through it and also pushes waste back out.
7178.m: A jellyfish has only one body opening.

7179.q: Can you also see great crested grebes in Switzerland in winter?
a: Yes, many spend the winter on lakes that do not freeze
No, they all fly to Africa
No, they hibernate in the reeds
7179.e: Many great crested grebes spend the winter on large Swiss lakes that do not freeze over. Winter visitors from the north join them.
7179.m: Great crested grebes spend the winter on ice-free lakes.

7180.q: How long does an adult stag beetle usually live?
7180.e: The adult beetles appear in early summer and live for only a few weeks. During this time they mate.
7180.m: Adult beetles live only a few weeks.

7181.q: What is the woodlouse called that can roll itself into a ball when in danger?
7181.e: Pill woodlice can roll themselves into an almost perfect ball. Their hard shell then protects their soft belly.
7181.m: Pill woodlice protect themselves by rolling up.

7182.q: How does an elephant use its trunk when swimming?
7182.e: Elephants are good swimmers and often stick their trunk out of the water like a snorkel. This lets them keep breathing even when their head is under water.
7182.m: The trunk works as a snorkel.

a: Only dense rainforests in South America
7183.e: Baboons live in open landscapes, semi-deserts and mountain areas. They need watering holes and safe places to sleep.

7184.q: Why does your body need iron?
a: To make haemoglobin in the blood
7184.e: Iron is needed for the haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen. People who lack iron often feel tired.

7185.q: Why do people like catching pike?
a: Because they taste good and are exciting to fish for
Because they are only kept as pets
Because they have gold in their belly
Because they would otherwise block up the lakes
7185.e: Pike is a popular fish to eat, and many people like the taste of its flesh. It is also popular with anglers because it is so strong.
7185.m: Pike are popular for eating and for angling.

7186.q: What is the home of many honeybees called?
7186.e: Many thousands of bees live together in a beehive. There they build their honeycombs and store their honey.

7187.q: Roughly how long do carrion crows sit on their eggs before the chicks hatch?
7187.e: The female sits on the eggs for about 18 to 20 days until the chicks hatch. During this time the male brings her food.
7187.m: Crows sit on their eggs for about three weeks.

7188.q: Which big cat lives in America and has rosettes with dots in the middle?
7188.e: The jaguar looks like the leopard but lives in America. Its rosettes usually have one or more dots inside.
7188.m: The jaguar lives in America, the leopard does not.

7189.q: How does the kestrel compare with larger birds of prey such as the golden eagle?
a: It is much smaller and mainly hunts small prey such as mice
It is just as big as the golden eagle and hunts roe deer
It is the largest bird of prey in Europe
It hunts only fish in large lakes
7189.e: Compared with the golden eagle, the kestrel is a much smaller bird of prey. While the golden eagle also catches larger animals, the kestrel specialises mainly in mice and small prey.
7189.m: The kestrel is much smaller than the golden eagle.

7190.q: What do adult alpine newts mainly eat?
7190.e: Alpine newts are carnivores and catch small invertebrates. These include insects, worms and snails.
7190.m: Alpine newts eat small insects and worms.

7191.q: What colour are the great tit's eggs?
7191.e: Great tit eggs are white with small reddish speckles. They are very small, like little pearls.
7191.m: The eggs are white with red speckles.

7192.q: For how long have people been keeping domestic geese?
7192.e: People already kept geese in ancient Egypt. This makes the goose one of the oldest domestic animals of all.
7192.m: Geese have been domestic animals for a very long time.

7193.q: Which animals compete with the spotted hyena for food?
7193.e: Lions and hyenas often fight over prey. These fights can be dangerous.
7193.m: Lions and hyenas compete for prey.

7194.q: What happened to the bison herds in North America in the 19th century?
a: They were almost wiped out by heavy hunting
7194.e: Massive hunting brought the bison to the brink of extinction. Only a few hundred animals survived.
7194.m: Overhunting almost wiped out the bison.

7195.q: What does the spawn, meaning the eggs, of the common toad look like?
a: Long strings like strings of pearls
Round clumps like those of frogs
7195.e: The common toad lays its eggs in long strings that are wrapped around water plants. This makes it different from frogspawn, which forms clumps.

7196.q: How does the common earwig spend the winter?
a: The animals retreat into hiding places and holes in the ground
They dig into lake shores and sleep in the water
They all die in autumn without leaving young
7196.e: In winter the earwig looks for sheltered places in the soil. The female stays there with her eggs.
7196.m: In winter they stay in hiding places in the ground.

7197.q: Why does often only one young golden eagle survive, even though two eggs are laid?
a: The older chick often attacks the younger one
The parents eat one egg on purpose
The second egg is usually not fertile
One egg always falls out of the nest
7197.e: The chick that hatches first is stronger and often attacks its younger sibling, so that the younger one starves or dies. This behaviour is called cainism.
7197.m: The older chick often pushes out the younger one.

7198.q: In what kind of water do the whitefish of Swiss lakes live?
a: In the brackish water of the coast
In the water of hot springs
7198.e: Swiss lakes contain fresh water. The whitefish live there their whole lives.
7198.m: Swiss whitefish live in fresh water.

7199.q: What does the Roman snail do during the day when it is very hot?
7199.e: When it is hot, the snail retreats to damp, shady spots. This stops it from drying out.
7199.m: When it is hot, it hides in the shade.

7200.q: What are birds called that, like the great tit, stay in the same place all year round?
7200.e: Birds that do not fly south are called resident birds. The great tit belongs to this group.
7200.m: The great tit is a resident bird.

7201.q: How heavy can a large male red kangaroo get?
7201.e: A large male red kangaroo can weigh almost 90 kilograms. That is as heavy as an adult human.

a: A request or demand handed in with signatures
A law that applies at once
A tax you have to pay
7202.e: With a petition, children and teenagers can also show their opinion. They collect signatures and hand them in to an authority.
7202.m: A petition is a request with signatures.

7203.q: Where does a baby starfish live at first?
a: It swims freely in the water
It sits on the seabed straight away
It lives in a mussel shell
7203.e: At first the young starfish swims around freely in the sea water. Only later does it settle on the seabed.
7203.m: Babies first swim freely in the water.

7204.q: Why is the Alpine ibex seen today as an example of successful species protection?
a: Because targeted protection measures saved it from extinction
Because it recovered by itself without any help
7204.e: The Alpine ibex had almost died out but was saved thanks to strict protection and targeted reintroduction. Today it is one of the best-known success stories of species protection in the Alps.
7204.m: The ibex is a species protection success.

7205.q: How do pairs of storks communicate, since they cannot sing?
a: By clattering their bills and with body posture
They do not communicate at all
7205.e: Because storks have no singing voice, they use bill clattering and certain movements to communicate with each other. In this way they show joy or give a warning, for example.

7206.q: How many eggs does a great tit usually lay in one clutch?
7206.e: A great tit often lays between eight and twelve small white eggs with red spots. That is quite a lot for such a small bird.
7206.m: Great tits lay many eggs at once.

7207.q: What probably helps lake trout find their home stream again?
7207.e: Migrating fish such as trout can detect smells in the water very well. This often helps them find their way back to the water where they hatched.
7207.m: Back to the home stream by smell.

7208.q: How does a lynx move through deep snow?
a: Its large paws work like snowshoes
It digs a tunnel through the snow
It mostly slides on its belly
7208.e: The broad paws spread the lynx's weight better over the surface of the snow. This means it sinks in less deeply than other animals.
7208.m: Large paws carry it through the snow.

7209.q: What happens to the colour of a ladybird shortly after it has come out of the pupa?
a: It is pale at first and only becomes strong later
It is bright red from the very start
It is striped black and white at first
7209.e: Right after hatching, the beetle's shell is still soft and pale. Only after a few hours does it harden and get its strong colour.
7209.m: The colour only comes after hatching.

7210.q: Where are most of the fins on a pike?
a: Right at the front on the head
There are no fins at all
7210.e: The pike's dorsal and anal fins sit far back, close to the tail fin. This lets it shoot forward in a flash.
7210.m: Fins at the back help with a fast start.

7211.q: What do you need at least for a simple circuit to work?
a: Battery, wires and something that uses electricity, such as a bulb
7211.e: For electricity to flow, there must be a closed connection: an energy source, wires and something that uses the electricity. If one part is missing, the circuit does not work.

7212.q: Who raises the young in a hyena clan?
a: The young are left alone straight away
The young are raised by birds
7212.e: In spotted hyenas it is mainly the mothers that look after the young. Fathers play hardly any part.

7213.q: What is the animal called that comes from a male donkey and a female horse?
7213.e: If a male donkey is crossed with a female horse, the result is a mule. It has features of both parents.
7213.m: Male donkey plus female horse makes a mule.

7214.q: Where in the world are members of the weasel family found?
a: On every continent except Australia and Antarctica
Only on islands in the Pacific
7214.e: The weasel family is very successful and lives on almost every continent; only in Australia and Antarctica is it naturally absent. This shows how adaptable this group of animals is.
7214.m: Weasels and martens live almost everywhere except Australia.

7215.q: Roughly how big is a newborn panda cub?
a: Already as big as its mother
7215.e: A baby panda weighs only about 100 grams at birth. That is tiny compared with its big mother.
7215.m: Panda babies are tiny at birth.

a: Yes, they even see colours very well
No, they only see black and white
7216.e: Goldfish have good colour vision and can tell many colours apart. This helps them find food.

7217.q: Where is the common buzzard mainly found?
a: In Europe and parts of Asia
7217.e: The common buzzard is widespread in large parts of Europe and Asia. In Switzerland it can be found in almost every suitable habitat.

7218.q: What does it mean that the perch is cold-blooded?
a: Its body temperature adjusts to the water
It always heats its blood to 37 degrees
It lives in the sea and in the lake by turns
7218.e: Cold-blooded animals produce hardly any body heat of their own. That is why the perch is less active in cold water.
7218.m: In the cold-blooded perch, body temperature follows the water temperature.

7219.q: Which Swiss breed of cattle has a coat with reddish-brown and white patches?
7219.e: Simmental cattle come from the Simmental valley in the Bernese Oberland and have reddish-brown and white patches. Brown Swiss cattle are plain brown, and Hérens cattle are black.
7219.m: Simmental cattle come from the Simmental valley.

7220.q: Why do you often hear foxes screaming loudly at night in winter?
a: They are looking for a partner
They are calling their cubs to eat
They use it to hunt mice
7220.e: In January and February foxes look for a partner. Then they call to each other with loud, sometimes spooky screams.
7220.m: Winter screams are for finding a partner.

7221.q: How big can the tunnel system of a single mole get?
a: It can be several hundred metres long
As big as a football pitch for every single tunnel
It is just one short hole
7221.e: Over time a mole digs a widely branching network of tunnels. Altogether it can be several hundred metres long.
7221.m: Mole tunnels can be very long.

7222.q: What colour is the cere of an adult male budgie usually?
7222.e: In adult male budgerigars the cere is often blue. In females it looks different.
7222.m: Males often have a blue cere.

7223.q: Which group of fish do whitefish belong to?
7223.e: Whitefish are related to trout and salmon and belong to the salmon family. Like them, they need cool, clean water.
7223.m: Whitefish belong to the salmon family.

7224.q: How does the flock help individual budgies look for food?
a: Together they find food sources more easily
Each bird always searches completely alone
The flock does not help with this
They swap their food with other kinds of animals
7224.e: In a flock, many eyes spot more easily where there are seeds and water. In this way all the budgies benefit from each other.
7224.m: In a flock it is easier to find food.

7226.q: Which group of animals do orangutans belong to?
7226.e: Orangutans are great apes, like gorillas, chimpanzees and us humans. They have no tail.

7227.q: How can you tell that dung beetles are beetles?
a: By the hard wing cases over the thin flying wings
By the body having no segments
By the scales on the wings
7227.e: Beetles have hard wing cases, and underneath them lie the thin wings used for flying. The dung beetle is built like this too.
7227.m: Hard wing cases show: this is a beetle.

7228.q: What do chickens see especially well with?
a: With their large eyes on the sides of the head
7228.e: Chickens' eyes sit on the sides of the head and are very large. This gives them a wide field of view so they can spot danger early.
7228.m: Large eyes help chickens to see.

7230.q: Where does the male great spotted woodpecker have a red patch?
a: On the back of its neck
7230.e: Only the males have a red patch on the back of the neck. This is how you can tell them apart from the females.
7230.m: A red neck shows it is a male.

7231.q: What do blackbirds often do in the garden that helps people?
7231.e: Blackbirds like to eat snails, worms and other small animals in the garden. In this way they help to reduce pests naturally.
7231.m: Blackbirds eat snails in the garden.

7233.q: Why can camels save water when it is hot?
a: They only start sweating at very high body temperatures
They lose no water through their skin
7233.e: Their body temperature can change a lot before they start to sweat. This saves water.
7233.m: Camels save water by letting their temperature change.

7234.q: How well do guinea pigs see with their eyes on the sides of their head?
a: They can see almost all the way around
They only see straight ahead like humans
They can only see at night
7234.e: Because guinea pigs' eyes sit on the sides of the head, they can see a very large area around them. This helps them notice danger quickly, even from the side.
7234.m: Guinea pigs can see almost all the way around.

7235.q: What do people sometimes build on roofs to help storks?
7235.e: So that storks can nest safely, people build special platforms on poles or roofs. There the storks can build their nests more easily.
7235.m: Nesting platforms help with nest building.

7236.q: What does the shape of a gorilla's hands show compared with human hands?
a: They are built in a very similar way
They have no fingers at all
7236.e: Like human hands, a gorilla's hands have five fingers including a thumb. This shows how closely gorillas are related to us.
7236.m: Gorilla hands are very like human hands.

7237.q: How does a giraffe usually move when it walks?
a: It moves both legs on one side at the same time
It always hops on one leg
7237.e: Giraffes are pacers. This means they first move both legs on the right side and then both legs on the left side.
7237.m: Giraffes walk with a pacing gait.

7238.q: What is a polar bear's favourite food?
7238.e: Seals are the polar bear's favourite food. It needs their fatty blubber to stay strong.

7239.q: Apart from Europe, where else is the least weasel found?
7239.e: The least weasel is one of the most widespread predators of the northern hemisphere. It lives in very different climate zones.
7239.m: Least weasels are widespread around the world.

7240.q: What is one difference between the lion and the jaguar?
a: The lion lives in prides, the jaguar mostly alone
The jaguar lives in prides, the lion alone
7240.e: Lions are the only big cats that live in prides. The jaguar lives in South and Central America and, like most cats, lives alone.

7241.q: Roughly how long do jaguars live in the wild?
7241.e: In the wild, jaguars usually live to about twelve to fifteen years old. In zoos they can live longer.
7241.m: Wild jaguars live to about 12 to 15 years.

7242.q: How does a stork usually catch its food?
a: It walks slowly through meadows and stabs quickly
It jumps from tree to tree
7242.e: The white stork walks slowly and carefully through damp meadows. When it sees prey, it strikes with its beak in a flash.
7242.m: The stork stalks through the meadow and strikes.

7243.q: Roughly how long is an adult common swift?
7243.e: Despite its long wings, the swift's body is quite small. From beak to tail it measures only about 16 to 17 centimetres.
7243.m: Its body measures only about 16 centimetres.

7244.q: What do many houseplants on a windowsill do?
a: They grow away from the light
7244.e: Plants turn their leaves towards the light because they need it to grow. This behaviour is called phototropism.

7245.q: What is normal if you see a guinea pig eating its own soft droppings straight away?
a: It is healthy, because this way it takes in important nutrients again
It is always a sign of illness
It only happens in very old animals
Only sick animals do it out of hunger
7245.e: Guinea pigs eat a special kind of soft dropping again to absorb important nutrients and vitamins better. This is completely normal and healthy behaviour.
7245.m: Eating soft droppings is normal and healthy.

7246.q: Which animal is related to the red squirrel?
7246.e: Squirrels, marmots and chipmunks all belong to the squirrel family. So they are related to each other.

7247.q: Apart from fish, what prey does the kingfisher sometimes eat?
7247.e: As well as small fish, the kingfisher also eats water insects, larvae and sometimes small tadpoles. This widens its menu depending on what is available.
7247.m: Insects and tadpoles are on the menu too.

7248.q: What does a red deer sometimes eat in winter when there is no grass?
7248.e: When little grass grows in winter, the deer also eats bark and young twigs. This can damage the trees.
7248.m: In winter the deer also eats bark.

7249.q: Which kind of duck has a colourful male with striking feathers that look like little sails?
7249.e: The male mandarin duck looks very colourful and striking. On its back it has orange feathers that look like little sails.
7249.m: Male mandarin ducks have colourful feathers.

7250.q: What do the categories of the IUCN Red List show for animal species?
a: How great a species' risk of extinction is
The body size of a species
How loud the animals' calls are
7250.e: The Red List sorts species into categories such as “vulnerable”, “endangered” or “critically endangered”. It helps to plan protection measures for threatened animals in a targeted way.
7250.m: The Red List shows how threatened species are.

7251.q: How fast does the great spotted woodpecker strike with its beak when drumming?
a: Very fast, many times per second
7251.e: The great spotted woodpecker pecks incredibly fast, one blow after another. It sounds like a short, loud rattle.

7252.q: How do many jackals live when it comes to partners?
a: As a pair that often stays together for a long time
In huge herds of hundreds of animals
With a different partner in new groups every year
7252.e: Many jackals form lasting pairs. Together they defend their territory and raise their young.
7252.m: Jackals often live in lasting pairs.

7253.q: What does a cow do when it is lying contentedly in the pasture?
7253.e: A contented cow often lies comfortably in the grass and calmly chews its food again. You can see this in many Swiss pastures.
7253.m: Contented cows calmly chew the cud.

7254.q: Roughly how many teeth can a shark lose and replace during its life?
7254.e: Sharks replace their teeth all the time throughout their lives. This means they always have sharp teeth for hunting.
7254.m: Sharks replace their teeth very often.

7256.q: What does the typical call of the common swift sound most like?
a: A deep bark like a dog's
A soft coo like a pigeon's
A quiet chirp like a cricket's
7256.e: The swift's call can be heard from far away and sounds shrill and piercing. You often hear it on summer evenings, especially from groups.
7256.m: Swifts have a shrill, piercing call.

7257.q: Who builds the breeding tunnels in the ground for many dung beetles?
a: The beetles dig them themselves, often as a pair
7257.e: The beetles dig tunnels under the pile of dung. Depending on the species, the female and male work together.
7257.m: The beetles dig their breeding tunnels themselves.

7258.q: What sound does a goat make?
7258.e: Goats call their herd or their kid with loud bleating. This is how they stay in contact.

7259.q: How fast can a mole dig?
a: Amazingly fast, several metres an hour
Not at all, it uses old tunnels
7259.e: With its strong paws, a mole can dig new tunnels amazingly fast. It manages several metres in a short time.

7260.q: What is one of the main reasons the European pond turtle has declined?
a: Too many trees in the Alps
7260.e: In the past, many marshes and ponds were filled in or drained. As a result the species lost its habitats.

7261.q: What status does the beaver have in Switzerland today?
a: It is forbidden to see it anywhere
7261.e: Today the beaver is a protected species in Switzerland. This means it must not be hunted or disturbed.
7261.m: The beaver is protected by law.

7262.q: What can sometimes happen to the male after mating?
a: It is eaten by the female
7262.e: Sometimes the female eats the smaller male after mating. This happens in some species of spider.
7262.m: The male sometimes has a hard time.

7264.q: What does an earthworm breathe with?
7264.e: Earthworms have no lungs. They take in air through their damp skin.

7265.q: What does a mother badger do when danger threatens?
a: She quickly brings her young back into the sett
She simply leaves the young behind
She runs away without looking back
She hides the young in the water
7265.e: A mother badger protects her young very carefully. When there is danger, she quickly leads them to the safety of the sett.
7265.m: Mother badgers protect their young well.

7266.q: What happens to a hamster's teeth throughout its life?
7266.e: A hamster's front teeth grow non-stop. That is why it has to gnaw all the time so that they do not get too long.

7267.q: What are goats especially well known for?
7267.e: Goats can climb very safely on steep rocks and mountainsides. Their hooves give them a good grip.

7269.q: Roughly how long can a great crested grebe stay under water when it dives?
7269.e: A typical dive lasts about 20 to 30 seconds. During this time the bird hunts for fish under water.
7269.m: A great crested grebe's dives last about 30 seconds.

7270.q: What do alpine newt larvae mainly eat?
7270.e: The larvae live in water and feed on tiny water organisms such as small crustaceans and plankton. As they grow, they also eat bigger prey.

7271.q: What happens when danger threatens great crested grebe chicks while they are sitting on their parent's back?
a: The parent dives and sometimes takes the chicks under water with it
The chicks jump into the reeds at once
The chicks fly away at once
The chicks hide in the nest on their own
7271.e: When there is danger, the parent bird can dive with the chicks on its back. This protects the young from enemies especially well.
7271.m: Parents dive with the chicks on their back.

7272.q: How well can dolphins usually see?
a: Quite well both under and above water
Only under water, blind above water
7272.e: Dolphins can see well in the water and also above the surface. This helps them in addition to their echolocation.
7272.m: Dolphins see well above and below water.

7273.q: What colour does polar bear fur sometimes look compared with fresh snow?
7273.e: Polar bear fur is not pure white but often slightly yellowish. Especially in summer it can become a little discoloured.
7273.m: The fur sometimes looks slightly yellowish.

7274.q: What does a kangaroo's fur usually feel like?
7274.e: Kangaroos have soft, thick fur. It protects them from sun and cold.
7274.m: Kangaroo fur is soft and thick.

7275.q: What do breeders pay particular attention to with alpacas?
7275.e: In alpaca breeding, animals with especially fine wool are chosen. This improves the quality of the wool.
7275.m: Alpacas are bred mainly for fine wool.

7276.q: What colour is the coat of the Chamois-coloured Swiss mountain goat?
a: Brown with a black stripe along the back
7276.e: This Swiss goat breed has a brown coat with a dark stripe along its back, like the chamois. That is where its name comes from.
7276.m: The mountain goat is brown like a chamois.

7277.q: What does Bernoulli’s principle describe, which helps explain how aircraft wings create lift?
a: In a faster flowing liquid or gas the pressure is lower
Fast flowing liquids always have the highest pressure
Pressure and speed of a flow are not connected
Flows automatically get warmer as speed increases
7277.e: When air flows faster over the curved upper side of a wing than under the flatter underside, lower pressure forms on top. This pressure difference creates a force that pushes the wing upwards.

a: Dogs that protect farm animals from wolves
7278.e: Livestock guardian dogs live with the sheep or goats and defend the herd against attacks by wolves. They grow up with the farm animals from a young age.
7278.m: Livestock guardian dogs protect sheep from wolves.

7279.q: How can you often recognise a female grasshopper or cricket?
a: By a pointed egg-laying tube at the end of the body
By being smaller than the male in all species
7279.e: Many females have a pointed egg-laying tube at the end of their body. They use it to lay their eggs later.

a: When water freezes on the ground
When the sun shines especially strongly
7280.e: Frost forms when the temperature falls below zero degrees and moisture on the ground or on plants turns to ice. You can often recognise it by white, glittering patches in the morning.
7280.m: Frost is frozen water on the ground.

7281.q: What colour can a seahorse's skin be, depending on the species?
a: Very different colours such as yellow, orange or red
7281.e: Depending on the species and habitat, seahorses can have many different colours. This also helps them to camouflage themselves.

7283.q: Which animal is the wood mouse closely related to?
7283.e: The wood mouse and the house mouse belong to the same family of long-tailed mice. The shrew looks similar but is not a true mouse.
7283.m: Wood mice and house mice are related.

7284.q: How does water move inside a starfish's body?
a: It is pumped through a system of tubes
It is pumped by the heart, like in us
7284.e: Inside the starfish's body there is a special system of tubes. Sea water is moved back and forth in it to control the tiny tube feet.

7285.q: What does the barn owl catch its prey with?
7285.e: The barn owl grabs mice with its sharp talons. This lets it hold on to the prey and carry it.

7286.q: What does the polar bear use its sharp claws for?
a: For gripping on the ice and for hunting
For fishing like with a rod
7286.e: With its sharp claws the polar bear does not slip on the smooth ice. They also help it catch seals.
7286.m: Claws help with grip and hunting.

7287.q: Why do great crested grebes sometimes eat their own feathers?
a: The feathers protect the stomach from sharp fish bones
They like the taste of feathers
7287.e: The swallowed feathers form a protective layer in the stomach against sharp bones. The chicks are even fed feathers.
7287.m: Feathers protect the stomach from fish bones.

7288.q: Which sense is especially important for ring-tailed lemurs?
7288.e: Ring-tailed lemurs have a moist nose and an excellent sense of smell. Smells help them communicate and mark their territory.
7288.m: Ring-tailed lemurs often rely on smell.

7289.q: Which country has a flag with three horizontal stripes in red, white and blue that served as a model for many other tricolours?
7289.e: The Dutch flag with its three horizontal stripes is regarded as one of the oldest tricolours and influenced the flags of Russia and Luxembourg, among others. Originally the top stripe was orange.
7289.m: The Dutch flag shaped many other tricolours.

7290.q: What does a male mosquito like to eat best?
7290.e: Male mosquitoes do not bite and feed only on nectar and sweet plant sap. This gives them energy for flying.
7290.m: Male mosquitoes drink only plant sap.

7291.q: Apart from protecting against germs, what other important job does the skin have?
a: It controls body temperature by sweating
7291.e: With sweat, the skin can cool the body. In this way it helps to keep body temperature steady.

7292.q: What does the principle of subsidiarity mean in the structure of the Swiss state?
a: Tasks are carried out at the lowest sensible level possible, e.g. by the municipality
Only the Confederation may take on tasks
Cantons may not pass their own laws
All tasks are allocated by drawing lots
7292.e: According to the principle of subsidiarity, a task should be carried out at the lowest level suited to it: first the municipality, then the canton, and only last the Confederation.
7292.m: The smallest suitable level solves the task.

7293.q: In which colours does alpaca wool come naturally?
a: In many natural shades such as white, brown and black
7293.e: Alpacas have natural coat colours from white through beige and brown to grey and black. Other colours are made by dyeing.
7293.m: Alpacas come in many natural colours.

7295.q: When does the world celebrate the International Day of Peace?
7295.e: Every year on 21 September the United Nations calls on people to think about peace. On this day, weapons should be used as little as possible.
7295.m: 21 September is the International Day of Peace.

7296.q: How does the European pond turtle pull its head into its shell?
a: It bends its neck backwards in an S shape
It folds its neck sideways under the edge of the shell
It cannot pull its head in at all
It turns its head right round
7296.e: The European pond turtle belongs to the hidden-necked turtles. Its neck folds into the shell in an S-shaped curve.
7296.m: Hidden-necked turtles pull in their neck in an S shape.

7297.q: When does the female golden eagle in Switzerland usually lay her eggs?
a: Usually in late winter or early spring
Only in the middle of winter in the snow
7297.e: Golden eagles start breeding early in the year; the females usually lay their eggs between February and April. This way the young can grow up in summer, when there is plenty of prey.
7297.m: The eggs are laid in early spring.

7298.q: Why is it risky to give someone the PIN of your bank card?
a: Others could use it to take money from your account or pay without you noticing
The PIN then automatically stops working
The bank then blocks the account immediately
It is not risky at all
7298.e: The PIN protects your account from access by others. Anyone who knows it can take out money or pay with it, so it should always stay secret.

7299.q: What are specially trained truffle pigs used for?
a: To find hidden truffle mushrooms in the ground
7299.e: Truffles are fungi that grow underground and are hard to find. Thanks to their keen noses, pigs can smell them and dig them up.
7299.m: Truffle pigs sniff out hidden fungi.

7300.q: Where do sheep in Switzerland often spend the winter when it gets too cold on the alpine pasture?
a: Down in the valley in a shed or on lower pastures
Ever higher up on the mountain top
In a cave in the forest
In the water of a lake
7300.e: In winter, when it gets too cold and snowy on the alpine pasture, the sheep come back down to the valley. There they have a shed or lower pastures.
7300.m: In winter sheep are down in the valley.

7301.q: What are the small heaps of earth that a mole makes called?
7301.e: While digging, the mole pushes the extra soil up to the surface. This creates the small mounds in the garden.
7301.m: Mounds of earth show mole tunnels.

7302.q: What is the muddy pool that wild boars roll around in called?
7302.e: The muddy pool for wild boars is called a wallow. There they cool down and look after their skin.
7302.m: The muddy pool is called a wallow.

7303.q: What was the fur of the beech marten used for in the past?
7303.e: In the past, the fur of beech martens, like that of many martens, was used for fur clothing. Today this use hardly plays a role in Switzerland any more.
7303.m: Marten fur was once used for clothing.

7305.q: Why are power stations with turbines dangerous for fish swimming downstream?
a: Fish can get into the turbines and be injured
Turbines change the colour of the fish
7305.e: When fish swim through a turbine with the water, they can be badly injured. That is why protective screens and bypasses are needed.

7306.q: How many species are in the genus “Lemur”, to which the ring-tailed lemur belongs?
a: None, the genus has died out
7306.e: The ring-tailed lemur is the only species in its genus. Other lemurs belong to other genera.
7306.m: The ring-tailed lemur is the only species in its genus.

7307.q: What protection status does the least weasel have in Switzerland?
a: It can be hunted without restriction
It legally counts as a pet
It has died out in Switzerland
7307.e: As a native wild species, the least weasel is protected. This is meant to secure its numbers in the long term.
7307.m: Least weasels are protected wild animals.

7308.q: What is the large community of all the bees in a hive called?
7308.e: It is called a bee colony because all the bees work together like one big community. Each bee has its own important job in it.
7308.m: Many bees form a bee colony.

7309.q: Which group of animals does the Alpine ibex belong to?
a: The horned animals, like goats and cattle
7309.e: The ibex is one of the horned animals and is closely related to the domestic goat. Its horns grow throughout its life and are never shed.
7309.m: Ibex are horned animals like goats.

7310.q: Roughly how fast can a sea turtle swim in the water?
a: Not fast at all, it never swims
7310.e: In the water, some sea turtles can swim amazingly fast for short periods. On land, on the other hand, they move much more slowly.
7310.m: In the water they swim amazingly fast.

7311.q: What role does the Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach play for the grey heron in Switzerland?
a: It studies and monitors its numbers
7311.e: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach collects data on the numbers and spread of the grey heron in Switzerland. This information helps to protect the species.
7311.m: The institute monitors grey heron numbers.

7312.q: What protects the delicate flying wings of the ladybird?
7312.e: Thin wings for flying are hidden under the colourful, hard wing cases. The wing cases open out to the side before the beetle takes off.
7312.m: Hard wing cases protect delicate wings.

7313.q: What are closed seasons for fish such as whitefish for?
a: So the fish can spawn undisturbed
So the fish get fat faster
So the fish learn to swim
7313.e: During spawning time, certain fish must not be caught. This leaves enough fish to produce young.

7314.q: Can the Indian rhinoceros from Asia swim?
a: No, it never goes into the water
7314.e: The Indian rhinoceros lives in damp grasslands with rivers and swamps. It likes going into the water and is a good swimmer.

7315.q: Where does the polar bear mainly live?
a: In the Arctic at the North Pole
In Antarctica at the South Pole
7315.e: The polar bear lives in the cold Arctic around the North Pole. There is a lot of ice and snow there.
7315.m: Polar bears live in the Arctic.

7316.q: What is a main reason for the decline of the grass snake?
7316.e: When ponds and wet meadows disappear, there is not enough food or places to hide. Roads are also a danger.

7317.q: How did the eagle-owl fare in Switzerland for a long time in the 20th century?
a: It had almost died out and was then protected
It lived only in zoos and never in the wild
It moved completely to Africa every year
7317.e: Because of hunting and loss of habitat, the eagle-owl had almost disappeared from Switzerland. Thanks to protection and reintroduction projects, it breeds again in many areas today.
7317.m: The eagle-owl had almost died out in Switzerland.

7318.q: Roughly how old can a great tit get in the wild?
7318.e: Many great tits live for only one or two years, but some manage several years. Life in the wild is dangerous for small birds.
7318.m: Great tits can live for a few years.

7319.q: Does the kingfisher always fly to warmer regions in winter?
a: No, many stay if the water does not freeze
Yes, all kingfishers leave every winter
No, not a single kingfisher ever migrates
Yes, they even leave in summer
7319.e: If the water stays free of ice, many kingfishers stay in their territory all year. Only when it is cold do some move to milder, ice-free areas.
7319.m: Many kingfishers stay if the water stays open.

7320.q: Where does the tawny owl like to nest best?
a: In nests it builds itself from twigs
Right on the ground among the leaves
7320.e: The tawny owl does not build a nest itself but uses existing tree holes, for example old holes left by woodpeckers. If there are none, it will also use nest boxes.
7320.m: The tawny owl nests in tree holes.

7321.q: How old can wild common buzzards get at best?
7321.e: In the wild, common buzzards can get amazingly old, and some reach an age of about 25 years. Most, however, die much earlier, often in their first year.
7321.m: Common buzzards can get very old.

7322.q: How does the grey heron usually hold its neck when flying?
a: Drawn back in an S shape
7322.e: Unlike the stork, the grey heron draws its neck back in an S shape when flying. This way it uses less energy.
7322.m: In flight it draws its neck back.

7323.q: How does the wild dog look different from a pet dog?
a: Its coat is patchy and its ears are big
Its coat is made of feathers
7323.e: The wild dog has a colourful patchy pattern and big, round ears. It also has no dewclaw at the front.
7323.m: Patches and big ears stand out.

7324.q: What is the ability to adjust well to different habitats called?
7324.e: The puma copes in many kinds of landscape. This is one reason for its huge range.

7325.q: What is a male orca called?
7325.e: Male orcas are called bulls. This word is used for many large sea animals.
7325.m: A male orca is called a bull.

7326.q: What makes the tawny owl's call basically different from the songs of many songbirds?
a: It consists of a few typical calls instead of a melodic song
It sounds exactly like birds twittering in the morning
It consists of over a hundred different melodies
7326.e: Unlike many songbirds with complex songs, the tawny owl uses a few distinctive calls to communicate. These calls are enough, though, to mark territories and find partners.
7326.m: The tawny owl calls instead of singing.

7327.q: What most clearly distinguishes the way of life of the beech marten from that of the pine marten?
a: The beech marten tends to live near settlements, the pine marten in the forest
The beech marten lives only in water, the pine marten on land
The pine marten lives only in the desert
Both live only high in the mountains above the tree line
7327.e: The beech marten has adapted well to human settlements, while the pine marten is found more in natural forests. These different preferences help to tell the two species apart in the wild.
7327.m: Beech marten: settlements, pine marten: forest.

7328.q: Roughly how many years can a chimpanzee live?
7328.e: In the wild, chimpanzees can live to about 40 to 50 years. In zoos they sometimes get even older.

7330.q: Where does the German name for the eagle-owl, “Uhu”, probably come from?
a: From a Latin word for moon
From the colour of its feathers
From an old Swiss place name
7330.e: The name Uhu imitates a sound and comes from the bird's deep call, which sounds like “oo-hoo”. Males in particular often make this call in late winter.
7330.m: The Uhu is named after its call.

7331.q: What does the mole use to smell its prey in the dark soil?
7331.e: The mole's nose is very mobile and sensitive. With it, the mole sniffs out worms and insects even in a completely dark tunnel.
7331.m: Its nose is its most important sense organ.

7332.q: Feta cheese is mainly made from the milk of which animal?
7332.e: Feta is mainly made from sheep's milk. Sheep's milk is especially rich in fat and protein.
7332.m: Sheep's milk is also used to make cheese.

7333.q: Which family do Bactrian camels belong to?
7333.e: Bactrian camels belong to the camel family. It also includes dromedaries, llamas and alpacas.
7333.m: The Bactrian camel is a camel.

7334.q: Why do sheep prefer to stay together in a group?
a: Because they feel safer that way
7334.e: Sheep are herd animals and feel safer in a group than alone. In the flock they look out for each other.
7334.m: Sheep feel safe in the flock.

7335.q: What is a big danger for wild tigers today?
a: Too much water in the jungle
7335.e: People hunt tigers illegally and destroy their habitat, for example by cutting down forests. This makes it hard for tigers to survive.

7336.q: Which animals like to eat dung beetles?
7336.e: Dung beetles are prey for birds, hedgehogs, badgers and bats. Anyone moving around on dung is easy to spot.
7336.m: The beetles are prey for many animals.

7337.q: How many eggs does a blackbird usually lay in a nest?
7337.e: A blackbird usually lays between three and five eggs in its nest. The female then sits on them until they hatch.
7337.m: Blackbirds usually lay three to five eggs.

7339.q: What is the small intestine's main job?
7339.e: In the small intestine, nutrients from the food mush are taken into the blood. Its inner wall is heavily folded to give lots of surface area.
7339.m: The small intestine takes in nutrients.

7340.q: What happened in Tiananmen Square in Beijing in 1989?
a: Protests for more democracy were bloodily crushed by the military
A peace treaty with Taiwan was signed
7340.e: In spring 1989, mainly students demonstrated in Tiananmen Square for political reforms. The Chinese government had the protests ended with military force.
7340.m: In 1989 protests in Beijing were ended by force.

7341.q: What is a well-known yellow toy shaped like a duck that floats in the bath?
7341.e: The rubber duck is a small yellow toy that often squeaks when you squeeze it. Many children play with it in the bath.
7341.m: Rubber ducks like to float in the bath.

7343.q: What are the wels catfish's eyes like compared with its body?
a: It has no eyes at all
7343.e: The wels catfish's eyes are tiny compared with its head. It relies more on other senses.
7343.m: Small eyes, keen sense of touch.

7344.q: What do chicks do shortly after hatching?
a: They look for a new home on their own
7344.e: Little chicks stay very close to the hen and follow her everywhere. This protects them from danger.

7345.q: Which larger animal family does the roe deer belong to?
7345.e: The roe deer belongs to the deer family. But it is much smaller than a red deer.
7345.m: Roe deer belong to the deer family.

7347.q: How heavy can a large orca bull get?
7347.e: A large orca can be as heavy as several cars put together. That is really a lot of weight.

7348.q: How do young pond skaters grow?
a: They do not grow at all
7348.e: The firm body armour does not grow with them. That is why the young moult several times.

7349.q: What is special about a snake's eyelids?
a: It has no movable lids, but a see-through scale
7349.e: A see-through scale, called a spectacle, protects the eye. That is why its gaze looks fixed.
7349.m: Snakes have spectacles instead of lids.

7350.q: By which body part are grasshoppers and crickets divided into two large groups?
a: By the length of the antennae
By the colour of the wings
By the length of the back legs
By the shape of the head
7350.e: A distinction is made between short-horned and long-horned groups. In one group the antennae are short, in the other they are often longer than the whole body.

7351.q: Which other animals are gibbons more closely related to than to macaques?
7351.e: Gibbons belong to the apes and are more closely related to the great apes than to macaques. They are known as lesser apes.
7351.m: Gibbons are related to the great apes.

7352.q: What do green sandpiper chicks have to do after hatching?
a: Jump from the tree nest down to the ground
Stay in the nest for months
7352.e: The chicks leave the nest early and soon follow their parents. To do this, they jump down out of the nest.
7352.m: The chicks leave the tree nest by jumping.

7353.q: How does a pike hunt its prey?
a: It lurks in hiding and shoots forward in a flash
It digs holes and catches the prey in the ground
It jumps out of the water and flies for a moment
7353.e: The pike hides among the water plants and waits patiently. When a fish comes past, it darts out in a flash.
7353.m: The pike lurks patiently in hiding.

7354.q: Roughly how fast does a housefly fly?
a: Only a few kilometres per hour
Over a hundred kilometres per hour
7354.e: Although it seems so quick, a housefly does not actually fly very fast. It manages only a few kilometres per hour.
7354.m: Flies fly more slowly than you might think.

7355.q: How many hens can a cockerel in a group of chickens usually protect and accompany?
a: Several hens at the same time
7355.e: A cockerel often lives together with several hens in a group. He protects them and goes with them when they look for food.
7355.m: A cockerel often lives with several hens.

7356.q: Where does the Roman snail mainly live in Switzerland?
a: In gardens and woods with chalky soil
7356.e: The Roman snail likes damp gardens and woods with chalky soil. It needs the lime for its shell.

7357.q: Which policy did Deng Xiaoping introduce in China after Mao's death?
a: Economic opening with market elements while keeping one-party rule
A complete return to Mao's Cultural Revolution
The dissolution of the Communist Party
Strict isolation from the world economy
7357.e: From 1978 Deng Xiaoping opened China's economy to market elements and foreign investment. Politically, however, the Communist Party continued to rule alone.

7358.q: What does a least weasel sometimes eat in addition to mice?
a: Large hoofed animals such as roe deer
7358.e: When it gets the chance, the least weasel also catches smaller birds or raids nests. Most of its food, however, is still mice.
7358.m: Birds are sometimes on the menu too.

7359.q: Why does the panda have to eat so much bamboo, even though it is a bear?
a: Because its body digests bamboo only poorly
Because it never feels full, just for fun
7359.e: The panda's body cannot get very much energy out of bamboo. That is why it has to eat huge amounts of it.
7359.m: A panda's body digests bamboo poorly.

7360.q: When is the beaver mainly active?
7360.e: Beavers are active at dusk and at night and usually rest in their lodge during the day. This way they avoid a lot of disturbance from people and predators.

7361.q: What body shape does the otter have that helps it swim?
7361.e: The slim, long body reduces water resistance and makes the otter a fast swimmer. This shape supports its smooth movements.
7361.m: A slim body makes it a good swimmer.

7362.q: What does the badger especially like to eat?
7362.e: The badger loves earthworms and can eat a lot of them in one night. But it is an omnivore and likes other food too.
7362.m: Earthworms are the badger's favourite food.

7363.q: What makes the buzzing sound when lots of wasps fly at the same time?
7363.e: The buzzing comes from the very fast wingbeats. These let wasps move safely through the air.

7364.q: Where in the world are starfish found?
a: In almost all the seas on Earth
7364.e: Starfish live in almost all the world's seas, from warm to cold waters. They are not found in fresh water.
7364.m: Starfish live all over the sea.

7365.q: Where does the wels catfish lay its eggs?
a: In a hollow among roots and plants
In a nest in a tree
7365.e: The eggs are laid in a shallow hollow near the shore among plants and roots. There they are protected.
7365.m: Wels catfish eggs lie in a nest hollow.

7366.q: Which of these tigers is the smallest?
7366.e: The Sumatran tiger is the smallest tiger. It lives on the island of Sumatra in Asia.
7366.m: The Sumatran tiger is the smallest.

7367.q: How are chamois classified when it comes to digestion?
7367.e: Like cows and deer, chamois are ruminants. They bring their food back up and chew it again to digest it better.

7369.q: Why is the sand lizard called “Zauneidechse” (fence lizard) in German?
a: Because it is often found by fences, walls and piles of stones
Because it lives only in zoos
Because it looks like a fence
7369.e: Such places give it warmth and hiding places at the same time. So the name refers to its typical habitat.
7369.m: Fences and walls are popular sunbathing spots.

7370.q: Who looks after the common wall lizard's eggs after they have been laid?
a: Nobody, the young develop on their own
7370.e: Common wall lizards do not care for their young. The eggs are buried and develop without any further help from the parents.
7370.m: Lizards do not care for their young.

7371.q: What do buffalo do when they greet or calm each other?
a: They lick each other or rub against each other
They swap food from their mouths
7371.e: Grooming each other strengthens the bond in the group. It happens in many herd animals.

7372.q: What is the place where salmon lay their eggs called?
a: A spawning pit in the gravel
7372.e: The female makes a hollow in the gravel bed with her tail. There she lays her eggs.
7372.m: Salmon eggs lie in pits in the gravel.

7373.q: How does an alpine newt react when it feels threatened?
a: It can play dead or flee
7373.e: When there is danger, the alpine newt first tries to flee. Some newts also play dead to fool their enemies.
7373.m: When in danger, the alpine newt flees quickly.

7374.q: What do adult fire salamanders mainly eat?
7374.e: Adult fire salamanders hunt small ground animals such as beetles, worms and snails at night. They eat only meat.

7375.q: What is the soft wool for jumpers made from?
7375.e: Sheep have a thick fleece that is sheared every year. This wool is spun into yarn for warm clothes.

7376.q: Up to what height can the adder be found in the Alps?
7376.e: The adder is one of the snakes that climbs highest. In the Alps it is found up to about 3000 metres.
7376.m: Adders live high up in the Alps.

7377.q: What makes the ibex's horns different from a deer's antlers?
a: Horns keep on growing, antlers are shed and regrown every year
Horns are made of bone, antlers of fur
Antlers grow all through life, horns do not
7377.e: Horns like the ibex's have a bony core with a horn sheath and stay for a lifetime. A deer's antlers, on the other hand, fall off every year and grow again.

7378.q: In ring-tailed lemurs, who usually gets to the food first?
7378.e: The higher-ranking females have priority when eating. Males often have to wait.

7379.q: Can you easily tell male and female fire salamanders apart by their colour?
7379.e: Males and females have the same colouring and look very alike. Only experts can spot small differences in body shape.
7379.m: Males and females look very alike.

7380.q: What happens if you keep a goldfish in a bowl that is far too small?
a: It often stays small and gets ill more quickly
7380.e: In a bowl that is too small, the goldfish does not have enough space or oxygen, which harms it and slows its growth. A proper home needs much more space.
7380.m: A bowl that is too small harms the goldfish.

7381.q: Where does the common toad like to live best?
a: In woods, gardens and damp areas
7381.e: The common toad feels at home in woods, gardens and damp places. It just needs a pond or stream nearby to spawn in.
7381.m: Common toads live in woods and gardens.

7382.q: What is special about the panda's paws?
a: It has a kind of extra thumb
7382.e: A special bone works like a thumb. With it the panda can hold bamboo firmly.
7382.m: The panda has a gripping thumb.

7383.q: Which part of the body helps the wild camel cope even with salty water?
7383.e: Wild camels can even drink water with quite a lot of salt in it. Their kidneys get rid of the salt well.
7383.m: Wild camels can cope with salty water.

7384.q: What was the military alliance of the communist states in the Cold War called?
7384.e: The Warsaw Pact was the counterpart to NATO. Its members were the Soviet Union and its allies.
7384.m: The Warsaw Pact was the alliance of the East.

7385.q: What does the koala need its sharp claws for?
7385.e: The long, sharp claws help the koala hold on safely to the branches. This stops it slipping when it climbs.

7386.q: On which paper do you write Yes or No in a vote?
7386.e: You write Yes or No on the ballot paper. Then you put it in the voting envelope and hand it in.
7386.m: I write Yes or No on the ballot paper.

7387.q: What is grit or bird sand useful for in budgies?
a: It makes their feathers more colourful
7387.e: Tiny grains of grit help the budgie's stomach grind up hard seeds better. This lets it digest its food well.

7388.q: How does a beaver dam usually change its surroundings?
a: A pond forms that gives many animals a new habitat
The forest is completely cut down
7388.e: The dam holds back water to form a pond, where fish, amphibians and water birds find a new habitat. In this way many other species benefit from the beavers' work.

7389.q: Why should you not take goldfish out of the water with your bare hands?
a: Because it can damage their protective slime layer
7389.e: If you touch a goldfish with bare hands, you can damage the delicate layer of slime on its skin. This makes it more likely to get ill.
7389.m: Try not to touch goldfish with your hands.

7390.q: What does the common buzzard like to eat most of all?
7390.e: In German it is called the “mouse buzzard” because it mainly hunts mice and voles. In a poor year for mice, though, it also eats other prey.
7390.m: Voles come top of the list.

7391.q: Which plant is a favourite food of some mountain gorillas?
7391.e: Mountain gorillas like eating young bamboo shoots and wild celery. These plants grow high up in their mountain forests.

7392.q: What can often tell you the age of a chamois more precisely?
a: The yearly rings on its horns
The colour of its coat alone
7392.e: A chamois's horns grow a little more every year and form visible rings. If you count these rings, you can work out the animal's approximate age.
7392.m: Yearly rings on the horns reveal the age.

7393.q: Which group of birds do the green sandpiper and the wood sandpiper belong to?
7393.e: Waders often live on shores and in shallow water. Lapwings and snipes belong to this group too.

7394.q: How does the raven's tail in flight differ most from that of a carrion crow?
a: It is forked like a swallow's
It is very short and round
7394.e: In flight you can recognise the raven by its wedge-shaped tail, while the carrion crow's tail is cut straight across. This is one of the most important ways to tell them apart.
7394.m: A wedge-shaped tail sets it apart from crows.

7395.q: Which animal is Isengrim in the old fable of Reynard the Fox?
7395.e: In the old animal fable of Reynard the Fox, the wolf is called Isengrim. He is tricked again and again by the cunning fox.
7395.m: Isengrim is the wolf in the fable.

7396.q: How many young does a vixen usually have at once?
a: Never any cubs of her own
7396.e: A vixen usually gives birth to between three and six cubs. The young are born in spring and are blind at first.
7396.m: A vixen has three to six cubs.

7397.q: How have golden eagle numbers in Switzerland developed since the protection law?
a: They have clearly recovered and grown again
They have stayed exactly the same as before 1953
7397.e: Thanks to legal protection and less persecution, golden eagle numbers in Switzerland have clearly recovered over the decades. Today several hundred pairs breed in the Alps again.

7398.q: Which animals like to hunt grasshoppers?
7398.e: Many birds and spiders love eating grasshoppers. That is why grasshoppers have to hide well.

7399.q: What does the badger's tail look like?
a: It has no tail at all
7399.e: Compared with the fox, the badger has a rather short, bushy tail. It is much less noticeable than its striped face.
7399.m: Badgers have a short, bushy tail.

7400.q: In which national park can you see Cape buffalo in the wild?
a: In the Bavarian Forest National Park
In the Hohe Tauern National Park
7400.e: Kruger National Park in South Africa is home to large herds of buffalo. They are protected there.
7400.m: National parks protect buffalo in Africa.

7401.q: What colour eyes do newborn pumas usually have?
7401.e: Young pumas have blue eyes at first. At about one year old they turn brownish to yellowish.

7402.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult male leopard get?
7402.e: Males usually weigh between 60 and 90 kilograms. That is about as much as an adult human.
7402.m: Male leopards weigh up to about 90 kilos.

7403.q: How do cows usually feel when they are together with other cows?
7403.e: Cows are herd animals and feel safe and comfortable in a group with other cows. They do not like being alone as much.
7403.m: Cows feel safe in the herd.

7404.q: How do gibbons such as the lar gibbon usually move through the forest?
a: They swing by their arms from branch to branch
They hop on two legs on the ground
They glide with flaps of skin
7404.e: Gibbons have very long arms and swing from branch to branch. This makes them very fast in the treetops.

7405.q: Which senses are especially well developed in a goose?
a: Only the sense of touch in the feathers
7405.e: Geese can see and hear well. This lets them notice danger early and warn their group.
7405.m: Geese see and hear very well.

7406.q: What regularly happens to the sand lizard's skin?
a: It sheds its skin because the old skin does not grow with it
It never grows and never has to shed its skin
It changes colour completely every day
7406.e: Like other reptiles, the sand lizard sheds its old skin in pieces as soon as it has become too tight. Underneath there is already a new, fresh skin.
7406.m: Sand lizards shed their skin regularly.

7407.q: In many countries, what is the stork a sign of?
7407.e: In many countries people are happy when a stork nests on their roof. It is seen as a bringer of good luck.
7407.m: The stork is seen as a lucky charm.

7408.q: What is a male red fox called?
7408.e: The male fox is called a dog. This word is also used for male dogs.
7408.m: A male fox is called a dog.

7410.q: Where do spotted hyenas often raise their young?
7410.e: The young live in dens that are often used by several mothers. There they are protected from enemies.
7410.m: Hyena cubs grow up in a den.

7411.q: Why is the European tree frog protected by law in Switzerland?
a: Because its numbers have fallen sharply
Because it is poisonous to humans
7411.e: Because suitable ponds and habitats have been lost, the European tree frog has become rare. That is why it is protected in Switzerland.

7412.q: How does the common wall lizard typically react when it spots prey?
a: It creeps up slowly and suddenly snaps
It waits motionless in one spot for days
It calls loudly to the prey
It digs a hole and waits in it
7412.e: The common wall lizard approaches carefully and waits for the right moment. Then it snaps in a flash.

7413.q: Among Asian elephants, which ones often have no tusks or only very short ones?
a: Only the calves in their first year
None, they all have tusks of the same length
7413.e: In females the tusks are usually small and hardly stick out of the mouth. Some males have none either; they are called makhnas.

7414.q: Why is the stag beetle's tongue like a brush?
7414.e: Its mouthparts are built for licking up tree sap. It can hardly chew solid food.
7414.m: The brush takes up liquid sap.

7415.q: How many toes does a raven's foot have, and how are they arranged?
a: Four toes, three pointing forward and one back
7415.e: Like most birds, the raven has four toes on each foot. Three point forward and one strong toe points back, which gives it a firm grip.
7415.m: The raven has four toes, three at the front and one at the back.

7416.q: Which organ pumps blood through our body?
7416.e: The heart is a muscle that works like a pump and carries blood through the whole body. It beats many thousands of times every day.

7417.q: What is this development with egg, larva, pupa and beetle called?
7417.e: In this kind of development the larva looks completely different from the adult animal. Butterflies develop like this too.
7417.m: Development through egg, larva, pupa and beetle is called complete metamorphosis.

7418.q: What is the sea ice on which polar bears often hunt called?
7418.e: Pack ice is frozen sea water that freezes into large sheets of ice in winter. Polar bears catch their seals on it.
7418.m: Polar bears hunt on the pack ice.

7419.q: What did DDT do to peregrine falcons?
a: The eggshells became too thin and broke easily
The birds could no longer fly
7419.e: The poison DDT upset the females' calcium balance, which made the eggshells thinner. As a result many eggs broke in the nest.
7419.m: The poison DDT made the eggshells thin.

7420.q: Where does the golden hamster originally come from?
7420.e: The golden hamster comes from dry areas in Syria. There it lives wild in burrows underground.

7421.q: What do male lake trout often get on their lower jaw at spawning time?
7421.e: At spawning time the male develops a hook, called a kype, on its lower jaw. It is part of its breeding colours and can be seen in fights with rivals.
7421.m: Males have a hook at spawning time.

7422.q: What problem does the beech marten sometimes cause with cars?
a: It bites through cables in the engine
It scratches the outside of the tyres
7422.e: Beech martens often bite rubber parts and cables in the engine, especially during the mating season or when marking their territory. This can cause expensive damage to the car.
7422.m: Beech martens like biting through car cables.

7423.e: Kingfisher eggs are glossy white and almost round. Even so, they are well protected in the dark nest chamber.
7423.m: Kingfisher eggs are white and glossy.

7424.q: What job does the okapi have in the rainforest?
a: It helps to spread plants and seeds
It pollinates flowers like a bee
7424.e: When it eats and through its droppings, the okapi spreads seeds. In this way it adds to the variety of the forest.
7424.m: Okapis spread seeds in the forest.

7425.q: Roughly how long is an elephant calf in its mother's belly before it is born?
7425.e: Elephants have the longest pregnancy of all land animals. It lasts almost two years.
7425.m: Elephants are pregnant for almost two years.

7426.q: Where do ring-tailed lemurs sleep at night?
a: In trees, cuddled closely together on cold nights
In deep holes in the ground
