7426.e: Ring-tailed lemurs rest on branches at night. When it is cool, they huddle closely together and keep each other warm.
7426.m: Ring-tailed lemurs sleep together in trees.

7427.q: Do the hippopotamus's canine teeth grow throughout its life?
a: No, they fall out after a year
7427.e: A hippo's large canine teeth keep growing throughout its life. This means they can become very long and impressive.

7428.q: When may chamois traditionally be hunted in Switzerland?
a: Only during the hunting season set by law
7428.e: In Switzerland there are exact legal rules and seasons for hunting chamois. These are meant to protect their numbers and stop overhunting.
7428.m: Chamois hunting is regulated by law.

7429.q: What role does the wood mouse play in the forest for other animals?
a: It is important food for many predators and birds
It eats all the other animals
7429.e: The wood mouse is an important source of food for owls, foxes and other predators.
7429.m: It is food for many animals.

7430.q: How does the bearded vulture break up large bones that it cannot swallow?
a: It drops them on rocks from a great height
It bites through them with very strong teeth
It softens them by cooking them in the sun
It lets other animals chew them up
7430.e: The bearded vulture carries large bones high into the air and drops them onto flat slabs of rock. There they break into smaller pieces that it can eat.

7431.q: Why do goldfish often prefer to live in groups?
a: Because they are better protected from enemies that way
Because otherwise they cannot find the water
7431.e: Swimming in a group protects individual fish better from predators. That is why goldfish and their wild relatives often live in shoals.

7432.q: What are the reindeer's broad hooves for?
a: They stop it from sinking into the snow
They are for swimming under water
7432.e: The hooves are broad and can spread apart. This means the reindeer sinks less deeply into snow and soft ground.
7432.m: Broad hooves carry it over snow.

7433.q: Roughly how heavy is an adult white stork?
7433.e: An adult stork weighs about three to four kilograms. Even so, it can fly well thanks to its large wings.
7433.m: A stork weighs about 3 to 4 kilos.

7434.q: What happens to the dromedary's coat over the course of the year?
a: It is shed and replaced in spring
7434.e: In winter the coat is thicker. When it gets warmer, the animal changes its coat.

7435.q: Do mute swans usually fly to warm countries in winter?
a: They fly to the North Pole
7435.e: Unlike many migratory birds, mute swans often stay in the same area all year round. Only when there is very hard frost do some move a little further away.
7435.m: Mute swans usually stay all year.

a: A mountain from which hot rock can come out
A mountain made of pure ice
7436.e: Deep inside a volcano it is extremely hot. Sometimes melted rock, called lava, rises up to the surface.
7436.m: Lava can come out of a volcano.

7437.q: What does a honeybee defend itself with?
7437.e: If a bee feels threatened, it can sting. When it does, it also releases a little venom.
7437.m: Bees defend themselves with their sting.

7438.q: What is the capital of the canton of Solothurn?
7438.e: Solothurn is not only the name of the canton but also the name of its capital. The cantonal government meets there, for example.
7438.m: The capital has the same name as the canton.

7439.q: Where do guinea pigs originally live wild in nature?
7439.e: The domestic guinea pig comes from the wild cavy, which lives in South America. Over many hundreds of years people bred it into the well-known pet.
7439.m: Wild guinea pigs live in South America.

7440.q: Roughly how long is a female bison pregnant?
7440.e: The pregnancy lasts about nine months, similar to domestic cattle. After that a calf is born.
7440.m: Bison cows are pregnant for nine months.

7441.q: What do bumblebees carry on their back legs?
7441.e: On their back legs bumblebees have little baskets in which they collect pollen. They carry it back to the nest.
7441.m: Pollen baskets carry pollen to the nest.

7442.q: Can a tiger pull its claws in?
a: No, it has no claws at all
7442.e: Tigers can pull their claws in, just like pet cats. This keeps the claws sharp and stops them getting damaged.
7442.m: Tigers can pull their claws in.

7443.q: How many different species of rhinoceros are there in the whole world?
7443.e: There are five different species of rhinoceros in the world today. Two live in Africa and three in Asia.
7443.m: There are five rhino species worldwide.

7444.q: What colour is an adult lion's coat usually?
7444.e: A lion's coat is usually sandy brown or golden yellow. This colour helps it to blend in well in the dry savannah.
7444.m: Lion fur is usually sandy brown to golden yellow.

7445.q: How do the feathers of male and female blackbirds differ?
a: The male is black, the female brown
Both are coloured exactly the same
The female is black, the male colourful
7445.e: You can easily tell male and female blackbirds apart by their colour. The male is black, the female much browner.
7445.m: Male blackbirds are black, females brown.

a: The movement of water through a partially permeable membrane
The conversion of light into sugar
The evaporation of water in heat
7446.e: In osmosis water moves from a less concentrated to a more concentrated solution through a membrane that only lets certain particles through. This is how plant roots, for example, take up water from the soil.
7446.m: Osmosis lets water move through membranes.

7447.q: What does an adder do when it feels threatened?
a: It hisses and flattens its body
It rattles the tip of its tail
It puffs up a throat pouch
It plays dead like the grass snake
7447.e: It hisses loudly and takes up an S-shaped position. This is meant to scare off enemies.
7447.m: Hissing is a warning before a bite.

7448.q: Which subspecies of elephant lives on a large island in South-East Asia?
7448.e: The Sumatran elephant lives on the Indonesian island of Sumatra. It is considered critically endangered.
7448.m: The Sumatran elephant lives on Sumatra.

7449.q: Where does a large share of the perch fillets sold in Switzerland come from?
7449.e: Switzerland eats far more perch fillets than Swiss lakes can supply. That is why a large share is imported from abroad.

7450.q: What can happen to the colour of some common frogs when it is cold?
7450.e: The skin colour of the common frog can change slightly depending on temperature and mood. When it is cold, it often gets a little darker.
7450.m: When it is cold, the colour can get darker.

7451.q: Why do salmon eggs need clean, cool water?
a: It contains a lot of oxygen
It is warm like bath water
It contains a lot of sugar
7451.e: The eggs lie in the gravel and need a lot of oxygen. Cool, clean water contains more of it than warm or muddy water.

7452.q: What does a grasshopper hear with?
a: With small ears on its legs or belly
With ears on its head like a human
7452.e: Grasshoppers have no ears on their head. Their hearing organs are often on the legs or the abdomen.
7452.m: Their ears are not on their head.

7453.q: Where does a mosquito prefer to lay its eggs?
7453.e: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in puddles, water butts or small ponds with calm water. Later the larvae can swim there.
7453.m: Mosquito eggs like to lie in water.

7454.q: What do carrion crows sometimes do with leftover food?
a: They hide it to use later
They throw it away at once
They give it to other kinds of birds
7454.e: Carrion crows hide extra food in various places so they can find it again later. This behaviour is called caching and shows their good memory.
7454.m: Carrion crows hide food for later.

7455.q: What kind of feet does a sheep have?
7455.e: Sheep have split hooves, also called cloven hooves. With them they can walk safely even on steep meadows.

a: A person who makes wrongdoing or abuse of power public.
7457.e: Whistleblowers publish secret information about wrongdoing, often at great personal risk. They play an important role in uncovering abuse of power.

7458.q: What is it called when all citizens may vote directly on a question?
7458.e: In a popular vote, all voters may say Yes or No to a question directly. This is typical of Switzerland.
7458.m: In a popular vote everyone says Yes or No.

7459.q: In which habitats does the sand lizard feel especially at home?
a: In warm, dry places such as railway embankments or banks
7459.e: It needs open, sunny and rather dry areas with places to hide. That is why it is often found on railway embankments, vineyard walls or banks.
7459.m: Warm, dry areas are its favourite places.

7460.q: Which group of animals does the octopus belong to?
7460.e: The octopus is a mollusc and belongs to the cephalopods. Cuttlefish and squid also belong to this group.

7461.q: Roughly how big does a grasshopper in Switzerland get?
a: As small as a speck of dust
7461.e: Most grasshoppers in Switzerland are only a few centimetres long. Even so, they can jump a long way.
7461.m: Grasshoppers grow to only a few centimetres.

7462.q: Which sea turtle is the largest species in the world?
7462.e: The leatherback is the largest of all sea turtles. It can even grow longer than a person is tall.
7462.m: The leatherback is the largest species.

7463.q: What role did the European tree frog once play as a “weather frog”?
a: People kept it in jars because its climbing supposedly showed the weather
It was bred as a pet to catch insects
It was used to measure time
7463.e: People used to believe that the tree frog's behaviour in a jar could predict the coming weather. This idea gave it the nickname “weather frog”.
7463.m: The nickname “weather frog” comes from olden times.

7464.q: What does the mother feed her orca baby with?
a: She does not feed it at all
7464.e: The orca baby drinks milk from its mother. All mammals do this with their young.
7464.m: Orca babies drink their mother's milk.

7465.q: Which group of animals does the adder belong to?
7465.e: The adder is a snake and so belongs to the reptiles. It has dry, scaly skin and does not lay eggs in water.
7465.m: The adder is a reptile, not an amphibian.

7466.q: Which call is typical of the kestrel?
a: A deep hoot like an owl's
A loud caw like a crow's
A melodic twitter like a blackbird's
7466.e: The kestrel often gives a quick, high call that sounds like “kee-kee-kee”. You hear this call especially often near the nest.
7466.m: Its call sounds high, like kee-kee-kee.

7467.q: What does a duck use to keep its feathers waterproof?
a: Oil from a small gland near its tail
7467.e: Ducks use their beak to squeeze oil from the preen gland and spread it through their feathers. Then the water simply runs off.

7468.q: How does the choice of ground help when marmots place their burrow?
a: Burrows are often in places with a good view all round
Burrows are always in the middle of thick forest
Burrows are always right in the river
Burrows are always under the roof of a house
7468.e: Marmots often dig their burrows on slopes or near rocks with a good view of the surroundings. This lets them spot enemies creeping up early.
7468.m: A good view protects against enemies.

7469.q: Which fish often attaches itself to a shark and eats its leftovers?
7469.e: The remora attaches itself to the shark with a sucking disc. This way it travels along and gets leftovers without harming the shark.
7469.m: The remora travels on the shark.

7470.q: What does a kestrel do to defend its territory against other kestrels?
a: It flies threateningly at intruders and calls loudly
It digs a ditch round its territory
It marks its territory with a strong smell like a fox
It hides quietly and never fights back
7470.e: If other kestrels come into its territory, the owner often behaves threateningly and flies at the intruder, calling loudly. This is meant to drive the rival away.
7470.m: Threat flights and calls protect the territory.

7471.q: Why is the Roman snail called “Weinbergschnecke” (vineyard snail) in German?
a: Because it is often found in vineyards
Because it looks like a wine bottle
7471.e: In the past the snail was often found in vineyards. That is where its German name comes from.
7471.m: It was often found in vineyards.

7472.q: Which animal is the giraffe's biggest natural enemy?
7472.e: Lions mainly attack young or sick giraffes. Adult giraffes can defend themselves well with powerful kicks.
7472.m: Lions are the biggest danger for giraffes.

7473.q: What is a reflex, for example pulling your hand back from something hot?
a: An automatic, unconscious reaction via the spinal cord
7473.e: In a reflex, the signal is processed directly in the spinal cord without waiting for the brain. This lets the body react especially fast to danger.
7473.m: Reflexes work faster than conscious thought.

7474.q: In which season do you see the most butterflies in Switzerland?
7474.e: In summer especially many flowers are in bloom, so butterflies find the most food then. That is why you see the most butterflies at this time.

7475.q: What does the wood mouse's fur feel like?
7475.e: The wood mouse's fur is soft and thick. It protects it well from the cold.
7475.m: Its fur is soft and thick.

7476.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult giant panda get?
7476.e: Adult pandas are quite large, heavy animals. Males are usually a little heavier than females.
7476.m: A panda weighs about 100 to 150 kilograms.

7477.q: When is the stoat's mating season?
7477.e: Mating takes place in early summer. Even so, the young are born much later.
7477.m: The mating season is in early summer.

7478.q: How does a pair of eagle-owls often behave over several years?
a: Both often stay loyal to the same partner and territory for years
They change partner and territory completely every year
They never live as a pair, always alone
The males change partner every day
7478.e: Eagle-owls usually stay loyal to the same partner and the same territory for several years. The territory is often used again and again over a long time.
7478.m: Eagle-owl pairs often stay together for a long time.

7480.q: What kind of mouthparts does the earwig have?
7480.e: With its strong chewing mouthparts it can bite up leaves, flowers and small animals. It does not have a sucking tube like a butterfly.
7480.m: It eats with biting and chewing mouthparts.

7481.q: Where does a roe deer like to live best?
a: In woods and at the edges of woods with fields
7481.e: Roe deer like it when woods and open fields lie close together. There they find shelter and food at the same time.
7481.m: Roe deer love woodland edges and fields.

7484.q: What does the wels catfish's dorsal fin look like?
a: All of them have none at all
7484.e: The wels catfish's dorsal fin is small and sits far forward. This makes it different from many other fish.
7484.m: The wels catfish's dorsal fin is tiny.

7485.q: How old can an Asian elephant get in human care?
7485.e: Elephants live to a great age. With good care they can reach 60 years or more.

7486.q: What enemies does the mole have?
7486.e: When a mole comes to the surface, it can be caught by foxes, owls or cats. Under the ground, however, it is fairly safe.

7487.q: Do elks (moose) live in Switzerland as permanent wild animals?
a: No, they only rarely turn up as stray visitors
7487.e: There are no permanent elk populations in Switzerland. Now and then, single animals wander in from the east.
7487.m: In Switzerland elks are stray visitors.

7488.q: How many legs does a cockchafer have?
7488.e: Like all insects, the cockchafer has six legs. They are attached to its chest.

a: A carp with only a few large scales
A carp with almost no scales at all
A carp with lots of small scales
A carp with shiny silver skin and no scales
7489.e: Mirror carp have only a few scales, but they are large and shiny. They were bred like this on purpose.
7489.m: Mirror carp have a few large scales.

7491.q: How does a pond skater notice that an insect has fallen onto the water?
a: From the colour of the prey
From the temperature of the water
7491.e: Struggling insects make small ripples on the water. The pond skater feels them with sense organs on its legs.
7491.m: It feels ripples with its legs.

7492.q: In which year was the UN founded?
7492.e: The UN was founded after the Second World War so that countries could work together for peace. Since then many states have cooperated in the organisation.

7493.q: What is the sound that bumblebees make when flying called?
7493.e: The fast wingbeats make a buzzing sound. You often hear it before you see the bumblebee.

7494.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult beech marten get?
a: About one and a half kilograms
About 5 kilograms, like a large cat
7494.e: An adult beech marten usually weighs about one to two kilograms. That makes it much lighter than many other predators such as foxes or badgers.
7494.m: Beech martens weigh only a few kilograms.

7495.q: What do ducks often do on the shore to look after their feathers?
a: They clean them carefully with their beak
They rub them on tree bark
They just let the rain wash them
7495.e: Ducks spend a lot of time arranging and oiling their feathers with their beak. This keeps the feathers waterproof and warm.

7496.q: What does the nest under an anthill look like?
a: It has many tunnels and chambers
It is one single large room
There are no tunnels at all
7496.e: Under the visible mound there is a nest with many tunnels and rooms. The queen, larvae and workers live there.

7497.q: What is the great spotted woodpecker's tongue like?
a: Very long, and it can stick it far out
7497.e: The long tongue can reach deep into holes in trees. This lets it get at insects hidden deep in the bark.

7498.q: When is the fire salamander mainly active?
a: At night and in damp, rainy weather
Only at midday in great heat
Only in the depths of winter
7498.e: Because its skin must not dry out, it usually comes out of its hiding place at night or when it rains. During the day it stays hidden.
7498.m: Rain and darkness bring it out.

7499.q: What do young goat kids especially like to do for fun?
7499.e: Kids are very playful and love leaping about wildly, even on rocks. This trains their muscles and jumping power.
7499.m: Kids jump and hop a lot.

7500.q: How many eggs does a common buzzard usually lay in one clutch?
7500.e: A common buzzard usually lays two to three eggs per brood. The eggs are whitish with brown spots.
7500.m: Two to three eggs per clutch.

7501.q: What does the elk's (moose's) upper lip look like?
7501.e: The upper lip is long and grips twigs and leaves well. This lets it feed very skilfully.

7502.q: Where do millipedes often lay their eggs?
a: In small hollows in the earth or in the soil
7502.e: Many females lay their eggs in the soil or build small chambers. Some species surround them with droppings or earth.
7502.m: Eggs often lie protected in the soil.

7503.q: In which month does the cuckoo usually return from Africa to Switzerland?
7503.e: The cuckoo usually returns from its winter quarters in Africa in April. Soon after, its typical spring call starts in Switzerland.

7504.q: What happens to the eyes of newborn puppies?
a: They are closed at first and open after about two weeks
They are fully open from birth
Puppies have no eyes at first
The eyes only open after a year
7504.e: Puppies are born with their eyes closed and only open them after about ten to fourteen days. Their ears are also closed at first and open during this time.
7504.m: Puppies' eyes open after two weeks.

7505.q: What is the magpie's most striking feature?
7505.e: The long tail, graduated like steps, can be almost as long as the rest of the body. It helps the magpie steer in flight.
7505.m: The long tail makes the magpie easy to recognise.

7506.q: In kangaroos, which is usually bigger?
7506.e: Male kangaroos are usually much bigger and stronger than females. They can even be twice as heavy.

7507.q: How does the orchid mantis camouflage itself?
a: It buries itself in the sand
7507.e: The orchid mantis lives in South-East Asia. Its shape and colour look like a flower, which attracts prey.

7508.q: What is a hippopotamus's skin like?
7508.e: A hippo's skin is very thick but has almost no hair. This protects it well, but it dries out easily.
7508.m: Hippo skin is thick and almost bare.

7509.q: Why did the bearded vulture disappear from the Alps at the start of the 20th century?
7509.e: People hunted the bearded vulture because they wrongly thought it was dangerous. The last bearded vulture in the Alps was shot in 1913 in the Aosta Valley in Italy.
7509.m: Hunting wiped out the bearded vulture.

7511.q: How many claws does a panda normally have on each paw?
7511.e: Like other bears, the panda has five claws on each paw. With them it can climb well and hold on to bamboo.
7511.m: A panda has five claws on each paw.

7512.q: How does an adult brown trout usually behave towards other trout?
a: It lives in a huge shoal
It swims to the sea every day
7512.e: Brown trout are often loners and stay in one good spot. Intruders are driven away.

7513.q: How do ants find their way between food and the nest?
7513.e: Ants lay a scent trail with special substances called pheromones. Other ants can then follow the trail.
7513.m: Ants smell their way to food.

7514.q: What is the importance of fur colour for young wolves in their surroundings?
a: It helps them to camouflage themselves
It always shows their rank in the pack straight away
It never changes during their life
It is identical in all wolves worldwide
7514.e: The fur colour often matches the habitat, for example greyish brown in forests or lighter in snowy areas. This makes the animals harder for prey and enemies to spot.

7515.q: Which other animals belong to the same family as the beech marten?
7515.e: Beech martens belong to the weasel family. It also includes the badger, otter and stoat, which all share related body features.
7515.m: Badgers and otters are relatives of the beech marten.

7516.q: Which animal in Switzerland can sometimes hunt wild boar?
7516.e: In some areas of Switzerland there are wolves that can hunt young or weak wild boar. Adult wild boar, however, have few natural enemies.

7517.q: What does stocking mean in fishing?
a: Young fish are released into a lake or river
Fish are removed from the lake
Fish are counted and then eaten
7517.e: Fish farms raise young lake trout and release them into streams or lakes. This is meant to support threatened populations.
7517.m: Stocking means releasing young fish into a body of water.

7518.q: What makes the beaver different from the coypu, which it is sometimes confused with?
a: The beaver has a broad, flat tail, the coypu a round one
The beaver lives only in the sea
7518.e: The most obvious difference is the tail, which is broad and flat in the beaver but round and thin in the coypu. Their size and fur are also clearly different.
7518.m: The tail gives away the difference.

7519.q: What does it mean when a wolf lays its ears flat against its head?
a: It can show fear or submission
It means the wolf has no ears any more
It is just a sign of heat
7519.e: Flattened ears are part of a wolf's body language and can show submission or fear. Together with other signals, this helps us understand the animal's mood better.

7522.q: Roughly how many degrees can a tawny owl turn its head?
a: Not at all, its head is fixed
7522.e: Thanks to special neck bones, the tawny owl can turn its head almost three quarters of a full turn. This lets it locate sounds exactly without turning its body.
7522.m: The tawny owl turns its head up to 270 degrees.

7523.q: Why is there a closed season for brown trout?
a: So that they can spawn undisturbed
Because the water is too cold for fishing then
7523.e: During the closed season they must not be caught. This keeps the next generation safe.

7524.q: Do dragonflies have a pupa stage?
a: Yes, in a cocoon under water
7524.e: Dragonflies go through egg, larva and adult. There is no pupa stage.

7525.q: Which animal is related to the starfish?
7525.e: Like the starfish, the sea urchin belongs to the echinoderms. Both animals live on the seabed.
7525.m: The sea urchin is related to it.

7526.q: Which animals are natural enemies of the common wall lizard?
a: Birds such as the kestrel, and snakes
7526.e: Birds of prey and snakes hunt wall lizards on purpose. That is why the lizard dashes into hiding places in a flash when there is danger.

7527.q: What does a budgie usually do when it gets a fright?
7527.e: When there is danger, a budgie takes off and flies away in a flash. In the wild this behaviour protects it from enemies.
7527.m: When frightened, the budgie flies away quickly.

7528.q: Roughly how long does it take until young sparrows can fly?
7528.e: After only about two weeks young sparrows are fledged, which means they can leave the nest and fly. In birds this usually happens faster than in other animals.
7528.m: After two weeks sparrows can fly.

7529.q: What role does marmot fat play in traditional Swiss folk medicine?
a: It was used as an ointment for muscle and joint pain
It was used only for cooking desserts
It was used as fuel for lamps
It was used as dye for fabrics
7529.e: In the Alps, people used to make ointments from marmot fat. This marmot ointment was traditionally rubbed on for muscle and joint complaints.
7529.m: Marmot fat was used as a traditional ointment.

7530.q: Does the pike build a nest for its eggs?
a: No, it lays the eggs freely among plants
Yes, a large nest of branches
Yes, it digs a deep hole in the ground
7530.e: Unlike some birds, the pike does not build a nest. It simply lays its sticky eggs among water plants.
7530.m: The pike lays its eggs without a nest.

7531.q: What is the ranking order like among baboons?
a: There is a hierarchy with higher-ranking and lower-ranking animals
They are always all of equal rank
7531.e: There are ranking orders in the group. Higher-ranking animals often get first choice of food and sleeping places.

7532.q: Do female bison have horns too?
7532.e: Both cows and bulls have horns. The cows' horns are a little slimmer.

7533.q: What is the small round head covering that some Jewish men and boys wear called?
7533.e: The kippah is worn out of respect for God, especially when praying or in the synagogue. It covers only a small part of the head.
7533.m: The kippah is a Jewish head covering.

7534.q: What is especially striking about the raven's throat?
a: Long, shaggy feathers that look like a beard
Smooth, short feathers with nothing special
7534.e: Longer feathers grow on the raven's neck and chin and look like a shaggy beard. It raises these feathers especially when calling or excited.
7534.m: Long throat feathers form a beard.

7535.q: What does World Population Day raise awareness of?
a: Issues around population growth and its consequences
7535.e: On World Population Day, 11 July, attention is drawn to issues such as population growth, health and education. It was started by the UN.
7535.m: World Population Day is about population growth.

7536.q: What kind of teeth does a mole have?
a: Small, pointed teeth for catching prey
Only broad grinding teeth like a cow
7536.e: The mole has many small, pointed teeth. With them it can hold and break up worms and insects well.

7537.q: What do aphids use to suck plant sap?
7537.e: The mouthpart is like a fine needle and pierces the plant's sap channels. This is how the aphids get at the sap.
7537.m: A piercing mouthpart taps into the plant.

7538.q: What does a gorilla build anew every evening?
a: A sleeping nest of leaves and twigs
7538.e: Every evening the gorilla gathers leaves and branches and builds itself a soft nest. It sleeps in it until the next morning.
7538.m: Gorillas build a new nest every night.

7539.q: What happens to the mother and calf after the birth?
a: The calf is looked after by its mother and the herd
The calf is left alone straight away
The calf is raised by its father
The calf lives in a nest
7539.e: The whole herd helps to raise the calf. Aunts and older sisters look after the calf too.
7539.m: The whole herd helps to raise the young.

7540.q: What job do the adrenal glands have?
a: They produce hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol
They filter the blood like the kidneys
7540.e: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys and produce important hormones for stress reactions and metabolism. Adrenaline and cortisol are among them.
7540.m: The adrenal glands make stress hormones.

7541.q: Why is the slow worm, called “Blindschleiche” (blind creeper) in German, not actually blind?
a: It has no eyes at all
It sees only light and dark
It has eyes under its skin
7541.e: The slow worm can see well and has movable eyelids. The German name probably comes from an old word meaning shining.

7542.q: What does the edible frog need to breed successfully?
a: One of its two parent species nearby
7542.e: Because the edible frog is a hybrid, it often has to mate with one of its parent species. Without them nearby, breeding works poorly.
7542.m: The edible frog needs its parent species nearby.

7543.q: What role does the brown bear often play in the ecosystem when it eats berries?
a: It spreads the plants' seeds through its droppings
It completely destroys all the plants
It has no influence on plants at all
It eats only the seeds and leaves the berries
7543.e: When the bear eats berries, it also swallows the seeds, which later come out undigested in its droppings. This helps plants spread to new areas.
7543.m: Bears spread plant seeds through their droppings.

a: A day that reminds people of children’s rights
A day without school for everyone
7546.e: World Children’s Day reminds us that all children in the world have rights, for example the right to school and protection. The UN supports this day.
7546.m: World Children’s Day reminds us of children’s rights.

7547.q: What can a great tit do especially well on a fat ball?
7547.e: Great tits can skilfully hold on to a fat ball upside down and eat at the same time. This shows how agile and skilful these small birds are.
7547.m: Great tits often eat hanging upside down.

7548.q: What did the UN adopt in 1948?
a: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
7548.e: In the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the UN set out which rights every person in the world should have. It is seen as an important basis for many later laws.
7548.m: In 1948 the UN declared human rights.

7549.q: What does the great tit especially like to eat in winter?
7549.e: In winter there are hardly any insects, so the great tit eats seeds and nuts. At bird feeders it especially likes sunflower seeds.
7549.m: In winter it eats seeds and nuts.

7550.q: Which people's right do many cantons have, but not the Confederation?
7550.e: At federal level the people can only use an initiative to demand a change to the constitution, not a new law directly. Many cantons, however, also have the legislative initiative.
7550.m: At federal level there is no legislative initiative.

7552.q: Where do young salmon first grow up after hatching?
a: In salt lakes in the desert
7552.e: The young fish first grow up in the fresh water where they hatched. Only later do they move to the sea.
7552.m: Young salmon first grow up in fresh water.

7553.q: In great tits, who usually sits on the eggs?
7553.e: Usually the female sits on the eggs and keeps them warm. During this time the male brings her food at the nest.
7553.m: The female sits on the eggs.

7554.q: What is a group of spotted hyenas called?
7554.e: Spotted hyenas live in large groups called clans. A clan can have many dozens of animals.

7555.q: Where do llamas often leave their droppings?
a: Only in the shade of trees
7555.e: Llamas often use fixed spots as a toilet. This helps to reduce parasites on the pasture.

7556.q: What does the cheetah's spine do when it runs fast?
a: It is very flexible and bends a lot
It does not move at all
7556.e: The cheetah's spine is especially flexible. This lets it take huge strides when running and become very fast.
7556.m: A flexible spine makes the cheetah fast.

7557.q: Where does the lake trout swim to spawn?
a: Into the streams that flow into the lake
To the deepest part of the lake
Into the reed beds on the shore
7557.e: To spawn, lake trout swim up the streams and rivers that flow into the lake. There they find clean gravel.
7557.m: To spawn, it swims up streams.

7558.q: How does the European tree frog usually behave during the day?
a: It sits quietly and well camouflaged on leaves
It hunts all day, calling loudly
It digs in the sand all day
7558.e: During the day the tree frog usually sits quietly and well camouflaged on leaves. Only at dusk does it become more active and look for food.
7558.m: Quiet by day, active at night.

7559.q: Roughly how long does it take for a slow worm to become old enough to breed?
7559.e: It grows slowly and only becomes able to breed after a few years. This fits with its long life.
7559.m: Slow worms can only breed after several years.

7560.q: Why can a badger become a competitor for hedgehogs?
a: Because it looks for the same food
Because it likes playing with hedgehogs
Because it warns hedgehogs before winter
Because it goes for walks with hedgehogs
7560.e: Badgers and hedgehogs often eat the same insects and worms. That is why the two animals sometimes compete for the same food.
7560.m: Badgers and hedgehogs share their food.

7561.q: What makes the peregrine falcon one of the most widespread birds in the world?
a: It is found on almost every continent in many habitats
It can only survive in cages
It is found on only one single island
7561.e: The peregrine falcon adapts to all kinds of habitats, from cliffs and deserts to cities. That is why it is found on almost every continent.

7562.q: Can a hippopotamus run fast on land despite its size?
a: Yes, it can run surprisingly fast
7562.e: Although hippos look heavy and clumsy, they can run amazingly fast on land. That is why you should never get too close to them.

7563.q: How do baboons usually carry their tail?
a: Always hanging down to the ground
7563.e: Many baboons carry their tail in an arch. But it does not help them grip branches.

7564.q: What are the young of the African wild dog called?
7564.e: As with other dogs, the young are called pups. They are born in a den.
7564.m: Young wild dogs are called pups.

7565.q: What can happen if a beech marten gets into a henhouse?
a: It can kill several hens at the same time
It lays its own eggs there too
It protects the hens from the fox
It eats only the hens' food
7565.e: If a beech marten gets into a henhouse that is not secured, it can kill several hens at once because of an instinct called surplus killing. This makes it unpopular with people who keep chickens.
7565.m: In a henhouse the beech marten can do a lot of damage.

7566.q: What does “cash discount” mean on a bill?
a: A price reduction if you pay the bill very quickly
An extra charge for paying late
7566.e: A cash discount (in German “Skonto”) is a small price reduction you get if you pay a bill within a short time. It rewards paying quickly.
7566.m: A cash discount rewards paying quickly.

7567.q: How does a jellyfish move through the water?
a: It squeezes its bell together and swims that way
7567.e: The jellyfish squeezes its bell-shaped body together and pushes water out. This pushes it forward.
7567.m: A jellyfish swims by pulsing its bell.

7568.q: What kind of eyes does the sand lizard have compared with many night animals?
a: It is active by day and has eyes adapted to daylight
It can only see in complete darkness
7568.e: Because it hunts and suns itself in daylight, its eyesight is well adapted to bright conditions. Night animals, on the other hand, often have larger pupils.
7568.m: As a day animal, it sees best in light.

7569.q: What happens during a solar eclipse?
a: The moon moves in front of the sun
7569.e: When the moon is exactly between the Earth and the sun, it casts its shadow on the Earth. Then it goes dark for a short time.
7569.m: The moon moves in front of the sun.

7570.q: What does a shark's skin feel like when you touch it?
7570.e: A shark's skin is covered with tiny hard tooth-like scales. That is why it feels rough if you stroke it the wrong way.
7570.m: Shark skin feels rough like sandpaper.

7571.q: What relationship do meerkats sometimes have with ground squirrels?
a: They sometimes share burrows and warn each other
7571.e: Meerkats and ground squirrels sometimes live side by side and share burrows. Both benefit from the other's alarm calls.
7571.m: Sometimes they share burrows with ground squirrels.

7572.q: What is the bees' winter cluster made of?
a: Bees huddled tightly together to keep warm
7572.e: The bees form a tight ball of bodies, and it is warmest in the middle. The bees take turns in the colder places on the outside.
7572.m: The winter cluster is made of many bees.

7573.q: Two children are sitting on a seesaw. What happens if one is much heavier than the other?
7573.e: The heavier a child is, the more strongly they push their side of the seesaw down. This is a simple lever effect.
7573.m: The heavier side pushes the seesaw down.

7574.q: Does the badger really hibernate like a hedgehog?
a: No, it only has a winter rest
7574.e: The badger does not truly hibernate. It rests a lot and becomes less active, but wakes up from time to time.
7574.m: Badgers only have a winter rest.

7575.q: Which animals is the leopard most closely related to?
7575.e: Leopards, lions, tigers and jaguars belong to the same genus of big cats. A typical feature is that they can roar.
7575.m: Leopards, lions, tigers and jaguars are closely related big cats.

7576.q: What does a ladybird like to eat best?
7576.e: Ladybirds are busy hunters and like eating small aphids best. A single beetle can eat a great many of them.

7577.q: What kind of coat does a squirrel have all over its body?
a: A thick, soft coat of fur
7577.e: Squirrels are covered all over in soft, thick fur. This keeps them warm and dry.

7578.q: Which body parts do chimpanzees especially use for climbing?
a: Hands and feet with gripping thumbs
7578.e: Chimpanzees can grip well with their hands and feet, because both have a thumb. This lets them climb safely through the trees.
7578.m: Hands and feet help chimpanzees climb.

7579.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Bern?
7579.e: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern and even gave the city its name. The story goes that the founder chose the first animal he killed for it.
7579.m: Bern has a bear on its coat of arms.

7580.q: Which wing shape is typical of the golden eagle when soaring?
a: Very narrow, pointed wings like a falcon's
7580.e: When soaring, the golden eagle spreads its broad wings, and at their tips single feathers spread apart like fingers. This shape helps it fly steadily even when there is little wind.
7580.m: Its wing tips look like fingers.

7581.e: The eggs are laid on or in water. The larvae develop in the water.

7582.q: What does a leopard's typical call often sound like?
7582.e: The leopard's call is often compared to the sound of a saw. It uses it to get attention.
7582.m: The leopard's call sounds like sawing.

7583.q: What does a typical duck's beak look like?
a: Pointed and long like a needle
7583.e: Most ducks have a broad, flat beak. With it they can search for food well in water and mud.
7583.m: Duck beaks are broad and flat.

7584.q: How many wings does a mosquito have?
7584.e: A mosquito has only one pair of wings, so two in total. Many other insects such as beetles have four wings.

7585.q: Which big cat also lived in Europe during the Ice Age?
7585.e: Many thousands of years ago the cave lion lived in Europe. It is extinct today, but it was a close relative of today's lions.
7585.m: There used to be cave lions in Europe.

7586.q: What happens to a brown bear's body during its winter rest?
a: Its heartbeat and body temperature drop slightly
The bear grows a lot during this time
7586.e: During the winter rest a brown bear's heartbeat and body temperature drop only slightly, unlike in animals that truly hibernate. Even so, it spends the cold season almost without food or movement.
7586.m: In winter the bear's body slows down.

7587.q: What does it mean when people say an ant colony is like a superorganism?
a: All the ants work together like one big living being
Each ant lives completely on its own
The colony consists of only one ant
7587.e: An ant colony works like a single large living being. Each ant contributes to the whole with its job.
7587.m: An ant colony is a superorganism.

7588.q: Why do wild budgies often travel around in large flocks?
a: They are looking for water and food
They are fleeing from the snow
They never sleep in the same place twice
7588.e: In Australia there are often long dry periods. That is why budgies move on in flocks to find water and food.
7588.m: Budgies look for water and food together.

7589.q: Which danger threatens otters most today?
7589.e: Many otters die because they are run over when crossing roads near rivers and lakes. This is their biggest danger today.
7589.m: Road traffic is the greatest danger for otters.

7590.q: What do experts in Switzerland recommend when you are out in an area with bears?
a: Make enough noise so that the bear moves away in time
Always creep along very quietly so as not to wake it
Leave food on the path to attract it
Run straight at the bear to scare it off
7590.e: Anyone hiking in areas where brown bears live should make enough noise. This way the bear notices people early and can get out of their way.
7590.m: Making noise when hiking helps to avoid meeting bears.

7591.q: What do dolphins sometimes do with seaweed or seagrass for fun?
a: They carry it on their fin or beak
They eat it as their main food
They build a nest out of it
They weave clothes out of it
7591.e: Some dolphins carry seaweed or seagrass on their fin or snout for fun. This shows how playful these animals are.

7592.q: What kind of eyes does the wood mouse have?
a: Large, dark eyes for seeing at night
Tiny eyes that are almost blind
7592.e: The wood mouse's large eyes help it see well even in the dark.

7593.q: Experts divide streams and rivers into sections according to typical fish. What is the upper, cool and fast-flowing section called?
7593.e: In the cool, oxygen-rich upper course, trout are the main fish. That is why this section is called the trout zone.
7593.m: The trout zone is in the upper course.

a: Yes, for several months every winter
Yes, but only for one day
Yes, but only when it is very cold
7594.e: Guinea pigs stay active all year round and do not sleep any longer in winter than usual. In winter, though, they need special protection from the cold.

7595.q: What does a Bactrian camel do when it has been very thirsty and finds water?
a: It can drink a great many litres in a few minutes
7595.e: A thirsty camel can drink over a hundred litres in a short time. Its blood cells can cope with this.
7595.m: Thirsty camels drink an enormous amount.

a: It hops on its powerful back legs
7596.e: Rabbits have strong back legs that let them hop fast. This means they can also escape quickly from danger.

7598.q: What does a bumblebee like to eat best?
7598.e: Bumblebees drink sweet nectar from flowers and collect pollen as food for their larvae. They get both from many different flowers.

7599.q: Where does the slow worm like to stay?
a: In damp, shady places with hiding places
7599.e: It likes damp meadows, edges of woods and gardens with leaves, stones or wood. There it finds food and places to hide.
7599.m: Slow worms like damp hiding places.

7600.q: What is the perch's lateral line for?
a: It senses movements in the water
7600.e: The lateral line organ contains sense cells that detect currents and pressure waves. This lets the fish notice prey and enemies even in murky water.
7600.m: The lateral line senses movements in the water.

7601.q: Which group of animals does the alpine newt belong to?
7601.e: The alpine newt is an amphibian and belongs to the tailed amphibians. It lives both in water and on land.
7601.m: Alpine newts are amphibians with tails.

7602.q: Where does a common toad spend the winter?
a: Buried in soil or under leaves
7602.e: In winter the common toad buries itself in soil, leaves or a compost heap. There it is protected from the cold.
7602.m: Toads hide under leaves in winter.

7603.q: What kind of teeth does a kangaroo mainly need?
7603.e: Because kangaroos eat a lot of grass, they need broad teeth to grind up the tough grass. Their teeth are replaced again and again during their life.
7603.m: Kangaroos have teeth for grinding grass.

7604.q: What does a goose mainly need its long neck for?
a: To reach grass and plants on the ground
7604.e: With its long neck the goose can graze comfortably without moving its whole body. It can also keep a good lookout for danger.
7604.m: The long neck helps with grazing.

7605.q: Why are a tiger's stripes like a fingerprint?
a: Every tiger has a unique stripe pattern
All tigers have exactly the same stripes
7605.e: No two tigers are alike; the stripe pattern is different on every tiger. This makes it possible to recognise individual tigers.
7605.m: Every tiger has its own pattern.

7606.q: How do brown bears mainly communicate?
a: With sounds such as grunting, body posture and scent marks
Only with loud roaring like a lion
Only by drumming with their paws
7606.e: Brown bears make quiet grunting and huffing sounds and show their mood through body posture. They also leave scent marks on trees.
7606.m: Bears communicate with sounds and scent marks.

7607.q: Why do you sneeze when dust gets into your nose?
a: Your body wants to blow the dust out quickly
Your nose wants to annoy you
7607.e: Sneezing is a reflex that removes foreign objects from the nose. That way the nose is clear again.

7608.q: How do the eyes of dragonflies and damselflies differ?
a: In damselflies the eyes are set far apart
7608.e: In damselflies the eyes sit on the sides of the head with a gap between them. In many dragonflies they touch or lie close together.
7608.m: In damselflies the eyes are far apart.

7609.q: What role do gibbons play for the forest?
a: They spread the seeds of the fruit they eat
7609.e: Gibbons eat fruit and later pass out the seeds again. In this way they help new trees grow in the forest.
7609.m: Gibbons spread seeds in the rainforest.

7610.q: What does a penguin do when it is moving on land and the ground gets steep?
a: It slides down on its belly
7610.e: On steep or snowy slopes, the penguin often lies on its belly and slides down. This is quicker and easier than walking.

7611.q: Why are kangaroos especially important and well known for Australia?
a: They are a symbol of the country
7611.e: Kangaroos are seen as the typical animal of Australia and are known all over the world. They even appear on the country's coat of arms.
7611.m: Kangaroos are a symbol of Australia.

7612.q: Why is the snow leopard threatened by people?
a: Because of poaching and conflicts with herders
7612.e: It is hunted for its fur. Sometimes it kills farm animals, and herders take revenge.

7614.q: What does a magpie's typical call sound like?
a: A quiet twitter like a canary
7614.e: Magpies give loud, rattling calls that often serve as a warning about enemies. This call can be heard from far away and is typical of the species.
7614.m: Magpies have a loud, chattering call.

7615.q: What does a chimpanzee mainly eat?
7615.e: Chimpanzees are omnivores. They mostly eat fruit and plants, but sometimes they also catch small animals.

7617.q: What is the region in northern Europe where the Sami live called?
7617.e: Lapland stretches across Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia. Many reindeer live there.

7618.q: When does the adult cockchafer come out of the pupa?
a: In autumn, but it stays in the ground until spring
Straight away in summer, and it flies at once
In the middle of winter, and it flies
It only hatches after ten years
7618.e: The beetle is already formed in autumn but spends the winter in the ground. In spring it comes out.
7618.m: The beetles spend the winter in the ground.

7619.q: Do female chamois have horns too?
a: Yes, females and males both have horns
No, only the young have horns
7619.e: Unlike some other animals, both male and female chamois have horns. The males' horns, however, are usually a little thicker.
7619.m: Male and female chamois both have horns.

7620.q: What was the bonobo often called in the past?
7620.e: In the past people spoke of the pygmy chimpanzee. But the name is a little misleading, because bonobos are only slightly lighter and slimmer than chimpanzees.
7620.m: The bonobo used to be called the pygmy chimpanzee.

7621.q: Which family of amphibians does the Alpine salamander belong to?
7621.e: The Alpine salamander belongs to the family of true salamanders, which also includes the better-known fire salamander. The two species have a similar body shape.
7621.m: It belongs to the true salamander family.

7622.q: What does the okapi's neck look like compared with the giraffe's?
7622.e: The okapi has a short neck, which suits its life in the forest. It eats leaves at head height or lower.

7623.q: What does the cockchafer often do before taking off?
a: It pumps itself up and warms its flight muscles
7623.e: The beetle moves its wings and body to warm up its flight muscles. Then it takes off with a buzz.
7623.m: Before flying it warms its muscles.

7624.q: Where does the name “fire salamander” probably come from?
a: From an old legend that it could live in fire
7624.e: In the past people believed the fire salamander could survive in the middle of a fire, because it often crawled out of burning wood where it had been hiding. That is probably where its name comes from.

7625.q: In which habitat does the eagle-owl feel especially at home?
a: Cliffs, quarries and landscapes with many gorges
Only in the middle of big cities
7625.e: Eagle-owls prefer rocky habitats such as cliffs, gorges or quarries, often together with forest. Such places offer sheltered nesting sites and good hunting.
7625.m: The eagle-owl likes cliffs and gorges.

7626.q: Where do you take a dog when it is ill or needs a vaccination?
7626.e: Vets examine sick animals and give them the vaccinations they need. This keeps the dog healthy.
7626.m: When an animal is ill, the vet helps.

a: A fixed monthly amount with which young people plan many of their own costs, such as clothes or leisure
A wage that young people get from the state
A wage that only apprentices receive
Money you only get on public holidays
7627.e: In the youth wage model, young people regularly get a fixed amount and budget it themselves for certain areas such as clothing or leisure. This helps them learn early how to handle money.
7627.m: A youth wage is practice in budgeting on your own.

7628.q: What decides how many National Council seats a canton gets?
a: The number of people living in the canton
The year the canton was founded
Always the same number per canton
7628.e: The seats in the National Council are shared out among the cantons in proportion to the resident population. That is why large cantons such as Zurich have many more seats than small ones.
7628.m: A canton with more inhabitants gets more National Council seats.

7630.q: What are animals that break down dead plant material such as wood called?
7630.e: Stag beetle larvae help to break down wood. This returns nutrients to the soil.

7631.q: What does a debt collection agency do?
a: It collects unpaid bills from late payers on behalf of creditors
It gives free advice on tax questions
It manages savings accounts for banks
7631.e: A debt collection agency is hired to collect unpaid bills when someone has not paid. This can mean extra costs for the debtor.

7632.q: What is the fire salamander's striking yellow and black colouring mainly for?
a: As a warning signal to predators
7632.e: The bright colours warn predators that the animal is poisonous. This is called aposematism or warning colouration.

7633.q: Which group of animals does the snow leopard belong to?
7633.e: The snow leopard is a big cat and belongs to the genus Panthera. So it is related to the lion, tiger and leopard.
7633.m: The snow leopard is a big cat.

7634.q: How do hippos often communicate under water?
7634.e: Hippos make loud grunting and roaring sounds, even under water. This way they communicate over long distances.

7635.q: How does a trout find its prey even in murky water?
a: With its lateral line and its sense of smell
It does not, it eats nothing then
7635.e: Even when the water is murky, the trout can track down prey. It uses its sensitive lateral line and its sense of smell.
7635.m: Lateral line and nose help it hunt.

7636.q: How do the pincers help the earwig with flying?
a: By folding up the back wings
By launching it off the ground like a catapult
By steering in the air like a rudder
7636.e: The large back wings are folded in a complicated way. The pincers can help when folding them away.
7636.m: The pincers help fold the wings.

7637.q: What does a newborn panda's fur look like?
a: Completely black and white like its mother
7637.e: Panda babies are born pink and with almost no fur. Their black and white fur only grows after a few weeks.
7637.m: Panda babies are almost hairless at first.

7638.q: How do mallards often live outside the breeding season?
7638.e: Outside the breeding season many mallards join together in larger groups. Together they find food more easily and are safer from enemies.

7639.q: What is a group of grey heron nests in trees called?
7639.e: Many pairs of grey herons breed together in so-called heronries. This gives the birds a certain amount of protection.

a: No, they never go into the water
7641.e: Tigers love swimming and can cover long distances in the water. Among the big cats, they are especially fond of water.

7642.q: On which continent does the red panda live?
7642.e: The red panda lives in mountain forests in Asia, for example in the Himalayas and in China. There it climbs skilfully around in the trees.
7642.m: The red panda lives in Asia.

7643.q: What do mosquito larvae eat in the water?
7643.e: Mosquito larvae filter small algae and particles out of the water and eat them. This is how they grow until they change into adults.
7643.m: Larvae eat algae in the water.

7644.q: What special ability does the giraffe have when it comes to hearing?
a: It can turn its ears in different directions
It has no ears at all
7644.e: Giraffes can turn their ears to pick up sounds from different directions better. This helps them notice danger early.

7645.q: How many species of baboon are usually recognised?
7645.e: Six species are usually recognised: the hamadryas baboon, olive baboon, Guinea baboon, yellow baboon, chacma baboon and Kinda baboon. The gelada is not one of them.
7645.m: There are six species of baboon.

7646.q: What shape are the ladybird's antennae?
a: Short and a little thicker at the end
7646.e: The ladybird's antennae are rather short and have a small thickening at the end. The beetle uses them to smell and feel its surroundings.
7646.m: The antennae are short and thick at the end.

7647.q: Which animals does the praying mantis catch especially often?
7647.e: Flies, grasshoppers, crickets and moths are typical prey. Large species sometimes also catch small vertebrates.
7647.m: Flies and grasshoppers are on the menu.

7648.q: Roughly how old are young golden eagles when they fly for the first time?
7648.e: Young golden eagles stay in the nest for about 70 to 80 days before they fly out for the first time. Even after that, their parents go on feeding them for a few weeks.
7648.m: Young eagles fly out after about 10 weeks.

7649.q: What are the areas with grass and scattered trees where spotted hyenas live called?
7649.e: Savannahs are wide grasslands with few trees. Hyenas find a lot of prey there.
7649.m: Savannahs are the spotted hyena's habitat.

7650.q: What is the black staff symbol in the coats of arms of the two Basel cantons called?
7650.e: The black symbol in the coats of arms of Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft is called the Basel staff. It comes from a bishop's crozier, because Basel used to be a prince-bishopric.
7650.m: The Basel staff is reminiscent of a bishop's crozier.

7651.q: What is the long, pointed mouth of many dolphins called?
7651.e: Many dolphins have a long, pointed snout. The many small teeth sit in it. But they breathe through the blowhole on top of their head.
7651.m: The dolphin's long nose is called a snout.

7652.q: Where does the European garden spider like to build its web best?
a: Between plants, bushes or on fences
Only in the middle of water
In the snow on high mountain peaks
7652.e: The garden spider likes to stretch its web between two plants or on a fence. That way insects easily fly into it.
7652.m: It builds its web between plants.

7653.q: How fast can an orca swim?
7653.e: Orcas are very fast swimmers. They can be faster than most other sea animals.

7654.q: How can you tell that a stream or pond is suitable for fire salamander larvae?
a: It is clean, cool and flows slowly without many fish
It has to be very salty like the sea
It has to be completely dried out
It has to be very warm and still
7654.e: Fire salamander larvae need clean, cool, oxygen-rich water without too many fish that could eat the larvae. Small streams are especially suitable.

7655.q: What is the organ fish use to sense movements in the water called?
7655.e: The lateral line organ runs along the sides of the fish's body. It detects currents and movements nearby.
7655.m: The lateral line senses movements in the water.

7656.q: What do young frogs do as soon as they are fully developed?
a: They leave the water and go on land
They stay in the pond for ever
7656.e: As soon as they have their young frog shape, the little frogs leave the water and explore the land. They usually only return to the water when it is their own time to breed.
7656.m: Young frogs soon leave the water.

7657.q: What covers the common wall lizard's skin, unlike that of frogs?
7657.e: The scaly skin protects the wall lizard and stops it drying out. Frogs, on the other hand, have moist skin that lets water through.
7657.m: Dry scales instead of moist skin.

7658.q: At what height in the Alps can you still find common frogs?
a: Only on the summit of the Matterhorn
7658.e: The common frog is very adaptable and is found even high up in the Alps, sometimes over 2000 metres above sea level. There it still finds small ponds to spawn in.
7658.m: Common frogs also live high in the mountains.

7659.q: Why is the edible dormouse called “Siebenschläfer” (seven sleeper) in German?
a: Because it hibernates for about seven months
Because it always has seven young
Because it sleeps seven hours every day
7659.e: The edible dormouse hibernates for a very long time, often from autumn into spring. That is about seven months.
7659.m: The edible dormouse sleeps for about seven months.

7660.q: How well do alpacas cope with cold?
a: Well, thanks to their thick fleece
Not at all, they need tropical heat
They sleep through the winter like marmots
7660.e: Their thick fleece protects alpacas from the cold. They are adapted to cool mountain areas.
7660.m: A thick fleece protects against cold.

7661.q: Which North American subspecies of the brown bear is especially well known?
7661.e: The grizzly bear is a subspecies of the brown bear that lives in North America. It is known for the grizzled, brownish-grey tips of its fur, which gave it its name.
7661.m: The grizzly is a brown bear.

7662.q: What is the traditional “Gamsbart” (chamois beard) hat decoration made from?
a: From the long hair on the chamois's back
From the beard hairs on its chin
From the hair in its ears
7662.e: The Gamsbart is made from the strip of longer hair on the chamois's back, not from real beard hairs. In the past it was a popular hunting souvenir.
7662.m: The Gamsbart comes from the back, not the chin.

7663.q: Where are woodlice most often found?
7663.e: Woodlice love damp, dark and sheltered places. That is why they hide under stones, bark or leaves.
7663.m: Woodlice like it dark and damp.

7664.q: What does a cockchafer grub look like?
a: Whitish, fat and curved into a C shape
Green and smooth like a snail
7664.e: The grubs are yellowish white with a brown head. They usually lie curled up in the soil.
7664.m: The grubs are white and curved.

7665.q: Roughly how high can a roe deer jump?
7665.e: Roe deer are good jumpers. They can jump over obstacles that are more than a metre high.
7665.m: Roe deer jump far and high.

7666.q: Which animal do baboons sometimes hunt as prey?
7666.e: Olive and yellow baboons in particular sometimes catch the young of small antelopes. But this is only part of their diet.

7667.q: What do great tit chicks look like shortly after hatching?
7667.e: Newly hatched great tit chicks have no feathers yet and cannot see. They depend completely on their parents.
7667.m: Young chicks are naked and blind.

7668.q: What can sheep do well with their ears?
a: They hear well and turn their ears towards a sound
They hear only very high notes
They do not need ears to hear
7668.e: Sheep can hear quite well and turn their ears slightly towards a sound. This way, for example, they quickly notice when someone is coming.
7668.m: Sheep hear well and turn their ears.

7669.q: In what kind of family does the beaver usually live?
a: In a family group with parents and young of different ages
7669.e: Beavers usually live together in small family groups made up of the parents and young of different ages. The group shares the work on the lodge and the care of the young.

7670.q: What do you call stars that can be joined up into pictures in the night sky?
7670.e: Long ago people joined bright stars into figures, for example the Plough. These patterns are called constellations.
7670.m: Constellations are patterns of bright stars.

7671.q: What kind of ears does the wood mouse have?
a: Tiny ears you can hardly see
Long floppy ears like a hare
7671.e: The wood mouse has strikingly large ears that let it hear even quiet sounds well.
7671.m: The wood mouse has large ears and hears well.

7672.q: What does a ladybird chew its food with?
a: It does not chew, it swallows everything whole
With a sucking tube like a butterfly
7672.e: The ladybird has small jaws that it uses to break up its prey, such as aphids. With them it can eat solid food well.
7672.m: Small jaws for breaking up food.

7673.q: How does a young harbour seal learn to catch fish?
a: Its mother feeds it for a whole year
At first it eats only seaweed
7673.e: As soon as a young seal no longer gets milk, it has to learn to catch fish by itself. It usually gets surprisingly good at it after a short time.
7673.m: Young seals quickly learn to hunt.

7674.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult red deer stag get?
7674.e: A large stag can weigh 150 to 200 kilograms. That is as heavy as two or three adults put together.
7674.m: A stag can weigh up to 200 kg.

7675.q: What can the barn owl do when there are lots of mice?
a: Hunt by day instead of at night
7675.e: When there are enough mice, a barn owl can even breed twice a year. This way it has more young.
7675.m: Plenty of food means more broods.

7676.q: What does a dog normally like to eat best?
7676.e: By nature dogs tend to be meat eaters, even though today they usually get balanced dog food. Their teeth are well suited to chewing meat.

7677.q: Why are roads especially dangerous for hedgehogs?
a: Because they roll up when in danger instead of running away
Because they sleep only on roads
7677.e: When there is danger, the hedgehog rolls up instead of running away. But on the road that does not help against cars.
7677.m: Hedgehogs roll up instead of running away.

7678.q: Which sea animal has three hearts and blue blood?
7678.e: The octopus has three hearts that pump its blood around its body. Its blood is blue because it contains copper instead of iron.

7680.q: Which sense organ is especially well developed in the octopus?
7680.e: The octopus has very good eyes and can see well even in low light. With them it spots prey and danger in the sea.

7681.q: Which two species of rhinoceros live in Africa?
7681.e: The white rhinoceros and the black rhinoceros live in Africa. Both can be recognised by the shape of their mouth: the white rhino has a broad mouth, the black rhino a pointed one.
7681.m: Two species of rhino live in Africa.

7682.q: How did the first ibex get back to Switzerland?
a: They were secretly brought from Italy and bred in a wildlife park
They wandered across the border by themselves
They were sent from a zoo in America
7682.e: Because the Italian king protected his ibex strictly, some animals were secretly smuggled into Switzerland. They were then bred in the Peter und Paul wildlife park in St Gallen.

7683.q: Who led the brutal rule of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia?
7683.e: Pol Pot ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979. Under his rule, millions of people died from forced labour, hunger and violence.
7683.m: Pol Pot led the Khmer Rouge.

7684.q: What is an enemy of young wels catfish?
a: Larger predatory fish such as the pike
The golden eagle in the mountains
7684.e: Young wels catfish are eaten by larger predatory fish and water birds. As they grow bigger, they have fewer enemies.
7684.m: Young wels catfish have more enemies.

7685.q: Which teeth help martens, like other carnivores, to cut up meat?
7685.e: Martens are carnivores and, like them, have strong carnassial teeth. With them they can bite through the meat and skin of smaller prey well.

7686.q: What is the name of one of the old town gates in the old town of Solothurn?
7686.e: The Basel Gate is one of the old gates through which people once had to pass to enter the town of Solothurn. Solothurn once had a complete town wall with several towers and gates.
7686.m: The Basel Gate leads into Solothurn's old town.

7687.q: How does a stoat defend itself when a larger enemy attacks it?
a: With a strong-smelling liquid from its glands
With a sting in its tail
7687.e: Like other martens, the stoat has glands that release a strong-smelling liquid when it is in danger. This smell can drive attackers away.
7687.m: A smelly liquid scares off enemies.

7688.q: What extra substance does a woodlouse eat to strengthen its shell?
7688.e: Woodlice need lime for their shell. They take it in with their food and from the soil.

7689.q: How old does a sparrow usually get in the wild?
7689.e: In the wild, sparrows often live only two or three years, because many dangers lie in wait for them. In a protected environment they can sometimes get a little older.
7689.m: Sparrows usually live only a few years.

7690.q: What does a brown bear especially like to eat in autumn while it builds up fat reserves for the winter?
7690.e: In autumn a brown bear eats lots of energy-rich berries and nuts to build up a thick layer of fat before winter. It needs these fat reserves during its winter rest.
7690.m: In autumn the bear eats lots of berries.

7691.q: What is a male Bactrian camel called?
7691.e: Male camels are called bulls and females are called cows. A young camel is called a calf.

7692.q: What is special about the kestrel's beak, typical of falcons?
a: It has a tooth-like notch called the falcon's tooth
It is completely straight like a duck's
It has no tip for tearing meat
It is longer than its whole head
7692.e: Falcons have a small tooth-like notch on the upper beak, called the falcon's tooth. They use it to break their prey's neck.
7692.m: The falcon's tooth helps to kill the prey.

a: Happy hopping out of pure joy
A game of hide and seek
7693.e: When guinea pigs feel very happy, they sometimes suddenly jump about wildly. This joyful hopping is called popcorning.

7694.q: Roughly how old can a red deer get in the wild?
7694.e: Red deer can live to about 15 to 20 years in the wild. In captivity some live even longer.
7694.m: Red deer live to about 15 to 20 years.

7695.q: Besides worms and insects, what else does the badger like to eat?
a: Fruit too, such as berries and windfall apples
7695.e: The badger is an omnivore and also loves sweet fruit. In autumn it likes eating apples that have fallen and berries.
7695.m: Badgers also like berries and fruit.

7696.q: What does the badger do in winter, even though it is often mistaken for true hibernation?
a: It has a winter rest and wakes up now and then
It moves to warmer countries in winter
It stays exactly as active all year
It loses all its fur in winter
7696.e: The badger has a winter rest in which it greatly reduces its activity, but it does not fall into true hibernation like some small mammals. It wakes up from time to time and can be active for short periods.
7696.m: Badgers have a winter rest, not hibernation.

7697.q: Where exactly are the feather “ears” of the great crested grebe?
a: On the back of the head, as two dark tufts of feathers
At the end of the tail
7697.e: The feather ears are two dark, upright tufts of feathers on the back of the head that give the bird its typical look. They are especially easy to see in its breeding plumage.
7697.m: The feather ears sit on top at the back of the head.

7698.q: What do a jackal's ears look like?
7698.e: Upright ears help with hearing. They can also be turned in different directions.

7699.q: Where does the German name for the ibex, “Steinbock” (stone buck), which is also the German name of the star sign Capricorn, come from?
a: From the animal's habitat among rocks and stones
From its liking for eating stones
From a place called Stein in Switzerland
From its discoverer, a scientist called Stein
7699.e: The name Steinbock refers to the animal's habitat in rocky, stony ground high in the mountains. The German name of the star sign is taken from this animal.
7699.m: The name refers to its rocky home.

7700.q: Why are baboons sometimes seen as problem animals by farmers?
7700.e: Baboons can eat maize and other crops. This brings them into conflict with people.

7701.q: How do gorillas often show their feelings in their face?
a: With facial expressions, similar to humans
They have no facial expressions at all
7701.e: Gorillas can show different feelings with their face, for example fear or curiosity. This is one reason why they are like us humans in some ways.
7701.m: Gorillas show feelings in their face.

7703.q: What do otters usually do during the day?
a: They rest hidden in their den
They are at their most active hunting
They travel long distances over land
7703.e: During the day otters retreat to their den, called a holt, and rest. They become active mainly at dusk and at night.
7703.m: By day the otter rests in its holt.

7704.q: How does the European pond turtle usually react when people come near?
a: It slides into the water and dives
It sits still and carries on eating
It buries itself in the sand
7704.e: European pond turtles are very shy. Even at the smallest disturbance they disappear into the water.
7704.m: Pond turtles are shy and dive quickly.

7705.q: What is the pecking order in chickens?
a: The ranking order in the group
7705.e: In every group of chickens there is an order of who may eat first. This ranking order is called the pecking order.

7707.q: How is the wood mouse different from the house mouse?
a: It has larger eyes and ears and reddish-brown fur
It is much bigger than a dog
7707.e: You can recognise the wood mouse by its large eyes and ears and its reddish-brown fur. The house mouse is usually greyer.
7707.m: Large eyes show it is a wood mouse.

7708.q: How many pairs of legs does a centipede have on each body segment?
7708.e: Centipedes have one pair of legs on each body segment. Millipedes have two pairs on most segments.
7708.m: Centipedes have one pair of legs per segment.

7709.q: Which alpaca has especially long, shiny locks?
7709.e: The Suri has long fleece that hangs down in locks. The Huacaya looks more like a fluffy cuddly toy.

7710.q: Why is the earwig not really a worm?
a: Because it has legs, antennae and wings
7710.e: Real worms such as the earthworm have neither legs nor wings. The earwig is an insect with a body made of segments.

7711.q: What have scientists discovered about how dung beetles find their way?
a: They can use the sky, even the Milky Way
They follow the trails of ants
7711.e: Experiments showed that dung beetles use the starry sky at night to tell which way they are rolling. They use the bright band of the Milky Way to do this.
7711.m: Dung beetles find their way by the starry sky.

7712.q: How is the Bactrian camel different from the dromedary in size and build?
a: It is more strongly built and has longer hair
It is much smaller and hairless
It has longer, thin legs with no hair
7712.e: Bactrian camels are stockier and have a thick coat, especially in winter. They are adapted to cold winters.
7712.m: Bactrian camels are stronger and shaggier.

7713.q: Why are many dragonfly species endangered in Switzerland?
a: Because ponds, streams and wetlands are disappearing
Because they like too much snow
Because they are eaten by roe deer
Because they eat only fir needles
7713.e: Draining, building and pollution take away the dragonflies' habitat. That is why many species are on the Red List.

7714.q: What is the principle called by which the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities share out tasks between them?
7714.e: In Switzerland there are three levels: the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities. Each level takes on certain tasks; this is called federalism.
7714.m: Federalism shares out tasks across three levels.

7715.q: What does the Federal Council do before a vote to make its position known?
a: It issues an official voting recommendation
7715.e: The Federal Council gives a recommendation on every proposal, saying whether to vote yes or no. This recommendation is also printed in the voting booklet.
7715.m: The Federal Council recommends Yes or No.

7717.q: Which bird family does the magpie belong to?
7717.e: The magpie belongs to the crow family, just like crows and ravens. These birds are considered especially clever.
7717.m: Magpies are clever members of the crow family.

7718.q: In which well-known fairy tale does a wolf play a big, dangerous part against a girl and her grandmother?
7718.e: In the fairy tale Little Red Riding Hood, the wolf dresses up as the grandmother to trick the girl. This story is one of the best-known fairy tales of the Brothers Grimm.
7718.m: A wolf appears in Little Red Riding Hood.

7719.q: What, among other things, does the bison use its shoulder hump for?
a: For the muscles that carry its heavy head
As a water store like a camel
As a hiding place for its young
7719.e: The hump contains strong muscles that hold up the large head. They also help when it clears snow away with its head.
7719.m: The hump is made of strong muscles.

7720.q: How long can an ant queen live?
7720.e: An ant queen can live for many years. That is much longer than an ordinary worker lives.
7720.m: The queen lives a very long time.

7721.q: In which order does a housefly grow up?
7721.e: A maggot hatches from the egg. The maggot becomes a pupa, and the adult fly then hatches from the pupa.

7722.q: How do people protect salmon so that they can live in rivers again?
a: With fish ladders and by restoring rivers to a natural state
7722.e: Fish ladders and natural rivers help migrating fish. There are projects to bring salmon back to the Rhine.
7722.m: Fish ladders and river restoration help salmon.

7723.q: In which body of water that also borders Switzerland does the lake trout live?
7723.e: Lake Constance is a large, cool Alpine lake and so a typical habitat. There are also lake trout in many Swiss lakes.
7723.m: Lake Constance is a lake trout lake.

7724.q: What can ducklings already do shortly after hatching?
a: Swim and look for food themselves
7724.e: Ducklings leave the nest very early. They can swim and look for food with their mother shortly after hatching.

7725.q: Which species of baboon is the largest?
7725.e: The chacma baboon is the largest species of baboon. It lives in southern Africa.
7725.m: The chacma baboon is the largest species.

7726.q: How fast does a cheetah speed up at the start of its sprint?
a: Almost as fast as a sports car
Only a few centimetres per second
It does not, it always starts slowly
7726.e: A cheetah can go from standing still to top speed in a few seconds. That is almost as quick as a fast car.

7727.q: Which birds sometimes eat mosquitoes too?
7727.e: Swallows often fly low over meadows and water and snap small insects such as mosquitoes out of the air. In this way they help to reduce the number of mosquitoes.

7728.q: Which danger threatens the sand lizard in Switzerland in particular?
a: The loss of suitable habitats to building and farming
Lack of food in the zoo
7728.e: Dry, sunny areas are becoming rarer because they are built on or used for farming. This makes it hard for the sand lizard to survive.
7728.m: Habitat loss is a serious threat to the sand lizard.

7729.q: What is a feature of the adder's scales?
a: They are keeled and feel rough
They are as smooth as a mirror
They are as soft as fur
7729.e: The scales on its back have a small ridge running along them. That is why they do not feel smooth.

7730.q: What does the golden jackal eat?
7730.e: The golden jackal eats whatever it finds. This ranges from small mammals to fruit.
7730.m: The golden jackal eats all sorts of food.

7731.q: What do baby turtles use to open the eggshell?
a: The claws on their back legs
They wait for their mother to help
7731.e: The egg tooth is a small hard point on the snout. It falls off later when it is no longer needed.
7731.m: The egg tooth helps with hatching.

7732.q: In what form does the praying mantis spend the winter in our region?
a: As eggs in a foam case
As an adult in the snow
As a pupa in a cocoon in the water
7732.e: The adults die in autumn. The eggs get through the winter protected in the egg case.
7732.m: Only the eggs survive the winter.

7733.q: What striking teeth do adult male wild boar have?
a: Long gnawing teeth like a hare
Pointed venomous fangs like a snake
Flat grinding teeth at the front of the mouth
7733.e: Adult male boar have strong tusks curving upwards, which they can use to defend themselves. In females these teeth are much smaller.

7734.q: Where do tigers mainly live in the wild?
7734.e: Tigers live in various countries in Asia, for example India and Russia. There are no wild tigers in Africa.

7735.q: Which country has a flag that, apart from its proportions, looks almost exactly like the flag of Monaco?
7735.e: The flags of Indonesia and Monaco both consist of a red and a white stripe, but they differ in their proportions. Indonesia has used its flag since independence in 1945.
7735.m: Indonesia and Monaco have almost identical flags.

7736.q: What job does an elephant do in the ecosystem?
a: It spreads seeds and creates clearings
7736.e: Seeds are spread far and wide in its dung. Elephants also make gaps in the forest where new life can grow.
7736.m: Elephants spread seeds and open up forests.

7737.q: What is a sign that an animal is an insect?
7737.e: All insects have six legs. Spiders have eight and so they are not insects.

7738.q: What lets the European tree frog make long jumps?
a: Flaps of skin on its sides
7738.e: With its strong, long back legs the tree frog can jump a long way. This lets it escape quickly from possible predators.
7738.m: Strong back legs make long jumps possible.

a: A South American fish that can give electric shocks
A kind of eel from Switzerland
