An eel that is feeling cold
7739.e: The electric eel lives in the Amazon region and produces strong electric shocks. It is not closely related to the European eel.
7739.m: The electric eel is not a true eel.

7740.q: How is the common buzzard protected by law in Switzerland?
a: Like all birds of prey, it is protected by law
It can be hunted all year round
It is not protected at all
Only its eggs may be collected
7740.e: In Switzerland all native birds of prey, including the common buzzard, are protected by law. It is forbidden to catch or kill them or to disturb their nests.
7740.m: Protected by law like all birds of prey.

7741.q: Which insect likes to eat mosquito larvae in the water?
7741.e: Dragonfly larvae also live in water and hunt small mosquito larvae there. In this way they help to keep the number of mosquitoes down.
7741.m: Dragonfly larvae eat mosquito larvae in the water.

7742.q: In which habitat on warm coasts are seahorses also often found?
7742.e: Mangrove forests grow in shallow salt water on warm coasts. Among their roots seahorses find plenty to hold on to and lots of food.

7743.q: How many kidneys does a healthy person usually have?
7743.e: The two kidneys lie to the left and right of the spine. Together they filter the blood and make urine.

7744.q: What does it usually mean when a cockerel spreads his wings and dances around a hen?
a: He wants to impress the hen
7744.e: With spread wings and a little dance, a cockerel often shows his interest in a hen. This behaviour is part of natural courtship.
7744.m: The cockerel courts with spread wings.

7745.q: In which habitats are carrion crows often found in Switzerland?
a: In fields, in parks and also in towns
7745.e: Carrion crows are very adaptable and live in Switzerland on farmland, in parks, at the edges of woods and even in the middle of towns. They find enough food there.
7745.m: Crows even live in the middle of Swiss towns.

7746.q: What does a carp like to eat best?
7746.e: Carp are not fussy and eat almost anything they find on the bottom. This includes worms, small animals and bits of plants.
7746.m: Carp eat almost anything on the bottom.

7747.q: For roughly how long have people been keeping pigs?
7747.e: People began to domesticate pigs about 9000 years ago. This makes the pig one of the oldest domestic animals of all.
7747.m: Pigs have been domestic animals for thousands of years.

7748.q: How do dolphins sleep without drowning?
a: One half of the brain stays awake
They hold their breath for days
7748.e: Even when sleeping, dolphins have to come up now and then to breathe. That is why only one half of their brain sleeps while the other stays awake.
7748.m: In dolphins only one half of the brain sleeps.

7749.q: What does a common buzzard often do after catching a mouse?
a: It carries it to a perch to eat it
It lets it go again at once
It buries it in the ground for ever
It throws it into the nearest water
7749.e: When the common buzzard has caught prey, it often carries it to a branch or post to eat it in peace. From there it also has a good view of its surroundings.
7749.m: The prey is carried to a perch.

7750.q: Where does the German name for the common buzzard, “Mäusebussard” (mouse buzzard), originally come from?
a: From its liking for mice as prey
From coming from a country called Mouse
From its colour, which looks like mouse fur and has nothing to do with hunting
From a famous scientist called Bussard
7750.e: The name goes back to the bird's liking for mice as important prey. “Bussard” is an old word for a larger bird of prey.
7750.m: The name points to hunting mice.

7751.q: What do you sometimes find on the beach that a small shark has hatched from?
7751.e: Some sharks lay eggs in a leathery case. When the young has hatched, the empty case is sometimes washed up on the beach.
7751.m: Some sharks hatch from egg cases.

7752.q: What does a wasp often do when it smells something sweet?
a: It flies over to it curiously
7752.e: Wasps have a good sense of smell for sweet things. That is why they come flying quickly when something smells nice.
7752.m: Wasps smell sweet things very well.

7753.q: How does the jaguar creep up on its prey?
7753.e: The pattern of its coat camouflages it in the shade and among the leaves. This lets it stalk close to its prey.
7753.m: Its coat camouflages the jaguar in the forest.

7754.q: Why are wild boar sometimes unpopular with farmers?
7754.e: When wild boar look for food on fields, they churn up the ground. This can mean great damage for farmers.

7755.q: Where does the German name for the marmot, “Murmeltier”, probably originally come from?
a: From a Latin word for mountain mouse
Because the animals murmur all the time like people talking
7755.e: The name Murmeltier probably goes back to the Latin words mus montanus, which mean mountain mouse. Over several stages of the language, today's word developed from it.

7756.q: What is special about the perch's front dorsal fin?
a: It is made only of soft rays
It is poisonous like a jellyfish
It has turned into a sucker
7756.e: The first dorsal fin is supported by hard, spiny rays. When there is danger, the perch raises it, which makes it harder to swallow.
7756.m: The spiny fin protects the perch from enemies.

7757.q: Why does the cheetah like living in open savannahs?
a: Because it has plenty of room to run there
Because there is especially a lot of water there
Because it can climb well there
Because it is especially cold there
7757.e: In the open savannah the cheetah can see its prey from far away. There it also has enough room to run fast.
7757.m: The cheetah needs open land to run.

7758.q: Roughly how long does a common earwig grow?
7758.e: The common earwig is a rather small insect. It usually measures about one to two centimetres.
7758.m: It is only about one to two cm long.

7759.q: Why do salmon often have a silvery colour in the sea?
a: It camouflages them from enemies in open water
7759.e: Silvery fish are hard to see in open water. This protects them from predatory fish and seabirds.

7760.q: What do reindeer, as ruminants, do with their food?
a: They bring it back up and chew it again
They collect it in cheek pouches
They eat it only in liquid form
7760.e: Ruminants first swallow their food almost unchewed. Later they bring it back up and chew it thoroughly.

7761.q: How are a dragonfly's eyes built?
7761.e: Dragonflies have huge compound eyes made of many single eyes. With them they can see almost all the way round and spot movement very well.

7762.q: What body shape does the pike have?
a: Long and slim like an arrow
7762.e: The pike's body is long and slim like an arrow. This makes it very fast in the water.
7762.m: The pike is long and slim.

7763.q: What colour is the sticky liquid that comes out of a hippopotamus's skin?
7763.e: A hippo's skin gives off a reddish, oily liquid. It looks almost like blood, but it is not blood.

7765.q: Roughly how tall can an adult brown bear be when standing on its back legs?
7765.e: When a large brown bear stands up on its back legs, it can reach a height of up to 2.5 metres. This makes it look especially impressive and huge.
7765.m: Standing upright, a bear can be up to 2.5 metres tall.

7767.q: Roughly how big is a magpie's wingspan?
7767.e: A magpie's wingspan is about 52 to 60 centimetres. Despite this size, its flight often looks rather heavy.

7768.q: Where does a female wolf usually give birth to her pups?
a: In a sheltered cave or den
In the middle of an open meadow
In the water at the lake shore
7768.e: For the birth, female wolves look for a sheltered cave, a crack in the rocks or a den they dig themselves. There the pups are protected from the weather and enemies.
7768.m: Pups are born in a sheltered den.

7769.q: What role did dromedaries play in trade across the Sahara?
7769.e: Caravans of pack camels carried salt across the desert, for example. Dromedaries cope well with heat and thirst.
7769.m: Dromedaries carried goods across the desert.

7770.q: How does the cuckoo's egg manage not to stand out?
a: It looks almost the same as the host bird's eggs
It is much smaller than all the others
7770.e: The female cuckoo lays eggs whose colour and pattern look like the host bird's eggs. That is why the host birds often do not notice the trick.
7770.m: Cuckoo eggs fool the host birds.

7771.q: How many eggs does a female red kite usually lay per brood?
a: Only one egg in her whole life
7771.e: The female usually lays two to three eggs in the nest. Occasionally there is only one, or up to four.
7771.m: The red kite usually lays one to three eggs.

7772.q: Apart from lakes, where else are perch raised?
a: In fish farms with water recycling systems
7772.e: Perch are also bred in fish farms, often in recycling systems where the water is cleaned and used again. This way fish for eating can be produced all year round.
7772.m: Perch also grow up in fish farms.

7774.q: In which famous story do a donkey, a dog, a cat and a cockerel appear together?
7774.e: In this famous fairy tale four old animals set off together to become town musicians. The donkey sets the first note.
7774.m: A donkey is one of the town musicians in the fairy tale.

7776.q: What do a butterfly's antennae often have at the end, unlike those of many moths?
7776.e: Butterflies almost always have antennae with a small club at the end. Moths, on the other hand, often have feathery or thin antennae without a thickening.
7776.m: Butterflies have clubs on their antennae.

7777.q: For how long does a common swift stay in the air almost non-stop outside the breeding season?
a: Almost the whole rest of the year
Only a few minutes a day
Only for a few weeks in spring
7777.e: Except during the breeding season, swifts hardly ever land. Eating, drinking, sleeping and even mating mostly happen in flight.
7777.m: It stays in the air almost all year.

7778.q: Why can a roe deer fawn hardly be smelled in its first few days?
a: It has almost no smell of its own, which protects it from enemies
It wears a perfume from its mother
7778.e: A newborn fawn has almost no smell. This protects it from being sniffed out by predators such as the fox.
7778.m: Fawns hardly smell, which protects them.

7779.q: What does a great crested grebe do when it has caught a fish that is too big to swallow straight away?
a: It often brings it to the surface and works on it before swallowing
It lets the fish go again at once
It shares the fish with other birds
It buries the fish on the shore
7779.e: Large fish are first turned into the right position at the surface so they are easier to swallow. The bird often turns the prey with its beak while doing this.
7779.m: Large fish are worked on before swallowing.

7780.q: What does a pack of African wild dogs often do before setting off to hunt?
a: It greets each other excitedly with calls and running about
It falls into a deep sleep
7780.e: Before the hunt there is often a kind of greeting ceremony. The animals run around, call and get in tune with each other.
7780.m: Before the hunt there is a greeting ritual.

7781.q: How do male and female least weasels differ in size?
a: Both are exactly the same size
7781.e: Male least weasels are often almost twice as heavy as females. This size difference is found in many species of the weasel family.

7782.q: What are the striking tufts on an eagle-owl's head really?
a: Real ear flaps made of cartilage
What is left of old antlers
7782.e: The tufts of feathers on the eagle-owl's head look like ears but are only feathers. The real ear openings are hidden under the feathers of the face.
7782.m: An eagle-owl's ear tufts are not real ears.

7783.q: How many toes does a giraffe have on each foot?
7783.e: Giraffes are even-toed hoofed animals, like cows and deer. They walk on two large toes on each foot.
7783.m: Giraffes have two toes on each foot.

7784.q: When does the pike lay its eggs?
a: On one single day in summer
7784.e: In spring the pike swims into shallow water with plants to lay its eggs there. The warm water helps the eggs develop.

7785.q: Why does a cat sometimes hunt even when it is not hungry at all?
a: Because the hunting instinct is inborn
Because it gets bored and therefore turns nasty
Because it only does it in its dreams
7785.e: A cat's hunting instinct is inborn and has nothing to do with hunger. Playing with a mouse or a ball trains this instinct.
7785.m: Hunting is part of a cat's natural instinct.

7786.q: Why does a suction cup stick to a smooth tile?
a: Air pressure presses it on from the outside
The suction cup is a magnet
The suction cup gets warm and melts
7786.e: The air is pushed out from under the suction cup, so there is low pressure there. The air pressure from outside then presses it firmly against the wall.
7786.m: Air pressure holds the suction cup in place.

7787.q: What colour are blackbird eggs usually?
7787.e: Blackbird eggs are usually greenish blue with small brown speckles. This colour camouflages them well in the nest.
7787.m: Blackbird eggs are greenish blue with spots.

7788.q: Why is polar bear fur so good against the cold?
a: The hairs are hollow and keep in warmth
All the hairs fall out in winter
7788.e: Each of the polar bear's hairs is hollow inside. This means they insulate especially well against the cold.
7788.m: Hollow hairs keep the polar bear warm.

7789.q: What is the process called in which a millipede sheds its old outer covering?
7789.e: The firm outer skeleton does not grow with the animal. That is why it is shed regularly.
7789.m: The outer skeleton does not grow with it.

7790.q: In which Swiss city is the International Olympic Committee based?
7790.e: The International Olympic Committee organises the Olympic Games and is based in Lausanne. That is why Lausanne is also called the “Olympic Capital”.

7791.q: Roughly how big can an adult beaver get, not counting the tail?
7791.e: Without its tail, an adult beaver's body measures about 80 to 100 centimetres. This makes it one of the largest rodents in Europe.
7791.m: Beavers grow up to 1 metre long.

7792.q: Which kinds of water does the grass snake use?
7792.e: It needs calm water with lots of plants along the bank. There it finds food and places to hide.
7792.m: Calm water with plants on the bank.

7793.q: Why are bumblebees useful for people and nature?
a: They pollinate plants so that fruit can grow
They eat the weeds in the garden
They make honey for the supermarket
7793.e: Without pollinators such as the bumblebee, many kinds of fruit and vegetables could not grow. That is why bumblebees are very important for our food.

7794.q: What can you often see on your body after a mosquito bite?
a: A small tear in the skin
7794.e: After a bite a small red bump often forms and itches. This comes from the saliva that the mosquito releases when it bites.

7795.q: What do you call the journey water makes from the sea, through the clouds and back down to Earth?
7795.e: Water evaporates from lakes and seas, forms clouds and falls down again as rain. This journey repeats again and again.
7795.m: Water travels round and round in a cycle.

7796.q: Why is a full shopping trolley harder to push than an empty one?
7796.e: There are lots of things in the full trolley, so it weighs more. The heavier something is, the more force you need to push it.

7797.q: Where do most of the world's kingfisher species mainly live?
7797.e: The greatest variety of kingfisher species is found in tropical regions of Africa, Asia and Australia. Our native kingfisher is one of the few species in temperate regions.
7797.m: Most kingfisher species live in the tropics.

7798.q: Can a trout swim well against the current?
a: Only when it is still young
7798.e: Trout have strong muscles and a slim body. With them they can even swim against the current to reach their spawning grounds.
7798.m: Trout swim strongly against the current.

7799.q: Which kind of dolphin do you see most often in films and animal parks?
7799.e: The bottlenose dolphin is the best-known kind of dolphin. You often see it in films and animal parks.
7799.m: The bottlenose dolphin is the best-known dolphin.

7800.q: What does a llama mainly eat?
7800.e: Llamas are plant eaters. They mainly eat grasses, hay and herbs.

7801.q: What can a pond skater not do with its body?
a: Breathe under water for long periods
Suck out prey with its mouthpart
7801.e: It needs air and lives on the surface. It has no gills for living under water.
7801.m: It needs air and lives on the surface.

7802.q: In which season does the red kite usually lay its eggs in Switzerland?
a: In spring, usually March or April
In the middle of winter, January
7802.e: The red kite starts breeding in spring, as soon as it is back from its winter quarters or the winter is over. This way the young can grow up in summer with plenty of food.
7802.m: The red kite breeds in spring.

7803.q: In which regions of Switzerland does the edible dormouse mainly live?
a: In the Swiss Plateau and the Jura
Only high up on Alpine glaciers
Only in Ticino by the sea
7803.e: The edible dormouse prefers broadleaf woods in the Swiss Plateau and the Jura. It is hardly found at very high altitudes.
7803.m: It lives mainly in the Swiss Plateau and the Jura.

7804.q: How long does a pair of wolves usually stay together?
a: Often for many years, sometimes for life
Never, wolves pair up at random
7804.e: Wolves often form long-lasting pairs and frequently stay with the same partner for years or even their whole life. This pair usually forms the core of the pack.
7804.m: Wolf pairs often stay together for a long time.

7805.q: Who is often in charge in a group of bonobos?
7805.e: In bonobos, the females stick closely together and often have a high rank. So, unlike in chimpanzees, it is usually not the males who are in charge.
7805.m: In bonobos the females are often in charge.

7807.q: What does panachage mean in an election?
a: Writing names from different lists on the same ballot paper
Handing in a blank ballot paper
7807.e: With panachage, you mix candidates from different parties on one ballot paper. This is possible in proportional elections such as the National Council election.
7807.m: Panachage mixes names from different lists.

7808.q: In which landscape does the barn owl like to hunt best?
a: On glaciers high in the mountains
In the river in the middle of town
7808.e: The barn owl likes hunting best over open fields and meadows. That is where it finds the most mice.
7808.m: Open fields are its hunting ground.

7809.q: What does the male common frog do at the pond in spring to stay with a female?
a: He clings tightly to her back
He builds her a nest of grass
He carries her eggs in his mouth
7809.e: The male climbs onto the female's back and holds on tight. When the female lays the eggs in the water, the male is right there.
7809.m: The male clings to the female.

7810.q: Roughly how long is a mother koala pregnant?
7810.e: A koala's pregnancy is very short and lasts only about 35 days. After that the baby is tiny and not yet fully developed.
7810.m: Koala babies are born after about a month.

7811.q: Why are hard winters dangerous for the barn owl?
a: Because it can hardly find mice under the snow
Because it cannot see anything in the snow
7811.e: When there is a lot of snow, the barn owl has trouble finding the mice under the blanket of snow. Then it can go hungry and grow weaker.

7812.q: Why is the Roman snail an unwelcome guest in some gardens?
a: Because it likes nibbling garden plants
7812.e: Some gardeners are not so keen on Roman snails because they nibble lettuce and other plants. But snails are important for nature.

7813.e: The stoat hunts both by day and by night. This makes it a very flexible predator.
7813.m: The stoat hunts day and night.

7814.q: What do penguins do to keep their feathers clean and waterproof?
a: They preen them with their beak and oil
7814.e: Penguins use their beak to spread a special oil from a gland over their feathers. This is called preening, and it keeps the feathers waterproof.
7814.m: Penguins preen their feathers with oil.

7815.q: Why is a hot summer dangerous for brown trout?
a: The prey animals get too big
7815.e: The warmer the water, the less oxygen it can hold. For cold-water fish it then becomes life-threatening.

7817.q: What is the job of a guide dog for the blind?
a: It guides and supports a visually impaired person in everyday life
7817.e: Guide dogs are specially trained to accompany blind or visually impaired people safely through everyday life. For example, they recognise obstacles and traffic lights.
7817.m: Guide dogs help visually impaired people.

7818.q: Why do many vets have cats neutered?
a: To prevent uncontrolled breeding and stray cats
So that the cat grows faster
So that it can miaow better
So that it has more kittens
7818.e: Neutering stops cats from breeding uncontrollably and too many stray cats from appearing. It can also reduce certain behaviours and illnesses.

7819.q: How many toes do hyenas have on their paws?
7819.e: Hyenas have four toes on each front and back paw. They cannot pull in their claws.
7819.m: Hyenas have four toes on each paw.

7820.q: What do sheep often do when they get a fright?
a: They run away quickly in a tight bunch
They stand alone and fall asleep
7820.e: When sheep get a fright, they usually run away quickly in a tight bunch. In the close group they feel safer from danger.
7820.m: Sheep flee in a tight bunch.

7821.q: In which European countries, among others, is the kingfisher found?
a: Among others, in Switzerland, Germany and France
Nowhere in Europe, only in Africa
7821.e: The kingfisher is widespread in large parts of Europe, including Switzerland, Germany and France. It lives wherever there are suitable waters.
7821.m: The kingfisher lives in many European countries.

7822.q: How old can an eel get in captivity?
7822.e: Eels can get very old in aquariums, in some cases over 80 years. In the wild they usually die much younger.

7823.q: What does a starfish like to eat best?
7823.e: Starfish like eating mussels and other animals on the seabed. They are skilful hunters.

7824.q: What is the Roman snail's shell made of?
7824.e: The Roman snail's shell is made of hard lime. It protects the snail's soft body.
7824.m: A snail shell is made of lime.

7825.q: Which salamander lives high in the Alps and gives birth to fully formed young instead of larvae?
7825.e: The Alpine salamander lives at higher, colder altitudes. Its young develop completely inside the mother's body, without any larvae in the water. Fire salamanders and newts, on the other hand, need water for their larvae.
7825.m: Alpine salamanders do not need water for larvae.

7826.q: Which animal is the donkey's closest relative?
7826.e: Donkeys and horses both belong to the horse family. They can even have young together.

7827.q: Roughly how many different jobs does a worker bee have during her life?
a: Several, with different jobs depending on her age
Only one for her whole life
7827.e: Young workers first clean the hive, then feed the larvae, and only later fly out to collect food. So the jobs change during a bee's life.

7828.q: What is special about the mole's skin for life in tunnels?
a: It is loose, so it can turn easily
It is prickly like a hedgehog's
It sticks tightly to the body
7828.e: The mole's skin sits loosely around its body. This makes it easier for it to turn round in narrow tunnels.

7829.q: What is the Bear Pit in Bern known for?
a: Brown bears have been kept there for a long time
A ski race takes place there every year
7829.e: Brown bears have been kept in the Bear Pit in Bern for centuries. The bear is closely linked to the city of Bern and is even connected with its name.
7829.m: Bern's brown bears live in the Bear Pit.

7830.q: What does the kingfisher's beak look like?
a: Long and pointed like a dagger
7830.e: The beak is long, straight and pointed like a dagger. With it the kingfisher can snap up fish in a flash.
7830.m: The kingfisher has a dagger-like beak for catching fish.

7831.q: Which large group of animals does the stag beetle belong to?
7831.e: Stag beetles have six legs and a body made of head, thorax and abdomen. This makes them insects, or more exactly beetles.
7831.m: The stag beetle is an insect and a beetle.

7832.q: Which kind of trout lives in the sea and swims into rivers to spawn?
7832.e: The sea trout spends part of its life in the sea. To lay its eggs it then swims back into the rivers where it was born.
7832.m: Sea trout migrate from the sea into rivers.

7833.q: What does a chimpanzee often do to show respect to a higher-ranking chimpanzee?
7833.e: Lower-ranking chimpanzees often make quiet grunting sounds in front of a higher-ranking animal. This shows that they accept the ranking order.
7833.m: Quiet sounds show respect in the group.

7834.q: How is a beech marten built compared with a pet cat?
a: Exactly the same weight and build
7834.e: The beech marten is about as long as a cat, but much slimmer, and weighs only about one and a half kilograms. This makes it a skilful hunter.
7834.m: The beech marten is slimmer and lighter than a cat.

7835.q: Why do trout sometimes jump out of the water?
a: To catch insects or get past obstacles
To breathe air like a whale
To warm up in the sun
7835.e: Trout sometimes jump to snap up insects above the surface of the water. They sometimes also get past small waterfalls with a jump.
7835.m: Trout jump for insects and over obstacles.

7836.q: Apart from their work, what do people use from domestic camels?
7836.e: The wool is made into textiles, and the milk is used as food. Meat is sometimes used too.

7837.q: What does a meerkat's tail look like?
7837.e: The tail is slim and comes to a point. It also helps the meerkat balance when standing upright.
7837.m: The tail is thin and pointed.

7838.q: What do the pupils in a goat's eye look like?
7838.e: A goat's pupils lie across the eye like a broad line. This lets goats see almost all the way round and spot danger early.

7839.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female alpine newt lay in one season?
7839.e: A female lays her eggs one at a time, spread over several weeks. Altogether this often comes to about 100 to 200 eggs per season.
7839.m: A female lays about a hundred eggs.

7840.q: Which feature is typical of the ladybird compared with many other beetles?
a: Its round shape and striking spots
Being as big as a finger
7840.e: Ladybirds are easy to recognise by their round, dome-shaped body with colourful spots. This makes them different from many other kinds of beetle.
